intro:
Times Square is the junction of Broadway and Seventh Avenue in Midtown Manhattan, and the bars on our list fan out from it in three directions. One group sits in the West 40s near the Port Authority Bus Terminal, another runs along Broadway and the side streets of the upper 40s, and a third gathers on West 54th to 57th Streets around Seventh Avenue, close to Carnegie Hall. The 42nd Street station complex, with twelve lines, covers the south end, while 49th Street, 50th Street and 57th Street–7th Avenue handle the rest.

Happy hour in Times Square is mostly a weekday, early evening affair, and restaurants supply many of the deals: oysters at Blue Fin, barbecue at Famous Dave's, tropical cocktails at Havana Central, flavored vodka at Russian Samovar. A second wave starts late at night, at Tanner Smith's every day and at Bartley's early in the week. If you have theater tickets, the timing helps: most windows close before evening curtains go up, so have a drink first and eat after the show.

picks.why: Blue Fin is a seafood restaurant at 1567 Broadway, two minutes from the 49th Street N, R and W stop. Its happy hour runs every day and leans on food, with market oysters, mini lobster rolls and crispy cauliflower. The restaurant's own menu adds a second window late at night and limits the deal to the bar area, so take a stool.

Castell is a rooftop lounge inside the AC Hotel at 260 West 40th Street, with Spanish tapas, small plates and flatbreads on the menu. On weekdays the deal covers cocktails, wines and beer, which makes it a handy after-work meeting point three minutes from the 42nd Street–Port Authority station. Reservations go through OpenTable.

Famous Dave's is the food-first pick here. On weekdays its happy hour list covers fries, fried pickles, rib tips, a chopped pork sandwich, a wing basket and a build-your-own burger, enough to make a meal before a show. It is on West 47th Street, a minute from the 49th Street station, and our listing shows no booking link.

Hard Rock Cafe sits at 1501 Broadway, two minutes from the Times Square station and its twelve lines. The weekday deal is served at the bar and covers domestic and import drafts plus cocktails, and the menu also mentions wells, wines and shareable plates. The address is easy to give to friends who do not know Midtown, and tables can be booked on OpenTable.

Tanner Smith's is a pub on West 55th Street and the only spot on our list here with a late-night happy hour every single night, running from late evening to close. Negronis, old fashioneds, Aperol spritzes, pinot noir and two craft beers are on it. The 57th Street–7th Avenue N, Q, R and W stop is a minute away, and Resy takes bookings.

Faces & Names, a bar at 159 West 54th Street, keeps the same happy hour seven days a week, from mid-afternoon into the early evening. Bottled domestic beers, house wine, well drinks and a bucket of select beers are on the list, plus a daily special that changes with the day of the week. The 7th Avenue B, D and E stop is a minute's walk.

Russian Samovar, a restaurant and piano bar on West 52nd Street, pours flavored vodka mixed drinks, domestic beer and house wine at happy hour prices Monday to Friday. Its menu also lists happy hour appetizers such as vareniki and fried pelmeni, and a second window late at night. Book on Resy; the 50th Street C and E stop is two minutes away.

sections.body: Twelve lines meet at the 42nd Street complex, which joins the Times Square and Port Authority stations and is closest to bars on West 40th to 44th Streets such as Castell, Fushimi and Gyu-Kaku. For the upper 40s, use 49th Street on the N, R and W, or 50th Street on the C and E or the 1. The 7th Avenue stop on the B, D and E and 57th Street–7th Avenue on the N, Q, R and W serve the cluster near Carnegie Hall, and 47th–50th Streets–Rockefeller Center on the B, D, F and M covers Sixth Avenue.

Menu prices in New York leave out the 8.875 percent sales tax, and servers expect an 18 to 20 percent tip on top. Around Times Square several restaurants, including Blue Fin, Fushimi and Bill's Bar & Burger, limit the deal to the bar, so a table may mean full price. Every bar page shows the date we last checked its happy hour; glance at it before you build a pre-show plan around one.

faq.a: Yes. Tanner Smith's on West 55th Street runs a late-night happy hour every night, and Bartley's on West 54th Street has one Sunday through Wednesday. Blue Fin and Russian Samovar list a second, late window on their own menus, and Gui Steakhouse on Eighth Avenue mentions a daily late hour.
faq.q: Is there happy hour after a Broadway show near Times Square?

faq.a: Famous Dave's has the longest food list, with fries, rib tips, wings and burgers on weekdays. Blue Fin discounts oysters and mini lobster rolls every day, Altair discounts its menu pizza, Bill's Bar & Burger takes money off its snack appetizers, and Fushimi serves wagyu small plates at the bar.
faq.q: Which Times Square happy hours include food?

faq.a: Blue Fin, Faces & Names, Whiskey Trader, Carnegie Diner & Cafe, Fushimi, Gui Steakhouse and Double Knot all run their deals every day. Sir Henry's on Eighth Avenue has a weekend-only happy hour on Saturday and Sunday that ends in the afternoon, built around brunch-style shareables.
faq.q: Where can I get happy hour on a weekend near Times Square?

faq.a: Yes. Castell Rooftop Lounge in the AC Hotel on West 40th Street runs its deal on weekdays, and Starchild Rooftop Bar & Lounge on West 48th Street calls its Tuesday to Thursday early evening deal Horizon Hour, with cocktails and bar bites.
faq.q: Is there a rooftop happy hour in Times Square?

intro:
Park Slope fills the blocks between Fourth Avenue and the western edge of Prospect Park in Brooklyn. The bars on our list gather on two strips. Fifth Avenue holds the larger group, from 200 Fifth and Emmy Squared Pizza down to 390 Social, and the R at Union Street is the nearest stop for more of them than any other station. The second strip is Eighth Avenue and the side streets around 11th and 12th Streets, where Ottava, Pasta Louise, Provini, Bar Toto and Saint Eves sit a few minutes from the 7th Avenue stop on the F and G.

Happy hour in Park Slope leans toward restaurants with a short wine and cocktail list, plus a couple of bars that knock something off the whole drinks menu. Spritzes, negronis, house wine and draft beer come up again and again, and a few places add wings, crostini or tacos. Nearly every deal here is a weekday affair, and many stop on Thursday, so check a Friday plan first. For Sunday, 390 Social and Chela are the names to remember.

picks.why: Whisk & Whiskey is a bar two minutes from the Union Street R, and its Wednesday to Friday happy hour covers the full spread: draft beers, wines, well drinks and two house cocktails, with a Narragansett and well shot pairing on the menu too. Its own deal text also promises the discount all day Sunday, so it doubles as a weekend option.

High Dive is a dive bar four minutes from the Union Street R with one of the longest weekday windows on our list, running Monday through Friday from mid-afternoon well into the evening. Well drinks and PBR get a set price, and everything else at the bar comes down a little as well. Listed hours run past midnight every night.

Emmy Squared Pizza at 315 5th Avenue serves pizza, burgers and salads, and its weekday happy hour pairs select beer, house wine and well cocktails with sriracha glazed chicken wings. The window opens in the afternoon Monday through Friday, so it suits an early dinner. Union Street on the R is six minutes away, and tables book through Resy.

Bar Toto, a restaurant at 411 11th Street, runs its deal Monday to Thursday from the afternoon into early evening. The list covers cocktails such as a Negroni, Aperol Spritz, Old Fashioned and Americano, house wine in prosecco, white, rosé and red, and draft beer. The accessible 7th Avenue station on the F and G is five minutes away.

Provini is a restaurant at 1302 8th Avenue, four minutes from the accessible 7th Avenue F and G stop. From Monday to Thursday it discounts white, red and rosé wines plus Peroni on draft, and its happy hour menu lists crostini and a parmesan crème brûlée to eat alongside. Ask your server which wines are pouring that day.

The Commissioner is a pub about four minutes on foot from the Union Street R. Monday through Thursday it takes something off every draft and sets one price for wine, a well drink, or a beer and shot. Its menu also runs Taco Tuesday and a wine and wings deal on Wednesday, and listed hours go late every night.

390 Social, a bar at 390 5th Avenue, is one of the few spots here with a Sunday happy hour: it runs Friday and Sunday from an earlier start, and Tuesday through Thursday in the early evening. We have no itemized offers on file, so ask at the bar. The 9th Street station on the F, G and R is three minutes away, and Resy handles bookings.

sections.body: Two stations do most of the work. The R at Union Street, on Fourth Avenue, is closest to the Fifth Avenue group, including Whisk & Whiskey, High Dive, Blueprint and The Commissioner. The 7th Avenue station on the F and G is accessible and sits near the Eighth Avenue cluster of Ottava, Provini and both Pasta Louise locations. Farther south, 9th Street, shared by the F, G and R, is nearest to 390 Social, Chela and Stella's. Each listing shows the walk from its stop.

The number on a Park Slope menu is not the final number. New York adds 8.875 percent sales tax, and an 18 to 20 percent tip is customary on top of that. Restaurants often keep the deal to bar seating, so mention it when you sit down. Every listing shows the date we last checked it; glance at that first, because weekday deals get trimmed without much notice.

faq.a: 390 Social runs a Sunday window alongside its Friday one, and Chela lists Sunday afternoons in addition to weekdays. Whisk & Whiskey says its deal runs all day Sunday as well. Most other spots on our list, including Bar Toto, Ottava, Provini and The Commissioner, finish their week on Thursday.
faq.q: Which Park Slope bars have happy hour on Sunday?

faq.a: Emmy Squared Pizza discounts sriracha glazed chicken wings, Blueprint has a happy hour food price, and Provini lists crostini on its happy hour menu. Pasta Louise serves its spritz with a bowl of chips, and The Commissioner adds Taco Tuesday and wings on Wednesday.
faq.q: Where can I get food with happy hour in Park Slope?

faq.a: Chela starts at midday on weekdays, the earliest start on our list for the neighborhood. High Dive runs from mid-afternoon into the evening Monday through Friday, and LoFi keeps its discount on every drink going into the evening on weekdays too.
faq.q: Which Park Slope happy hour starts earliest or runs longest?

faq.a: Union Street on the R is the closest stop for the largest group, including Whisk & Whiskey, High Dive and Emmy Squared Pizza. The 7th Avenue F and G station serves Eighth Avenue spots like Ottava and Provini, and 9th Street on the F, G and R is nearest to 390 Social and Chela.
faq.q: What subway stops serve Park Slope happy hours?

intro:
Williamsburg sits on the Brooklyn side of the East River, the first L stop out of Manhattan at Bedford Avenue and a short walk from the Williamsburg Bridge. The bars on our list cluster in a few pockets: Grand Street and Bedford Avenue near the Bedford Avenue station, Kent and Wythe Avenues toward the waterfront, Broadway under the elevated J, M and Z tracks by Marcy Avenue, and Graham Avenue and Bushwick Avenue on the east side, served by the Graham Avenue and Montrose Avenue L stops. The G adds stations at Metropolitan Avenue and Broadway.

Most happy hour in Williamsburg is a drinks affair: draft beer, well drinks, house wine and a few cocktails at a set price, with oysters, wings and bar snacks at some places. Bars outnumber restaurants on our list, and most deals run on weekdays, so Tuesday through Thursday is the safest bet. A handful, including Post No Bills and Testo, keep the discount going every day of the week. Several restaurants honor the deal only at the bar, so grab a stool rather than a table.

picks.why: Post No Bills is a bar on Bushwick Avenue, a one-minute walk from the Montrose Avenue L stop. Its discount runs every day of the week and lasts later into the evening than most on our list, covering drafts, well drinks, house cocktails and a lineup of margaritas plus a negroni. Good for a Sunday that needs no planning.

Two windows make The Rosemont easy to plan around: one on weeknights and an earlier start on Saturday and Sunday, both running well into the evening. The deal centers on classic cocktails. It sits at 63 Montrose Avenue, three minutes from the Broadway stop on the G, and its listed weeknight hours go deep into the night if you want to stay.

For oysters with your drink, head to Layla, a European-leaning bar at 352 Bedford Avenue. The weekday happy hour pairs oysters with draft beers and aperitivi, which makes it a natural after-work stop. Marcy Avenue on the J, M and Z is about seven minutes away on foot, and tables can be booked through Resy.

OTB at 141 Broadway is our weekend pick, since the window we have on file falls on Saturday and Sunday afternoons. Margaritas, Aperol, house wine and a beer-and-a-shot combo share the deal list with oysters and a plain hot dog. Book through Resy, or walk six minutes from Marcy Avenue on the J, M and Z.

Hungry after work? Northern Bell, a bar on Metropolitan Avenue two minutes from the Lorimer Street L, runs its deal Monday through Friday with a dedicated happy hour food list and smoked wings alongside discounted drafts, well drinks and glasses of wine. Reservations go through Resy, which helps on a Friday.

Recette is a French restaurant on Havemeyer Street, five minutes from the Metropolitan Avenue G and L station. Its happy hour is a daytime weekend affair on Saturday and Sunday, with a discount on wine by the bottle, so it suits a long weekend lunch more than an after-work drink. Reserve on Resy.

Monarch describes itself as an izakaya, and its Tuesday to Friday happy hour leans that way, with a percentage off sake plus a set price on cocktails. The restaurant is at 146 Metropolitan Avenue, about six minutes on foot from Bedford Avenue on the L. Our listing shows no booking link, so plan to walk in.

sections.body: The L is the main line here, with stops at Bedford Avenue, Lorimer Street, Graham Avenue and Montrose Avenue, and Bedford Avenue is the closest station for more bars on our list than any other. The G stops at Metropolitan Avenue, where it connects with the L at Lorimer Street, and at Broadway. The J, M and Z run along Broadway to Marcy Avenue, an accessible station that covers the South Side. Each listing shows the walking time from its nearest stop.

Menu prices in New York do not include the 8.875 percent sales tax, and a tip of 18 to 20 percent on top is standard. Many deals apply at the bar only, and Carneval notes that a gratuity is already included on every bill, so read the check. Happy hours change often, so look at the date we last checked each bar on its page before you head out.

faq.a: Post No Bills, Sleepwalk, Maracuya, Testo, Fushimi, The Richardson and Velvet Lounge list happy hour every day, and Fandi Mata runs it Tuesday through Sunday. The Rosemont has a separate weekend window, while OTB, Recette and Cozy Royale run theirs only on Saturday and Sunday.
faq.q: Which Williamsburg bars have happy hour on weekends?

faq.a: Cozy Royale on Humboldt Street is the one late-night option on our list, with a window in the late evening on Saturday and Sunday. For a later weekday finish, Post No Bills and The Rosemont keep their deals going longer into the evening than most bars here.
faq.q: Is there late-night happy hour in Williamsburg?

faq.a: Bedford Avenue on the L is the nearest stop for more bars on our list than any other station, covering Grand Street, Bedford Avenue and the waterfront blocks. Graham Avenue, Lorimer Street and Montrose Avenue on the L serve the east side, the G stops at Metropolitan Avenue and Broadway, and Marcy Avenue on the J, M and Z serves Broadway and the South Side.
faq.q: What subway stops are closest to Williamsburg happy hours?

faq.a: Layla discounts oysters, OTB adds oysters and a hot dog on weekends, and Northern Bell has smoked wings and a happy hour food list. Hole In The Wall offers wings and several kinds of fries, The Anchored Inn pairs a burger with a draft beer, Reclamation Bar has a basket of pizza, and Bar Baserri includes Spanish olives.
faq.q: Which Williamsburg happy hours include food?

intro:
Spanish tapas are the focus at Boqueria, a restaurant in Chelsea District, Manhattan. Its happy hour has one window for weekdays and another for Saturday and Sunday, which starts later than the weekday one.

The address is 53 W 19th St. The F and M trains at 23rd Street are a four-minute walk. The drinks and tapas it covers are listed on this page, with live prices. Live hours are shown on this page.

Right on Houston Street, Houston Hall is a pub at 222 W Houston St in Greenwich Village, with American bar food in its listing. The Houston Street station on the 1 line is 1 minute away on foot.

The Houston Hall happy hour runs Tuesday through Friday, from late afternoon into the evening, and all day on Sunday. It covers beers in three sizes, wine, cocktails and frozen drinks, plus an empanada sampler, a slider trio and a personal cheese pizza. The drinks and dishes are listed on this page, with live prices.

The Upper West Side stretches between Central Park and Riverside Park from 59th Street to 110th Street, and its happy hours follow the avenues rather than one nightlife strip. Amsterdam Avenue between 72nd and 86th Streets holds the largest share of our list, with a tight knot of bars around 79th Street. Columbus Avenue has its own run of restaurants from the low 70s to the upper 80s, West 72nd Street adds a few more, and a smaller group sits near 103rd Street. The 1 on Broadway and the B and C under Central Park West handle nearly every trip.

Upper West Side happy hour leans toward restaurants more than bar crawls: spritzes at Italian spots, margaritas at Mexican ones, oysters and sushi, plus a couple of beer-focused bars with small-pour drafts. Weekday windows dominate, though Playa Betty's, Leyla, Harvest, Tessa and The Ribbon run theirs every day. Kouzan, Da Capo and The Ellington serve the deal at the bar only, so if you want a table, choose a place like Playa Betty's that honors it in the dining room and on the sidewalk too.

picks.why: Gebhard's Beer Culture is a beer bar at 228 West 72nd Street, one minute from the 72nd Street 1, 2 and 3 station. On weekdays its happy hour starts at opening and covers small-pour drafts, including Guinness and rotating taps, plus full Guinness pints and house wine. If draft beer is the goal on this side of the park, start here.

Playa Betty's is a Mexican restaurant at 320 Amsterdam Avenue with a happy hour every day of the week. Frozen palomas, sangria, margaritas, Pacifico pints, IPAs, cans and buckets of Coronitas are on the list, along with Betty's Burger. The deal applies at the bar, in the dining room and on the sidewalk, and the 72nd Street station is three minutes away.

The Wolfe is a pub at 425 Amsterdam Avenue whose weekday happy hour starts before lunch and runs into the early evening, one of the longest windows on our list for the area. Bottled and canned beers, drafts, mixed drinks and classics such as an Aperol spritz are included. Walk three minutes from 79th Street on the 1, or book through Resy.

Viand, a restaurant on Columbus Avenue near 86th Street, keeps its weekday deal simple: house wine, beer and a classic cocktail, with wings, nachos and spring rolls as happy hour snacks. The window opens mid-afternoon and runs into the early evening Monday through Friday. The 86th Street B and C stop is three minutes away, and our listing shows no booking link.

La Perla Nascosta, a bar on West 79th Street a minute from the 79th Street 1 stop, builds its happy hour around spritzes: Aperol, Campari and Hugo, plus negronis, margaritas, rosé and prosecco. The deal runs Sunday through Friday, so it covers a Sunday afternoon as well as weeknights. Tables can be reserved on Resy.

Smoke Jazz & Supper Club is at 2751 Broadway, three minutes from 103rd Street on the 1. Its happy hour runs Wednesday through Sunday from late afternoon into the early evening, with Aperol, Hugo and amaro spritzes, sparkling rosé, sangria and carafes of wine, plus happy hour entrées such as a bar steak. A good weekend option north of 96th Street.

Kissaki Sushi on Columbus Avenue pairs a half dozen oysters with a glass of champagne or chablis as its weekday happy hour, served in the early evening, later than most deals in the neighborhood. It is one set offer rather than a menu, so treat it as a starter before dinner. Walk four minutes from 72nd Street.

sections.body: Two subway corridors cover the neighborhood. The 1 makes local stops along Broadway at 72nd, 79th, 86th, 96th and 103rd Streets, and the 2 and 3 add express service at 72nd and 96th; 72nd Street is the nearest station for more bars on our list than any other. The B and C run under Central Park West with stops at 72nd Street, 81st Street–Museum of Natural History, 86th Street and 103rd Street, which suits the Columbus Avenue restaurants. Walking times from each stop are on the listings.

Plan for the 8.875 percent sales tax that New York adds to menu prices, then an 18 to 20 percent tip. Kouzan, Da Capo and The Ellington keep the deal at the bar, and Cotta Osteria extends it to outdoor seating but not the dining room. Before you walk over, look at the last-checked date on each bar's page, since happy hour menus here change often.

faq.a: Playa Betty's, Leyla, Harvest, Tessa, The Ribbon, Covacha, Arte Cafe, Amelie Wine Bar and Hi Life Bar & Grill list happy hour every day. Smoke Jazz & Supper Club runs Wednesday through Sunday, Bob's Your Uncle has a separate weekend deal on well drinks, draft beer and select cocktails, and Hoptimist includes Saturday.
faq.q: Which Upper West Side bars have happy hour on weekends?

faq.a: Kissaki Sushi on Columbus Avenue offers a half dozen oysters with champagne or chablis on weekdays.
faq.q: Where can I get oysters at happy hour on the Upper West Side?

faq.a: 5 Napkin Burger on Broadway lists a late window Sunday through Thursday on top of its afternoon deal, and The Ellington near 103rd Street keeps its bar happy hour going all night on Thursday. Asset on Columbus Avenue runs its deal all night on Monday.
faq.q: Is there late-night happy hour on the Upper West Side?

faq.a: Viand serves wings, nachos and spring rolls, Hoptimist pairs a draft pilsner with a smash burger and fries, and Playa Betty's has Betty's Burger. The Gin Mill, a sports bar on Amsterdam Avenue, discounts appetizers such as fries and tots on weekdays, and The Ribbon includes fresh fish tacos.
faq.q: Which Upper West Side happy hours include food?

intro:
The East Village covers the stretch of Manhattan east of the Bowery and Third Avenue, between 14th Street and Houston Street, with Tompkins Square Park between Avenues A and B. The bars on our list line up along a few corridors: Second Avenue, First Avenue, Avenue A, and the side streets around St. Marks Place and East 7th Street. The L at 1st Avenue is the closest stop for more of them than any other station, while the F at 2nd Avenue and the 6 at Astor Place cover the southern and western blocks.

East Village happy hour is mostly about drinks. Draft beer, house wine, well drinks and cocktails at a set price are the norm, and a few places go further, with two-for-one rounds at Kingston Hall and half off everything at Downtown Social. Plenty of spots on our list keep a deal running on Saturday or Sunday, so a weekend afternoon works here too. Food deals are fewer, so check each listing for wings, fries or burger combos before you count on dinner.

picks.why: Kingston Hall, a bar at 149 2nd Avenue, is the two-for-one stop on our list: beer, prosecco and well drinks all come doubled. The deal runs every day, with an earlier start on Sunday, so it works as well for a weekend afternoon as for after work. Astor Place on the 6 is four minutes away.

Open late by its listed hours, Niagara on Avenue A starts its happy hour when the doors open and keeps it going seven days a week. Draft beer, house wine and well drinks are the discounted pours. Walk about seven minutes from the 1st Avenue L, or come straight from Tompkins Square Park, which is close by.

Smør brings Scandinavian cooking to East 12th Street, two minutes from the 1st Avenue L. The discount covers house wines and cocktails and applies every day of the week, so an early Saturday dinner gets the same deal as a Tuesday. Book a table on Resy if you are bringing a group.

If you want food with your drinks, Emmy Squared on 1st Avenue serves pizza, burgers and salads, and its weekday happy hour adds sriracha glazed chicken wings to house wine, well cocktails and beer. The window opens in the afternoon, so it suits an early finish from work. The F at 2nd Avenue is five minutes away.

Juke Bar is on 2nd Avenue, a three-minute walk from the 3rd Avenue L. Its deal list is all drinks: house spirits, wine, beer, whiskey, vodka and a few specialty shots. Happy hour runs Sunday through Friday, leaving Saturday as the only full-price day, and its listed hours stretch late if the night keeps going.
Westville East is a restaurant at 173 Avenue A with a drink deal on cocktails, wine and beer. The deal runs on weekdays, and the 1st Avenue L stop is three minutes away.

Downtown Social takes the simplest approach, marking everything half off during its Monday to Friday happy hour, food included. The bar shares the 149 2nd Avenue address with Kingston Hall, four minutes from Astor Place, so you can compare both deals in one stop. Reservations are taken on Resy.

sections.body: The L runs along 14th Street with stops at 1st Avenue and 3rd Avenue, and 1st Avenue is the nearest station for more bars on our list than any other. The F at 2nd Avenue, on Houston Street, covers the southern blocks around First Avenue and Avenue A, and Astor Place on the 6 is the easy choice for Second Avenue. Bars near Avenue B can also be reached from Essex Street on the F, J, M and Z. Walking times are on each listing.

Expect the 8.875 percent New York sales tax to be added to menu prices, and plan on an 18 to 20 percent tip on top. Deals are often limited to the bar area, so ask before you sit at a table. Happy hours change without notice, so each bar page shows the date we last checked it; look at that before you go.

faq.a: Niagara, Phoenix Bar, Smør, La Palapa Cocina Mexicana, Hard to Explain, 12th Street Ale House, Sing Sing Ave A. and Upstate list happy hour every day, and Kingston Hall runs it daily with a separate Sunday window. Bin 141 runs Tuesday through Sunday, while Juke Bar, Bar Snack, Spicy Moon and 11 Tigers include Sunday.
faq.q: Which East Village bars have happy hour on weekends?

faq.a: Lovers of Today on East 7th Street lists a late-night happy hour Sunday through Wednesday that starts after most other deals have ended. It is the only late window on our list for the neighborhood; Niagara, Juke Bar and Phoenix Bar run earlier deals but keep long listed hours.
faq.q: Is there late-night happy hour in the East Village?

faq.a: 1st Avenue on the L is the nearest stop for the most bars on our list, including Niagara, Smør and Westville East. Astor Place on the 6 serves the Second Avenue bars such as Kingston Hall and Downtown Social, 3rd Avenue on the L is closest to Juke Bar, and 2nd Avenue on the F covers Emmy Squared and Avenue A south of St. Marks Place.
faq.q: What subway stops are closest to East Village happy hours?

faq.a: Emmy Squared discounts sriracha glazed chicken wings, Augers Well has a burger, fries and beer combo, and Downtown Social takes half off everything, food included. Ruffian also discounts food, and Aura Bar and Kitchen offers truffle fries, pulled pork sliders and calamari during its Tuesday to Sunday happy hour.
faq.q: Which East Village happy hours include food?

intro:
Billed as a cocktails and bar food spot, The Bonnie is at 29-12 23rd Avenue in Astoria, two minutes from Astoria–Ditmars Boulevard station on the N and W.

The Bonnie has more happy hour than most: Monday through Thursday from late afternoon into the early evening, Friday from midday, and a late-night window every night until close. The early deal is money off select draft beer, wine and well drinks; the late one adds an espresso martini, a spicy margarita or a beer and a shot. Reservations are available through the booking link, and a website is listed.

Greenwich Village spreads out from Washington Square Park, roughly between 14th Street and Houston Street on Manhattan's west side. Our list falls into three pockets. One sits around the park on West 8th Street, West 3rd Street and Bleecker Street, close to the West 4th Street–Washington Square station and its A, B, C, D, E, F and M trains. A second follows Seventh Avenue South down to Carmine, Cornelia and Downing Streets, and a third lines Hudson Street on the western edge. The 1 train covers those last two at Christopher Street–Stonewall and Houston Street.

Happy hour in Greenwich Village is a mix of wine bars, pubs and small restaurants, and drinks lead: house wine, drafts, spritzes and a handful of cocktails. Oysters turn up on several lists, at 8th Street Winecellar, Lelabar and APERITIVO by CARTA. Weekdays carry most of the deals, but The Grey Dog, Lelabar, The Leroy House and North Square run theirs every day. Little Havana, Arvine and Bobo restrict the deal to the bar or a back room, so ask where to sit when you walk in.

picks.why: 8th Street Winecellar is a wine bar at 28 West 8th Street, a short walk from Washington Square Park and four minutes from West 4th Street–Washington Square. Its happy hour runs every day into the evening with select glasses and bottles, and a separate oyster happy hour adds discounted oysters Monday through Thursday. Our listing shows no booking link, so plan to walk in.

The Red Lion at 151 Bleecker Street is a sports bar and music venue whose weekday happy hour covers its house draft beer, well drinks, house wine and a Red Lion mule or margarita. The bar pitches it as a warm-up before the band takes the stage. Walk five minutes from West 4th Street or book a table through Resy.

The Spaniard, a bar serving classic American food at 190 West 4th Street, takes money off draft beer on weekdays and adds a short happy hour food menu, including a single smash burger with fries and a griddled all-beef hot dog. It sits a minute from Christopher Street–Stonewall on the 1, and reservations go through Resy.

Little Havana on Cornelia Street keeps its happy hour at the bar only, Monday to Friday from late afternoon. The food side is the draw: nachos topped with black beans and house cheese sauce, plus French fries, both at happy hour prices. West 4th Street–Washington Square is two minutes away, and our listing shows no booking link.

The Grey Dog on Carmine Street is an American restaurant with a happy hour every day of the week, running into the early evening. House wine, its own Michigan lager, a Tommy's margarita, a Venetian spritz, rosé and bar bites are on the list, which makes it an easy weekend stop. Houston Street on the 1 is two minutes away, and Resy handles bookings.

Bobo is a French bar and restaurant on West 10th Street that saves its happy hour for late on Friday and Saturday nights, served in the den only. Martinis, from classic gin or vodka to an espresso version, and wines by the glass are on it. Christopher Street–Stonewall is a minute away, and Resy takes reservations for dinner beforehand.

Katana Kitten is a cocktail bar at 531 Hudson Street with a Japanese bent to its weekday happy hour: a japerol spritz made with shochu and Aperol, a few other cocktails using sake and yuzu, and food such as edamame. It runs Monday through Friday in the late afternoon. The Christopher Street–Stonewall stop is four minutes away, and our listing has no booking link.

sections.body: West 4th Street–Washington Square is the big transfer point, with the A, C and E on the Eighth Avenue line and the B, D, F and M on the Sixth Avenue line; it is closest to the bars around the park and on Bleecker and Cornelia Streets. The 1 runs down Seventh Avenue South, stopping at Christopher Street–Stonewall, nearest to the West 10th and West 4th Street bars, and at Houston Street, which serves Carmine Street and Hudson Street. From the north, the 14th Street stations on the 1, 2, 3, F, M and L put APERITIVO by CARTA within a short walk.

The 8.875 percent New York sales tax is not included in menu prices, and an 18 to 20 percent tip goes on top of that. In the Village, bar-only rules are common: Little Havana, Arvine and Bobo all limit where the deal applies. Look at the date we last confirmed each happy hour on its page before heading out, because small places here change their menus without much notice.

faq.a: 8th Street Winecellar runs an oyster happy hour Monday through Thursday, Lelabar on Hudson Street lists oysters by the piece every day, and APERITIVO by CARTA on West 10th Street includes oysters alongside wine and spritzes on weekdays.
faq.q: Where can I find oysters at happy hour in Greenwich Village?

faq.a: Bobo on West 10th Street runs a late happy hour in its den on Friday and Saturday nights. Spicy Moon on West 3rd Street adds a late window Sunday through Thursday, and Empellon Taqueria lists late-night tacos on Friday and Saturday.
faq.q: Is there late-night happy hour in Greenwich Village?

faq.a: The Grey Dog, 8th Street Winecellar, Lelabar, The Leroy House, North Square and Amelie Wine Bar run happy hour daily. Sabor Argentino runs Thursday through Sunday, The Market Table Tuesday through Sunday, L'accolade adds a Saturday window, and The Malt House has a weekend-only deal with jumbo wings and parmesan fries.
faq.q: Which Greenwich Village bars have happy hour on weekends?

faq.a: Yes. Amity Hall, a sports bar on West 3rd Street, runs one of the longest windows on our list, from midday into the evening on weekdays. Judy Z's Sports Tavern & Kitchen on Seventh Avenue South covers beers, mixed drinks and frozen drinks Wednesday through Friday, and The Red Lion on Bleecker Street pairs sports with live music.
faq.q: Are there sports bars with happy hour in Greenwich Village?

intro:
The Financial District fills the southern tip of Manhattan, from Battery Park up past Wall Street toward the Brooklyn Bridge, with the Hudson on one side and the East River on the other. Our list splits into three pockets. The densest runs along Pearl, Stone and Broad Streets near Whitehall Street on the 1, R and W, where Toro Loco, Mexi, Route 66 Smokehouse and Mad Dog and Beans sit a few doors apart. A second group gathers around John Street and Maiden Lane by the Fulton Street hub, and Trinity Place has Half Moon and Wogies right at the Rector Street stop.

Financial District happy hour is built for the end of the workday. Almost every deal runs Monday through Friday from mid-afternoon, and many wrap up by early evening, so leaving the office on time matters. Margaritas show up on many menus, alongside draft beer, house wine and sangria. Weekends are thinner, though Zizi's Wine Bar, Broadstone Bar & Kitchen, Fresh Salt, Le District and Urban Cove Society & Kitchen keep their deals daily. One tip: Bill's Bar and Burger and Mad Dog and Beans honor their prices at the bar only.

picks.why: Route 66 Smokehouse is an American restaurant at 79 Pearl Street with a straightforward weekday deal: beer, wines, well drinks and frozen drinks, with specialty martinis on Martini Monday. The window opens in the afternoon and runs into early evening. Whitehall Street is three minutes away, and Resy handles tables if you are booking for a group.

Toro Loco sits at 15 Stone Street, two minutes from Whitehall Street on the 1, R and W. Its weekday happy hour leans on margaritas, frozen or on the rocks with a fruit flavor option, plus red and white sangria, rosé, wine, canned beers and the house lager on draft. It wraps up by early evening, so come straight from work.

Half Moon, a bar at 50 Trinity Place, opens its happy hour at midday, the earliest start in the neighborhood on our list, and holds it until early evening Monday through Friday. The menu covers a house margarita, an espresso martini, a Gold Rush, Guinness and other drafts, house wine and a soft baked pretzel. The Rector Street R and W stop is a minute away.

Zizi's Wine Bar on John Street runs its happy hour every day until early evening, with a discount on bottles, a smaller one on reserve bottles and money off the food menu. That makes it one of the few weekend options downtown. Fulton Street, an accessible station, is a minute's walk, and reservations go through Resy.

Bill's Bar and Burger is an American spot at 85 West Street, on the Hudson side of the neighborhood. On weekdays it offers draft beers, classic shakes, pitchers and half off its snack attack apps, but only at the bar. The window covers the after-work hours, and the 1 at Rector Street is a three-minute walk.

Mad Dog and Beans is a Mexican restaurant at 83 Pearl Street with a Monday to Thursday happy hour that starts in the afternoon. Its signature margarita on the rocks, a frozen margarita, a house red or white wine and Mexican beer are all on special, at the bar only. Whitehall Street is three minutes away on foot.

Hide Rooftop at 24 John Street is the rooftop bar on our downtown list. Its deal has two windows, a longer one Monday to Wednesday and a shorter one on Thursday and Friday, covering a margarita and other cocktails plus boneless wings, margherita pizza and pommes frites. Fulton Street, with step-free access, is one minute away.

sections.body: Fulton Street, an accessible hub for the 2, 3, 4, 5, A, C, J and Z, is a minute from Hide Rooftop and Zizi's Wine Bar and also serves the Seaport spots, Sadie's and Urban Cove Society & Kitchen. Whitehall Street on the 1, R and W covers the Pearl and Stone Street cluster. Wall Street on the 2 and 3 is closest to Full Shilling, Mezcali and Joseph's Ristorante, while the 4 and 5 stop at Wall Street sits next to Trinity Place. Rector Street works for the west side: the R and W for Half Moon and Wogies, the 1 for Bill's Bar and Burger. Mexi is nearest Broad Street on the J and Z.

Downtown deals come with the usual add-ons: 8.875 percent sales tax on top of menu prices, and a tip of 18 to 20 percent. Wogies also adds a service fee to every check, so read the bill before you tip. Bar-only rules are common in this neighborhood. Each listing carries the date we last checked it, so glance at that before you walk over.

faq.a: Zizi's Wine Bar, Broadstone Bar & Kitchen, Fresh Salt, Le District and Urban Cove Society & Kitchen list a deal every day, and Mexi on Stone Street runs Tuesday through Sunday. Industry Kitchen also lists a short Sunday window in its deal text.
faq.q: Which Financial District bars have happy hour on weekends?

faq.a: Toro Loco on Stone Street discounts frozen and rocks margaritas, Mad Dog and Beans pours its signature and frozen versions at the bar, and Half Moon offers a house margarita. Hide Rooftop, Industry Kitchen, Wogies and Trinity Place include one as well.
faq.q: Which Financial District happy hours have margaritas?

faq.a: Hide Rooftop has boneless wings, margherita pizza and pommes frites, Bill's Bar and Burger takes half off its snack apps, and Half Moon lists a soft baked pretzel. Whiskey Tavern adds wings, nachos and fries, Zizi's Wine Bar discounts its food menu, and Mezze on the River offers dips with grilled pita.
faq.q: Which FiDi happy hours include food?

faq.a: Hide Rooftop on John Street is the rooftop on our list, a minute from the Fulton Street station, with deals Monday through Friday. For outdoor seating, Sadie's on Fulton Street is listed with outdoor space.
faq.q: Is there a rooftop happy hour in the Financial District?

intro:
The Upper East Side runs from 59th Street to 96th Street between Central Park and the East River, and on our list its happy hours sit almost entirely east of Lexington Avenue. Second Avenue carries the most, from the low 70s up through the 80s in Yorkville, while First Avenue picks up the 60s and 70s and Third Avenue has a short run near 92nd Street. The Q under Second Avenue, with stations at 72nd, 86th and 96th Streets, is the nearest line for most bars we list, and the 4, 5 and 6 on Lexington serve the western edge.

Pubs and sports bars make up a big share of Upper East Side happy hour, and several of them keep the offer simple: half off the whole bar at Stumble Inn, two-for-one drinks at Sojourn Social, small-pour beers and flights at Treadwell Park. A few start at midday on weekdays, so a late lunch can count. For a later round, Meller's Sports Hub & Grill and Third Avenue Ale House both run late-night windows. Second Avenue between 70th and 90th Streets works as one long strip, so trying two places in an evening is easy.

picks.why: Stumble Inn is a sports bar at 1454 Second Avenue with one of the simplest deals on our list: half off the entire bar, Monday through Friday from opening into the early evening. Its own menu adds nightly specials after that, such as draft mugs and canned beers on Monday and Tuesday. The 72nd Street Q stop is four minutes away; book through Resy.

Sojourn Social, a restaurant at 1708 Second Avenue, runs two-for-one drinks on weekdays from midday into the evening, and you can mix and match signature cocktails, draft beer and wine by the glass. It also pairs a cocktail with the Social Burger or a crispy chicken sandwich. Walk three minutes from 86th Street on the Q, or reserve on OpenTable.

Treadwell Park is a beer hall at 1125 First Avenue, so beer leads its weekday deal: select small-pour beers and beer flights, with wine, mixed cocktails, chips and guacamole and beef sliders also on the list. It sits in the low 60s, about seven minutes from Lexington Avenue–63rd Street, a natural first stop at the southern end of the neighborhood. Book on Resy.

Westville on First Avenue near 72nd Street is a restaurant with a deal every day of the week: classic, spicy or smoky margaritas, sangria, signature and seasonal cocktails, wine, beer and mocktails, which helps when part of the group is not drinking. The 72nd Street Q stop is three minutes away, and our listing shows no booking link.

Meller's Sports Hub & Grill on Second Avenue starts its happy hour late at night and keeps it going into the small hours, Sunday through Thursday. Wine, frozen drinks, mixed drinks, margaritas, canned beers and hard seltzers are on the list. It is two minutes from the 86th Street Q stop, and our listing shows no booking link, so just walk in.

Jones Wood Foundry is a British gastropub on East 76th Street with a weekday happy hour served at the bar. All draft beers, cask ale included, and house wines are discounted, and apps and snacks come off the regular price too. It is a five-minute walk from 72nd Street on the Q, and Resy handles table bookings.

Third Avenue Ale House at 1644 Third Avenue covers more of the week than most pubs here: a weekday window in the late afternoon, a Saturday and Sunday window around midday, and a separate late-night happy hour on food and drinks every night. It is four minutes from 96th Street on the Q, at the north end of the neighborhood.

sections.body: The Q runs under Second Avenue with stops at 72nd, 86th and 96th Streets, and 72nd Street is the nearest station for more bars on our list than any other, with 86th Street close behind. The 4, 5 and 6 on Lexington Avenue are a few blocks west, at 86th Street for the Third Avenue bars and at Lexington Avenue–59th Street for the southern edge. First Avenue spots in the low 60s are closest to Lexington Avenue–63rd Street. Places near York Avenue are a longer walk from any station, so check the walking time on each listing.

Menu prices here do not include New York's 8.875 percent sales tax, and a tip of 18 to 20 percent is expected on top. Jones Wood Foundry and Cafe d'Alsace serve their deals at the bar, so a dining table may be full price. Pub specials on this side of town change often, sometimes by the night, so check the last-checked date on each bar's page first.

faq.a: Meller's Sports Hub & Grill on Second Avenue runs a late-night window Sunday through Thursday, and Third Avenue Ale House has a late-night food and drink deal every night. The Penrose on Second Avenue also lists select drinks at a set price late every night.
faq.q: Is there late-night happy hour on the Upper East Side?

faq.a: Westville, The Uptown Restaurant & Bar, Dylan Murphy's, La Voglia, Cafe d'Alsace, August, The Alvin Public House and The Drunken Munkey run daily. Ethyl's Alcohol & Food goes Tuesday through Sunday, Third Avenue Ale House adds Saturday and Sunday afternoons, and Toloache has a weekend-only window.
faq.q: Which Upper East Side bars have happy hour on weekends?

faq.a: Yes. Stumble Inn takes half off the entire bar on weekdays, and Sojourn Social pours two-for-one drinks, mixing cocktails, draft beer and wine, Monday through Friday. Reif's Tavern on East 92nd Street takes a little off every drink on weekdays.
faq.q: Are there two-for-one or half-price happy hours on the Upper East Side?

faq.a: Ethyl's Alcohol & Food has a burger and French fries on its list, Treadwell Park serves chips and guacamole and beef sliders, and Jones Wood Foundry discounts apps and snacks. Third Avenue Ale House includes food in its late-night deal, and Cafe d'Alsace runs a small plates happy hour at the bar.
faq.q: Which Upper East Side happy hours include food?

intro:
Downtown Brooklyn's Bijan's is an American restaurant and bar at 81 Hoyt Street, two minutes on foot from Hoyt-Schermerhorn Streets, where the A, C and G trains stop.

The Bijan's happy hour runs on weekdays and covers select house cocktails, all draft and bottled beer, and house wine. OpenTable is the reservation link given for the restaurant. Live prices and hours are shown on this page.

Chu Ros Thai, a restaurant at 1590 Lexington Avenue in East Harlem, Manhattan, lists a happy hour every day of the week. The Chu Ros Thai happy hour has an end time but no start time on file, and no offers are published, so the days are all this page can promise.

The 6 train stops at 103rd Street, a two-minute walk away. No reservation link is listed.

Riviera Maya is a Mexican and Latin bar at 28-28 Steinway Street in Astoria, eight minutes on foot from 30th Avenue station on the N and W.

Its happy hour runs six days a week, every day except Saturday. On Tuesday it lasts all day; on the other days it runs from midday into the early evening. The deal covers beer, frozen and classic margaritas, sangria, a chilcano and a passion fruit pisco sour, each at a set price. A website is listed.

Two pints is the deal Fortina lists, and it applies Monday through Thursday. This Downtown Brooklyn bar is at 445 Albee Square West, a two-minute walk from DeKalb Avenue, where the B, Q and R trains stop.

The Fortina happy hour names only that pair of pints and no other items. Prices and hours are live on this page.

East Harlem covers the northeast corner of Manhattan, roughly from 96th Street up to the Harlem River, between Fifth Avenue and the East River. Our list for happy hour in East Harlem splits into two clusters. Several spots line Lexington Avenue in the low 100s, all within a few minutes of the 103rd Street stop on the 6. The others sit farther east: Teddy's F&B Bar & Grill on Second Avenue in the 110s, and Santiago's Beer Garden on First Avenue in the upper 110s.

This is a small, mixed list, with neighborhood bars next to a Thai restaurant and a tapas spot. Teddy's leads on food, with empanadas and sliders on its happy hour menu, while Santiago's has the longest drink list. Teddy's and Chu Ros Thai keep their deals going seven days a week, which helps if you can only get uptown on a Saturday. Most windows here wrap up in the early evening, so aim to arrive soon after work rather than late.

picks.why: Teddy's F&B Bar & Grill on Second Avenue is the food stop on our East Harlem list. Its happy hour runs every day of the week and covers empanadas, cheeseburger sliders, onion rings and mozzarella sticks, plus a wings and draft beer combo and buckets of beer. The 110th Street station on the 6 is about five minutes away.

Santiago's Beer Garden, on First Avenue above 116th Street, puts a long list of drinks on its weekday deal: margaritas, mojitos, sangria, a house punch, mixed drinks, house shots and bottled beer. It runs Monday to Friday from late afternoon, and tables can be reserved on Resy. Allow about eight minutes on foot from 116th Street on the 6.

Perch is a bar at 1693 Lexington Avenue, three minutes from the 103rd Street stop on the 6. Happy hour runs on weekdays, with a short window early in the week and an earlier start on Thursday and Friday. The menu posted with the deal includes oysters with champagne mignonette, a house burger, croquettes and a smoked trout rillette.

Chu Ros Thai is a Thai restaurant on Lexington Avenue, two minutes from 103rd Street on the 6. Its happy hour runs every day of the week, Saturday and Sunday included, and ends in the early evening, so it suits an early dinner. Our listing does not itemize the deal, so ask what is included when you sit down.

The Lexington Social is a tapas restaurant at 1634 Lexington Avenue, about a minute from the 103rd Street station. Our current listing shows a happy hour every day, starting in the early afternoon on weekdays and running late into the night on Monday and Tuesday, a good fit for a long lunch or an early start to the night. Its listed hours run late every night.

sections.body: Every bar we pick here is on the 6, which runs under Lexington Avenue. The 103rd Street station is the closest for Chu Ros Thai, Perch and The Lexington Social, all within three minutes. Get off at 110th Street for Teddy's on Second Avenue, and at 116th Street for Santiago's Beer Garden on First Avenue, the longest walk of the group at about eight minutes.

Menu prices here leave out New York's 8.875 percent sales tax, and an 18 to 20 percent tip is customary on top. Deals are frequently honored only at the bar, so check before you take a table. Every listing shows when we last confirmed its happy hour; look at that date before you set out.

faq.a: Teddy's F&B Bar & Grill and Chu Ros Thai both list happy hour every day, Saturday and Sunday included. Perch and Santiago's Beer Garden run theirs on weekdays only.
faq.q: Which East Harlem bars have happy hour on weekends?

faq.a: Teddy's F&B Bar & Grill has the most food on its deal, including empanadas, sliders, onion rings and mozzarella sticks. Perch posts oysters, a burger and croquettes alongside its happy hour, and Chu Ros Thai and The Lexington Social are both restaurants.
faq.q: Where can I eat during happy hour in East Harlem?

faq.a: All of them are on the 6. Use 103rd Street for Perch, Chu Ros Thai and The Lexington Social on Lexington Avenue, 110th Street for Teddy's, and 116th Street for Santiago's Beer Garden.
faq.q: Which subway stops are closest to East Harlem happy hours?

faq.a: Santiago's Beer Garden, with margaritas, mojitos, sangria, a house punch, mixed drinks, shots and bottled beer on its weekday list.
faq.q: Which East Harlem happy hour has the most drink options?

intro:
This Cobble Hill pub in Brooklyn is a four-minute walk from Bergen Street, where the F and G trains stop. The Brazen Head happy hour runs on weekdays and covers well drinks, a discount on well liquor and wine, and Aslin Old Town Lager.

No reservation link is listed for the pub. Live prices and the current hours appear elsewhere on this page, so check them before you go.

Margaritas are the listed deal at Xochitl Taqueria, a restaurant in Cobble Hill, Brooklyn. The Xochitl Taqueria happy hour runs on weekdays, and the subway is very close: Bergen Street, served by the F and G, is a one-minute walk.

The listing names only margaritas, with no food or other drinks mentioned. No reservation link is listed. Check this page for live prices and hours.

Hello Bar Bk, at 1110 Nostrand Avenue in Crown Heights, Brooklyn, offers its happy hour six days a week, Tuesday through Sunday, so only Monday is left out. The Hello Bar Bk happy hour lists cocktails, wine and beer.

The 2 and 5 trains at Sterling Street are a three-minute walk away. No booking link is listed for the bar, and live prices and hours are shown on this page.

Nostrand Avenue station, served by the 3 train, is a one-minute walk from Nostrand Station Bar & Lounge at 822 Nostrand Avenue in Crown Heights, Brooklyn. The Nostrand Station Bar & Lounge happy hour runs Tuesday through Friday.

The deals mix drinks and food: beers, shots and margaritas, plus taco, wing and empanada specials. No reservation link is listed. See this page for live prices and the current hours.

Reservations for PiCH go through OpenTable, which makes this Crown Heights restaurant easy to plan around. It is in Brooklyn, a three-minute walk from Parkside Avenue, the Q stop.

The PiCH happy hour runs on weekdays. The restaurant publishes the times but not the deal, so the specific drinks and food are not listed here. Live hours are shown on this page.

Bites are the listed deal at The Green Room PLG, a bar at 408 Rogers Avenue in Crown Heights, Brooklyn. The Green Room PLG happy hour runs Sunday through Thursday, so it includes Sunday and skips Friday and Saturday.

Sterling Street, with the 2 and 5 trains, is a three-minute walk. Reservations can be made through Resy using the booking link. Drinks are not named in the listing. Live prices and hours are on this page.

On Church Avenue in Flatbush, Brooklyn, Coco Chinese Restaurant is listed in our guide as a bar. The Coco Chinese Restaurant happy hour runs Sunday through Thursday and covers cocktails, house wine by the glass, and beer.

The address is 1706 Church Ave, and Church Avenue station, with the B and Q trains, is a two-minute walk. No reservation link is listed. Live prices and hours are shown on this page.

Perch, a bar at 1693 Lexington Avenue in East Harlem, Manhattan, is tagged for oysters, though its happy hour listing does not name any deals. The Perch happy hour runs on weekdays and is a short one, a single hour.

Take the 6 to 103rd Street and walk about three minutes. The bar publishes the times but not the deal. No booking link is listed, so check this page for live hours.

For Santiago's Beer Garden, the nearest subway is the 6 at 116th Street, an eight-minute walk, which is a longer trip than most spots in this guide. The bar is at 2337 1st Ave in East Harlem, Manhattan.

The Santiago's Beer Garden happy hour runs on weekdays and lists margarita, sangria, vodka and wine deals. A Resy link is provided for reservations. Live prices and hours are on this page.

Food and drinks both get a deal at Teddy's F&B Bar & Grill, a bar at 2171 2nd Avenue in East Harlem, Manhattan. The Teddy's F&B Bar & Grill happy hour runs every day and includes two empanadas, cheeseburger sliders, a bucket of beer, cocktails and a Rolling Rock lime margarita.

The 6 train at 110th Street is a five-minute walk. No reservation link is listed. Live prices and hours are on this page.

Every day of the week, 11 Tigers offers a happy hour. The East Village bar is in Manhattan, and the L train at 1st Avenue is a four-minute walk away.

The 11 Tigers happy hour has no deals listed, since the bar publishes the times but not the deal. Reservations are handled through Resy using the booking link. Check this page for the live hours before you make plans.

Aura Bar and Kitchen runs a happy hour Tuesday through Sunday. The Aura Bar and Kitchen happy hour lists draft beer, wine, craft and classic cocktails, pulled pork sliders, truffle mac and cheese, crispy calamari, Turkish meatballs and truffle fries.

The bar is at 111 1st Ave in the East Village, Manhattan, and the F train at 2nd Avenue is a six-minute walk. Reservations go through Resy using the booking link. Check this page for live hours before you plan around it.

Every day of the week has a happy hour at 12th Street Ale House, a bar at 192 2nd Avenue in the East Village, Manhattan. The 12th Street Ale House happy hour lists an end time but no start time, and no specific deals are published.

The L train at 3rd Avenue is a three-minute walk. No reservation link is listed for the bar. Check this page for live hours and any prices that are available.

Menu cocktails, draft beer and wine are the listed offers at the Congress happy hour, which runs every day: Monday through Thursday from late afternoon into the early evening, late on Thursday night, Friday from early afternoon, and Saturday and Sunday in the afternoon. Congress is described as a bar and restaurant at 208 Court Street in Cobble Hill, Brooklyn, three minutes from Bergen Street station on the F and G.

Starting from opening on weekdays, the Augers Well happy hour runs until early evening and lists two things by name: a burger, fries and beer combo, and draft beer. Augers Well is a bar in the East Village, Manhattan, and the L train at 1st Avenue is a six-minute walk.

The listing has no reservation link. Live prices and hours are on this page.

The Lexington Social runs a happy hour every day, with the longest windows on Monday and Tuesday, from the afternoon late into the night. This tapas restaurant is at 1634 Lexington Avenue in East Harlem, Manhattan, one minute on foot from 103rd Street on the 6.

The tags for The Lexington Social happy hour point to cocktails. No booking link is listed. Live details are on this page.

Rosa’s At Park runs its happy hour on three days only: Tuesday, Thursday and Friday. This bar is at 2568 Park Avenue in Mott Haven, Manhattan, and the 4 and 5 trains at 138th Street-Grand Concourse are a two-minute walk.

The Rosa’s At Park happy hour lists a deal called Classics, and the tags point to cocktails and wine. Reservations go through OpenTable. Live prices and hours are on this page.

Bar Snack sits at 92 2nd Avenue in the East Village, Manhattan, a five-minute walk from Astor Place and the 6 train. The Bar Snack happy hour runs Sunday through Thursday, with a long window that starts early in the day.

Tags point to a food deal, but the bar publishes the times and not the specifics. No reservation link is listed. See this page for live hours.

Tuesday through Sunday, Bin 141 runs a happy hour at 43 Avenue A in the East Village, Manhattan. It is a restaurant, and the tags point to cocktails and wine, though no specific deals are listed.

The Bin 141 happy hour stays open into the evening. Take the F to 2nd Avenue and walk about five minutes. No booking link is listed. Check this page for live hours and prices.

The Lucky Tiger happy hour runs on weekdays, in the late afternoon and again late at night until close, and lists cocktails, mocktails, wine and food. The bar serves Asian fusion at 66 Pearl St in the Financial District, Manhattan.

Whitehall Street-South Ferry, where the 1, R and W trains stop, is a two-minute walk. Reservations go through OpenTable. Check the live prices and hours before you go.

Bottled beer, well drinks, drafts, classic cocktails and house wine, all at set prices, are listed for the Minibar happy hour, which runs on weekdays and ends in the early evening; no start is given.

Minibar is a bar at 482 Court Street in Carroll Gardens, Brooklyn, a five minute walk from Carroll Street station on the F and G. A website is listed for current details.

Forest Hills sits in central Queens along Queens Boulevard, with Austin Street as its main shopping strip and the Forest Hills–71st Avenue station as its transit hub. Our Forest Hills happy hour list is short and strung along that corridor. Rove and Tap House share a block of Austin Street, a few minutes from 71st Avenue. Guantanamera is farther east on Queens Boulevard by the 75th Avenue stop, and Cobblestones Pub and Biergarten is out near Union Turnpike, at the Kew Gardens edge of the neighborhood.

The deals here are simple: draft beer, wine and mixed drinks at a set price, plus caipirinhas, mojitos and piña coladas at Guantanamera. Most of them are weekday affairs. Rove is the exception on Austin Street, with wine and beer specials every day, Saturday and Sunday included. Guantanamera's window opens at midday and closes before the after-work rush, so it suits a late lunch better than a drink after the office.

picks.why: Cobblestones Pub and Biergarten is on Queens Boulevard, two minutes from the accessible Kew Gardens–Union Turnpike station on the E and F. From mid-afternoon on weekdays it sets one price for draught beers, glasses of wine and single mixed drinks, and adds half-price wings with a drink for dine-in guests. Delirium is left out of the beer deal.

Guantanamera is a restaurant at 110-72 Queens Boulevard, a one-minute walk from the 75th Avenue stop on the E and F. Its weekday happy hour starts at midday and ends in the late afternoon, covering sangria, red or white wine and bottled beer, plus caipirinhas, piña coladas, mojitos and margaritas on the restaurant's own list. Good for a long lunch.

Rove is a bar at 72-27 Austin Street and the one Austin Street spot on our list with a deal every day of the week. The happy hour covers wine and beer specials until the early evening, and the bar also runs a brunch menu. It is five minutes on foot from Forest Hills–71st Avenue, an accessible station on the E, F, M and R.

Tap House is on the same block of Austin Street at number 72-07, four minutes from the Forest Hills–71st Avenue station. Happy hour runs Monday to Friday from late afternoon to early evening. Our listing does not itemize the deal, so ask at the bar, and if it falls short, Rove is a short walk along the block.

sections.body: Forest Hills–71st Avenue is the main station, with E, F, M and R service and step-free access, and both Austin Street bars are within five minutes of it. The E and F also stop at 75th Avenue, steps from Guantanamera, and at Kew Gardens–Union Turnpike, an accessible station two minutes from Cobblestones. Everything on this list is a short walk from Queens Boulevard.

New York adds 8.875 percent sales tax to the prices you see, and an 18 to 20 percent tip is the norm. Cobblestones keeps its wing deal to dine-in guests, and other places may limit deals to the bar, so ask. Check the date we last verified each bar on its page, since happy hours can change.

faq.a: Rove on Austin Street lists wine and beer specials every day, Saturday and Sunday included. Cobblestones, Guantanamera and Tap House run their deals on weekdays only.
faq.q: Which Forest Hills bars have happy hour on weekends?

faq.a: Guantanamera starts at midday on weekdays and wraps up in the late afternoon. Cobblestones Pub and Biergarten begins in mid-afternoon.
faq.q: Which Forest Hills happy hour starts earliest?

faq.a: Cobblestones Pub and Biergarten offers half-price wings with the purchase of a drink for dine-in guests. The other deals on our list are drinks only.
faq.q: Can I get food at happy hour in Forest Hills?

faq.a: Forest Hills–71st Avenue on the E, F, M and R for Rove and Tap House, 75th Avenue on the E and F for Guantanamera, and Kew Gardens–Union Turnpike on the E and F for Cobblestones.
faq.q: What subway stops serve Forest Hills happy hours?

intro:
A discount that applies to everything is the deal at Downtown Social, a bar at 149 2nd Ave in the East Village, Manhattan. The Downtown Social happy hour runs on weekdays, with an end time but no start time on file.

The 6 train at Astor Place is a four-minute walk. Live prices and hours are on this page.

Pizza, burgers and salads are the focus at Emmy Squared, a restaurant at 83 1st Avenue in the East Village, Manhattan. The Emmy Squared happy hour runs on weekdays and covers house wine, well cocktails, beer and sriracha glazed chicken wings.

The F train at 2nd Avenue is a five-minute walk. Live prices and hours are shown on this page.

Every day of the week, Ponty Bistro in Harlem runs a happy hour. The Ponty Bistro happy hour covers beers, wines, house cocktails and bar bites, so it reaches both drinks and food. This restaurant sits at 2375 Adam Clayton Powell Jr. Boulevard in Manhattan. The nearest subway stop is 135th Street, served by the 2 and 3 trains, about five minutes away on foot. The listing also carries tags for cocktails, wine and a food deal.

On Malcolm X Boulevard in Harlem, Sylvia's Restaurant serves Southern cooking, and its happy hour runs on weekdays. The Sylvia's Restaurant happy hour lists the Harlem Blues Margarita and a Prosecco Beer among its offers. The address is 328 Malcolm X Boulevard, two minutes on foot from the 125th Street station, where the 2 and 3 trains stop. A Resy link on the listing handles reservations, and the page is also tagged for cheap beer, cocktails and wine.

Mexican food, from tacos and burritos to seafood, anchors Taco Hut, a bar at 1884 Park Ave in Harlem. The Taco Hut happy hour runs on weekdays, though the bar publishes the times but not the deal itself. For the subway, the 125th Street station (2 and 3 trains) is four minutes away on foot. The listing tags the spot for cocktails and a food deal, so those are the areas to ask about when you arrive.

Frozen margs, well drinks and drafts headline The Heights Bar & Grill happy hour, which runs every day of the week. The restaurant is at 2867 Broadway, listed under Harlem in Manhattan, and the 1 train stops at Cathedral Parkway-110th Street, a one minute walk away. Because the offers span frozen cocktails, well drinks and beer on tap, the happy hour covers a few different kinds of drink. The listing also carries a cheap-beer tag.

Toast, a bar at 3157 Broadway in Morningside Heights, offers frozen margaritas during its happy hour, which runs every day, with a late-night window on weeknights. The Toast happy hour also covers house red and white wine, well drinks, all drafts and flavored martinis. The 1 train stops at 125th Street, two minutes away on foot, which makes the trip from the subway short.

The A10 Kitchen happy hour changes shape across the week. Monday through Thursday share one window, Friday has its own, and Saturday and Sunday each start earlier than the weekday sessions. The venue is a bar in the East Village, Manhattan.

No deals are listed, only the times. Reservations can be made through Resy using the booking link. Live hours for each day are shown on this page.

American food, breakfast, brunch and a cocktail bar are the cuisine tags attached to Café Maud, a restaurant at 132 2nd Avenue in the East Village, Manhattan. Astor Place, with the 6 train, is a five-minute walk.

The Café Maud happy hour runs on weekdays, ending in the early evening. The restaurant publishes the times but not the deal, so no drinks or food are named here. No reservation link is listed. See this page for live hours.

Monday through Thursday, 5 Napkin Burger pours draft beer and wine for its happy hour. The 5 Napkin Burger happy hour is listed for this hamburger restaurant at 630 9th Avenue in Hell's Kitchen. Getting there means the 42nd Street-Port Authority Bus Terminal station, four minutes on foot, which is served by the 1, 2, 3, 7, A, C, E, N, Q, R, S and W lines. The listing tags the place for cocktails, wine and a food deal.

The Alfie's happy hour runs every day at this New American restaurant at 800 9th Avenue in Hell's Kitchen, from late morning on weekdays and late afternoon on weekends, with a late-night window every night. The drinks and dishes it covers are listed on this page, with live prices. The nearest station is 50th Street, with C and E trains, about four minutes away on foot. The page also carries all-day and weekend tags.

Draft beer, house wine carafes, Narragansett American Lager, Montauk Juicy Hazy IPA and Villians West Coast IPA all show up in the Bua happy hour listing, which runs on weekdays. Bua is a bar at 122 St Marks Pl in the East Village, Manhattan, six minutes on foot from 1st Avenue on the L train.

Live prices and hours appear on this page, including the start time.

Cheap beer in NYC usually means a happy hour draft, a can of domestic lager or a house pint priced well below the regular tap list. Plenty of bars on our list carry the cheap beer tag, and Manhattan holds most of them. Times Square and the blocks of Koreatown, Flatiron and the Financial District have the densest clusters, with the Upper West Side, Murray Hill and Midtown close behind. In Brooklyn, Williamsburg leads, followed by Greenpoint and Bushwick. Astoria carries the Queens entries, and the Bronx is represented too.

Expect the deal to name a type rather than a brand: domestic drafts, house beers, select cans. A few bars go further with a bucket of bottles or a pitcher. Most run on weekdays between the end of the workday and dinner, and a fair share add Saturday or Sunday. One tip: ask which taps count before you order, because some bars limit the price to one or two lines.

picks.why: Hard Rock Cafe sits at 1501 Broadway, two minutes from the Times Square station and its twelve lines. During the weekday happy hour, domestic and imported drafts each get a set price, and cocktails are discounted too. It works as a stop before a show, and the restaurant takes reservations, which helps with a group in Midtown.

Boho Karaoke Orchard on Orchard Street on the Lower East Side starts its deal when it opens and keeps it going into the evening every day of the week. Draft beer and shots are the two items on the list. Delancey Street on the F, J, M and Z is three minutes away, so it is easy to reach from Brooklyn as well.

Treadwell Park is a beer hall on 1st Avenue on the Upper East Side. On weekdays its happy hour beers come in at one of the lower prices on this page, with wine, mixed cocktails and beef sliders also on the deal list. Lexington Avenue–63rd Street on the M and Q is about seven minutes on foot, and reservations are available.

Pete's Candy Store in Williamsburg is six minutes from Lorimer Street on the G and L. Its weekday list covers drafts, beer, well drinks and wines, all at modest happy hour prices. The window closes in the early evening, so it suits an after-work round rather than a late start, and there is no booking link to worry about.

Syndicated Bar Theater Kitchen is a bar on Bogart Street in Williamsburg, two minutes from the Morgan Avenue L. Select drafts are the cheapest item on its weekday happy hour, with house wine and classic cocktails also discounted. The window is a short one after work, Monday through Friday. Our listing shows no booking link, so plan to walk in.

Sweet Spot Sporting Lounge & Bar sits on 31st Street in Astoria, a minute from Astoria–Ditmars Boulevard on the N and W. Its weekday happy hour discounts beers, shots and a food item, and it opens in mid-afternoon, earlier than most on this page. If you ride the N or W to the end of the line, it is the first stop off the train.

sections.body: Midtown dominates: Times Square, Koreatown and Flatiron together account for about a fifth of the cheap beer bars on our list. Downtown, part of the Financial District group sits around Stone Street and Pearl Street near Whitehall Street–South Ferry. In Brooklyn, look along the L in Williamsburg and Bushwick, or near the G in Greenpoint, where Keg & Lantern and Black Rabbit are a short walk apart.

Beer specials are posted before tax and tip. Add the 8.875 percent New York sales tax and a tip of 18 to 20 percent to every round. Some bars honor the price only for seats at the bar, and some only for certain taps. We date every listing, so check when a bar was last verified before you make the trip.

faq.a: Hard Rock Cafe on Broadway, Faces & Names and Bartley Dunne's on West 54th Street, and Cafe Express Deli on 8th Avenue all list beer deals. Faces & Names and Cafe Express Deli run theirs every day of the week.
faq.q: Which bars near Times Square have cheap beer at happy hour?

faq.a: A fair share of the bars on this page include Saturday or Sunday. Niagara in the East Village, Black Rabbit and Papacito's in Greenpoint, Post No Bills in Williamsburg and Boho Karaoke Orchard on the Lower East Side run every day.
faq.q: Are there cheap beer happy hours on weekends?

faq.a: Barfly in Gramercy runs a late-night window Sunday through Thursday, and Bartley Dunne's near Times Square has one Sunday through Wednesday. Boxers HK in Hell's Kitchen keeps its weekday beer deal going later into the evening than most.
faq.q: Is there late-night cheap beer in NYC?

faq.a: Williamsburg has the most entries, including Pete's Candy Store, Post No Bills, Crystal Lake Brooklyn and Syndicated Bar Theater Kitchen. Greenpoint adds Keg & Lantern and Black Rabbit, and Bushwick has Talon Bar.
faq.q: Where can I find cheap beer in Brooklyn?

intro:
Saint Mark's Place is the address for Empellón Al pastor, a bar at number 132 in the East Village, Manhattan, six minutes on foot from the L train at 1st Avenue. The Empellón Al pastor happy hour runs on weekdays.

No offers are listed, so the bar publishes the times but not the deal. Check this page for live hours before you head over.

Draft cocktails are the listed deal at Coopers Craft & Kitchen, a pub at 87 2nd Avenue in the East Village, Manhattan. The Coopers Craft & Kitchen happy hour runs on weekdays and begins at midday, continuing into the evening.

Astor Place, with the 6 train, is a five-minute walk. No reservation link is listed. Check this page for live hours.

Wednesday through Friday is the stretch when Eastpoint runs its happy hour. The bar is at 25 Avenue B in the East Village, Manhattan, and no deals are listed, so it publishes the times but not the deal.

The nearest station is Essex Street, where the F, J, M and Z trains stop, a seven-minute walk. Reservations go through SevenRooms. Check this page for live hours.

On weekdays, Goodnight Sunny runs a happy hour at 134 1st Avenue in the East Village, Manhattan. The bar sits six minutes from 1st Avenue station on the L train.

The Goodnight Sunny happy hour has no deals published, only the days and hours. No reservation link is listed for the bar. Live hours are shown on this page, so check them before you go.

Midweek is peak season. Wednesday sits with Thursday at the top of our list for happy hours, and almost every weekday schedule covers Wednesdays, whether it runs Monday to Friday, Monday to Thursday, Tuesday to Sunday or Sunday to Wednesday. Williamsburg leads the neighborhoods for Wednesday deals, followed by Times Square, the East Village and the Upper West Side, with Hell's Kitchen and Greenwich Village not far behind.

What sets a Wednesday happy hour in NYC apart is the back end of the week's late-night and karaoke deals. Several bars run a Sunday-to-Wednesday schedule, so Wednesday night is the last chance each week for Maru Karaoke Lounge's discounted private rooms in Koreatown, Blue Haven's late window in Murray Hill and Bartley Dunne's late cocktail deal near Times Square. Tip: with this many choices, filter by the subway line you take home and pick a bar a few minutes from your stop.

picks.why: Maru Karaoke Lounge on West 32nd Street runs its happy hour Sunday through Wednesday in the evening, so Wednesday closes out its week. The deal text takes half off private karaoke rooms, and domestic beer, shots, well drinks and a cocktail list come at set prices. Herald Square, with eight lines, is three minutes away.

Bartley Dunne's, a cocktail pub on West 54th Street, saves its deal for late at night, Sunday through Wednesday. Negronis, Aperol spritzes, Moscow mules and Heineken draft are on the list, which makes it a fit for a drink after a Broadway show. The 7th Avenue station on the B, D and E is a one-minute walk, and tables can be booked.

Santa Panza, an Italian restaurant at 1079 Broadway in Bushwick, runs its happy hour Monday through Thursday in the early evening. Its deal text takes money off pizza, wines by the glass and draft beer, and the listed offers include an Aperol spritz, seasonal sangria, a housemade limoncello shot, a martini and marinated olives. Kosciuszko Street on the J is three minutes away.

Upstairs Cocktail Bar sits on the second floor at 71-22 Roosevelt Avenue in Woodside, two minutes from the 69th Street stop on the 7. Its deal runs Monday through Saturday in the early evening and sticks to cocktails: gimlets, classic margaritas, martinis and mules. It is an easy way to break up a Wednesday ride home on the 7.

Cantina Valencia Tex-Mex & Tequila Bar on Richmond Road in Staten Island runs a weekday happy hour with drink and bite specials at the bar only, according to its deal text. Our listing does not itemize the offers, so ask what is included. Jefferson Avenue on the Staten Island Railway is about eight minutes away, and reservations are available.

sections.h: Last call for the Sunday-to-Wednesday crowd
sections.body: A small group of bars run their deals Sunday through Wednesday and sit out Thursday through Saturday. On our list that includes Maru Karaoke Lounge in Koreatown, Blue Haven in Murray Hill, Bartley Dunne's near Times Square and Lovers of Today in the East Village, whose window opens in the small hours. If any of them is on your list, Wednesday is the night to go.

Expect the 8.875 percent sales tax on top of every price you see here, plus an 18 to 20 percent tip. Ask whether a deal applies at tables or only at the bar, since that varies from place to place. Look for the last-checked date on each bar's page; it tells you how fresh our information is.

faq.a: On our list, Wednesday and Thursday have the most bars with a happy hour, just ahead of Tuesday and well ahead of the weekend. Saturday has the fewest by a wide margin.
faq.q: What is the busiest night for happy hour in NYC?

faq.a: Maru Karaoke Lounge in Koreatown runs its evening happy hour Sunday through Wednesday, with half off private karaoke rooms plus discounted beer, shots, well drinks and cocktails. Herald Square is a three-minute walk.
faq.q: Where is there a karaoke happy hour on Wednesday?

faq.a: Blue Haven in Murray Hill and Bartley Dunne's near Times Square run late-night deals Sunday through Wednesday, and Barfly in Gramercy continues through Thursday.
faq.q: Which Wednesday happy hours run late?

faq.a: Yes, plenty on our list. Astoria has the most, with spots like Sweet Afton and The Ditty, and Upstairs Cocktail Bar in Woodside and The Beast Next Door Cafe & Bar in Long Island City run deals on Wednesdays too.
faq.q: Are there Wednesday happy hours in Queens?

intro:

The L train at 3rd Avenue is a three-minute walk. No reservation link is listed. Live prices and hours are on this page.

The Donna happy hour has no deals published, only the days and hours. Reservations can be made through Resy using the booking link. Check this page for live hours before you go.

Verdello is listed under Harlem at 994 Columbus Avenue in Manhattan, a four minute walk from Cathedral Parkway-110th Street, where the B and C trains stop. Reservations can be made through an OpenTable link on the listing. With no offers published, a quick question to the restaurant is the way to learn what the happy hour includes.
