The bar is at 668 10th Ave in Hell's Kitchen, seven minutes on foot from 50th Street, where the C and E trains stop. The Ardesia Wine Bar happy hour covers wines, cocktails and beer on weekdays. Reservations are available through a Resy link on the listing, which also tags the place for cocktails and wine. Since the offers include all three drink types, the happy hour is not limited to a single pour.

The 50th Street station, served by the C and E trains, is seven minutes away on foot. With no offers listed, it is worth checking directly with the bar for what the happy hour includes before heading over from the subway.

Wine, sangria and fries are the named items on the All & Sundry happy hour, which runs on weekdays and winds down in the early evening. This American bar sits at 312 W 58th St in Hell's Kitchen, two minutes on foot from 59th Street-Columbus Circle, where the 1, A, B, C and D trains stop. The listing tags the bar for cocktails, wine and a food deal.

A discount on all drinks and a deal on Herradura Silver tequila anchor the Baires Grill happy hour on weekdays. Baires Grill - New York is a bar at 350 W 50th St in Hell's Kitchen, two minutes on foot from the 50th Street station, where the C and E trains stop. Reservations are linked through OpenTable on the listing, which also tags the bar for cocktails and wine.

Every day of the week, Blue Seafood Bar keeps a happy hour window, though the restaurant lists the times without the deal. The Blue Seafood Bar happy hour is found at 856 9th Avenue in Hell's Kitchen, five minutes on foot from 59th Street-Columbus Circle, where the 1, A, B, C and D trains stop. Reservations go through an OpenTable link on the listing, and the page carries a wine tag along with a weekend tag.

Beer is the one named offer on the Boxers HK happy hour, which runs on weekdays and stretches into the evening. Boxers HK, a bar at 742 9th Ave in Hell's Kitchen, sits four minutes on foot from the 50th Street station, where the C and E trains stop. Its listing carries tags for cheap beer, wine, a food deal and sports, though only beer is named in the deal itself.

The by & by happy hour runs every day, and the bar publishes the times but not the deal. Categorized as a bar or restaurant, by & by is at 644 10th Ave in Hell's Kitchen, seven minutes on foot from the 42nd Street-Port Authority Bus Terminal station and its 1, 2, 3, 7, A, C, E, N, Q, R, S and W lines. A Resy link on the listing handles reservations. Tags mention cocktails, wine and a food deal.

Southern Thai cooking is the draw at Chalong, a restaurant at 749 9th Avenue in Hell's Kitchen, and the Chalong Southern Thai happy hour runs every day. The listing gives the times but not the deal, with only a cocktails tag hinting at what is poured. The nearest station is 50th Street, served by the C and E trains, four minutes away on foot. Reservations can be made through an OpenTable link on the listing.

The Conor's Goat happy hour runs on weekdays. The pub is in the East Village, Manhattan, and the listing includes no deals, just the days and the hours.

No street address is on file, but the F train at 2nd Avenue is a four-minute walk. No reservation link is listed for the pub. Live hours are shown on this page.

A bar at 224 East 10th Street in the East Village, Manhattan, Hard to Explain lists a happy hour for all seven days of the week. The Hard to Explain happy hour has no deals listed, only the times.

The L train at 1st Avenue is a five-minute walk. No reservation link is listed for the bar. Check this page for live hours before you go.

Kingston Hall, at 149 2nd Avenue in the East Village, Manhattan, serves its happy hour Monday through Saturday, and Sunday has a window of its own with an earlier start. The Kingston Hall happy hour lists beer, prosecco and well drinks.

Astor Place, where the 6 train stops, is a four-minute walk. No reservation link is listed. See this page for live prices and the hours for each day.

The Sura Spritz and soju drinks are the named offers at SURA, both at set prices. The SURA happy hour runs on weekdays in the early evening.

The bar is at 31 Wyckoff Avenue in Bushwick, Brooklyn, one minute from Jefferson Street station on the L. Cocktails and food deals are among its tags, and reservations go through the booking link.

Late evening is when the Central Park Tavern happy hour begins, Sunday through Thursday, with an Old Fashioned and a Spicy Margarita named among the offers. The bar and pub sits at 327 W 57th St in Hell's Kitchen, three minutes on foot from 59th Street-Columbus Circle, where the 1, A, B, C and D trains stop. The listing carries a late-night tag.

Tacos and party platters set the tone at La Palapa Cocina Mexicana, a Mexican restaurant at 77 Saint Marks Place in the East Village, Manhattan. The La Palapa Cocina Mexicana happy hour runs seven days a week and lists micheladas and beer.

The L train at 1st Avenue is a six-minute walk. Live prices and hours are on this page.

After midnight is when Lovers of Today runs its happy hour, a window that falls in the small hours rather than the early evening. The bar is at 132 ½ East 7th Street in the East Village, Manhattan, and the days listed are Sunday through Wednesday.

The L train at 1st Avenue is a seven-minute walk. No deals are listed. No booking link is given. Check this page for live hours.

Lucy's is a short walk from the L train: 1st Avenue station is six minutes from the bar at 135 Avenue A in the East Village, Manhattan. The Lucy's happy hour runs on weekdays.

The listing gives the days and hours but no deals, so the bar publishes the times but not the deal. No reservation link is listed. Check this page for live hours before you plan an evening around it.

Bud and Bud Light, well drinks and red or white wine are the deals named in the Phoenix Bar happy hour, which runs seven days a week. The bar is at 447 East 13th Street in the East Village, Manhattan, and the L train at 1st Avenue is just a one-minute walk.

No reservation link is listed for the bar. Live prices and hours are shown on this page.

Niagara starts its happy hour from opening on every day of the week and runs it until early evening. The bar is at 112 Avenue A in the East Village, Manhattan, seven minutes from 1st Avenue on the L train.

The Niagara happy hour lists draft beer, house wine and well drinks. No reservation link is listed. Check this page for live prices and the exact hours.

Ruffian, a bar at 125 E 7th St in the East Village, Manhattan, runs a weekday happy hour that includes a discount on everything, plus separate discounts on wine and on food. The L train at 1st Avenue is a seven-minute walk.

The Ruffian happy hour is the kind of deal where the savings reach both the glass and the plate. No reservation link is listed. Live hours are on this page.

Large frozen margaritas are the listed deal at San Loco, a bar at 151 Avenue A in the East Village, Manhattan. The San Loco happy hour runs on weekdays, starting at midday and finishing in the early evening, and tags also point to wine and a food deal.

The L train at 1st Avenue is a five-minute walk. No reservation link is listed. See this page for live prices and hours.

Ngon Vietnamese Kitchen NYC sits at 85 2nd Avenue in the East Village, Manhattan, five minutes on foot from 2nd Avenue and the F train. The Ngon Vietnamese Kitchen NYC happy hour runs on weekdays, and tags suggest cocktails, wine and a food deal.

No specific items are listed, only the times. No reservation link is given. Live hours are on this page.

Sunday through Thursday, Spicy Moon runs a happy hour at 328 East 6th Street in the East Village, Manhattan. It is a restaurant, and the listing names no specific deals.

The F train at 2nd Avenue is a five-minute walk. Reservations go through Resy using the booking link. The restaurant publishes the times but not the deal, so check this page for live hours.

Weekdays from midday into the evening, The Copper Still holds its happy hour at 151 2nd Avenue in the East Village, Manhattan. The pub is four minutes from Astor Place, where the 6 train stops.

Tags point to cocktails and wine, but the listing has no named deals. No reservation link is listed. Live prices and hours are on this page.

Upstate, a restaurant at 95 1st Avenue in the East Village, Manhattan, has a happy hour on every day of the week. Reservations go through Resy using the booking link, which is handy for planning.

The 2nd Avenue stop on the F train is a five-minute walk. The Upstate happy hour has no deals listed, so the restaurant publishes the times but not the deal. Check this page for live hours.

Tuesday through Sunday, the Friki Tiki happy hour brings a discount on everything, plus wine, beer, a drink special and an appetizer. This tiki bar is at 357 West 44th Street in Hell's Kitchen, four minutes on foot from the 42nd Street-Port Authority Bus Terminal station and its 1, 2, 3, 7, A, C, E, N, Q, R, S and W lines. A Resy link on the listing covers reservations, and the page is tagged for cocktails, wine and a food deal.

Lucky pours its happy hour on weekdays, with an end time but no start time on file. The bar is in the East Village, Manhattan, and the listing names discounted draft beer, a margarita, Aperol, and three beers: Founders All Day IPA, Montauk Wave Chaser IPA and Raging Bitch IPA.

The address is 168 Avenue B. The L train at 1st Avenue is a five-minute walk. No reservation link is listed. Live prices and hours appear on this page.

Scandinavian cooking defines Smør, a restaurant at 441 East 12th Street in the East Village, Manhattan. The Smør happy hour runs seven days a week and lists house wines and cocktails.

Only two minutes separate the restaurant from 1st Avenue station, where the L train stops. Live prices and hours are shown on this page.

Sangria, red or white wine and beer are what the Guantanamera happy hour puts on offer, weekdays only. The restaurant is at 939 8th Avenue in Hell's Kitchen, four minutes on foot from the 57th Street-7th Avenue station, where the N, Q, R and W trains stop. The listing also carries tags for cocktails and wine, but the three items above are the ones named in the deal, so they are the safest to plan around.

Northern Indian cooking is the specialty at Jaz, a restaurant at 813 9th Ave in Hell's Kitchen. Its happy hour runs every day, but the Jaz happy hour comes as times only, since the restaurant publishes the schedule and not the deal. The 50th Street station, served by the C and E trains, is five minutes away on foot. No booking link is listed, so the restaurant itself is the place to ask about offers.

At 856 9th Ave in Hell's Kitchen, Kashkaval Cheese Market lists a happy hour that runs Sunday through Friday and ends in the early evening. The Kashkaval Cheese Market happy hour comes as a schedule only, with no deal published, though the listing carries a wine tag. This bar is five minutes on foot from 59th Street-Columbus Circle, where the 1, A, B, C and D trains stop.

Every day of the week and into the late evening, West Bank Cafe lists a happy hour. The West Bank Cafe happy hour is found at 407 W 42nd St in Hell's Kitchen, four minutes on foot from the 42nd Street-Port Authority Bus Terminal station and its 1, 2, 3, 7, A, C, E, N, Q, R, S and W lines. Reservations go through a Resy link.

Sunday through Friday, a happy hour window at the tables ending in the early evening is listed for Kashkaval Garden, a restaurant at 852 9th Avenue in Hell's Kitchen. At the bar and chef's table the Kashkaval Garden happy hour runs all day, every day, and covers beers, well drinks, house wine, specialty mocktails and single tapas. A wine tag appears on the listing. For the subway, 59th Street-Columbus Circle is five minutes away on foot and is served by the 1, A, B, C and D trains.

Reservations through OpenTable are linked from the Sushi Damo listing, a restaurant at 330 West 58th Street in Hell's Kitchen. The Sushi Damo happy hour runs every day, with the times published and the deal left out. Subway riders can use 59th Street-Columbus Circle, two minutes away on foot, where the 1, A, B, C and D trains stop. A weekend tag also appears on the page.

Pita glazed wings, mango habanero boneless wings and mango habanero cauliflower bites make up The Brazen Tavern happy hour, weekdays only. The tavern is an American and Irish pub at 356 W 44th St in Hell's Kitchen, three minutes on foot from the 42nd Street-Port Authority Bus Terminal station and its 1, 2, 3, 7, A, C, E, N, Q, R, S and W lines. The offers named are all food, matching the food-deal tag on the listing.

Wine, well drinks, canned beer and a Harpoon American Flyer Lager are on the list for The Molly Pitcher Club happy hour, which runs Tuesday through Friday. The bar is at 675 9th Ave in Hell's Kitchen, five minutes on foot from the 50th Street station, where the C and E trains stop. The listing carries a wine tag, and no booking link is provided.

Wine is the focus of The Purple Tongue Wine Bar, at 410 W 43rd St in Hell's Kitchen. The Purple Tongue Wine Bar happy hour runs Tuesday through Friday, and the bar publishes the times but not the deal. The 42nd Street-Port Authority Bus Terminal station is five minutes away on foot, with the 1, 2, 3, 7, A, C, E, N, Q, R, S and W lines. No reservation link is listed.

A martini is the named offer on the VERS happy hour, which runs every day and ends in the early evening. The bar is at 714 9th Avenue in Hell's Kitchen, three minutes on foot from the 50th Street station, where the C and E trains stop. Reservations are available through a Resy link on the listing, which also tags the bar for cocktails and a food deal.

Italian and Asian fusion cooking come together at SESAMO, a bar at 764 10th Ave in Hell's Kitchen. The SESAMO happy hour runs Sunday through Thursday and finishes in the early evening, though the deal itself is not published, only the times. The 50th Street station, with C and E trains, is seven minutes away on foot. A Resy link on the listing covers reservations, and tags include late-night and a food deal.

Up in Inwood, La Bodega is a bar at 51 Vermilyea Ave, and its happy hour is listed every day of the week. The La Bodega happy hour comes as a schedule only, since the bar publishes the times but not the deal. Dyckman Street, on the 1 line, is the nearest station, four minutes away on foot. Reservations are available through an OpenTable link on the listing, and a weekend tag also appears on the page.

Mini burgers, Republica wings, tacos and guacamole empanadas make up the Republica happy hour, which runs on weekdays and stretches into the evening. The bar serves Latin American food, with steak and seafood on the cuisine list, and sits at 160 Dyckman St in Inwood. The Dyckman Street station, served by the A train, is three minutes away on foot. The offers named are all food, matching the food-deal tag on the listing.

Tuesday through Friday, Tryon Public House runs a happy hour at 4740 Broadway in Inwood. The Lower East Side sits below East Houston Street and east of the Bowery, running toward the Williamsburg Bridge at Delancey Street. Orchard Street carries the most bars, with Isla & Co., Gugu Room, Mary's, Boho Karaoke Orchard and Hair Of The Dog within a few blocks of each other. Broome Street adds a trio around Sally Can Wait and Ten Bells, Ludlow, Rivington and Clinton Streets fill in the middle, and a western strip on Chrystie and lower Rivington Streets brings in Home Sweet Home, Ray's and Loreley near the Bowery stop on the J and Z. Delancey Street and Essex Street on the F, J, M and Z serve most of the rest.

Happy hour in the Lower East Side starts early and often runs every day. Ten Bells, Bar Belly and Boho Karaoke Orchard all begin their deals when the doors open, and a good share of our list includes Saturday or Sunday. Expect draft beer, house wine, well drinks and frozen or craft cocktails, with oysters, tacos, burgers and sliders at a few addresses. One tip: Tre limits its Thursday deal to the bar, so ask before taking a table anywhere on this list.

picks.why: Ten Bells on Broome Street is a bar that runs its deal every day from opening, built around oysters and a half-liter carafe of wine. That makes it one of the easiest weekend options in the neighborhood. Delancey Street on the F, J, M and Z is two minutes away, and Resy takes reservations if you are bringing a group.

Sally Can Wait, a bar at 252 Broome Street, keeps its happy hour simple: drafts, wines, well drinks and frozen cocktails, each at a set price, Monday through Friday until early evening. It is a few doors from Ten Bells and Barrio Chino and two minutes from the Delancey Street station, so a second stop is easy.

Hair Of The Dog is a sports bar at 168 Orchard Street with one of the earliest starts around: its weekday happy hour opens at midday with half off all drinks and a slider on special, exclusions applying. Once that ends, its menu lists nightly specials such as half-price beer on Monday. The 2nd Avenue F is three minutes away.

La Caverna at 122 Rivington Street runs its longest window on Taco Tuesday, from late afternoon into the evening, with beef, chicken or veggie tacos, margaritas, tequila shots and beers on special. Wednesday, Thursday, Friday and Sunday bring beer, wine, well drinks and a margarita tower. It runs later than most deals on our list here. Essex Street on the F, J, M and Z is a two-minute walk.

Sonnyboy is a restaurant at 65 Rivington Street with a Tuesday to Saturday happy hour, which makes it a rare Saturday option. Craft cocktails, wines by the glass and beer are on special, burgers in beef, fried chicken or kangaroo join in, and Tuesday adds half off bottles of wine. Delancey Street is four minutes away; book through Resy.

Tre is a restaurant at 173 Ludlow Street with two windows: weekday early evenings, and a longer stretch on Saturday and Sunday afternoons. White, red and rosé wines, Champagne and Aperol are the discounted pours. On Thursdays the deal applies at the bar only, according to its menu. The F at 2nd Avenue is three minutes away.

Boho Karaoke Orchard at 152 Orchard Street is a karaoke bar whose deal runs every day from opening into the late evening, one of the longest windows on our list here. Shots such as lemon drops and soju, draft beer, wine, sake bombs and mixed drinks are discounted, and private rooms get a happy hour rate too. Delancey Street is three minutes away.

sections.body: Delancey Street and Essex Street, both served by the F, J, M and Z, are the nearest stops for most bars on our list, covering Orchard, Broome, Clinton and Rivington Streets. The F alone also stops at 2nd Avenue on Houston Street, closest to Hair Of The Dog, Lydia's and Tre on the north side, and at East Broadway, the stop for 169 Bar and Bar Belly to the south. On the western edge, Bowery on the J and Z is a minute or two from Home Sweet Home, Ray's, Loreley Restaurant & Biergarten and Jadis Wine Bar.

Add New York's 8.875 percent sales tax to anything you see on the menu, then an 18 to 20 percent tip. Bar-only rules are common: Tre states one for Thursdays. Deals on this side of town shift, so look at the last-checked date on each bar's page before heading out.

faq.a: Ten Bells, Isla & Co., Gugu Room, Nurse Bettie, Bar Belly, Jadis Wine Bar and Boho Karaoke Orchard all list a daily deal. Mary's runs Sunday through Thursday and Sonnyboy Tuesday through Saturday, while 169 Bar keeps its happy hour for Saturday and Sunday only.
faq.q: Which Lower East Side bars have happy hour every day?

faq.a: Boho Karaoke Orchard runs its deal into the late evening every day, and La Caverna keeps Taco Tuesday going into the evening. Loreley Restaurant & Biergarten also stretches its Tuesday deal into the late evening, and Hair Of The Dog adds nightly specials after its weekday happy hour ends.
faq.q: Where can I find a late happy hour on the Lower East Side?

faq.a: Ten Bells discounts oysters, La Caverna has tacos on Tuesday, and Hair Of The Dog puts a slider on special. Ray's lists a burger, fries and hot wings, Izakaya Juraku discounts house fries and spicy edamame, Casa Colven offers nachos, and Sonnyboy includes burgers.
faq.q: Which Lower East Side happy hours include food?

faq.a: Yes. Ten Bells on Broome Street discounts oysters every day from opening, alongside a carafe of wine. It is the only bar on our Lower East Side list with oysters in its deal.
faq.q: Is there an oyster happy hour on the Lower East Side?

Monday to Thursday afternoons are when Margarita Island runs its happy hour. Listed as a cocktail bar at 1105 Bowery Street in Brooklyn, it is a four minute walk from West 8th Street–New York Aquarium station on the F and Q.

The Margarita Island happy hour finishes in the early evening. The listing does not publish the drinks or deals covered. A website is listed.

Felice, a restaurant at 84 Montague Street in Brooklyn Heights, serves a weekday happy hour from late afternoon into the early evening. Clark Street station on the 2 and 3 is five minutes away on foot.

The Felice happy hour has no specific deals listed, so the restaurant publishes the times but not the offer. Reservations are available through the booking link, and a website is listed.

Henry Street in Brooklyn Heights holds The Binc, a bar at number 60 and one minute from High Street station on the A and C.

The Binc happy hour is held Monday through Thursday in the early evening. Nothing is listed about the drinks or food covered, so the times are the only detail published. A website is listed for anyone who wants to check before heading over.

Wine is the one drink tag on Cherry On Top, a bar at 379 Suydam Street in Bushwick, Brooklyn. Three minutes from DeKalb Avenue station on the L, it holds a weekday happy hour in the early evening.

The Cherry On Top happy hour has no specific offers listed, so the bar publishes the times but not the deal. A website is listed.

A lime margarita and a shot, both at set prices, are the listed offers at Gordo's Cantina. The Gordo's Cantina happy hour runs on weekdays, with a long window from midday into the early evening.

The bar is at 140 St Nicholas Avenue in Bushwick, Brooklyn, two minutes from DeKalb Avenue station on the L. Cocktails are among its tags, and a website is listed.

Shots, wine, well drinks and signature cocktails, each at a set price, make up the Hart Bar happy hour, and it is held every day of the week. The window runs through the early evening.

Hart Bar is at 538 Hart Street in Bushwick, Brooklyn, four minutes on foot from Central Avenue station on the M. A website is listed for more detail.

Mezcali, a bar at 83 Maiden Ln in the Financial District, Manhattan, lists a weekday happy hour. The Mezcali happy hour has no deals published, only the days and hours.

The 2 and 3 trains stop at Wall Street, two minutes away on foot. No reservation link is listed for the bar. Live hours are shown on this page, and they are worth checking before heading over.

Beer, a spicy pickle smash burger and a shot are the three set-price items on the Soup Queen Bk happy hour menu. The window sits in the afternoon, every day of the week.

The bar is at 143 Troutman Street in Bushwick, Brooklyn, a four minute walk from Central Avenue station on the M. Cheap-beer and food-deal tags are on the listing, and a website is available.

Wine and house cocktails, each at a set price, are the offers listed for the Therapy Wine Bar happy hour. It runs every day, weekends included, with a long window from midday into the early evening.

Therapy Wine Bar is listed as a wine bar at 260 Malcolm X Boulevard in Bed-Stuy, Brooklyn, seven minutes from Utica Avenue station on the A and C.

Beer, wines, well drinks and specialty martinis are what the Route 66 Smokehouse happy hour covers on weekdays. The American restaurant is at 79 Pearl Street in the Financial District, Manhattan.

Whitehall Street-South Ferry is a three-minute walk, and the 1, R and W trains stop there. Reservations go through Resy using the booking link. Check this page for live prices and hours.

Tuesday is when the city's happy hour list fills back in. Most bars on our list run a deal on Tuesdays, dozens more than on Mondays, and Brooklyn picks up the biggest share of the newcomers as restaurants that close or skip Mondays come back. Williamsburg has more Tuesday deals than any other neighborhood on our list, with Times Square, the East Village and the Upper West Side close behind.

A Tuesday happy hour in NYC also comes with a tradition: Taco Tuesday. La Caverna on the Lower East Side builds its whole Tuesday deal around tacos, margaritas and tequila, and Riviera Maya in Astoria stretches its Tuesday window across most of the day. Weekday windows still dominate, opening in the afternoon and wrapping up in the early evening, so the after-work slot is the safe bet. Tip: for bars that run Tuesday to Friday, such as Monarch in Williamsburg, Tuesday is the first chance of the week.

picks.why: La Caverna on Rivington Street turns Tuesday into a taco night: beef, chicken or veggie tacos, margaritas, tequila shots and beers all come at a set price. Its window opens after work and runs later into the evening than most Tuesday deals on our list. Essex Street, served by the F, J, M and Z, is a two-minute walk.

Riviera Maya is a Mexican and Latin bar on Steinway Street in Astoria whose deal text calls Tuesday an all-day happy hour; our listing shows it running from midday into the evening. Frozen and classic margaritas and beer are the main offers, and the deal text also lists sangrias and a pisco cocktail. The 30th Avenue N and W stop is about eight minutes away.

Monarch Izakaya at 146 Metropolitan Avenue keeps its happy hour to Tuesday through Friday, so Tuesday opens its week. Sake comes with a discount and select cocktails at a set price, while Kirin and snacks also appear in its deal text. Bedford Avenue on the L is about six minutes on foot, the first stop out of Manhattan.

Hello Bar Bk on Nostrand Avenue in Crown Heights skips Monday and runs its happy hour Tuesday through Sunday, covering cocktails, wine and beer at set prices. Its deal text also says the kitchen stays open late. The Sterling Street stop on the 2 and 5 is three minutes away, an easy hop for anyone riding those lines home.

Loreley Restaurant & Biergarten at 7 Rivington Street keeps its Tuesday happy hour going until late evening, well past the usual after-work cutoff. The deal takes money off everything on the list, from draft beer to steins and pitchers, plus select bottled wine. It is two minutes from Bowery on the J and Z, and the restaurant takes reservations.

Piccolino Restaurant, an Italian place on Amboy Road in Great Kills, Staten Island, starts its happy hour on Tuesday and runs it through Friday, at the bar only. The food list is the long one here: chicken wings, mozzarella sticks or fried zucchini with fries, and penne vodka, next to lychee martinis, margaritas, beer and wine. Great Kills station is two minutes away.

sections.body: Plenty of restaurants on our list either close on Monday or start their discounts a day later. Tuesday-to-Friday schedules, like Monarch's and Piccolino's, and Tuesday-to-Sunday ones, like Hello Bar Bk's and Sesamo's in Hell's Kitchen, all switch on every Tuesday. That is why Brooklyn picks up so many extra deals on Tuesdays. If you have one night to explore a neighborhood outside Manhattan, Tuesday through Thursday give you the widest choice.

Menu prices leave out the 8.875 percent sales tax, and a tip of 18 to 20 percent is customary. Taco and bar specials are often served at the bar only, Piccolino's included, so sit there if you want the deal. Our check date is listed on every bar page; look at it before you go, since specials can change without notice.

faq.a: La Caverna on the Lower East Side discounts beef, chicken and veggie tacos with margaritas, tequila shots and beer on Tuesday. Riviera Maya in Astoria runs an all-day Tuesday happy hour built around margaritas.
faq.q: Where can I find Taco Tuesday happy hour deals in NYC?

faq.a: Monarch in Williamsburg and Piccolino Restaurant on Staten Island run Tuesday through Friday, and Hello Bar Bk in Crown Heights and Sesamo in Hell's Kitchen run Tuesday through Sunday.
faq.q: Which bars start their happy hour on Tuesday?

faq.a: Loreley Restaurant & Biergarten and La Caverna, both on the Lower East Side, keep Tuesday deals going into the late evening. Later still, Barfly in Gramercy, Blue Haven in Murray Hill and Meller's Sports Hub & Grill on the Upper East Side run late-night windows that include Tuesday.
faq.q: Is there a Tuesday happy hour that runs late?

faq.a: Williamsburg, followed by Times Square, the East Village and the Upper West Side. In Queens, Astoria leads, and on Staten Island, Piccolino Restaurant in Great Kills joins the weekday regulars on Tuesday.
faq.q: Which neighborhood has the most Tuesday happy hours?

intro:
Toro Loco pours a long list of drinks during its weekday happy hour: Toro Loco Lager, cocktails, a frozen margarita, red and white sangria, wine and rosé. The bar is at 15 Stone St in the Financial District, Manhattan.

Whitehall Street-South Ferry, where the 1, R and W trains stop, is a two-minute walk. No reservation link is listed. See this page for live prices and hours.

A sports bar happy hour in NYC is mostly about discounted drafts and well drinks before or during a game, and our list has a short roster of bars tagged as sports bars with a deal attached. The Manhattan ones are spread from Greenwich Village and Hell's Kitchen up to the Upper East Side, and the Brooklyn ones are in Williamsburg, Greenpoint, Bushwick and Clinton Hill.

Most of these deals run on weekdays from late afternoon into the evening, which lines up with weeknight games. A couple break the pattern: The Dawson 39 near Bryant Park starts at lunchtime and includes Saturday, and Meller's on the Upper East Side runs a deal that begins late at night. Some bars pause specials on major game nights, so confirm before you build an evening around one.

picks.why: Boxers HK on Ninth Avenue describes itself as Hell's Kitchen's gay sports bar, with LED screens for the games. Its weekday happy hour runs from late afternoon into the evening and covers beer and wine, well drinks and call drinks. The C and E at 50th Street are four minutes away.

The Dawson 39 is an Irish restaurant and sports bar on West 39th Street whose own listing promises wall-to-wall HD TVs over two floors. Its happy hour has one of the longest windows here, from lunchtime to early evening Monday through Friday, and all day on Saturday and Sunday. The B, D, F, M and 7 at 42nd Street-Bryant Park are two minutes away.

Meller's Sports Hub & Grill is the late option for Upper East Side sports fans, with a deal that opens late at night and lasts into the small hours from Sunday to Thursday. The list takes in canned beers, wine, frozen and mixed drinks and margaritas. It is a two-minute walk from the Q at 86th Street.

O'Flanagan's is an Upper East Side pub on First Avenue with a weekday happy hour from late afternoon into the evening. Its own menu covers well drinks, flavored Stolichnaya vodkas, and Bud Light, Yuengling and Coors Light on tap, with domestic bottles too. The Q at 72nd Street is about seven minutes away.

Dive Bar BK on Troutman Street in Bushwick is tagged as both a dive and a sports bar, and its own page advertises UFC and boxing watch parties, some ticketed. Happy hour runs on weekday evenings and Saturdays. The L at Jefferson Street is a minute away.

Judy Z's Sports Tavern & Kitchen sits at the start of Seventh Avenue South and runs its happy hour Wednesday through Friday in the early evening. Beers, mixed drinks and frozen drinks are covered, and the bar also sells beer by the bucket. The 1 at Houston Street is two minutes away, and it takes reservations.

sections.body: With a short list, there is no single sports bar district on our list. The Upper East Side has O'Flanagan's and Meller's, and Williamsburg has Guarapo and The Woods. Others are spread across the city, from Rocco's Sports & Rec near the Bleecker Street station to The Emerson on Myrtle Avenue in Clinton Hill, with Tavern29 by the 28th Street stop on the 6 adding a pub with a long weekday window.

On big game nights, specials may be paused, so check with the bar before you count on the deal. Menu prices leave out the 8.875 percent city sales tax, and a tip of 18 to 20 percent is standard. Look at each bar's last-checked date before you plan around a happy hour.

faq.a: The Dawson 39 near Bryant Park and Dive Bar BK in Bushwick both include Saturday, and Meller's on the Upper East Side runs Sunday through Thursday. Most other sports bars on our list run weekdays only.
faq.q: Which NYC sports bars have happy hour on Saturday?

faq.a: Boxers HK in Hell's Kitchen describes itself as a gay sports bar and runs a weekday happy hour with beer, wine and well drinks.
faq.q: Is there a gay sports bar with happy hour in NYC?

faq.a: Dive Bar BK in Bushwick, The Emerson in Clinton Hill, and Guarapo Latin Fusion Sports Restaurant and Bar and The Woods in Williamsburg.
faq.q: Which sports bars in Brooklyn have happy hour?

faq.a: Meller's Sports Hub & Grill on the Upper East Side runs one from late night into the small hours, Sunday through Thursday. Barfly in Gramercy, listed as a sports bar by cuisine, runs a similar late deal.
faq.q: Is there a late night sports bar happy hour?

intro:
Steakhouse cooking is the specialty at Ben & Jack's Steakhouse, 255 5th Ave in Midtown District, Manhattan. The Ben & Jack's Steakhouse happy hour runs on weekdays and lists beer, house wine, prosecco, a martini, a margarita, red or white sangria and Blue Point oysters.

The 1 train at 28th Street is listed as a two-minute walk. No reservation link is listed. See this page for live prices and hours.

American cooking is the draw at Bill's Bar and Burger, a restaurant at 85 West Street in the Financial District, Manhattan. Its weekday happy hour combines a snack discount with draft beer, beers and pitcher attack apps.

The 1 train at Rector Street is a three-minute walk. The Bill's Bar and Burger happy hour prices and hours are shown live on this page.

Mediterranean and Greek cooking is the focus at Mezze on the River, a bar at 375 S End Ave, listed under the Financial District in Manhattan. The Mezze on the River happy hour runs on weekdays and lists cocktails such as a spicy feta cocktail and a Negroni, plus wine and beer.

WTC Cortlandt, with the 1 train, is a six-minute walk. Live prices and hours are on this page.

New American cooking is the style at Urban Cove Society & Kitchen, a restaurant at 33 Peck Slip in the Financial District, Manhattan. The Urban Cove Society & Kitchen happy hour runs every day and lists beer, glasses of select wine, featured cocktails, a Clear Negroni and a Cynar Negroni.

Fulton Street station is a six-minute walk, with the 2, 3, 4, 5, A, C, J and Z trains.

Wine is the specialty at Zizi's Wine Bar, 45 John Street in the Financial District, Manhattan, and its happy hour runs seven days a week. The Zizi's Wine Bar happy hour lists a discount on everything and a separate food discount.

Fulton Street station is a one-minute walk, with the 2, 3, 4, 5, A, C, J and Z trains. Live hours are on this page.

Le Bistroquet, a bar at 50 W 22nd St in the Flatiron District, Manhattan, lists a weekday happy hour. The F and M trains at 23rd Street are a one-minute walk away.

The Le Bistroquet happy hour has no deals published, only the days and hours. No reservation link is listed. Check this page for the live hours before you head over.

Sen NYC offers its happy hour on Tuesday only, at 12 W 21st St in the Flatiron District, Manhattan. The C and E trains at 23rd Street are listed as a two-minute walk, and tags point to a food deal.

The Sen NYC happy hour has no named items, since the bar publishes the times but not the deal. No reservation link is listed. See this page for live hours.

Society Billiards + Bar pairs its weekday happy hour with a margarita deal, and tags also point to cocktails, wine and a food deal. The bar is at 10 East 21st Street in the Flatiron District, Manhattan.

The R and W trains at 23rd Street are a two-minute walk. The Society Billiards + Bar happy hour has no reservation link listed. Live prices and hours are on this page.

A pub happy hour in NYC is the plain, dependable kind: discounted pints, house wine and well drinks at an Irish bar, a tavern or a beer hall, usually on weekdays after work. Manhattan holds most of the bars on our list tagged as pubs, with the Upper East Side leading, followed by Koreatown, then Murray Hill and Greenwich Village. Brooklyn's are spread across Williamsburg, Park Slope, Gowanus, Prospect Heights and Cobble Hill, and Queens and Staten Island add a few more.

Expect domestic drafts, Guinness at a few, a margarita or espresso martini at some, and food at a minority. Weekday deals from late afternoon into the early evening are the norm, while a few pubs run late shifts or keep a deal for weekend daytime.

picks.why: Croton Reservoir Tavern sits on West 40th Street across from Bryant Park and runs a weekday happy hour from late afternoon into the evening. The deal covers margaritas, classic cocktails, sangria, select wines, draft beer and well drinks. The B, D, F, M and 7 at 42nd Street-Bryant Park are a minute away, and the tavern takes reservations, which helps with an after-work group.

Phebes is a pub on the Bowery with a weekday deal that runs from late afternoon to early evening. Guinness and Stella drafts are named on its list, along with other beers, wines and cocktails. The Bleecker Street station, with the 6 and the B, D, F and M, is four minutes away, and it accepts reservations.

Treadwell Park is a beer hall on First Avenue in the low 60s with a weekday happy hour that covers beers, wine and mixed cocktails, plus beef sliders on the food side. It runs from late afternoon into the early evening. The M and Q at Lexington Avenue-63rd Street are about seven minutes away, and it takes reservations.

Jack Demsey's is an Irish and American pub on West 33rd Street with a long weekday window, from late morning to early evening. Drafts such as Demsey's Ale and Coors Light, house wine and well drinks are on the list, plus a hangover burger. Herald Square, served by the B, D, F, M, N, Q, R and W, is two minutes away.

The Brazen Head is a Cobble Hill pub with a straightforward weekday happy hour from late afternoon into the evening: well drinks, house wine and Aslin Old Town Lager. The F and G at Bergen Street are about four minutes away, so it is an easy first stop on a Smith Street or Court Street night.

The Little Whiskey on Wilson Avenue in Bushwick has a weekday happy hour that runs until early evening, and all day on Monday, with PBR tall boys, Miller High Life, wine and well drinks on the list. It is one of the simplest deals on this page, and the L at Morgan Avenue is about six minutes away.

Cobblestones Pub and Biergarten on Queens Boulevard is one of the few Queens pubs on our list, with a weekday deal from midafternoon into the evening. Draughts, wine by the glass and mixed drinks are covered. The E and F at Kew Gardens-Union Turnpike are a two-minute walk.

sections.body: Most pubs here open their deal in the late afternoon and close it in the early evening on weekdays. A few go longer: Jack Demsey's, Sefton and The Wolfe start in the late morning or at lunchtime. Some run late instead, among them Tanner Smith's and Bartley Dunne's near Times Square and Blue Haven in Murray Hill. The Malt House in Greenwich Village is the weekend outlier, with a Saturday and Sunday daytime deal.

Pub deals are usually poured at the bar and may skip holidays and big match days. Add 8.875 percent sales tax and an 18 to 20 percent tip to the menu price. Pubs change their specials often, so look at each bar's last-checked date.

faq.a: Jack Demsey's and Playwright Irish Pub near Herald Square, Tara Mor on West 30th Street, The Dawson on West 45th Street, Mulligan's Pub on Madison Avenue and The Brazen Tavern in Hell's Kitchen all run happy hours, mostly on weekdays.
faq.q: Which Irish pubs in NYC have happy hour?

faq.a: Yes, more than any other neighborhood on our list, including O'Flanagan's, Sefton, Jones Wood Foundry, The Penrose, The Alvin Public House and Treadwell Park.
faq.q: Are there pub happy hours on the Upper East Side?

faq.a: Tanner Smith's runs one nightly, and Bartley Dunne's and Blue Haven in Murray Hill run theirs from Sunday to Wednesday.
faq.q: Do any pubs have a late happy hour?

faq.a: The Brazen Tavern in Hell's Kitchen lists wings and cauliflower bites, Treadwell Park has beef sliders, Vida Verde has chorizo empanadas and fries, Evalyn's Tap House in Gowanus offers Bavarian pretzels from Tuesday to Sunday, and The Penny Farthing near Union Square includes burgers.
faq.q: Which pubs have happy hour food?

intro:
Up on the 10th floor of the Hyatt Place hotel at 133-42 39th Ave, Leaf Bar & Lounge is a Flushing bar tagged for rooftop seating and cocktails. Flushing-Main Street, served by the 7 train, is a 3-minute walk away.

The Leaf Bar & Lounge happy hour runs every day, including Saturday and Sunday. The bar publishes the times but not the deal, so what is on offer is not listed here. The live schedule on this page shows the current window.

All seven days are covered by the happy hour at Sagaponack, a bar at 4 W 22nd St in the Flatiron District, Manhattan. The R and W trains at 23rd Street are a two-minute walk.

The Sagaponack happy hour has no deals published, only the days and hours. Reservations can be made through Resy using the booking link. Live hours are shown on this page.

Barbecue is the specialty at Hill Country Barbecue Market, a restaurant at 30 West 26th Street in the Flatiron District, Manhattan. The Hill Country Barbecue Market happy hour runs on weekdays and lists specialty cocktails and beers.

The R and W trains at 28th Street are a three-minute walk. Live prices and hours are shown on this page.

A very long window, running most of the day, is how John Doe Craft Bar & Kitchen handles its happy hour, and it applies every day of the week. The bar is at 253 5th Ave in Midtown District, Manhattan, and the one deal named is oysters.

The R and W trains at 28th Street are a two-minute walk. Tags also mention outdoor seating. No reservation link is listed. Live hours are on this page.

On Queens Boulevard in Forest Hills, Guantanamera runs as a restaurant at 110-72 Queens Boulevard. The 75th Avenue station, served by the E and F trains, is a 1-minute walk from the door.

Expect sangria, red or white wine and beer on the Guantanamera happy hour menu. The window runs on weekdays and starts around midday, which makes it an early one. The listing also tags the place for cocktails and wine, though the deal itself names only those three drinks.

Rove sits at 72-27 Austin St in Forest Hills, a bar tagged for cocktails and wine. From Forest Hills-71st Avenue, where the E, F, M and R trains stop, it is a 5-minute walk.

The Rove happy hour is listed for every day of the week, weekends included, and ends in the early evening. The bar publishes the times but not the deal, so no drinks or food are named here. Look at the live schedule on this page for the current hours.

On Austin Street in Forest Hills, Tap House is a bar at 72-07 Austin Street with a food deal noted in its tags. The nearest subway is Forest Hills-71st Avenue, with E, F, M and R service, about 4 minutes on foot.

Weekdays are when the Tap House happy hour runs, from late afternoon into the early evening. Specific drinks and dishes are not published, only the schedule, so the details of the food deal are not spelled out here. The live listing on this page has the current times.

DeKalb Avenue in Fort Greene has Colonia Verde, a restaurant at number 219. Clinton-Washington Avenues, on the G line, is a 5-minute walk.

The Colonia Verde happy hour runs Monday through Thursday in the early evening, with no Friday or weekend window listed. The restaurant publishes the times but not the deal, so no drinks or food are named. Reservations are handled through a Resy link, which is worth using if you want a table around that window.

Karasu sits at 166 Dekalb Ave in Fort Greene, a bar close to Fulton Street on the G line, about 4 minutes away on foot.

Drinks on the Karasu happy hour include select sake, a classic Toki highball, a Midori rum highball and a whisky shot. The food side lists cold edamame, a Karasu burger and furikake fries. Some of the sake is listed as bar only. It runs Monday through Thursday in the early evening, and reservations go through Resy.

Butler Street in Gowanus is the address for Evalyn's Tap House, a pub at 236 Butler Street. Union Street, on the R line, is a 6-minute walk.

Craft draft beer and Bavarian pretzels make up the Evalyn's Tap House happy hour. It runs from late afternoon into the early evening from Tuesday to Sunday, and all day on Monday, when beers, well drinks and cocktails are on the deal. No reservation link is published, and the live listing on this page shows the current hours.

SoHo is the grid of cast-iron blocks between Houston and Canal Streets, running roughly from Sixth Avenue east to Lafayette Street, and our list also takes in the Hudson Square blocks to the west. Spring, Thompson and MacDougal Streets hold Boqueria Soho, Pera SoHo, San Carlo Osteria Piemonte, Cómodo and Emmett's, and West Broadway runs from Dos Caminos down to Soho Diner near Canal. Farther west, Westville is on Hudson Street and Lazy Point on Spring Street; to the east, NoMo Kitchen is on Crosby Street and Grand Street Social on Grand Street.

Restaurants outnumber bars here, so a SoHo happy hour usually means discounted drinks with something to eat: tapas, Mexican snacks, deep-dish pizza and fries. Most deals are weekday, late-afternoon affairs, though Grand Street Social keeps its menu for Saturday and Sunday. If you are out late on a weekend, Soho Diner runs its happy hour only on Friday and Saturday nights, long after the others have closed.

picks.why: Dos Caminos is a Mexican restaurant on West Broadway with a weekday happy hour of margaritas and snacks like beef empanadas, chips and guacamole, queso and taquitos. Per the restaurant, a second window opens late in the evening, served at the bar and patio only. The Prince Street R and W station is a four-minute walk.

Emmett's is a MacDougal Street restaurant serving deep-dish and thin-crust pizza and Italian beef sandwiches. It runs what it calls a Happy Hour and a Half, at the bar only, Tuesday through Friday, with spritzes, wines by the glass, draft beers, mozzarella sticks and handcut fries. Spring Street on the C and E is three minutes away.

Boqueria Soho is a Spanish tapas bar and restaurant on Spring Street, two minutes from the C and E. Its happy hour runs on weekday afternoons, and the restaurant's own page lists a shorter weekend version too, which few places on this page offer. The menu itself is not in our data, so book on Resy and ask about the deal when you arrive.

Soho Diner, at 320 West Broadway near Canal Street, is the late option: its happy hour runs only on Friday and Saturday nights, after nearly every other deal on this page has ended. The menu is food, including Soho hot wings, crispy cheese curds, a smoky black-eyed pea hummus and a smash burger. The Canal Street A, C and E is a minute away.

Cómodo is a cocktail and wine bar on MacDougal Street with a weekday happy hour aimed at the gap between work and dinner. The list includes an Aperitivo Spritz made with grapefruit, pomegranate and cava, plus a Rioja white and a red by the glass. It is three minutes from the Houston Street 1, and Resy handles reservations.

Westville is a restaurant at 333 Hudson Street, on the western edge of our SoHo list, with happy hour on weekdays from late afternoon into the early evening. Cocktails, wine and beer are on it. The Houston Street 1 is three minutes away.

sections.body: Spring Street on the C and E serves Boqueria Soho, Emmett's, Pera SoHo, San Carlo, Milady's and Lazy Point. The 1 at Houston Street is closest to Cómodo and Westville, and Prince Street on the R and W is four minutes from Dos Caminos. For the Canal Street end, including NoMo Kitchen, Grand Street Social and Soho Diner, use the Canal Street stations, which between them serve the A, C, E, 6, J, N, Q, R, W and Z.

The prices on this page are before tax and tip, so budget for the 8.875 percent NYC sales tax and an 18 to 20 percent tip. Emmett's limits its deal to the bar, and Dos Caminos keeps its late window to the bar and patio, so a dining-room table may not qualify. Glance at the last-checked date on each listing before you head out.

faq.a: Boqueria Soho adds Saturday and Sunday afternoons, and Grand Street Social runs its happy hour menu only on Saturday and Sunday. Milady's includes Sunday, and Soho Diner serves its late happy hour on Friday and Saturday nights.
faq.q: Which SoHo bars have happy hour on weekends?

faq.a: Yes. Soho Diner serves happy hour food late on Friday and Saturday nights, and Dos Caminos lists a late-evening weekday window at its bar and patio. Lazy Point on Spring Street adds a Friday evening window to its Wednesday and Thursday deal.
faq.q: Is there a late-night happy hour in SoHo?

faq.a: Dos Caminos has empanadas, guacamole and taquitos, Emmett's has mozzarella sticks and handcut fries, Soho Diner has wings and a smash burger, and NoMo Kitchen discounts bites along with house drinks.
faq.q: Which SoHo happy hours include food?

intro:
Myrtle Avenue is home to The Emerson, a bar at 561 Myrtle Ave that carries a sports tag. From Classon Avenue on the G line it is a 7-minute walk, so expect a bit of a stroll from the station.

The Emerson happy hour covers draft beer at a discount and well drinks. It runs Tuesday through Friday, from late afternoon into the early evening. Nothing else about the deal is published, and there is no reservation link, so plan to walk in.

You can find The Great Georgiana at 248 DeKalb Avenue in Fort Greene, a bar tagged for wine and a food deal. Clinton-Washington Avenues, on the G line, is 3 minutes away on foot.

The Great Georgiana happy hour lists Pacifico draft, house wines, a shot and frozen specials, plus seasoned fries and chicken bites for food. It runs on weekdays from late afternoon into the early evening. No reservation link is published, so this is a walk-in setup.

Rockwell Place in Fort Greene holds The Rockwell Place, a bar at 31 Rockwell Place tagged for cocktails. Nevins Street, where the 2, 3, 4 and 5 trains stop, is a 2-minute walk.

The Rockwell Place happy hour is listed Tuesday through Friday in the early evening. The bar publishes the times but not the deal, so the drinks included are not named here. There is no booking link, which suggests simply showing up, and the live page has the current hours.

Saar Indian Restaurant sits on West 51st Street in Times Square and counts as an Indian restaurant. For the subway, take the C and E trains to 50th Street, then walk about one minute.

The Saar Indian Restaurant happy hour applies on weekdays, in the afternoon. The restaurant has not published what the deal includes, only when it runs. A booking link is provided if you want to reserve ahead.

Gowanus is the low-lying stretch of Brooklyn around the Gowanus Canal, with Park Slope uphill to the east and Carroll Gardens and Cobble Hill to the west. Our picks for happy hour in Gowanus sit between the canal and Fourth Avenue. Evalyn's Tap House is on Butler Street at the northern end, Gowanus Gardens is next to the Union Street stop on the R, and Table 87 Coal Oven Pizza is on Third Avenue, a couple of minutes from the Fourth Avenue–9th Street station.

Two pubs and a pizza restaurant make up the core of the list, and all three run their deals on weekdays. Gowanus Gardens takes money off its house cocktails, including the non-alcoholic ones, plus every tap, bottle and can. Evalyn's pairs Bavarian pretzels with craft draft beer, and Table 87 covers house wine, house beer and a short cocktail list. Gowanus Gardens opens earliest, in mid-afternoon, which makes it the easy first stop if you finish work early.

picks.why: Gowanus Gardens is a pub a one-minute walk from Union Street on the R. Its weekday happy hour starts in mid-afternoon and takes money off the house cocktail menu, non-alcoholic cocktails included, plus all taps, bottles and cans. The listed hours run late every night, so you can stay on after the deal ends.

Evalyn's Tap House is a pub at 236 Butler Street, about six minutes from Union Street on the R. Its happy hour pairs Bavarian pretzels with craft draft beers from late afternoon. Our listing shows it every day, with an all-day Monday deal on beers, well drinks and cocktails.

Table 87 Coal Oven Pizza is a pizza restaurant at 473 Third Avenue, two minutes from the Fourth Avenue–9th Street station on the F, G and R. Weekday happy hour covers house wines, house beer and cocktails such as a negroni, a basil gimlet and a spicy hibiscus mezcalita. Tables can be booked on Resy.

sections.body: The R is the main line. Union Street puts you a minute from Gowanus Gardens and about six minutes from Evalyn's Tap House on Butler Street. Farther south, the Fourth Avenue–9th Street station links the F and G with the R, and Table 87 is two minutes from it. All three are on the east side of the canal, so no bridge crossing is needed.

Sales tax of 8.875 percent comes on top of New York menu prices, and so does a tip, usually 18 to 20 percent. Some bars keep the deal to the bar area, so ask first. Every listing shows the date we last confirmed it, which is worth a look given that Evalyn's days already differ between sources.

faq.a: Evalyn's Tap House includes Bavarian pretzels in its deal. Table 87 Coal Oven Pizza is a pizza restaurant, though its listed happy hour covers drinks.
faq.q: Which Gowanus happy hours include food?

faq.a: Gowanus Gardens and Table 87 Coal Oven Pizza run Monday through Friday. Evalyn's Tap House runs every day, with an all-day deal on Monday.
faq.q: What days do Gowanus bars run happy hour?

faq.a: Gowanus Gardens, which begins in mid-afternoon on weekdays. Evalyn's Tap House and Table 87 start later in the afternoon.
faq.q: Which Gowanus bar starts happy hour earliest?

faq.a: Union Street on the R for Gowanus Gardens and Evalyn's Tap House, and Fourth Avenue–9th Street on the F, G and R for Table 87 Coal Oven Pizza.
faq.q: What subway stops are closest to Gowanus happy hours?

intro:
The West Village is the western corner of Greenwich Village, between Seventh Avenue South and the Hudson River, running up to 14th Street, where it meets the Meatpacking District. Our list follows three lines through it: Hudson Street in the blocks south of Gansevoort Street, Greenwich Avenue and the side streets around Bank and Perry, and the Meatpacking blocks on Ninth Avenue, Little West 12th Street and Washington Street. The 8th Avenue station at 14th Street, served by the A, C, E and L, is the nearest stop for the largest share, and the 1 at Christopher Street–Stonewall covers the southern streets.

West Village happy hour skews toward restaurants and cocktail bars, and the fine print matters: Osteria Nonnino and Jack & Charlie's No. 118 run every day but only at the bar and outdoors, while Rockbar on Christopher Street keeps it simple with two-for-one beer and liquor. Rory's Rooftop takes half off drinks and appetizers on weekdays, and oysters show up at Jack & Charlie's. Many windows close in the early evening, so aim to arrive soon after work.

picks.why: Jack & Charlie's No. 118 is a New American bar and restaurant at 118 Greenwich Avenue with a happy hour every day of the week, served at the bar and on the patio only. Oysters by the piece and a happy hour Caesar salad are on its sunset menu. The 8th Avenue station on the A, C, E and L is two minutes away, and Resy handles bookings.

Rockbar NYC at 185 Christopher Street runs a two-for-one happy hour on beer, well liquor and call liquor, Monday through Friday from early evening. Its listed hours run late, especially on Friday and Saturday, so you can stay on after the deal ends. It is about seven minutes on foot from Christopher Street–Stonewall on the 1, toward the river end of the street.

Osteria Nonnino on Hudson Street pours red and white wine by the glass or carafe, beer and well cocktails at happy hour prices every day, with truffle fries and bruschetta on the food side. The deal applies at the bar and outdoor area only, so skip the dining room. The A, C, E and L at 8th Avenue are three minutes away; book on OpenTable.

Rory's Rooftop on West 14th Street takes half off drinks and appetizers on weekdays in the late afternoon, and it is the only rooftop on our West Village list. The bar's own pitch mentions a putter, so golf is part of the draw. It is six minutes from the 8th Avenue A, C, E and L station.

Hudson Hound at 575 Hudson Street runs a Tuesday to Friday happy hour with draught beer, a Malfy Rosa lemonade, Aperol spritz, Teremana margarita and sangria at set prices, plus wine by the glass or bottle and bar food at a discount. The window is short, in the late afternoon. Christopher Street–Stonewall is five minutes away, and our listing shows no booking link.

Wogies on Greenwich Avenue is a restaurant with one of the longer weekday windows here, from mid-afternoon into the evening. All drafts, all wines and select cocktails, including the Wogies spritz, an espresso martini and a Krazy margarita, are discounted. A service fee is added to checks, so factor that in. Christopher Street–Stonewall on the 1 is three minutes away.

sections.body: The 8th Avenue station at 14th Street, served by the A, C, E and L, is the nearest stop for more bars on our list than any other, covering Hudson Street above Bank Street, the western end of Greenwich Avenue and the Meatpacking blocks. The 1 stops at Christopher Street–Stonewall, closest to Hudson Hound, Wogies, The Mary Lane and Rockbar near the river. Bars around Seventh Avenue and Bank Street are also easy from 14th Street on the 1, 2, 3, F, M and L. West Village streets bend off the grid, so trust the walking times on each listing over a quick look at the map.

Menu prices leave out the 8.875 percent New York sales tax, and plan on an 18 to 20 percent tip as well. Bar-only and patio-only rules are common in the West Village: Osteria Nonnino, Jack & Charlie's No. 118, Mēdüzā Mediterrania and Bill's Bar & Burger all set limits. Look at the last-checked date on each listing to see how recently we confirmed the deal.

faq.a: Jack & Charlie's No. 118 on Greenwich Avenue and Osteria Nonnino on Hudson Street run happy hour seven days a week, both limited to the bar and outdoor seating. Left Bank on Perry Street lists a weekend window alongside its weekday one, and Coffee + Cocktails on Ninth Avenue includes Sunday.
faq.q: Which West Village bars have happy hour every day?

faq.a: Rockbar NYC on Christopher Street pours two-for-one beer, well and call liquor on weekdays, and Rory's Rooftop on West 14th Street takes half off drinks and appetizers Monday through Friday. Bill's Bar & Burger on Ninth Avenue takes half off its snack appetizers at the bar.
faq.q: Is there a two-for-one or half-price happy hour in the West Village?

faq.a: Jack & Charlie's No. 118 serves oysters and a Caesar salad, Osteria Nonnino has truffle fries and bruschetta, and Rory's Rooftop takes half off appetizers. Mēdüzā Mediterrania pairs its cocktails with small bites Monday through Thursday, Coffee + Cocktails offers bar snacks, and Left Bank has an appetizer special.
faq.q: Which West Village happy hours include food?

faq.a: The 8th Avenue station at 14th Street, on the A, C, E and L, is nearest to the most bars on our list, including Jack & Charlie's No. 118, Osteria Nonnino and Rory's Rooftop. Christopher Street–Stonewall on the 1 serves Hudson Hound, Wogies and Rockbar NYC.
faq.q: What subway stop is closest to West Village happy hours?

intro:
Fushimi Times Square works as a bar at 311 West 43rd Street in Times Square. The closest subway stop is 42nd Street–Port Authority Bus Terminal (the 1, 2, 3, 7, A, C, E, N, Q, R, S and W trains), a two-minute walk away.

Fushimi Times Square happy hour runs every day, from late afternoon into the early evening. The bar publishes the times but not the deal. Reservations go through the booking link on this page.

Gui Steakhouse, a restaurant on 8th Avenue in Times Square, has its happy hour details below. For the subway, take the C and E trains to 50th Street, then walk about three minutes.

Only the times are published here, not the specifics of the deal. The Gui Steakhouse happy hour runs every day, from the afternoon into the early evening. A booking link is provided if you want to reserve ahead.

Gyu-Kaku sits on West 44th Street in Times Square and counts as a restaurant. 42nd Street–Port Authority Bus Terminal is the nearest station, served by the 1, 2, 3, 7, A, C, E, N, Q, R, S and W trains and a two-minute walk from the door.

The Gyu-Kaku happy hour runs from Sunday through Thursday, from late morning into the early evening. The restaurant has not published what the deal includes, only when it runs. You can reserve through the booking link provided here.

Hard Rock Cafe can be found on Broadway in Times Square. It is a restaurant. The closest subway stop is Times Square (the 1, 2, 3, 7, A, C, E, N, Q, R, S and W trains), a two-minute walk away.

The listing names domestic drafts, import drafts and cocktails. Hard Rock Cafe happy hour is the part to plan around, since it runs on weekdays, from late afternoon into the early evening. Reservations go through the booking link on this page.

Michael's New York serves the Times Square area as a bar on West 55th Street. The closest subway stop is 5th Avenue–53rd Street (the E and F trains), a two-minute walk away.

The bar has not published what the deal includes, only when it runs. Michael's New York happy hour runs on weekdays, from late afternoon into the early evening. Reservations go through the booking link on this page.

Russian Samovar Restaurant and Piano Bar, a restaurant on West 52nd Street in Times Square, has its happy hour details below. The closest subway stop is 50th Street (the C and E trains), a two-minute walk away.

The deal is posted as flavored vodka mixed drinks, domestic beer and house wine. The Russian Samovar Restaurant and Piano Bar happy hour applies on weekdays, from late afternoon into the early evening. Reservations go through the booking link on this page.

Havana Central is listed as a Cuban restaurant at 151 West 46th Street in Times Square. For the subway, take the N, R and W trains to 49th Street, then walk about two minutes.

Havana Central happy hour runs on weekdays, from the afternoon into the early evening. Listed items include tropical cocktails, espresso martinis and wines.

Around Times Square, Mozzarella & Vino operates as an Italian restaurant. For the subway, take the E and F trains to 5th Avenue–53rd Street, then walk about two minutes.

Mozzarella & Vino happy hour runs every day, from late afternoon into the early evening. The listing names the Hugo Martini Negroni. The listing is for Times Square in Manhattan.

Redeye Grill works as a brasserie and American restaurant at 890 7th Avenue in Times Square. 57th Street–7th Avenue is the nearest station, served by the N, Q, R and W trains and a one-minute walk from the door.

Redeye Grill happy hour applies from Tuesday through Friday, from late afternoon into the early evening. Listed items include the Porn Star Martini.

Starchild Rooftop Bar & Lounge is listed as a bar at 305 West 48th Street in Times Square. The closest subway stop is 50th Street (the C and E trains), a two-minute walk away.

Starchild Rooftop Bar & Lounge happy hour applies from Tuesday through Thursday, from late afternoon into the early evening. The bar publishes the times but not the deal. Reservations go through the booking link on this page. Its listing carries a rooftop tag.

Utsav NYC works as a bar with Indian, Indo-Chinese and Bengali cuisine at 1185 6th Avenue in Times Square. For the subway, take the B, D, F and M trains to 47th–50th Streets–Rockefeller Center, then walk about one minute.

Utsav NYC happy hour comes every day, from late afternoon into the early evening. The bar publishes the times but not the deal. The website is linked from this page.

Whiskey Trader, a pub on West 55th Street in Times Square, has its happy hour details below. 57th Street is the nearest station, served by the M train and a two-minute walk from the door.

The deal is posted as wine, shots and cocktails. The Whiskey Trader happy hour comes every day, from late morning into the early evening. The website is linked from this page.

Union Square is the crossroads where Broadway meets 14th Street, and our list fans out from it in every direction rather than sitting on the square itself. East along 14th Street at Third Avenue, Linen Hall and The Penny Farthing are next-door neighbors by the 3rd Avenue L. South and west, The Grey Dog on University Place, Josie Woods Pub and White Oak Tavern on Waverly Place, and Da Andrea on West 13th Street lean toward Greenwich Village, while Kyma is a few blocks north on West 18th Street.

The Union Square station is a major hub, with the 4, 5, 6, L, N, Q, R and W, so this is an easy place to meet people coming from anywhere. The happy hours here are generous with time: White Oak Tavern lists Thursday as all day, and The Grey Dog runs daily. A Union Square happy hour also tends to come with food, from Greek bites at Kyma to Italian boards at Da Andrea.

picks.why: The Grey Dog is an American restaurant at 90 University Place, three minutes from the Union Square hub, and its happy hour runs every day, weekends included. The list covers the house Michigan lager, red, white and rosé house wine, a Tommy's margarita, a Glow Up Mule, a Venetian spritz and bar bites such as Sticky Nuggs. Reservations are available.

The Penny Farthing is a sports pub at 103 Third Avenue, a minute from the 3rd Avenue L, with a weekday happy hour on mixed well drinks, draft beers, bottles and wine. Its menu also lists day-specific specials, such as burgers on Monday, half-price wine bottles on Tuesday nights and espresso martinis on Wednesday. It takes reservations.

Linen Hall, an American restaurant at 101 Third Avenue next to The Penny Farthing, runs one of the longer weekday happy hours on this page, from late afternoon well into the evening. Each weekday also has a theme, per its menu: half-price wine bottles Monday, margaritas Tuesday, espresso martinis Wednesday and Aperol spritzes Thursday. The 3rd Avenue L is one minute away.

Kyma is a Greek and Mediterranean seafood restaurant at 15 West 18th Street with happy hour Tuesday through Friday from mid-afternoon. House wines like rosé, sauvignon blanc and pinot noir, prosecco, beers including Mythos and Lagunitas IPA, and bites such as spanakopita and calamari are on the list. Book ahead; the 14th Street station is four minutes away.

Da Andrea is an Italian restaurant on West 13th Street, two minutes from the 6th Avenue station, with a weekday happy hour in the late afternoon. The happy hour menu includes a board of two daily cheeses and two cold cuts with honey and walnuts, a fritto misto of calamari, shrimp and zucchini, and truffle roasted potatoes. Reservations are available.

White Oak Tavern is a gastropub at 21 Waverly Place, two minutes from 8th Street-NYU on the R and W. Its happy hour starts at lunchtime on Monday, Tuesday, Wednesday and Friday, and the bar lists Thursday as all day. Cocktails include a rosé sangria with elderflower and peach and a jalapeño Daisy Picante. Reservations are available.

Josie Woods Pub at 11 Waverly Place runs its happy hour Monday through Friday, from mid-afternoon into the early evening. The list includes buffalo wings. It is two minutes from the 8th Street-NYU R and W station.

sections.body: Union Square station connects the 4, 5, 6, L, N, Q, R and W and sits three minutes from The Grey Dog. The L's 3rd Avenue stop is a minute from Linen Hall and The Penny Farthing, and 8th Street-NYU on the R and W is two minutes from Josie Woods Pub and White Oak Tavern. For Da Andrea and Kyma on the west side, use the 14th Street and 6th Avenue stations for the 1, 2, 3, F, L and M.

Plan on 8.875 percent sales tax plus an 18 to 20 percent tip on top of menu prices. The day-specific specials at Linen Hall and The Penny Farthing change through the week, so check which day you are going. Each listing carries a last-checked date; confirm with the bar if it looks old.

faq.a: The Grey Dog on University Place runs happy hour every day, Saturday and Sunday included.
faq.q: Which bars near Union Square have happy hour on weekends?

faq.a: Yes. White Oak Tavern runs its happy hour all day on Thursday.
faq.q: Is there a late happy hour near Union Square?

faq.a: Kyma has spanakopita and calamari, Da Andrea has a cheese and cold cut board and fritto misto, The Grey Dog has bar bites, and Josie Woods Pub has buffalo wings.
faq.q: Where can I get happy hour food near Union Square?

faq.a: Linen Hall rotates half-price wine bottles, margaritas, espresso martinis and Aperol spritzes through the week, and The Penny Farthing runs its own daily specials, from burgers on Monday to espresso martinis on Wednesday.
faq.q: Which Union Square bars have day-specific drink deals?

intro:
Amiya can be found on Hudson Street in Tribeca. It is a bar.

Times are posted, but the bar does not publish the deal itself. Amiya happy hour is the part to plan around, since it comes on weekdays, from late afternoon into the early evening. The website is linked from this page. The listing is for Tribeca in Manhattan. Live prices and hours are shown on the page itself.

Artesano is listed as a bar with Mexican and Latin cuisine at 90 Chambers Street in Tribeca. Chambers Street is the nearest station, served by the 2, 3, A, C, E, R and W trains and a one-minute walk from the door.

Artesano happy hour comes on weekdays, in the afternoon. The bar publishes the times but not the deal. You can reserve through the booking link provided here.

Bar 135 happy hour comes on weekdays, from the afternoon into the early evening. Only the times are published here, not the specifics of the deal.

The bar is at 135 Reade Street in Tribeca. The closest subway stop is Chambers Street (the 1, 2 and 3 trains), a one-minute walk away. The website is linked from this page. Check the page for live hours and prices before you go.

Benares serves the Tribeca area as a restaurant. For the subway, take the 2, 3, A, C, E, R and W trains to Park Place, then walk about one minute.

Deals named for it: beer, wines and a house cocktail. Benares happy hour comes every day, from the afternoon into the early evening. A booking link is provided if you want to reserve ahead.

Sir Henry’s can be found on 8th Avenue in Times Square. It is a cocktail bar. 50th Street is the nearest station, served by the C and E trains and a two-minute walk from the door.

The listing names sourdough sausage roll bites. Sir Henry’s happy hour is the part to plan around, since it applies on Saturday and Sunday, ending in the afternoon.

Tanner Smith's happy hour applies every day, starting late in the evening. The deal is posted as a Negroni, an Old Fashioned, an Aperol Spritz, Pinot Noir, Founders Solid Gold and Fiddlehead IPA.

The pub is at 204 West 55th Street in Times Square. For the subway, take the N, Q, R and W trains to 57th Street–7th Avenue, then walk about one minute. Its listing carries a late-night tag.

The Alderman serves the Times Square area as a bar with tavern-inspired fare on West 48th Street. 49th Street is the nearest station, served by the N, R and W trains and a one-minute walk from the door.

The bar has not published what the deal includes, only when it runs. The Alderman happy hour applies every day, from early morning until late morning.

At 900 7th Avenue in Times Square, Trattoria Dell'Arte operates as an Italian restaurant. The closest subway stop is 57th Street–7th Avenue (the N, Q, R and W trains), a one-minute walk away.

Trattoria Dell'Arte happy hour applies on weekdays, from the afternoon into the early evening. Times are posted, but the restaurant does not publish the deal itself.

Koreatown is centered on West 32nd Street between Fifth Avenue and Broadway, a block from Herald Square and Macy's, and our list radiates out from there. Two karaoke bars sit right on 32nd Street, Irish pubs and bar-restaurants fill West 33rd to 36th Streets around Herald Square, and a few more line Seventh Avenue and West 35th Street near Penn Station. The page also reaches south to West 27th and 28th Streets and Broadway, an area most people call NoMad, near the 28th Street stop on the R and W.

Koreatown happy hour comes with a twist: both karaoke bars on 32nd Street discount early in the week, and Maru takes half off private rooms during its window. Around Herald Square the deals are classic after-work fare, with drafts, well drinks and house wine at set prices, plus oysters at Legasea. Most windows are weekday only, though Juniper, Muses 35 and Seeyamañana run every day, and Glass Ceiling Rooftop runs Tuesday through Saturday. Waiting on a train at Penn Station? The bars on West 35th Street and Seventh Avenue are two minutes away.

picks.why: Maru Karaoke Lounge at 11 West 32nd Street runs its happy hour Sunday through Wednesday in the evening, and the headline is half off private karaoke rooms. Domestic beer, shots such as Jameson or Fireball, well drinks and a cocktail are discounted at the same time. The 34th Street–Herald Square station is three minutes away, with eight lines to choose from.

Chorus Karaoke, a few doors down at 25 West 32nd Street, takes half off its specials before early evening, Sunday through Thursday. The bar's own rules set a one-drink minimum per person later on weeknights and higher minimums on Friday and Saturday nights, so arriving during the deal saves more than the discount alone. Walk three minutes from Herald Square.

Jack Demsey's is an Irish pub on West 33rd Street whose weekday happy hour starts in the late morning and lasts until early evening, one of the longest windows here. Drafts such as Bud, Bud Light, Michelob Ultra, Coors Light and its own Demsey's Ale are on it, along with house wines and well drinks. 34th Street–Herald Square is two minutes away.

Playwright Irish Pub on West 35th Street runs its happy hour Monday through Friday from late afternoon into the evening, a little later than most nearby. Select beers and select drinks come at set prices, and the pub adds food specials during the window. It is three minutes from the 34th Street–Herald Square station, and Resy takes bookings.

Legasea Bar & Grill at 485 Seventh Avenue keeps its weekday happy hour at the bar only, with oysters, fries, beer, wine and martinis at set prices. The window opens mid-afternoon and runs into the early evening, and the bar notes that walk-ins are welcome. The 1, 2 and 3 at 34th Street–Penn Station are two minutes away.

Stella 34 Trattoria sits at 151 West 34th Street, a minute from Herald Square, and serves its weekday happy hour exclusively at the bar. Signature cocktails are the focus, and the restaurant's menu mentions a complimentary small margherita pizza with a qualifying purchase. Bookings go through OpenTable if you want a table for dinner afterward.

The Ragtrader Bo Peep NYC on West 36th Street is the food pick: its weekday happy hour starts at midday and includes onion soup arancini, spinach artichoke dip, fries and fried chicken sliders. That makes it a fit for a late lunch as much as an after-work drink. 34th Street–Herald Square is two minutes away, and Resy handles reservations.

sections.body: 34th Street–Herald Square is the anchor, with the B, D, F, M, N, Q, R and W, and it is the nearest station for the karaoke bars on 32nd Street and the pubs on West 33rd to 36th Streets. To the west, 34th Street–Penn Station serves the A, C and E on Eighth Avenue and the 1, 2 and 3 on Seventh Avenue, close to Juniper, Muses 35 and Legasea. The southern stretch is easiest from 28th Street on the R and W, a minute or two from Glass Ceiling Rooftop, Pergola and Seeyamañana.

Menu prices here leave out the 8.875 percent sales tax, and the standard tip runs 18 to 20 percent. Several deals in this area are limited to the bar, including Legasea, Stella 34 Trattoria and Muses 35, and the karaoke bars set drink minimums outside their happy hour. Our last-checked date on each bar's page shows how recent the details are, so look before you go.

faq.a: Yes. Maru Karaoke Lounge on West 32nd Street takes half off private karaoke rooms and discounts beer, shots and well drinks Sunday through Wednesday evenings. Chorus Karaoke on the same block halves its specials before early evening Sunday through Thursday, and Muses 35 Bar & Karaoke on West 35th Street runs a bar-only happy hour every day.
faq.q: Do Koreatown karaoke bars have happy hour?

faq.a: Legasea Bar & Grill serves oysters and fries at the bar on weekdays, The Ragtrader Bo Peep NYC has arancini, dip and chicken sliders, and Pergola on West 28th Street lists goat cheese poppers, hummus, lamb sliders and wings. Stella 34 Trattoria adds a small margherita pizza with your first signature cocktail.
faq.q: Where can I get food with happy hour in Koreatown?

faq.a: Glass Ceiling Rooftop on Broadway near 29th Street adds a late-night happy hour to its early evening one, and Seeyamañana on West 27th Street lists late-night bites Thursday through Saturday.
faq.q: Is there late-night happy hour in Koreatown?

faq.a: Juniper, Muses 35 and Seeyamañana run every day, and Glass Ceiling Rooftop runs Tuesday through Saturday. Hakata TonTon includes Sunday, and both karaoke bars on 32nd Street start their happy hour week on Sunday.
faq.q: Which Koreatown bars have happy hour on weekends?

intro: Frozen drinks, pitchers of sangria and martinis are what the Blend on the Water happy hour offers, weekdays only, over a window that stretches through the day into the early evening. The restaurant is at 4540 Center Boulevard in Long Island City, Queens, nine minutes on foot from the Vernon Boulevard-Jackson Avenue station on the 7 line. Reservations go through an OpenTable link on the listing.

Tuesday through Friday, Jackson's Eatery | Bar lists a happy hour at 1037 Jackson Ave in Long Island City, Queens. The Jackson's Eatery happy hour comes as a schedule only, since no deal is published, though tags on the listing mention cocktails and wine. The Vernon Boulevard-Jackson Avenue station, on the 7 line, is one minute away on foot. No booking link is provided.

Ramen is in the name at Nagaiki Ramen METTRA, listed as a bar at 28-17 Jackson Ave in Long Island City, Queens. The Nagaiki Ramen METTRA happy hour runs every day, with the times published and the deal left out, although a food-deal tag appears on the listing. The Queens Plaza station, served by the E, F and R trains, is two minutes away on foot. No booking link is listed.

Bandolero mezcal, sangria and wines are the named offers at the R40 happy hour, a short window on Wednesday and Thursday only.
