The bar is at 47-16 Vernon Blvd in Long Island City, Queens, three minutes on foot from the Vernon Boulevard-Jackson Avenue station on the 7 line. Reservations are available through an OpenTable link, and tags on the listing mention cocktails and wine.

Sunday through Friday, The Beast Next Door Cafe & Bar offers an amount off everything during its happy hour. The bar is at 42-51 27th Street in Long Island City, Queens, two minutes on foot from the Queensboro Plaza station and its 7, N and W trains. Tags on the listing cover cocktails, wine, weekends and a food deal. No booking link is provided.

Saturday and Sunday are the only days for the 169 Bar happy hour, a weekend window at 169 East Broadway on the Lower East Side. The bar publishes the times but not the deal, though tags on the listing mention cocktails and outdoor space. The East Broadway station, on the F line, is one minute away on foot. No booking link is provided.

From opening until the early evening, every day of the week, Bar Belly keeps a happy hour at 14B Orchard Street on the Lower East Side. This restaurant publishes the times but not the deal, so the Bar Belly happy hour is a schedule with no named items. The East Broadway station, on the F line, is three minutes away on foot. Tags mention cocktails, wine and a food deal.

Monday through Thursday, Barrio Chino runs a happy hour at 253 Broome Street on the Lower East Side. This restaurant publishes the times but not the deal, so the Barrio Chino happy hour is a schedule with no named items. The Delancey Street station, served by the F, J, M and Z trains, is two minutes away on foot. A Resy link on the listing handles reservations, and tags mention cocktails and wine.

A shot and a draft beer are the named offers at the Boho Karaoke Orchard happy hour, which runs every day from opening until the evening. The karaoke bar is at 152 Orchard St on the Lower East Side, three minutes on foot from the Delancey Street station, where the F, J, M and Z trains stop. Tags on the listing mention cheap beer, cocktails and wine. No booking link is provided.

Cafe Skye LES keeps a happy hour Wednesday through Friday at 43 Clinton St on the Lower East Side. The bar publishes the times but not the deal, so the Cafe Skye LES happy hour is a schedule with no named items. The Essex Street station, served by the F, J, M and Z trains, is four minutes away on foot. Reservations are available through an OpenTable link on the listing.

Nachos are the one named offer at the Casa Colven happy hour, which runs on weekdays. The bar is at 79 Clinton St on the Lower East Side, two minutes on foot from the Essex Street station, where the F, J, M and Z trains stop. The listing carries cocktails and food-deal tags, and reservations go through an OpenTable link.

American Brass, a French-style brasserie and American restaurant at 2-01 50th Avenue in Long Island City, Queens, lists several happy hour windows. One covers Monday through Thursday, another covers Friday and Saturday and runs later, and a Sunday window starts earlier. The American Brass happy hour has no published deal, only the schedule. The Vernon Boulevard-Jackson Avenue station, on the 7 line, is five minutes away on foot.

La Caverna is a restaurant on Rivington Street in the Lower East Side. Essex Street station, served by the F, J, M and Z, is just 2 minutes away on foot.

The La Caverna happy hour runs Tuesday through Friday and on Sunday, from late afternoon into the evening, with the longest window on Taco Tuesday. The listed deals cover beer, wine, well drinks and a margarita tower, and on Tuesday tacos, margaritas, tequila shots and beers. The page does not list a reservation link, so plan to walk in.

Gugu Room, a bar at 143 Orchard St on the Lower East Side, lists a happy hour every day of the week. The Gugu Room happy hour is published by its times only, with no deal named. The Delancey Street station, served by the F, J, M and Z trains, is three minutes away on foot. A Resy link on the listing handles reservations, and the page carries a weekend tag.

The Mayfly offers a happy hour on weekdays. This bar is at 269 East Houston Street in the Lower East Side, about 5 minutes on foot from Essex Street station, where the F, J, M and Z stop.

The Mayfly happy hour runs in the early evening, except on Tuesday, when it lasts until close, and the bar publishes the times but not the deal. Nothing on the page names specific drinks or food, and there is no reservation link.

Delancey Street station, with the F, J, M and Z, is a 3-minute walk from 139 Orchard Street, where Isla & Co. Lower East Side operates as a bar in the Lower East Side.

The Isla & Co. Lower East Side happy hour runs every day of the week and lists deals on cocktails, wines and beers. That makes it one of the more flexible schedules around, since no weekday or weekend is left out. Reservations can be made through the Resy link on the page.

Japanese food is the focus at Izakaya Juraku, a restaurant on Ludlow Street in the Lower East Side whose listed cuisines are izakaya and ramen. From 2nd Avenue station on the F it is a 4-minute walk.

Happy hour here is a food-led affair. The Izakaya Juraku happy hour lists house fries and spicy edamame, and it runs Tuesday through Friday only, so Monday and the weekend are off the table. A Resy link is available for reservations.

Prospect Heights is the wedge of Brooklyn bounded by Flatbush Avenue, Atlantic Avenue, Eastern Parkway and Washington Avenue, with Vanderbilt Avenue running through the middle. Our list for the area is drawn wider than those lines. Alta Calidad on Vanderbilt, Finn's Corner on Washington and 333 Lounge on Flatbush sit in or on the edge of the neighborhood, while the biggest cluster lines Fulton Street just north of Atlantic, from Bar Francis at number 810 to Bati Ethiopian Kitchen at 1057. Another group runs along Franklin Avenue toward Crown Heights.

The mix is food-forward, with Mexican, Ethiopian and pizza restaurants well represented, plus oysters at Bar Francis and Mayfield and cheap pints at Famous Last Words. Almost everything happens on weekdays, though Belli Osteria, Mayfield and Arden run their Prospect Heights happy hour every day. Tip: the C at Clinton-Washington Avenues is a one- to five-minute walk from most of the Fulton Street bars, so it is the easiest base for hopping between several in one evening.

picks.why: Alta Calidad is a Mexican restaurant at 552 Vanderbilt Avenue whose happy hour, listed Monday through Thursday, is mostly botanas: salsas with tortilla chips, spinach queso fundido with chile piquín, and nachos with beans, crema and pico de gallo. It takes reservations, and the Clinton-Washington Avenues C stop is five minutes away.

Finn's Corner is a pub at 660 Washington Avenue with a weekday happy hour that runs until the early evening. Well drinks, house wine and money off all beer, hard seltzer and cider are on the deal, and the menu also features frozen drinks like piña coladas and mango jalapeño margaritas. The Clinton-Washington Avenues C is about seven minutes on foot.

333 Lounge is a bar on Flatbush Avenue a one-minute walk from the 7th Avenue B and Q station. Its happy hour specials run Tuesday through Friday into the evening, and the lounge's own page adds a shorter Saturday window, one of the few in the area. We have no item list for it yet, so confirm the specials with the bartender.

Famous Last Words is a bar at 925 Fulton Street, one minute from the Clinton-Washington Avenues C, with a weekday happy hour built around beer: pints, IPAs including hazy and session styles, and a beer-and-shot pairing, plus well drinks and house wine. It runs Monday to Friday through the late afternoon, and the bar takes reservations.

Belli Osteria, at 860 Fulton Street, runs one of the few daily happy hours on this list, Saturday and Sunday included. Cocktails, beer, wine and bar bites are all part of the deal, in a short early-evening window. It sits a minute from the Clinton-Washington Avenues C station and takes reservations, which helps on weekends.

Bar Francis is a cocktail and wine bar at 810 Fulton Street whose happy hour runs Wednesday through Friday in the late afternoon. Each month it features two house cocktails alongside a selection of wine and beer, oysters and bar snacks. The Clinton-Washington Avenues C is three minutes away, and you can book ahead.

sections.body: The C at Clinton-Washington Avenues covers the Fulton Street run, from Bar Francis and Belli Osteria to Emily, Famous Last Words and Xochitl Taqueria, and it is also the closest stop for Alta Calidad and Finn's Corner. The B and Q at 7th Avenue are a minute from 333 Lounge. For the Franklin Avenue group, the shuttle's Park Place stop serves Mayfield and Ras, and Franklin Avenue-Medgar Evers College on the 2, 3, 4 and 5 is a minute from Arden.

Listed prices do not include the 8.875 percent NYC sales tax or the customary 18 to 20 percent tip, so expect to pay more than the menu says. Several windows here are short, Belli Osteria's and Emily's among them, so arrive early. Each listing shows its last-checked date, and older ones are worth a quick call.

faq.a: Bar Francis on Fulton Street serves oysters Wednesday through Friday, and Mayfield and Arden on Franklin Avenue include oysters at their daily happy hours.
faq.q: Where can I get happy hour oysters near Prospect Heights?

faq.a: Belli Osteria on Fulton Street, plus Mayfield and Arden on Franklin Avenue, run happy hour seven days a week.
faq.q: Which bars on the Prospect Heights list have happy hour every day?

faq.a: Bati Ethiopian Kitchen on Fulton Street lists two-for-one drinks on Wednesday and Thursday afternoons.
faq.q: Is there a two-for-one happy hour in Prospect Heights?

faq.a: Alta Calidad on Vanderbilt Avenue is about five minutes from the Clinton-Washington Avenues C station.
faq.q: What is the closest subway to the Vanderbilt Avenue happy hours?

intro:
Pull up to Mary's at 146 Orchard Street and you are in a pub on the Lower East Side. Delancey Street station is a 3-minute walk, with the F, J, M and Z all serving it.

The Mary's happy hour covers wine and cocktails. It runs Sunday through Thursday, which is a little different from the usual weekday-only pattern, because Sunday is included and Friday and Saturday are not. No reservation link is listed.

Reach The Commissary by heading to 7 Ludlow Street, where this bar sits in Chinatown. East Broadway station on the F is a 2-minute walk.

The Commissary happy hour is a short window offered Wednesday through Sunday, so it covers the weekend. The bar publishes the times but not the deal, which means no specific drinks or food are listed. A reservation link is available on the page.

You can reach Sally Can Wait at 252 Broome Street in the Lower East Side, about 2 minutes on foot from Delancey Street station (F, J, M, Z). It is listed as a bar.

The Sally Can Wait happy hour runs on weekdays and ends in the early evening, starting from opening. Listed deals are drafts, wines, well drinks and frozen cocktails, which covers most of what people order at a bar. There is no reservation link on file.

Wine and oysters are the two names that stand out on the Ten Bells deal list. This bar sits at 247 Broome Street in the Lower East Side, a 2-minute walk from Delancey Street station (F, J, M, Z).

The Ten Bells happy hour covers oysters and a carafe of wine, and it runs every day, starting when the doors open and finishing in the early evening. Tables can be reserved through the Resy link listed on the page.

At 90 Clinton Street in the Lower East Side, Yong Chuan serves Chinese food as a restaurant. Essex Street station is a 2-minute walk, with the F, J, M and Z all stopping there.

The Yong Chuan happy hour runs Tuesday through Friday in the early evening. The restaurant publishes the times but not the deal, so the specific items are not listed. You can book through the Resy link on the page.

In Midtown, Addictive NYC operates as a restaurant, and the nearest subway is 47th-50th Streets-Rockefeller Center, a 3-minute walk with the B, D, F and M. No street address is on file.

The Addictive NYC happy hour runs every day of the week and is an early-evening window. The restaurant publishes the times but not the deal, so the specific drinks or food are not listed. A reservation link to Resy is on the page.

Cocktails, drafts and two tacos are the items named in the Mad Tropical happy hour. It runs Tuesday through Sunday, weekends included, through the early evening.

Mad Tropical is a bar in Bushwick, Brooklyn; it is at 236 Troutman St, seven minutes on foot from Central Av station on the M. Beer, wine and food deals are among its tags, and a website is available.

At 320 W 36th St in Midtown, Burgerology Midtown operates as a bar, 2 minutes from 34th Street-Penn Station on the A, C and E.

The Burgerology Midtown happy hour is a weekday offer, and the deal list is long and food-forward: wine, draft beer, Burgerology sliders, short rib sliders, a turkey burger and buffalo chicken sliders. That makes it a pick for anyone who wants burgers alongside a drink. No reservation link is listed.

West 37th Street, number 59, is the address of Cafe China, a restaurant in Midtown. The closest subway is 34th Street-Herald Square, a 3-minute walk, with the B, D, F, M, N, Q, R and W.

Happy hour here is a daytime affair on weekdays, running from late morning into the afternoon. The Cafe China happy hour has no published deal, only the times. A Resy link covers reservations.

Right by Bryant Park, Croton Reservoir Tavern is a pub and American restaurant at 108 W 40th St in Midtown. The 42nd Street-Bryant Park station is only 1 minute on foot, serving the 7, B, D, F and M.

The Croton Reservoir Tavern happy hour runs Tuesday through Friday, from late afternoon into the evening; Monday is not part of it. The menu covers margaritas, classic cocktails such as an Old Fashioned and a Manhattan, sangria, an Aperol spritz, select wines, draft beer and well drinks. Tables can be booked through the OpenTable link.

Drafts are the headline at District Tap House, a bar at 246 West 38th Street in Midtown. Times Square-42nd Street is a 3-minute walk, served by the 1, 2, 3, 7, A, C, E, N, Q, R, S and W.

The District Tap House happy hour runs on weekdays in the late afternoon and early evening. Listed deals are cucumber infused vodka, drafts, orange bitters house wine and a Boroughs Tiny Juicy IPA. No reservation link is on file.

Troutman Street in Bushwick is home to Juke Bar, at number 400 and one minute from Jefferson Street station on the L.

The Juke Bar happy hour runs on weekdays from late afternoon into the early evening. The listing gives the days and hours but no drinks or prices, so the bar publishes the times but not the deal. A website is listed for current details.

Keybar runs its happy hour every day, weekends included, and the window sits in the early evening. The Keybar happy hour has no offers listed, only the schedule, so nothing about the drinks is published.

The bar is at 143 Troutman Street in Bushwick, Brooklyn, a four minute walk from Central Avenue station on the M. A website is listed for current details.

Tacos get a place on the La Loncheria happy hour list alongside margaritas, spicy cucumber margaritas, house wine, red sangria and tequila, all at set prices. It is held every day, weekends included, from late afternoon into the early evening.

La Loncheria is a bar at 41 Wilson Avenue in Bushwick, Brooklyn, six minutes from Morgan Avenue station on the L.

DeKalb Avenue in Bed-Stuy, Brooklyn, is the address for Secret Pour, a bar at number 1114 that is one minute from Kosciuszko Street station on the J.

The Secret Pour happy hour is held every day, weekends included, from late afternoon through the early evening. Wine is listed among its tags, but the bar publishes the times and not the deal. A website is listed.

Ludlow Street in the Lower East Side holds Tre, a restaurant with 2nd Avenue station on the F a 3-minute walk away.

It runs two happy hour windows: Monday through Friday in the early evening, and a longer one on Saturday and Sunday from the afternoon, which makes weekends an option too. The Tre happy hour lists white wine, red wine, champagne and Aperol, so the focus is wine and spritz-style drinks. No reservation link is listed.

Perry Street is the address for Left Bank, a restaurant at number 117 in the West Village, five minutes from the Christopher Street and Stonewall station on the 1 train.

On weekdays there is a happy hour in the early evening, and a shorter one in the late afternoon on Saturday and Sunday. The Left Bank happy hour covers any two apps, a burger with a beer, pasta with a glass of wine, parmesan fries, draught beer, wine by the glass, and margaritas and martinis. A booking link is on the page.

Outdoor seating and a cocktail focus describe The Mary Lane, an American bar at 99 Bank Street in the West Village, six minutes from the Christopher Street and Stonewall station on the 1 train.

Tuesday through Friday is when the Mary Lane happy hour takes place, from the late afternoon into the early evening. Cappelletti spritz, ginger beer and tequila drinks are the items listed.

Mondays only: that is when the Talon Bar happy hour is held, from the afternoon into the early evening, with beer at a set price. Talon Bar is at 220 Wyckoff Avenue in Bushwick, Brooklyn, four minutes on foot from Myrtle–Wyckoff Avenues station, which has the L and M.

A cheap-beer tag is on the listing, and a website is provided.

Oysters are the named offer at The Ten Bells Brooklyn happy hour, held every day of the week, weekends included, and ending in the early evening. No start is listed.

The bar is at 65 Irving Avenue in Bushwick, Brooklyn, three minutes from Jefferson Street station on the L. Wine is among its tags, and reservations go through the booking link.

A PBR tall boy, a Miller High Life, wine and a well drink are the items named for The Little Whiskey happy hour. It runs all day on Monday, and Tuesday through Friday it ends in the early evening, with no start listed.

The Little Whiskey is a pub at 36 Wilson Avenue in Bushwick, Brooklyn, six minutes from Morgan Avenue station on the L. Cocktails and wine are among its tags, and a website is listed.

Tuesday through Sunday, Marco Polo Ristorante runs a happy hour from late afternoon into the early evening, so weekends are covered. The restaurant is at 345 Court Street in Carroll Gardens, Brooklyn, three minutes from Carroll Street station on the F and G.

The Marco Polo Ristorante happy hour lists no specific deals. Oysters appear among its tags, and a website is listed.

Beer and wine at set prices are the listed offers at PLANTED CAFE, which is categorized as a bar and carries vegan, plant-based, gluten-free and coffee labels. The PLANTED CAFE happy hour runs on weekdays in the late afternoon.

It is at 333 Smith Street in Carroll Gardens, Brooklyn, one minute from Carroll Street station on the F and G. A website is listed.

West 26th Street in Chelsea is the address for Bar Avant Apres Bar, at number 601, eight minutes on foot from 34th Street–Hudson Yards station on the 7.

The Bar Avant Apres Bar happy hour is held every day, weekends included, in the early evening. No offers are listed, so the bar publishes the times but not the deal. Cocktails are among its tags, and a website is listed.

Mexi serves its happy hour from Tuesday through Sunday. The bar is at 57 Stone St in the Financial District, Manhattan, three minutes on foot from Broad Street station and the J and Z trains.

No deals are listed, so the bar publishes the times but not the deal. Reservations go through Resy using the booking link. Check this page for live hours before you plan a visit.

Park Slope's High Dive is tagged as a dive bar, and the High Dive happy hour runs on weekdays from the afternoon into the evening. The listed offers are well drinks at a set price and a discount on everything else.

The closest subway stop is Union Street on the R, a 4-minute walk. The bar links its website from the page, so the full menu is one click away before you head out.

A restaurant tagged for wine, Krupa Grocery sits in Park Slope just a 1-minute walk from 15th Street–Prospect Park, served by the F and G trains. The Krupa Grocery happy hour is listed Monday through Thursday, running from late afternoon into the early evening.

The place publishes the times but not the deal, so check its website for what is poured. A booking link is available if you want to reserve a table.

Weekdays are when the LoFi happy hour runs, wrapping up in the evening, and the listed offer is a discount on every drink. No start time is given, so check the live hours shown on this page.

LoFi is a cocktail-tagged bar on 2nd Street in Park Slope. From Union Street on the R train it is about a 5-minute walk. The offer is described as applying to every drink.

The Jalopy Tavern happy hour runs Tuesday through Friday, and it brings a discount on draught beer from late afternoon into the early evening. Jalopy Tavern is a pub and bar at 317 Columbia Street in Carroll Gardens, Brooklyn.

The nearest station is Carroll Street on the F and G, a ten minute walk away. A website is listed.

OpenTable handles reservations for BLACKBARN Restaurant. The New American spot is at 19 East 26th Street in Midtown District, Manhattan, a three-minute walk from 28th Street station and the 6 train.

The BLACKBARN Restaurant happy hour runs on weekdays. The restaurant publishes the times but not the deal, so no drinks or food are named here. Check this page for live hours.

Select drafts, house wine and classic cocktails are what the Syndicated Bar Theater Kitchen happy hour covers, on weekdays in the early evening. The bar is at 40 Bogart Street in Williamsburg, Brooklyn, a two minute walk from Morgan Avenue station on the L.

A food-deal tag is also on the listing, and a website is available for current details.

In Park Slope, Luya is a restaurant with cocktails and wine among its tags, a 3-minute walk from Union Street on the R train. The Luya happy hour is listed on weekdays, starting in the late afternoon and ending in the early evening.

The venue publishes the times but not the deal itself, so the specific drinks and specials are not something this page can name. A booking link is on file if you prefer to reserve a table for the visit.

On 8th Avenue in Park Slope, Ottava serves as a restaurant tagged for cocktails and wine. The Ottava happy hour covers cocktails and prosecco, both sold at set prices, from Monday through Thursday in the early evening.

Getting there is simple: the 7th Avenue station on the F and G lines is a 3-minute walk away. The window covers the first four days of the work week.

Provini, a restaurant on 8th Avenue in Park Slope, is tagged for wine and cheap beer. The Provini happy hour is listed Monday through Thursday in the late afternoon and early evening, with wines and Peroni draft available at set prices.

The F and G trains stop at 7th Avenue, a 4-minute walk away. No booking link is on file, so for a table you would need to check the restaurant's own channels.

Look for Saint Eves on 12th Street in Park Slope, a bar about a 3-minute walk from the 7th Avenue stop on the F and G lines. The Saint Eves happy hour is listed Monday through Thursday, in the early evening.

The bar publishes the times but not the deal, so the specific drinks and prices are not available here. No booking link is on file, and the live hours on this page are worth confirming.

A Park Slope restaurant, Stella's has a 4-minute walk to 9th Street, where the F, G and R trains stop. The Stella's happy hour is listed for Wednesday, Thursday and Friday, running from the afternoon into the early evening.

The restaurant publishes the window but not the deal, so what the happy hour covers is not stated. No booking link is on file for the restaurant, so check the live hours on this page.

White Oak Tavern can be found on Waverly Place in Union Square. It is a gastropub. For the subway, take the R and W trains to 8th Street–New York University, then walk about two minutes.

The deal covers cocktails such as rose sangria and a Daisy Picante, a pint of Allagash with a well shot, house spirit and mixer, and select beers and wines. White Oak Tavern happy hour is the part to plan around, since it comes on Monday, Tuesday, Wednesday and Friday, from midday into the early evening, and all day on Thursday.

Listed under Gowanus, Sea Witch is a bar at 703 5th Ave, tagged for wine. The 25th Street station on the R line is 5 minutes away on foot.

The Sea Witch happy hour takes a discount off pints. It runs on weekdays and ends in the early evening, though the listing gives no start time. No other drinks or food are named, and there is no reservation link. For the current hours, look at the live schedule on this page.

Along 5th Avenue in Park Slope, Siren operates as a restaurant at number 687, tagged for oysters, weekends and late nights. From 25th Street on the R line it is a 5-minute walk.

The Siren happy hour has two windows. One runs Tuesday through Thursday, and a second runs Friday through Sunday, each in the late afternoon and early evening. The restaurant publishes the times but not the deal, so the food and drinks are not named. Reservations can be made through OpenTable.

Third Avenue in Gramercy has Barfly, a sports bar at number 244, tagged for late nights, cheap beer and cocktails. The 23rd Street-Baruch College station, on the 6 line, is a 5-minute walk.

Late at night is when the Barfly happy hour runs, from Sunday through Thursday, and it stretches into the early morning. Listed items include beer, Altos tequila, Coors Light draft, Jameson and Screwball shots and a salted-rim spicy margarita. No reservation link is published for this one.

Pasta Louise Cafe serves Italian food as a restaurant on 8th Avenue in Park Slope, with a 2-minute walk to the 7th Avenue stop on the F and G lines. Its happy hour centers on a spritz at a set price and runs Tuesday through Friday in the afternoon.

The window sits in the afternoon, so the Pasta Louise Cafe happy hour suits an early visit.

Italian cooking and cocktails define Pasta Louise, a Park Slope restaurant on 8th Avenue. Subway riders can take the F or G to 7th Avenue and walk about 3 minutes.

The Pasta Louise happy hour offers a spritz at a set price, Tuesday through Friday, during the afternoon. That is the only deal named in the listing.

Gramercy's Carlotto is a bar at 100 E 19th St. Union Square is the closest hub: 14th Street-Union Square, with the 4, 5, 6, L, N, Q, R and W lines, is a 4-minute walk.

A short early-evening window makes up the Carlotto happy hour, offered Sunday through Friday. The bar publishes the times but not the deal, so no drinks or food are named. Reservations are available through a Resy link, which helps if you want a seat during that brief stretch.

No street address is listed for Little Rebel, a bar in Gramercy, but the 3rd Avenue station on the L line is 2 minutes away on foot. Its tags include all-day, cocktails and wine.

The Little Rebel happy hour names Altos tequila, Absolute Vanilla vodka and Absolute vodka. It runs on weekdays, starting around midday and finishing in the early evening, which is a long window. Reservations go through a Resy link, and the live page has current prices.

Oceans, a restaurant at 233 Park Avenue South in Gramercy, sits a 4-minute walk from 14th Street-Union Square, where the 4, 5, 6, L, N, Q, R and W trains stop.

The Oceans happy hour is offered Sunday through Friday, and the window is short, in the early evening. The restaurant publishes the times but not the deal, so the drinks and food on offer are not named here. No booking link is listed, so call ahead or walk in.

Seven Sins sits at 293 3rd Ave in Gramercy as an American bar, tagged for cocktails and wine. The 23rd Street-Baruch College stop on the 6 line is a 4-minute walk.

Draft beer, house wine, mixed drinks and craft cocktails are covered by the Seven Sins happy hour. It runs on weekdays from late afternoon into the early evening. Reservations go through Resy, and the listing shows a price range of two dollar signs. Current prices are on the live page.

Irving Place in Gramercy holds Pierre Loti, a restaurant and wine bar at 53 Irving Place. From 14th Street-Union Square, which has the 4, 5, 6, L, N, Q, R and W lines, it is a 3-minute walk.

The Pierre Loti happy hour runs every day, from late afternoon into the early evening. The restaurant publishes the times but not the deal, so the wines and plates on offer are not named. Reservations go through OpenTable.

East 14th Street is the address for Saperavi, a restaurant at 245 East 14th Street tagged for wine. The 3rd Avenue stop on the L line is 2 minutes away on foot.

Weekday afternoons are when the Saperavi happy hour runs, finishing in the early evening. The restaurant publishes the times but not the deal, so the wines and food covered are not named here. A reservation link to the restaurant's own site is provided, and the live schedule on this page shows the current hours.

On Prince Street in SoHo, Milady's is a bar that lists a happy hour from Sunday through Thursday. The Milady's happy hour runs from the afternoon into the early evening.

The bar publishes the times but not the deal, so what the happy hour covers is not stated. Spring Street, served by the C and E trains, is a 3-minute walk. No booking link is on file.

Italian food is the focus at Patrizia's, a restaurant at 462 2nd Avenue that is listed under Gramercy. The 28th Street station on the 6 line is a 7-minute walk, so plan on a longer approach than most spots on this side of town.

The Patrizia's happy hour runs Monday through Thursday, from the afternoon into the early evening. The restaurant publishes the times but not the deal, so no drinks or dishes are named here. The price range shows as two dollar signs.

House wine is the named offer on the Bistro Eloise happy hour, Tuesday through Friday, and the window stretches through the afternoon into the early evening. The bar is at 75-57 31st Ave in East Elmhurst, Queens, sixteen minutes on foot from the 65th Street station, where the M and R trains stop. Reservations go through an OpenTable link on the listing, which also tags the place for cocktails, wine and all-day service.

At 15 West 18th Street in Union Square, Kyma operates as a Greek, Mediterranean and seafood restaurant. The closest subway stop is 14th Street (the 1, 2, 3, F, L and M trains), a four-minute walk away.

Kyma happy hour applies from Tuesday through Friday, from the afternoon into the early evening. The listing names house wines, Noir Prosecco beers and IPA summer bites.

Boca Chica lists a weekday happy hour at 96-20 37th Ave in Corona, Queens. The bar publishes the times but not the deal, so the Boca Chica happy hour is a schedule with no named items. The nearest station is Junction Boulevard on the 7 line, four minutes away on foot. No booking link is listed, and the page carries no extra tags beyond the basics.

With 51st Street station (6, E, F) a 4-minute walk away, Cornerstone Tavern is easy to reach from its spot at 961 2nd Ave in Midtown. It is listed as a bar and tagged as a pub.

The Cornerstone Tavern happy hour runs on weekdays and starts in the morning, finishing in the early evening. Listed deals are Bud Light draft, well drinks, wine and Lagunitas IPA drafts.

Mexican food is the focus at Dos Caminos, a restaurant at 480 Lexington Avenue in Midtown. Grand Central-42nd Street, served by the 4, 5, 6, 7 and S, is a 4-minute walk.

The Dos Caminos happy hour runs on weekdays in the afternoon and lists beef empanadas and margaritas, so there is one food item and one drink to know about.

Josie Woods Pub serves the Union Square area as a bar on Waverly Place. 8th Street–New York University is the nearest station, served by the R and W trains and a two-minute walk from the door.

The Josie Woods Pub happy hour runs Monday through Friday, from the afternoon into the early evening. It covers draft and bottled beer, including the house Josie Woods Ale, well drinks, a flavored martini, daily shot specials, wine and prosecco, plus an order of buffalo wings. The full list is on this page, with live prices.

Brickyard Craft Kitchen and Bar works as a bar at 23 Park Place in Tribeca. The closest subway stop is Park Place (the 2, 3, A, C, E, R and W trains), a one-minute walk away.

Brickyard Craft Kitchen and Bar happy hour runs on weekdays, from late morning into the evening. The bar publishes the times but not the deal. The website is linked from this page.

Diablo's Cantina, a bar on West Broadway in Tribeca, has its happy hour details below. For the subway, take the 1 train to Franklin Street, then walk about two minutes.

The deal is posted as draft, wines and bar snacks. The Diablo's Cantina happy hour runs on weekdays, from the afternoon into the early evening. A booking link is provided if you want to reserve ahead.

Filé Gumbo Bar is listed as a bar at 275 Church Street in Tribeca. For the subway, take the 1 train to Franklin Street, then walk about two minutes.

Filé Gumbo Bar happy hour runs on weekdays, from the afternoon into the early evening. Listed items include kicked up beef sliders, grilled Cajun wings, house lager, house wines, specialty cocktails and char-grilled oysters. A booking link is provided if you want to reserve ahead.

At 250 Vesey Street in Tribeca, Market Bar operates as a bar. For the subway, take the 1 train to WTC Cortlandt, then walk about five minutes.

Market Bar happy hour runs on weekdays, from late afternoon into the early evening. Times are posted, but the bar does not publish the deal itself. The website is linked from this page. The listing is for Tribeca in Manhattan.

Mudville works as a bar at 126 Chambers Street in Tribeca. Chambers Street is the nearest station, served by the 2, 3, A, C, E, R and W trains and a one-minute walk from the door.

Mudville happy hour applies on weekdays, from the afternoon into the early evening. The bar publishes the times but not the deal. You can reserve through the booking link provided here.

Da Andrea happy hour applies on weekdays, from late afternoon into the early evening. Only the times are published here, not the specifics of the deal.

The restaurant is at 35 West 13th Street in Union Square. For the subway, take the 1, 2, 3, F, L and M trains to 6th Avenue, then walk about two minutes. A booking link is provided if you want to reserve ahead.

Edward's sits on West Broadway in Tribeca and counts as an American restaurant and bar. Chambers Street is the nearest station, served by the 1, 2 and 3 trains and a two-minute walk from the door.

The Edward's happy hour runs on weekdays, from the afternoon into the early evening. The bar has not published what the deal includes, only when it runs. You can reserve through the booking link provided here.

The Plaza At The Roxy is listed as a bar serving American food, seafood and oysters at 2 Avenue of the Americas in Tribeca. The closest subway stop is Franklin Street (the 1 train), a two-minute walk away.

The Plaza At The Roxy happy hour runs every day in the late afternoon, and all night on Monday. The deal covers East Coast oysters, select wines by the glass, a mini Roxy martini and select draft beer. Reservations go through the booking link on this page.

At 225 Liberty Street in Battery Park City, Blue Ribbon Sushi Bar operates as a Japanese bar. WTC Cortlandt is the nearest station, served by the 1 train and a four-minute walk from the door.

Blue Ribbon Sushi Bar happy hour comes on weekdays, from late afternoon into the early evening. The deal covers hand rolls and select sake and beer. A second window is listed on Saturday and Sunday, so check the page for the split.

El Vez can be found on Vesey Street in Battery Park City. It is a restaurant. The closest subway stop is WTC Cortlandt (the 1 train), a six-minute walk away.

Tribeca, the Triangle Below Canal Street, runs from Canal Street down to around Chambers Street, between Broadway and the Hudson River. Our bars cluster at its southern end. Chambers and Reade Streets hold Artesano, Mudville and Bar 135, each a minute from a Chambers Street station, and Park Place, a few blocks south, adds Brickyard Craft Kitchen and Bar and Benares. Farther north, West Broadway, Church Street and Sixth Avenue near the Franklin Street stop on the 1 bring in Filé Gumbo Bar and The Plaza At The Roxy.

Happy hour in Tribeca is mostly a weekday, after-work deal, with a couple that start much earlier: Artesano opens its window at midday, and Brickyard runs from late morning into the evening. Expect draft beer, house wine and margaritas, and more food than usual, from char-grilled oysters and Cajun wings at Filé Gumbo Bar to sliders at Brickyard. Benares is the one daily option in the core. Our Tribeca list also pulls in a few addresses outside the neighborhood, so check each one before you go.

picks.why: Filé Gumbo Bar at 275 Church Street has one of the fuller food deals downtown: char-grilled oysters, beef sliders, grilled Cajun wings, hush puppies, fried okra and house potato chips. Drinks cover a house lager, house wines and specialty cocktails. It runs Monday to Friday from mid-afternoon, two minutes from Franklin Street on the 1.

Benares serves Indian food a minute from the Park Place station, and it is the one spot in Tribeca proper on our list with a happy hour every day. Beer, wines and a house cocktail are on special from the afternoon into early evening, weekends included, which makes it an easy Sunday plan. Reservations go through Resy.

Brickyard Craft Kitchen and Bar at 23 Park Place keeps happy hour going Monday to Friday from late morning into the evening, the longest window on our Tribeca list. Bar bites include mac and cheese bites, beef or chicken sliders and veggie spring rolls. The bar notes that checks are subject to gratuity. Park Place station is a minute away.

The Plaza At The Roxy, at 2 Avenue of the Americas, is an oyster-focused bar whose deal text promises an all-day happy hour on Mondays, plus sunset specials in the late afternoon. It is the oyster pick in Tribeca, two minutes from Franklin Street on the 1, and Resy takes reservations.

Artesano is a Mexican and Latin spot at 90 Chambers Street, a minute from the Chambers Street station. Its weekday happy hour starts at midday and runs through the afternoon across the room, then carries on for a couple more hours at the bar only, so a late lunch and an after-work drink both count. Book through Resy.

Mudville at 126 Chambers Street is a bar a minute from the Chambers Street station on the A, C, E, 2 and 3. Its weekday happy hour menu, from mid-afternoon to early evening, lists bites such as house popcorn, guacamole, chicken parm eggrolls, cheese pizza and buttermilk chicken tenders. Resy handles reservations for groups.

sections.body: Chambers Street is the main gateway: the 1, 2 and 3 stop at West Broadway, near Bar 135 and Edward's, and the A, C and E stop at Church Street, close to Artesano and Mudville. Park Place on the 2 and 3, part of the same downtown complex, is a minute from Brickyard and Benares. The Franklin Street stop on the 1 covers the northern blocks, including Filé Gumbo Bar and The Plaza At The Roxy. Spots around Brookfield Place on this list are closest to WTC Cortlandt on the 1.

Menus here leave the extras off: 8.875 percent sales tax, then a tip of 18 to 20 percent, unless the check already includes gratuity, as Brickyard warns. El Vez and the later part of Artesano's window are bar-only. A last-checked date sits on every listing, and it is worth a look before you head down.

faq.a: Benares runs its happy hour every day, weekends included. Most other Tribeca bars on our list, such as Filé Gumbo Bar, Mudville and Brickyard Craft Kitchen and Bar, keep their deals to weekdays.
faq.q: Which Tribeca bars have happy hour on weekends?

faq.a: Filé Gumbo Bar on Church Street includes char-grilled oysters in its weekday happy hour, and The Plaza At The Roxy on Avenue of the Americas is an oyster bar with an all-day happy hour on Mondays.
faq.q: Where can I get oysters at happy hour in Tribeca?

faq.a: Brickyard Craft Kitchen and Bar starts in the late morning on weekdays, and Artesano begins at midday. Both are a minute from the Chambers Street and Park Place stations.
faq.q: What is the earliest happy hour in Tribeca?

NYC's throwback calendar is a handful of themed nights, each one named for an era or for nostalgia itself. They cluster in two places. In Manhattan it is the East Village, where DROM on Avenue A and the basement club Deluxx Fluxx on East 11th Street both run repeat nights. In Brooklyn it is Bushwick and Williamsburg, with parties at The Sultan Room, Purgatory and The Meadows.

The eras are easy to tell apart. PROMISCUOUS does 2000s club bangers, Take Me Out does 2000s indie and disco punk, and Bangerangerz plays the biggest 2010s club and pop tracks all night. Nightbreed goes back further, with synth, post punk, goth and 80s. Deluxx Fluxx keeps it loose with NOSTALGIA, a throwback classics night, plus a 2010s rap and R&B costume edition for Halloween weekend. reggaetonLABS adds a reggaeton throwbacks party on Thanksgiving Eve. Pick by decade and you will know what you are walking into.

picks.why: Take Me Out is the pick if your 2000s were indie rather than Top 40. Nick Marc of Tiswas plays indie-dance and disco punk at DROM on Avenue A in the East Village on Friday, November 20. The listing names Arctic Monkeys, The Strokes, LCD Soundsystem and Bloc Party as the kind of records you will hear, not as performers.

PROMISCUOUS brings a full night of 2000s club hits to The Sultan Room in Bushwick on Friday, November 13. The team behind the touring throwback night Sorry For Party Rocking runs it, and the reference points are Timbaland, Nelly Furtado and JT. It is a tribute night, so none of those artists will appear.

Nightbreed takes over the downstairs room at Purgatory in Bushwick on Thursday, October 29, with synth, post punk, goth and what the listing calls 80s sleaze for queer bats. Jamie K of SVMMON plays with special guest Jeffo!. It is an early-evening party and it is listed as free, which makes it an easy start to Halloween weekend.

Bangerangerz is a straight 2010s night at DROM in the East Village on Saturday, November 14. Alex Jay plays the decade's biggest club and pop tracks all night, from a list that runs through Avicii, Calvin Harris, Robyn, Charli XCX, Daft Punk and Disclosure. Those are songs on the playlist, not guests on the bill.

Nostalgia: Mask On is the Halloween weekend edition of the Deluxx Fluxx throwback night, billed in its title as a 2010s rap and R&B costume party, on Friday, October 30. The venue presents it in its basement club at 125 East 11th Street in the East Village. No DJs are named, so come for the decade and the costumes.

reggaetonLABS brings Reggaeton Throwbacks to the main room at The Meadows in Williamsburg on Wednesday, November 25, which is also Thanksgiving Eve. The theme is the golden era of perreo, so the listing points to classic reggaeton. No DJs are named yet, which makes this one a pick for the theme alone.

sections.body: For the '80s, Nightbreed at Purgatory goes dark with synth, goth and post punk. For the 2000s, choose PROMISCUOUS at The Sultan Room for club bangers or Take Me Out at DROM for indie and disco punk. The 2010s belong to Bangerangerz at DROM and to Nostalgia: Mask On, the rap and R&B costume night at Deluxx Fluxx. If you just want old favorites without picking a decade, Deluxx Fluxx runs NOSTALGIA: A Throwback Classic Night on Friday, November 13 and Friday, November 27, with no era named. Reggaeton fans have Reggaeton Throwbacks at The Meadows.

Every party on this page is 21+ unless its own page says otherwise, so bring a physical ID. Themed nights can sell out, and Halloween weekend and Thanksgiving Eve are the dates to buy ahead for. Doors, end times and current prices are on each party's page, right next to this text.

faq.a: PROMISCUOUS plays 2000s club bangers at The Sultan Room in Bushwick on Friday, November 13. Take Me Out covers 2000s indie-dance and disco punk at DROM in the East Village on Friday, November 20.
faq.q: Where can I find a 2000s throwback party in NYC?

faq.a: Yes. Bangerangerz at DROM in the East Village plays 2010s club and pop tracks all night on Saturday, November 14, with Alex Jay on the decks. Nostalgia: Mask On at Deluxx Fluxx on Friday, October 30 is billed as a 2010s rap and R&B costume party.
faq.q: Is there a 2010s party in NYC?

faq.a: Not at the moment. No emo night is listed on this page yet, and new ones will appear here when they are announced. For guitar-driven nostalgia in the meantime, Take Me Out at DROM plays 2000s indie and disco punk on Friday, November 20.
faq.q: Is there an emo night in NYC right now?

faq.a: Right now, one: Nightbreed, downstairs at Purgatory in Bushwick on Thursday, October 29, with synth, post punk, goth and 80s. The other throwback nights are ticketed, with live prices on each party's page.
faq.q: Are any throwback parties in NYC free?

NYC has 23 New Year's Eve parties listed for Thursday, December 31, 2026: 15 in Manhattan and 8 in Brooklyn. Brooklyn's are concentrated in Williamsburg, with 4, and Bushwick, with 3, plus &ME at the Brooklyn Navy Yard in Fort Greene. Manhattan spreads out more, with Koreatown at 3 and the Lower East Side and Chelsea at 2 each.

Most of the list falls into two camps. Joonbug presents 17 bar and lounge packages, usually a DJ on Top 40, hip-hop and house, often with a midnight countdown, and several with an open bar. The other six are club nights: &ME at the Duggal Greenhouse, Loud Luxury at Marquee, San Pacho at Elsewhere, Tinzo + Jojo and DJ Minx at 99 Scott, Gravagerz at SILO Brooklyn and a reggaeton warehouse party at The Meadows. Pick the camp first, then the room. Nothing on this page is sold out yet.

picks.why: &ME plays the Duggal Greenhouse at the Brooklyn Navy Yard, presented by Stranger Than. The promoter calls it his first solo New York show apart from Keinemusik, and it runs from New Year's Eve into the early morning of January 1. No support acts are confirmed yet, so this one is about the headliner and the room.

Elsewhere takes a New Year's Eve party to 99 Scott in Bushwick, with Tinzo + Jojo, listed by DICE as Book Club Radio, and DJ Minx. It is separate from the party at Elsewhere's own building, which has San Pacho in the Hall and two more rooms still to be announced. Elsewhere notes that openers and set times can change.

reggaetonLABS throws a nine-hour reggaeton party at The Meadows on Meadow Street in Brooklyn, running into New Year's Day. Riobamba, Danny NYC and DJ Loko are named. The ticket includes an hour of open bar at the start, a midnight champagne toast and an interactive countdown, in a warehouse the promoter says has a strong sound system.

If you want to see the ball drop without standing in the street, this is the most direct option: a Joonbug party on the 31st-floor rooftop of Margaritaville Resort Times Square, with views of the Ball Drop and the Manhattan skyline. A live DJ plays Top 40, hip-hop, house and mashups. No DJ is named.

The White Horse Tavern on Hudson Street dates back to the 1800s and is known for its literary history. On New Year's Eve, Joonbug runs it as an open bar night with a live DJ on Top 40, hip-hop and dance favorites, plus a midnight countdown. It is the West Village pick for people who want a pub, not a club.

Downtown Crawl Til the Ball Drops is a bar crawl rather than one room. Registration is at The Skinny Bar on Orchard Street on the Lower East Side, and the named stops so far are Bobby's Night Out on Loisaida Avenue and Coyote Ugly on East 14th Street, with more venues to be announced. Good for a group that gets restless.

sections.body: Choose your ticket early and read what it covers. At Superior Ingredients in Williamsburg, The Roof and The Room are separate tickets, and only All Access gets you into both. Hotel Alameda in Chelsea splits the night between Creatures Rooftop for the countdown and Music for a While downstairs for later. Nothing here is sold out yet, so now is when you have the full menu. The subway runs all night in NYC, which makes a late Brooklyn finish easier to get home from.

All 23 parties are 21+, so bring a valid ID. Tickets can sell out at any point before the night. Doors, end times and what each ticket includes are on each party's page, and lineups can move: Elsewhere notes that openers, set times and room assignments can change without notice.

faq.a: Rooftop Ball Drop View, on the 31st-floor rooftop of Margaritaville Resort Times Square, has views of the Ball Drop. Ainsworth Midtown on East 33rd Street has screens for it, and Sony Hall, off Times Square on West 46th Street, holds a midnight countdown.
faq.q: Where can I watch the ball drop at a party in NYC?

faq.a: &ME at the Duggal Greenhouse in the Brooklyn Navy Yard, Elsewhere's two parties (San Pacho at Elsewhere, Tinzo + Jojo and DJ Minx at 99 Scott), Gravagerz at SILO Brooklyn with live aerialists and a midnight balloon drop, and the reggaetonLABS party at The Meadows.
faq.q: What are the big club New Year's Eve parties in Brooklyn?

faq.a: Several. Sony Hall, Blind Barber and VIRGO list a five-hour premium open bar. White Horse Tavern and 5th & Mad list an open bar, and Ainsworth Midtown is described as an open-bar package. The Meadows reggaeton party includes one hour of open bar.
faq.q: Are there open bar New Year's Eve parties in NYC?

faq.a: Yes. Darling Rooftop on the 47th floor of the Park Lane Hotel on Central Park South, the Margaritaville rooftop in Times Square, El Nico Rooftop on top of The Penny Williamsburg, The Roof at Superior Ingredients and Creatures Rooftop at Hotel Alameda in Chelsea.
faq.q: Is there a rooftop New Year's Eve party in NYC?

The Azul On The Rooftop happy hour runs on weekdays from the late afternoon into the early evening, with gin and tequila named among the offers at set prices. A booking link is available.

The Boqueria Soho happy hour is listed on weekdays, beginning in the afternoon and ending in the early evening. The restaurant publishes the times but not the deal, so the dishes and drinks are not named. A booking link is available for reserving a table.

On Avenue of the Americas in SoHo, Cha Cha Tang is a bar tagged for cocktails, wine, cheap beer and a food deal. Houston Street on the 1 train is a 3-minute walk.

Its happy hour runs on weekdays from the late afternoon into the early evening. The Cha Cha Tang happy hour names house cocktails, beer, happy hour food and steamed crystal shrimp dumplings, all at set prices. Reservations go through the booking link.

Aperitivo spritz at a set price is the named deal at Cómodo, a SoHo bar on MacDougal Street. The Cómodo happy hour runs weekdays, from the afternoon into the early evening.

Houston Street on the 1 train is a 3-minute walk from the door. The bar is tagged for cocktails, wine and a food deal, and a booking link is available if you would rather hold a spot than show up.

Over on Spring Street in SoHo, Lazy Point is a bar tagged for cocktails and wine. Its happy hour runs just Wednesday and Thursday, from the afternoon into the evening, and cocktails are the named offer.

The Lazy Point happy hour is easy to reach: Spring Street, on the C and E lines, is a 5-minute walk. No booking link is on file for the bar.

Thursday through Sunday evenings are when the Madame X happy hour is on, and it includes the weekend. Offers named in the listing are well mixed drinks, well cocktails and beer, all at set prices.

Madame X is a SoHo bar on West Houston Street, tagged for cocktails. Prince Street on the R and W trains is a 5-minute walk. The listing has no booking link, so plan on showing up.

Beer and cocktails at set prices are the two categories named in the Mostrador NYC happy hour, which runs Tuesday through Saturday from late afternoon into the early evening, including Saturday.

Mostrador NYC is a bar on Walker Street in SoHo, tagged for cocktails, wine and a food deal. Canal Street, where the 6, J, N, Q, R, W and Z trains stop, is 2 minutes on foot. No booking link is on file.

At 594 Union Avenue in Williamsburg, Casa Pública serves Mexican food. The Bedford Avenue station and the L train are five minutes away.

Monday through Thursday, in the early evening, the Casa Pública happy hour runs, and on Mondays the drinks deal lasts until close. The tags point to a food deal, though the restaurant does not publish the items. A price range is listed for the menu.

Eleven minutes from the Marcy Avenue station and its J, M and Z trains, Bar Milagro is at 29 Dunham Place in Williamsburg.

The bar posts a happy hour for Tuesday through Friday, running from the early evening into the evening. The Bar Milagro happy hour has times only, because the deal itself is not published. Ask the bar what is on offer.

Oysters appear in the tags for Bee's Knees Cocktail Bar, at 65 North 7th Street in Williamsburg. The Bedford Avenue station and the L train are six minutes away.

The Bee's Knees Cocktail Bar happy hour has two windows. Tuesday through Thursday it runs in the early evening, and Friday starts a little earlier in the late afternoon. The deal is not published, only the times. A booking link is available.

Birds of a Feather, a restaurant at 191 Grand Street in Williamsburg, is six minutes from the Bedford Avenue station and the L train. All-day service, cocktails and wine appear in its tags.

The Birds of a Feather happy hour is a long one on weekdays, beginning around midday and ending in the early evening. The restaurant does not publish the specific offers. You can reserve through the booking link.

Crystal Lake Brooklyn, a bar at 647 Grand Street in Williamsburg, is five minutes from the Graham Avenue station on the L train.

The Crystal Lake Brooklyn happy hour covers weekdays, from the late afternoon into the early evening. The listed offers are drafts, well drinks and select wines by the glass, so beer, liquor and wine are all covered. No booking link is attached.

Dolly's Swing and Dive, a dive bar at 146 Wythe Avenue in Williamsburg, is five minutes from the Bedford Avenue station and the L train.

Weekdays are covered by the Dolly's Swing and Dive happy hour, which starts in the afternoon and runs into the early evening. The bar has not published the deal, only the hours, so ask at the bar about what is included.

Fandi Mata, seven minutes from the Lorimer Street station and its G and L trains, is a restaurant at 74 Bayard Street in Williamsburg.

Tuesday through Sunday is when the Fandi Mata happy hour runs, in the early evening, and that includes the weekend. The restaurant gives the times but no offers. A booking link is attached, and cocktails are the one drink category mentioned in its tags.

Fushimi has a food deal in its tags and a restaurant address of 475 Driggs Avenue in Williamsburg. The Bedford Avenue station and the L train are three minutes on foot.

The Fushimi happy hour runs every day, from late afternoon into the early evening, and the restaurant does not publish what it covers. Reservations are available through the booking link on the page.

Fifth Avenue in Park Slope is the home of 200 Fifth, a bar at number 200 with Union Street station on the R a 3-minute walk away.

The 200 Fifth happy hour runs on weekdays, from the late afternoon into the evening. Listed deals are bar drinks, house wine and champagne, so the focus is on drinks rather than food. An OpenTable link is available for reservations.

Carneval, a restaurant with a food deal in its tags, is three minutes from the Metropolitan Avenue station, where G and L trains stop. The address is 507 Grand St.

On weekdays the Carneval happy hour runs from the late afternoon into the early evening. The restaurant publishes the window but not the offers. Reservations are linked from the page.

French, Italian and American dishes are in the description of Francie, a restaurant at 134 Broadway in Williamsburg, seven minutes from the Marcy Avenue station and its J, M and Z trains.

The Francie happy hour is Monday through Thursday, in the early evening, and oysters are in the tags. The deal is not itemized. The price range is moderate.

Late at night is when Cozy Royale runs its deal. The bar is at 434 Humboldt Street in Williamsburg, four minutes from the Graham Avenue station and the L train.

The Cozy Royale happy hour runs Sunday through Thursday in the early evening, and again late every night. The bar lists the window without any offers. Late-night and weekend are both in its tags, and reservations are linked.

At 234 Union Avenue in Williamsburg, HaaM is a restaurant two minutes from the Broadway station and the G train.

From Monday to Thursday, the HaaM happy hour covers the late afternoon and early evening. Its tags mention a food deal, but the restaurant has not published the items. You can reserve through the booking link. Because only the schedule is listed, ask the restaurant what the deal covers.

On Bedford Avenue, at number 292 in Williamsburg, Hole In The Wall is a restaurant six minutes from the Bedford Avenue station on the L train.

On weekdays, from the afternoon into the early evening, the Hole In The Wall happy hour is on. The list covers an espresso martini, a Bee's Knees gin drink, Aperol, wine, drafts and bites, so it spans cocktails, beer and food.

Iona Bar, on Grand Street at number 180 in Williamsburg, is six minutes from the Bedford Avenue station and the L train. Cocktails and wine are among its tags.

The Iona Bar happy hour runs on weekdays, starting in the afternoon and going into the early evening. The bar does not publish what is included, just the schedule. Ask at the bar for current drink details, since no booking link is attached.

Out on Grand Street, Isla & Co is a bar at number 66 in Williamsburg, seven minutes from the Bedford Avenue station and the L train.

Every day of the week has a happy hour here, in the late afternoon and early evening, so the weekend is covered. The Isla & Co happy hour lists cocktails, wines and beers, and a food deal is tagged as well. Reserve through the booking link.

Sports and cocktails define Guarapo Latin Fusion Sports Restaurant and Bar, found at 58 North 3rd Street in Williamsburg. The Bedford Avenue station and the L train are seven minutes away.

The Guarapo Latin Fusion Sports Restaurant and Bar happy hour runs on Monday, Tuesday, Thursday and Friday, from the late afternoon into the early evening. A food deal is tagged, but the offers are not itemized.

Layla is described as a bar with European food, at 352 Bedford Avenue in Williamsburg. The Marcy Avenue station and the J, M and Z trains are seven minutes away.

The Layla happy hour runs on weekdays, in the late afternoon and early evening. Draft beer, oysters, Contessa Boatyard gin and aperitivi beers are the listed items. The price range is low to moderate, and a booking link is attached.

Limosneros, a restaurant at 366 Union Avenue in Williamsburg, is two minutes from the Metropolitan Avenue station and its G and L trains.

The Limosneros happy hour runs all day on Monday and Thursday, and from the afternoon into the early evening on Friday. Margaritas, sangria, wine margaritas and wine are the named drinks, with fried chicken wings on Thursday and appetizers such as mini quesadillas, queso fundido, nachos and mussels on Monday and Friday. Cocktails, wine and a food deal are in its tags.

Meraki Greek Bistro Brooklyn, a bar with outdoor seating, is at 252 Grand Street in Williamsburg, six minutes from the Bedford Avenue station and the L train.

Weekdays, from the afternoon into the early evening, are when the Meraki Greek Bistro Brooklyn happy hour runs. A food deal is tagged, but no items are published. Reservations are linked from the page.

Monarch, a restaurant at 146 Metropolitan Avenue in Williamsburg, is six minutes from the Bedford Avenue station and the L train.

The Monarch happy hour runs Tuesday through Friday, in the early evening. Sake gets a discount and cocktails are on the list, and a food deal is tagged too. No booking link is attached. Ask the restaurant whether the sake discount applies to every pour.

Bleecker Street in Greenwich Village has L'accolade, a restaurant at number 302. Christopher Street-Stonewall Station, on the 1 line, is 2 minutes away on foot.

The L'accolade happy hour is offered on weekdays in the early evening. The restaurant publishes the times but not the deal, so no drinks or dishes are named here. A Resy link handles reservations, which is useful if you want to arrive to a held table. The live schedule shows current hours.

Lelabar, at 422 Hudson St in Greenwich Village, is a bar tagged for wine, oysters and a food deal. The Houston Street stop on the 1 line is a 3-minute walk.

Beer, oysters sold individually, olives and wine are what the Lelabar happy hour covers. It runs every day, weekends included, ending in the early evening with no start time listed. No reservation link is published, and the live page shows the current hours.

Cornelia Street holds Little Havana Restaurant, filed as a bar at 30 Cornelia St in Greenwich Village. The West 4th Street-Washington Square station, with A, B, C, D, E, F and M trains, is a 2-minute walk.

Nachos and french fries are the named items in the Little Havana Restaurant happy hour. It runs on weekdays, in the late afternoon and early evening. A food deal is among its tags. No reservation link is published.

North Square, a restaurant in Greenwich Village, has no street address in the listing, though the West 4th Street-Washington Square station, with the A, B, C, D, E, F and M, is a 3-minute walk.

Every day of the week, weekends included, the North Square happy hour runs from the afternoon into the early evening. The restaurant publishes the times but not the deal, so no drinks or dishes are named. No reservation link is listed. Look at the live schedule for current hours.

In Greenwich Village, Rafele is a restaurant tagged for cheap beer, cocktails and wine. The listing gives no usable street address, but Houston Street, on the 1 line, is a 3-minute walk.

Wines (Montepulciano, Sauvignon Blanc and Prosecco), Aperol and beers make up the Rafele happy hour. It runs Monday through Thursday, in the late afternoon and early evening. Reservations go through a Resy link, and the live page has the current hours.

Argentinian steakhouse fare, pasta and Italian cooking are listed for Sabor Argentino, a bar at 57 7th Ave S in Greenwich Village. Christopher Street-Stonewall Station, on the 1 line, is a 3-minute walk.

The Sabor Argentino happy hour runs Thursday through Sunday, from the afternoon into the early evening, so it includes the weekend. The bar publishes the times but not the deal, so the drinks and food are not named. The price range shows as three dollar signs. No reservation link is published.

West 3rd Street in Greenwich Village is the setting for Spicy Moon, a restaurant at number 68. The West 4th Street-Washington Square stop, served by the A, B, C, D, E, F and M, is 4 minutes away on foot.

Sunday through Thursday, in the late afternoon and early evening, is when the Spicy Moon happy hour runs. The restaurant publishes the times but not the deal, so no drinks or dishes are named here. Reservations go through a Resy link. The live page has the current hours.

Greenwich Village is the neighborhood for The Happiest Hour, a restaurant with no street address in the listing. Christopher Street-Stonewall Station, on the 1 line, is a 4-minute walk.

Rotating craft beer, craft beer and pints are what The Happiest Hour happy hour covers. It runs every day, weekends included, from late afternoon into the early evening. No reservation link is published. For current hours and prices, see the live listing on this page.

At 430 Hudson St in Greenwich Village, The Leroy House is a bar with a weekend tag. The Houston Street station on the 1 line is a 3-minute walk.

The Leroy House happy hour runs every day, including Saturday and Sunday, in the late afternoon and early evening. The bar publishes the times but not the deal, so the drinks and food are not named here. Reservations go through Resy. Check the live schedule on this page for the current window.

Weekends belong to The Malt House, a pub at 206 Thompson Street in Greenwich Village with tags for a food deal and the weekend. West 4th Street-Washington Square, with the A, B, C, D, E, F and M, is a 5-minute walk.

Jumbo wings and Parmesan herbed fries are the named items in The Malt House happy hour. It runs on Saturday and Sunday and ends in the afternoon, with no start time listed. Reservations go through a Resy link.

Bedford Street in Greenwich Village is home to The Little Owl, a restaurant at 90 Bedford Street tagged for cocktails and wine. Christopher Street-Stonewall Station, on the 1 line, is a 3-minute walk.

Weekdays are when The Little Owl happy hour is listed, and the listed window falls in the morning. The drinks it covers are listed on this page, with live prices. Reservations go through OpenTable.

There are two windows to know at 390 Social, a bar at 390 5th Ave in Park Slope. One runs Tuesday through Thursday, and the other covers Friday and Sunday, so a weekend day is included. The 9th Street station (F, G, R) is a 3-minute walk.

The 390 Social happy hour is published as times only, without a list of deals. A Resy link is available for reservations.

Seafood is the cuisine at The Clam, a bar at 420 Hudson St in Greenwich Village, tagged for wine. The Houston Street stop on the 1 line is 3 minutes away on foot.

A cucumber cooler gin drink, wines and beer are listed in The Clam happy hour. It runs Tuesday through Friday, in the afternoon. The price range shows as three dollar signs. The live page has the current hours and prices.

On Carmine Street in Greenwich Village, at number 49, The Grey Dog serves as an American restaurant tagged for cocktails, wine and a food deal. Houston Street, on the 1 line, is a 2-minute walk.

House wine, Tommy's margarita, a Venetian spritz, rose and bar bites are named in The Grey Dog happy hour. It runs every day, weekends included, from late afternoon into the early evening. The price range shows as two dollar signs.

There are 23 free parties on the NYC calendar right now, and 21 are still open; the two Halloween parties, at Sleepwalk and Seventh Heaven, are sold out. Brooklyn has 12 and Manhattan 11. By neighborhood, the Lower East Side has 10, Williamsburg 9, Bushwick 3 and Nolita 1. Two venues carry most of the list: The Delancey hosts 10 reggaetonLABS nights, and Sleepwalk on Bushwick Avenue hosts 9, mostly its Wednesday vinyl happy hour.

The weekly pattern is simple. Fridays at The Delancey are Reggaeton Fridays, and Saturdays are Safaera, which adds Latin music to the reggaeton. Wednesdays at Sleepwalk are Date Nite, where Hotel Kismet puts crate diggers on vinyl with happy hour specials at the bar. Thursdays are the wild card: a goth night at Purgatory, a Nervous Records speakeasy at Shinsen and a melodic-to-hard techno night in the main room at SILO Brooklyn.

picks.why: Date Nite is the easiest free night on this page: a Wednesday happy hour at Sleepwalk on Bushwick Avenue, presented by Hotel Kismet, with DJs playing vintage and global grooves on vinyl. On November 4 the posted rotation points to DJ Gutzilla, though that date is not separately confirmed. It repeats every Wednesday through December 16.

Nervous Records sets up a speakeasy-style pop-up at Shinsen on the Bowery on Thursday, November 5, with Cosmo and Mike Nervous on the decks. Entry is by RSVP on DICE, and the listing tells you to arrive early. It is the only free Manhattan night on this page outside The Delancey.

Techno Thursday moves into the main room at SILO Brooklyn in Bushwick on November 19 for Melodic2Hard, presented with Aziman Tribe. The first half is hypnotic melodic techno, and the second half switches to fast hard techno until close. Roman Messer and Bruce Wayne lead a bill that also lists Asa, Phantom, Vida Libre, Tay and Gio.

Nightbreed fills the downstairs room at Purgatory in Bushwick on Thursday, October 29, with synth, post punk, goth and 80s for queer bats, in the listing's own words. Jamie K of SVMMON plays with special guest Jeffo!. It starts and ends early, which leaves the rest of Halloween weekend open.

Safaera is the reggaetonLABS Saturday party at The Delancey on the Lower East Side, with reggaeton and Latin music. The November 28 edition, the Saturday of Thanksgiving weekend, spells out the terms: no cover charge, a two-drink minimum for entry later in the night, and a DICE ticket that guarantees early entry. No DJs are named.

Reggaeton Fridays is the other half of the reggaetonLABS weekend at The Delancey, every Friday from November 6 through December 4. On November 6, a DICE ticket guarantees entry early in the night, so grab one instead of walking up late. The title tells you the music: reggaeton, with no DJs named.

sections.body: Free on this page means no ticket price, not a guaranteed walk-in. Most of these run on a free DICE RSVP: Nervous Records says entry is by RSVP and to arrive early, and the Techno Thursday title says free with RSVP. At The Delancey, a DICE ticket guarantees entry early in the night, and the Thanksgiving weekend listings add a two-drink minimum for later entry. Free nights also fill up. Both Halloween parties here, ParaPara at Seventh Heaven and BLOODLUST at Sleepwalk, are already sold out.

Every free party on this page is 21+, so bring a government ID, even to a Wednesday happy hour. Grab the RSVP as soon as you know you are going. Doors, end times and any entry cutoff are on each party's page, right next to this text.

faq.a: The Delancey on the Lower East Side has free reggaetonLABS parties every Friday and Saturday from November 6 through December 5: Reggaeton Fridays on Fridays and Safaera on Saturdays, which adds Latin music.
faq.q: Where can I go out for free in NYC on a weekend?

faq.a: Yes. Date Nite: Vinyl Happy Hour runs every Wednesday at Sleepwalk on Bushwick Avenue from October 28 through December 16, with vinyl DJs and happy hour specials. The posted rotation is DJ Gutzilla on the first and third Wednesdays, DJ Alyx Astryx on the second and a special guest on the fourth.
faq.q: Are there free happy hours with DJs in Brooklyn?

faq.a: For most of these, yes. Nervous Records Speakeasy at Shinsen is RSVP on DICE, Techno Thursday at SILO Brooklyn is free with RSVP, and at The Delancey a DICE ticket guarantees early entry. Two free Halloween parties on this page are already sold out.
faq.q: Do I need an RSVP for free parties in NYC?

faq.a: Techno Thursday: Melodic2Hard at SILO Brooklyn in Bushwick on Thursday, November 19 is free with RSVP. It moves from melodic techno to hard techno, with Roman Messer and Bruce Wayne leading the bill.
faq.q: Is there a free techno party in NYC?

intro:
At 7 Times Square, The Counter is a restaurant with a Times Square-42nd Street station 1 minute away, where the 1, 2, 3, 7, A, C, E, N, Q, R, S and W stop.

The Counter happy hour runs on weekdays in the afternoon. It lists bites and snacks, so the deal is food-oriented rather than drink-led. No reservation link is listed, and the page shows the live hours.

Loreley Restaurant & Biergarten is a beer hall at 7 Rivington St, 2 minutes from Bowery station on the J and Z, listed here under Nolita.

The Loreley happy hour runs Monday through Thursday, and the days are not all the same: on Monday and Tuesday it lasts into the late evening, while on Wednesday and Thursday it ends in the early evening. The deal is German-style beer and wine: draft beer and glass wine, one-liter steins, pitchers, Kölsch, beer cans and a beer flight, and select bottled wines. Reservations can be made through the Tock link on the page.

Cocktails, oysters and wings are what The GRID lists as its deals. It is a restaurant in Nolita with no street address on file, and the 3-minute walk to Bleecker Street station gets you to the 6, B, D, F and M.

The GRID happy hour window runs Tuesday through Friday in the late afternoon and early evening. An OpenTable link is available for reservations.

Botantica Bar is in Nolita, 2 minutes from Bleecker Street station, with the 6, B, D, F and M. It is a bar at 47 E Houston St.

The Botantica Bar happy hour runs every day, from opening into the early evening. Listed deals include a draft discount, a general discount on everything, well drinks and house wines. No reservation link is listed.

Spring Street station on the 6 is a 2-minute walk from Parm, a restaurant in Nolita at 248 Mulberry St.

The Parm happy hour runs on weekdays, from the afternoon into the early evening, and lists a specialty cocktail deal and appetizers. That gives it one drink and one food item to know about. There is no reservation link on the page.

Weekends are when Grand Street Social has its happy hour: Saturday and Sunday, from morning through the afternoon. It is a restaurant at 155 Grand Street in SoHo, and Canal Street station (6, J, N, Q, R, W, Z) is a 2-minute walk.

The Grand Street Social happy hour has no published deal, only the times, and there is no reservation link on the page.

Chrystie Street, number 131, holds Home Sweet Home, a bar in the Lower East Side. Bowery station on the J and Z is just 1 minute on foot.

The Home Sweet Home happy hour runs on weekdays, from opening until the evening. The bar publishes the times but not the deal, so no specific drinks are listed.

At 42 Rivington Street, in the Lower East Side, you will find Jadis Wine Bar, a restaurant with Bowery station (J, Z) a 3-minute walk away.

The Jadis Wine Bar happy hour is on every day of the week, from opening into the early evening. No deal is published, only the times, so the page cannot say which wines or dishes are discounted.

Bleecker Street station (6, B, D, F, M) is a 4-minute walk from 359 Bowery, where the pub Phebes operates. The page places it in the East Village.

The Phebes happy hour runs on weekdays and stays on until the evening. Listed deals are beers, Guinness and Stella drafts, wines and cocktails.

Two minutes on foot from Bowery station (J, Z), Ray's is a bar at 177 Chrystie Street in the Lower East Side.

The Ray's happy hour runs on weekdays, from opening until the early evening. The deal list mixes drinks and food: well shots, beer, house cocktails, a martini, a burger, fries and hot wings.

At 344 Bowery, The Wren is a restaurant that lists bar among its cuisines. Bleecker Street station (6, B, D, F, M) is a 3-minute walk, and the page places it in NoHo.

The Wren happy hour runs on weekdays, from the afternoon into the early evening. Only the times are published, not the deal.

Bar Toto, a restaurant at 411 11th Street in Park Slope, is a 5-minute walk from 7th Avenue station on the F and G.

The Bar Toto happy hour runs Monday through Thursday, from the afternoon into the evening, so Friday is not covered. Listed deals are cocktails, house wine and draft beer, a short list centered on drinks. No reservation link is listed on the page.

Burger Village, a restaurant at 222 7th Avenue in Park Slope, is a 6-minute walk from 7th Avenue station on the F and G.

The Burger Village happy hour runs Monday through Thursday, from the afternoon into the evening. The restaurant publishes the times but not the deal, so the page cannot say which items are discounted. No reservation link is listed.

In Park Slope, at 221 7th Ave, Bar Louise is a bar whose closest subway is the 7th Avenue station, served by the B and Q, a 5-minute walk.

The Bar Louise happy hour runs every day: all day on Monday with oysters, Tuesday through Friday in the afternoon, and an oyster happy hour on Saturday and Sunday afternoons. Listed deals include martinis, house wines and wine flights from Tuesday to Friday, and martinis with oysters at the weekend. A Resy link is available for booking.

Westville has a restaurant on Hudson Street in SoHo, 3 minutes on foot from Houston Street on the 1 train. Its happy hour runs on weekdays, from the late afternoon into the early evening.

The Westville happy hour lists cocktails, wine and beer at set prices. Tags also include cheap beer. No booking link is on file.

NoMo Kitchen, an American restaurant on Crosby Street in SoHo, lists a weekday happy hour from the afternoon into the early evening. The listing is tagged for a food deal but does not name specific items, so the NoMo Kitchen happy hour is known by its schedule only.

Canal Street is a 2-minute walk, and the 6, J, N, Q, R, W and Z trains all stop there. A booking link is available for reserving a table.

Spirits at a discount and two mezcals at set prices, Amaras Verde and Rompe Corazon, are named in the Novecento happy hour. It is listed every day of the week, from the afternoon into the early evening.

The bar is on West Broadway in SoHo, a 2-minute walk from Canal Street, where the 6, J, N, Q, R, W and Z trains stop. Cocktails and wine are among the tags, and a booking link is available.

Sullivan Street in SoHo holds Pepe Rosso, a restaurant tagged for wine, a 4-minute walk from Houston Street on the 1 train. The Pepe Rosso happy hour runs every day, weekends included, from the late afternoon into the early evening.

The restaurant publishes the times but not the deal, so there is nothing here about specific drinks or food. No booking link is on file.

Thompson Street is where to find Pera SoHo, a restaurant a 2-minute walk from Spring Street on the C and E trains. The Pera SoHo happy hour is listed on weekdays, from the late afternoon into the early evening.

The restaurant publishes the times but not the deal, so the drinks and food are not named. A booking link is available if you want to reserve ahead.

Two minutes from Spring Street, where the C and E trains stop, San Carlo Osteria Piemonte is a SoHo restaurant on Thompson Street. The San Carlo Osteria Piemonte happy hour runs on weekdays, from the afternoon into the early evening.

The restaurant publishes the times but not the deal, so the page cannot say which drinks or dishes are included. A booking link is available.

American, diner, breakfast and brunch are the cuisine labels on Soho Diner, a restaurant on West Broadway. Canal Street, served by the A, C and E trains, is a 1-minute walk away.

The Soho Diner happy hour is an overnight window listed for Friday and Saturday. Named items include black olives, SoHo hot wings and an aioli SoHo smash burger, all at set prices. Reservations are possible through the booking link.

The closest subway to Blueprint, a bar in Park Slope at 196 5th Ave, is Union Street on the R, a 3-minute walk.

The Blueprint happy hour runs on weekdays in the late afternoon and early evening. The deal list covers food, beer and house cocktails. There is no reservation link on the page, so it works as a walk-in.

Chela operates as a restaurant in Park Slope at 408 5th Ave, and the closest subway is 9th Street (F, G, R), a 3-minute walk.
