The Chela happy hour runs on weekdays and covers a long stretch from midday into the early evening. Only the times are published, not the deal, so the page cannot say which food or drinks are discounted. A Resy link is available for reservations.

Tex-Mex and tequila give Cantina Valencia its name, and the venue is a bar on Richmond Road in Staten Island tagged for wine. The Cantina Valencia Tex-Mex & Tequila Bar happy hour runs on weekdays from the afternoon into the early evening.

The bar publishes the times but not the deal, so no drinks are named here. Jefferson Avenue on the Staten Island Railway is an 8-minute walk. A booking link is available.

Dave & Buster's on Richmond Avenue in Staten Island is an American restaurant, tagged for cocktails and wine. The Dave & Buster's happy hour is listed on weekdays, beginning in the late afternoon and ending in the early evening.

The restaurant publishes the times but not the deal, so there is no list of drinks or food here. No transit stop and no booking link are on file for the address, which leaves the live hours on this page as the thing to check.

Chili's, the American and Tex-Mex restaurant on Richmond Avenue in Staten Island, lists a weekday happy hour from the afternoon into the early evening. The Chili's happy hour names a margarita and tequila at set prices.

The nearest rail stop on file is New Dorp on the Staten Island Railway, more than an hour away on foot, so plan how you will get there. The restaurant is tagged for cocktails and wine, and no booking link is listed.

Italian cooking is the category at Bar 314, a restaurant at 3143 Broadway in Morningside Heights. The 125th Street station on the 1 line is a 3-minute walk.

The Bar 314 happy hour is listed for every day of the week, with no end time in the listing. The restaurant publishes the schedule but not the deal, so no drinks or dishes are named here. Reservations go through a Resy link, which suits a weekend visit given its weekend tag. Current details are on the live page.

The Red Lion, at 151 Bleecker Street in Greenwich Village, is a bar whose listing mentions sports and live music. From West 4th Street-Washington Square, where the A, B, C, D, E, F and M stop, the walk is 5 minutes.

The Red Lion happy hour runs on weekdays, from late afternoon into the early evening. The bar publishes the times but not the deal, so the cocktails and wines are not named. Reservations go through Resy, and the price range shows as two dollar signs.

West 4th Street in Greenwich Village is home to The Spaniard, a bar at number 190 that lists classic American bar food. Christopher Street-Stonewall Station, on the 1 line, is just 1 minute away on foot.

Discounted draft beer, fries and ginger beer are named in The Spaniard happy hour. It runs on weekdays, from late afternoon into the early evening. Reservations go through a Resy link. See the live page for current prices.

Baylander Steel Beach has no street address listed, but this Harlem restaurant is a 6-minute walk from the 125th Street station on the 1 line.

Prohibition's giant pretzel, fresh lime falafel tacos and grilled shrimp tacos are the named items in the Baylander Steel Beach happy hour. It runs Tuesday through Friday, in the afternoon. A food deal is among its tags, and reservations go through a Resy link.

Frederick Douglass Boulevard in Harlem, at number 2149, is where BLVD Bistro operates as a restaurant. The 116th Street station, served by the B and C trains, is a 1-minute walk.

The BLVD Bistro happy hour is listed for every day of the week, weekends included, with no end time published. The restaurant lists the schedule but not the deal, so no drinks or dishes are named. Reservations go through a Resy link, and the live page has more current details.

Five parties are on for Thanksgiving week in NYC: four on Thanksgiving Eve, Wednesday, November 25, and one on Thanksgiving night, Thursday, November 26. Four are in Brooklyn, two in Bushwick (Elsewhere and The Chocolate Factory) and two in Williamsburg, both at Superior Ingredients. The fifth is in Manhattan, a house party at PUBLIC ArtSpace, the basement venue of the PUBLIC Hotel on Chrystie Street.

This is a house and disco night first. Louie Vega brings his annual Flashback to Superior Ingredients, and Natasha Diggs leads Soul In The Horn with DJ Scratch and Terry Hunter. Elsewhere's DayBreak has no lineup posted yet. If you are back from dinner on Thursday and still want to dance, Ground Control's annual Thanksgiving party with KOFLA and Cristian Arango uses the same Williamsburg main room one night later.

picks.why: Louie Vega's annual Flashback takes the Main Room at Superior Ingredients in Williamsburg on Wednesday, November 25, presented by Nervous Records and Dance.Here.Now. Vega plays an extended set of house classics, disco, boogie and MAW records, and the promoter is bringing in a boosted sound system. They pitch it as the opening night of the holiday season.

Soul In The Horn returns to The Chocolate Factory in Bushwick on Thanksgiving Eve. Natasha Diggs leads, with DJ Scratch, Terry Hunter, Sunny Cheeba and Moonbabe named in the description and special guests to be announced. The promoter lists house, soul, disco, funk, hip hop and global rhythms, the widest musical spread of the night.

TMML Presents throws a house party in PUBLIC ArtSpace, the basement venue of the PUBLIC Hotel at 215 Chrystie Street, on Wednesday, November 25. It is the only Thanksgiving Eve party on this page in Manhattan. The listing promises house music, but no DJs are named yet, so go for the room rather than a headliner.

Ground Control brings back its annual Thanksgiving night party at Superior Ingredients in Williamsburg on Thursday, November 26, after dinner. KOFLA and Cristian Arango are the two names in the Main Room, with no support acts or genres listed. It is the only party here on Thanksgiving itself, for anyone who wants a second night out.

DayBreak is Elsewhere's own Wednesday night party in Bushwick on November 25, filed as a DJ event on DICE. The listing does not name a lineup or say which of Elsewhere's rooms it uses. Pick it if you trust the venue's booking and want a second Bushwick option on Thanksgiving Eve besides Soul In The Horn.

sections.body: Thanksgiving Eve, the Wednesday before Thanksgiving, is one of the busiest bar nights of the year in the US. Thursday belongs to family, plenty of people have the next day off, and friends are back in town for the holiday. In 2026, Thanksgiving falls on Thursday, November 26, so the big night out is Wednesday, November 25. That is why four of the five parties on this page sit on the Wednesday.

All five parties are 21+, so bring ID. Thanksgiving Eve tickets can sell out, even though none on this page has yet. Lineups are still filling in: DayBreak and the TMML party name no DJs, and Soul In The Horn has special guests to be announced. Check each party's page for doors and current prices before you head out.

faq.a: Wednesday, November 25, 2026, the night before Thanksgiving on Thursday, November 26. Four of the five parties on this page fall on that Wednesday.
faq.q: When is Thanksgiving Eve 2026?

faq.a: In the Main Room at Superior Ingredients in Williamsburg, for his annual Flashback on Wednesday, November 25. He plays an extended set of house classics, disco and boogie.
faq.q: Where is Louie Vega playing on Thanksgiving Eve?

faq.a: Yes, one on this page: Ground Control's annual Thanksgiving party with KOFLA and Cristian Arango at Superior Ingredients in Williamsburg on Thursday, November 26.
faq.q: Are there parties in NYC on Thanksgiving night?

faq.a: TMML Presents at PUBLIC ArtSpace, the basement of the PUBLIC Hotel on Chrystie Street, is the Manhattan option: a house party on Wednesday, November 25. The other three Thanksgiving Eve parties on this page are in Brooklyn.
faq.q: Is there a Thanksgiving Eve party in Manhattan?

intro:
Broadway in Harlem has Cocteleria Perla Negra, a bar at number 3454, tagged for wine and a food deal. The 137th Street-City College stop on the 1 line is 4 minutes away on foot.

Tuesday through Sunday, in the early evening, is when the Cocteleria Perla Negra happy hour runs. The bar publishes the times but not the deal, so no drinks or food are named here. No reservation link is published. The live schedule has the current hours.

Lola La Marina can be found at 701 W 133rd St in Harlem, a bar. The 137th Street-City College station on the 1 line is a 5-minute walk.

Weekdays from late afternoon into the early evening make up the Lola La Marina happy hour. The bar publishes the times but not the deal, so no drinks or food are named, and there is no reservation link. For current hours, check the live listing on this page.

Caribbean cooking is the listed cuisine at Patrick's on the Hill, a bar at 1635 Amsterdam Ave in Harlem. The 137th Street-City College stop on the 1 line is a 5-minute walk.

OMG wings, french fries and cocktails are named in the Patrick's on the Hill happy hour. It runs Tuesday through Friday, in the early evening. The listing also tags a food deal, and the price range shows as two dollar signs. No reservation link is published.

Massawa, a restaurant at 1239 Amsterdam Avenue, is listed in Morningside Heights. The 116th Street-Columbia University station on the 1 line is a 6-minute walk.

Draft beer, wines and cocktails are covered by the Massawa happy hour. It has two windows: one on weekdays, and a separate one on Saturday and Sunday that finishes a little earlier. The listing tags it for cocktails and wine. No reservation link is published, and the live page has current hours.

Mother's, a pub at 347 Graham Avenue in Williamsburg, is a one-minute walk from the Graham Avenue station and the L train.

On weekdays, from the late afternoon into the early evening, the Mother's happy hour takes a discount off wine and cocktails. Both are among its tags. The listing shows a discount rather than fixed items. No booking link is attached, so ask at the pub.

Northern Bell, a bar at 612 Metropolitan Avenue in Williamsburg, is two minutes from the Lorimer Street station and the G and L trains.

The Northern Bell happy hour covers weekdays, from opening until the early evening. Offers include a discount on draft and on everything, well drinks, glasses of wine, happy hour food and smoked wings. Reservations are linked.

Williamsburg's OTB is a bar at 141 Broadway, six minutes from the Marcy Avenue station and the J, M and Z trains.

The OTB happy hour is a weekend one, on Saturday and Sunday, in the late afternoon and early evening. The listed items are margaritas, Aperol, house wine, a beer, a plain hot dog and a dozen oysters. A booking link is available.

Post No Bills is found at 253 Bushwick Avenue in Williamsburg, a one-minute walk from the Montrose Avenue station and the L train.

The Post No Bills happy hour is posted for every day, from opening into the evening. The list covers drafts, well drinks, cocktails, beer and two margaritas, including a grapefruit one and a fresh lime one. No booking link is attached.

French food is the category for Recette, a restaurant at 103 Havemeyer Street in Williamsburg, five minutes from the Metropolitan Avenue station and its G and L trains. The price range is moderate.

The Recette happy hour is a weekend one: Saturday and Sunday, from the morning into the afternoon. It is a discount on everything, and wine is tagged. Reservations are linked.

Reclamation Bar, at 817 Metropolitan Avenue in Williamsburg, is three minutes from the Graham Avenue station and the L train. Cocktails and a food deal are in its tags.

Monday through Thursday, the Reclamation Bar happy hour covers a long stretch of the afternoon into the early evening. Food and a basket of pizza are the named offers. No booking link is attached.

Sleepwalk sits at 251 Bushwick Avenue in Williamsburg, a bar one minute on foot from the Montrose Avenue station and the L train.

Every day has a happy hour at Sleepwalk, from opening until the early evening. The Sleepwalk happy hour applies to all drinks, which is the only offer detail the bar lists. No booking link is attached. Ask at the bar about anything beyond that.

Pete's Candy Store is at 709 Lorimer St. It is a bar in Williamsburg, six minutes from the Lorimer Street station and the G and L trains.

The Pete's Candy Store happy hour is on weekdays and runs from opening until the early evening. Draft, well drinks, wine and beer are listed, along with a beer and wine combination. Cheap beer and a food deal are among its tags.

Amsterdam Avenue in Morningside Heights has Max Soha, a restaurant at number 1274, tagged for cheap beer and wine. The 125th Street station, with the A, B, C and D trains, is a 6-minute walk.

Penne alla vodka, a drink, beers, Prosecco, red and white sangria, rose and white wine are all named in the Max Soha happy hour. It runs Monday through Thursday, in the late afternoon and early evening. No reservation link is listed.

Marina Cafe, a bar on Mansion Avenue in Staten Island, runs its happy hour on weekdays: from midday until close Monday through Thursday, and from midday into the early evening on Friday.

The Marina Cafe happy hour is listed without any named drinks or discounts, since the bar publishes the times but not the deal. The nearest station on file is Great Kills on the Staten Island Railway, a 15-minute walk. No booking link is on file.

South 4th Street, at number 90 in Williamsburg, is the address of South 4th Bar & Cafe, nine minutes from the Marcy Avenue station and the J, M and Z trains.

On weekdays, from the late afternoon into the evening, there is a happy hour. The South 4th Bar & Cafe happy hour is shown with times only, because the bar does not publish the deal. Ask at the bar about the drinks and food included. No booking link is attached.

In Williamsburg at 141 Leonard Street, Testo is a restaurant five minutes from the Broadway station and the G train. Wine is among its tags.

The Testo happy hour runs every day, in the early evening. The deal is a discount on all alcoholic drinks. That covers the whole week, including Saturday and Sunday. No booking link is attached, so ask the restaurant about tables.

Waterbury Street, at number 57 in Williamsburg, is where The Anchored Inn sits, a pub four minutes from the Montrose Avenue station and the L train.

The Anchored Inn happy hour is a weekday daytime one, from midday into the afternoon. It is a burger with a draft beer, which makes it a food and drink pairing rather than a general discount. No booking link is attached, so walk in or call ahead.

The Whiskey is at 524 Grand St. The bar is in Williamsburg, three minutes from the Metropolitan Avenue station and its G and L trains.

The happy hour is on weekdays, from opening until the evening, and all day on Monday. The Whiskey happy hour includes a beer and shot combination. Cocktails, wine and a food deal are in the tags. No booking link is attached.

Montrose Avenue is home to The Rosemont, a bar at number 63 in Williamsburg, three minutes from the Broadway station and the G train. Cocktails and wine are among its tags.

The Rosemont happy hour has two windows. On weekdays it starts in the early evening and runs into the evening, while Saturday and Sunday start earlier in the afternoon. Classic cocktails are the listed offer.

The Woods, a bar tagged for sports, is at 48 South 4th Street in Williamsburg, eleven minutes from the Marcy Avenue station and the J, M and Z trains.

The Woods happy hour runs Wednesday through Friday, from the late afternoon into the evening. The bar does not publish the deal, only the times. No booking link is attached. Ask at the bar about what the deal includes.

Tom & Joan's sits at 437 Graham Avenue in Williamsburg, a bar five minutes from the Graham Avenue station on the L train. Cocktails and wine are tagged.

Tuesday through Friday, the Tom & Joan's happy hour runs from opening until the evening. The named offers are a well drink, wine and Aperol. No booking link is attached. Check with the bar for current details.

On Broadway at number 174, Velvet Lounge is a bar in Williamsburg, five minutes from the Marcy Avenue station and the J, M and Z trains. Cocktails and wine are among its tags.

A happy hour runs every day from opening until the early evening. The Velvet Lounge happy hour has no published offers, so only the schedule is listed. Ask at the bar about the drinks and food included. No booking link is attached.

South 5th Street, at number 57 in Williamsburg, is the address of Wayne and Sons, a bar ten minutes from the Marcy Avenue station and the J, M and Z trains.

Monday through Thursday, in the late afternoon and early evening, the Wayne and Sons happy hour runs. Beers and bar snacks are the listed offers. A food deal is among its tags, and no booking link is attached.

Only on Fridays does the Joyce's Tavern happy hour run, and it spans the afternoon into the early evening. The tavern is a pub on Richmond Avenue in Staten Island, tagged for a food deal.

Eltingville on the Staten Island Railway is a 1-minute walk from the address. The pub publishes the times but not the deal, so what the food deal includes is not stated. No booking link is on file.

Piccolino Restaurant, an Italian place on Amboy Road in Staten Island, lists a long set of items in the Piccolino Restaurant happy hour. Chicken wings, mozzarella sticks with fries, penne vodka and fried zucchini with fries are listed with drinks including a lychee martini, margarita, beer and wine.

It runs Tuesday through Friday from the afternoon into the early evening. Great Kills on the Staten Island Railway is a 2-minute walk, and reservations go through the booking link.

Steiny's Pub stands on Hyatt Street in Staten Island, a 4-minute walk from St. George on the Staten Island Railway. The Steiny's Pub happy hour applies to all drinks and runs on weekdays, from the late afternoon into the early evening.

The venue is a pub, with no cuisine or menu details in its listing. No booking link is on file, so the live hours on this page are the thing to check before heading over.

The Rock House Bar & Grill lists a happy hour on every day of the week, from midday into the early evening, and carries an all-day tag. The bar is on Seguine Avenue in Staten Island.

The Rock House Bar & Grill happy hour is listed without any named drinks or food. The nearest station on file is Prince's Bay on the Staten Island Railway, a 17-minute walk. The listing has no booking link.

Select cocktails are the named offer at Maggie Mae's Bar, a Sunnyside bar on Queens Boulevard. The Maggie Mae's Bar happy hour is on weekdays and ends in the early evening, though no start time is listed.

The bar is tagged for cocktails and wine. The 7 train stops at 40th Street–Lowery Street, a 2-minute walk. No booking link is on file.

Monday through Saturday, The Monster Crab happy hour runs from the afternoon into the early evening. The Sunnyside restaurant is on Northern Boulevard and is tagged for cocktails and wine.

The restaurant publishes the times but not the deal, so the specific offers are not listed here. The M and R trains stop at 36th Street, a 5-minute walk. No booking link is on file.

Thursday to Sunday afternoons are when the Bitter Monk happy hour is listed, and it ends in the afternoon. The two named offers are a Vesper Martini and a Gaia Martini, both at set prices.

Bitter Monk is a cocktail-tagged bar on 34th Street in Sunset Park. The 36th Street station, served by the D, N and R trains, is a 4-minute walk. No start time or booking link is on file.

Found on 3rd Avenue in Sunset Park, Twist is a restaurant tagged for a rooftop, 5 minutes on foot from 45th Street on the R train. The Twist happy hour is listed every day except Tuesday, weekends included, from the afternoon into the early evening.

The restaurant publishes the times but not the deal, so the page cannot name any drinks or dishes. No booking link is on file.

Late night happy hour in NYC usually means a reverse happy hour: a second round of deals that starts after the dinner rush and, in a few cases, runs until the bar closes. Our list has a group of bars whose deal ends late in the evening or begins after dark, and a smaller set of them run a true late shift. Those are spread out, with the biggest group just south of Central Park around Times Square and Hell's Kitchen, and others in Gramercy, Murray Hill, the East Village, SoHo and the Upper East Side.

Expect a short menu rather than the full early-evening spread: draft beer, a beer-and-shot combo, a few house cocktails such as a Negroni or a spicy margarita. Most late deals skip Friday and Saturday and run Sunday through Wednesday or Thursday; Bobo and Soho Diner are the exceptions, saving theirs for the weekend. The subway runs all night, but trains come less often late at night, so check service before you order the last round.

picks.why: Barfly is a Gramercy sports bar on Third Avenue whose late happy hour starts well after dinner and runs into the small hours, Sunday through Thursday. The menu is built for a nightcap: Coors Light drafts, a beer-and-Jameson combo, other shots and a salted-rim spicy margarita. The 6 train at 23rd Street-Baruch College is a five-minute walk.

Tanner Smith's is a pub a block from the 57th Street-7th Avenue station (N, Q, R, W) and one of the few late deals that runs every night of the week, from late evening to close. It covers a Negroni, an Old Fashioned, an Aperol Spritz, Pinot Noir, and drafts like Founders Solid Gold and Fiddlehead IPA. Reservations are available.

Central Park Tavern on West 57th Street runs a late happy hour from Sunday to Thursday that starts late in the evening and lasts until close. The list covers an Old Fashioned, a spicy margarita, house red or white, a Hugo Spritz and Heineken on draft. Columbus Circle, with the 1, A, B, C and D, is three minutes away, and the bar takes reservations.

Meller's Sports Hub & Grill on Second Avenue is an Upper East Side sports bar with one of the latest deals on our list: it starts late at night and keeps going into the small hours, Sunday through Thursday. Wine, frozen drinks, mixed drinks, margaritas and Aperol are covered. The Q at 86th Street is two minutes away.

Bobo is a French bar and restaurant on West 10th Street that runs its happy hour only on Friday and Saturday nights, late, and only in the den. Expect martinis and wines by the glass. It takes reservations, and the 1 train at Christopher Street-Stonewall is about a minute's walk, which makes it an easy late stop in the Village.

Soho Diner turns into a late food stop on Friday and Saturday, when its happy hour runs in the small hours. The deal is about food rather than drinks: Soho hot wings, a smash burger, black olives and other plates from the diner menu. It sits on West Broadway, a minute from the A, C and E at Canal Street, and takes reservations.

Bar LunAtico on Halsey Street in Bed-Stuy runs its happy hour every day from early evening into late evening, and its own menu calls it happy hour dinner. That menu lists small plates such as Spanish olives and house focaccia, with vegan and gluten-free options marked. The A and C at Utica Avenue are about seven minutes away.

sections.h: What counts as late night here
sections.body: We put a bar on this page when one of its happy hour windows ends late in the evening or later, or starts after dark. That catches two different things. Most of them are regular after-work deals that simply run long and end around the time dinner wraps up. A smaller set are true reverse happy hours that open late, and those are the ones worth planning a night around. Reverse deals lean toward Sunday to Thursday, when bars have seats to fill.

Late menus are short and often served at the bar only, so grab a stool rather than a table. Menu prices do not include New York City sales tax of 8.875 percent or the tip, and 18 to 20 percent is standard. Late deals change more often than early ones, so look at each bar's last-checked date before heading out.

faq.a: On our list, Barfly in Gramercy, Tanner Smith's and Bartley's near Times Square, Central Park Tavern, Blue Haven in Murray Hill, Meller's Sports Hub & Grill on the Upper East Side and Lovers of Today in the East Village all run a second, late happy hour.
faq.q: Which NYC bars have a reverse happy hour?

faq.a: Yes, but fewer. Bobo in Greenwich Village and Soho Diner keep their late deals for Friday and Saturday, and Tanner Smith's runs its late deal every night, weekends included.
faq.q: Is there a late night happy hour on Friday or Saturday?

faq.a: Soho Diner's late deal is all food: wings, a smash burger and small plates. Bar LunAtico in Bed-Stuy serves a happy hour dinner menu every evening into late evening.
faq.q: Which late night happy hours include food?

faq.a: A few. Bar LunAtico in Bed-Stuy runs one daily, while American Brass in Long Island City and Sala Astoria in Astoria stretch their deals into the evening on certain nights.
faq.q: Are there late night happy hours outside Manhattan?

intro:
Cousin Larry's is listed as both a bar and an American restaurant, and it sits on Skillman Avenue in Sunnyside. The Cousin Larry's happy hour runs on weekdays and ends in the early evening, with a discount on bottles of wine.

From 52nd Street–Lincoln Avenue on the 7 train, the walk is about 4 minutes. The start time is not listed, so confirm the hours on this page.

Hell's Kitchen covers Midtown's West Side between Eighth Avenue and the Hudson River, roughly from 34th Street up to 59th Street, and on our list its bars crowd the avenues more than the side streets. Ninth Avenue is the spine, with a dense run through the upper 40s and 50s. Tenth Avenue adds a second strip, West 44th Street near the Port Authority Bus Terminal holds a pub and a tiki bar, and the top end sits close to Columbus Circle. The 50th Street station on the C and E is the nearest stop for more of these bars than any other.

Happy hour in Hell's Kitchen leans on simple, generous formats: two-for-one well drinks and half-price apps at VERS, half off every drink at the bar at Baires Grill, oysters and bubbly at Lady Blue. Many places sit a block or two from the Broadway theaters, so the early evening window doubles as a pre-show stop, and a few run a second window late at night. Daily deals are common, at VERS, Blue Seafood Bar, Sushi Damo, by & by and Chalong Southern Thai. Ninth Avenue is easy to walk, so start near 57th Street and work south.

picks.why: VERS is a bar at 714 Ninth Avenue whose happy hour runs every day until early evening. The house martini and margarita come at a set price, well drinks are buy one, get one, and appetizers are half price, one of the more generous combinations on our list. The 50th Street C and E stop is three minutes away; book on Resy.

Boxers HK describes itself as the neighborhood's gay sports bar, with screens for the games, and its weekday window runs later into the evening than most here. Beer, wine, well drinks and call drinks are all discounted Monday through Friday. It is at 742 Ninth Avenue, four minutes from 50th Street on the C and E, and our listing shows no booking link.

Friki Tiki is a tiki bar on West 44th Street with happy hour Tuesday through Sunday, so it covers the weekend when many neighbors do not. Zombies, frozen palomas and Hugo spritzes share the list with wine and canned beers such as Tecate and Red Stripe. The 42nd Street–Port Authority station is four minutes away, and Resy takes bookings.

Lady Blue, a cocktail bar at 363 West 46th Street, pairs a dozen oysters with a bottle of bubbly on weekdays and also discounts select small plates and a few cocktails, such as a limoncello lemon drop, a house margarita and a classic old fashioned. Draft beer and wine are on the list too. Walk five minutes from 50th Street, or reserve through Resy.

Baires Grill on West 50th Street keeps the math easy: on weekdays every drink at the bar is half off, premium spirits, wines and beers included, and food is served at the bar during the window as well. It is two minutes from the 50th Street C and E stop, and OpenTable handles reservations if you would rather book ahead.

The Brazen Tavern is an Irish pub at 356 West 44th Street with a food-heavy weekday happy hour: housemade chicken fingers, classic hummus, glazed wings, mango habanero boneless wings and cauliflower bites, among others. The window opens mid-afternoon and runs into the early evening, so it suits a meal before a show. The 42nd Street–Port Authority station is three minutes away.

Central Park Tavern on West 57th Street is the late-night option at the north end: its happy hour starts late in the evening and runs to close, Sunday through Thursday. Old fashioneds, spicy margaritas, house wines, Hugo spritzes and Heineken on draft are on it. 59th Street–Columbus Circle, with the 1, A, B, C and D, is three minutes away.

sections.body: The C and E stop at 50th Street on Eighth Avenue, the closest station for many bars on our list, mostly along Ninth Avenue and the side streets of the upper 40s. Farther south, the 42nd Street–Port Authority complex brings in twelve lines and covers West 42nd to 44th Streets. The north end is easiest from 59th Street–Columbus Circle on the 1, A, B, C and D. Tenth Avenue spots are a longer walk from any of these, about seven or eight minutes, and Kings of Kobe on West 42nd Street is nearest to 34th Street–Hudson Yards on the 7.

Add New York's 8.875 percent sales tax to the menu price, then tip 18 to 20 percent. Several deals here are bar only, including Baires Grill and Kings of Kobe, so a table can cost more. Menus in this part of town change often; check the last-checked date on each listing before you plan around one.

faq.a: Central Park Tavern on West 57th Street runs a late happy hour Sunday through Thursday. by & by on Tenth Avenue adds a late window every night, Blue Seafood Bar lists a daily late-evening deal, and 5 Napkin Burger on Ninth Avenue has a late window Sunday through Thursday.
faq.q: Is there late-night happy hour in Hell's Kitchen?

faq.a: VERS, Blue Seafood Bar, Sushi Damo, by & by, Chalong Southern Thai, Kings of Kobe, Jaz and Kashkaval Garden run every day. Friki Tiki goes Tuesday through Sunday, and Alfie's on Ninth Avenue has a weekend window.
faq.q: Which Hell's Kitchen bars have happy hour on weekends?

faq.a: VERS has buy-one-get-one well drinks and half-price appetizers every day, and Baires Grill takes half off all drinks at the bar on weekdays. For a set-price deal instead, The Molly Pitcher Club on Ninth Avenue prices wine, well drinks and canned beer the same Tuesday through Friday.
faq.q: Where can I get two-for-one or half-price drinks in Hell's Kitchen?

faq.a: The Brazen Tavern has the biggest food list, with chicken fingers, hummus and several kinds of wings. Anejo serves salsas, nachos and seasonal tacos, As is NYC offers a cheese board and olives, Vida Verde has chorizo empanadas and fries, and Lady Blue discounts select small plates.
faq.q: Which Hell's Kitchen happy hours include food?

intro:
Halloween parties NYC 2026 get a gift from the calendar: October 31 falls on a Saturday, so the party weekend runs from Thursday the 29th through Sunday, November 1, and our list has parties on every one of those nights. Friday and Saturday carry most of them, across Brooklyn, Manhattan and Queens.

Saturday is also parade night. The Village Halloween Parade marches north up Sixth Avenue from Canal Street to 15th Street that evening; anyone in costume can march and watching is free, according to the parade organizers. The avenue is barricaded while it runs and you cannot cross it, so if your party is on the other side, plan the crossing before you set out or head over after the parade.

The other date to know: daylight saving time ends at 2 a.m. on Sunday, November 1, when clocks go back to 1 a.m., per NIST. Saturday parties that run into the early morning get an extra hour, and so does the trip home. If you want more than one night, Thursday and Sunday are the quieter bookends, with a free 80s night in Bushwick on Thursday and a noon-to-midnight Circoloco session at the Brooklyn Navy Yard on Sunday.

picks.why: Nightbreed is the low-key opener: an 80s night downstairs at Purgatory on Central Avenue in Bushwick on Thursday, October 29, with Jamie K on the decks. Doors open at 8 p.m. and it wraps at midnight, so it works on a work night. It was listed free on DICE when we checked, it is 21+, and DICE shows no door sales.

SILOWEEN: Asylum puts Maesic at SILO Brooklyn on Scott Avenue in Bushwick on Friday, October 30, with a genre spread from afro-house and disco to techno. Doors at 10 p.m., running until 4 a.m. SILO's own FAQ says 21+ events need a government-issued photo ID or passport at entry, and that the venue is wheelchair accessible.

Nevermore is a goth rave at DROM on Avenue A in the East Village, and its Halloween edition lands on Friday, October 30 with drum and bass on the genre list. Doors open at 11 p.m. and it runs until 3 a.m., 21+. Tickets are on DICE, where refunds are limited to 24 hours after purchase.

The Halloween Dance Cruise boards the Liberty Belle at Pier 36 on South Street on Saturday, October 31, with a playlist that covers 80s, EDM, hip-hop, K-pop and pop. Boarding starts at 7 p.m. and the cruise ends at 11 p.m., so a late party on land is still possible afterward. It is 21+, sold on DICE by NYPartyCruise.

Slash Her pairs a Halloween party with a drag show at Cassette on Forest Avenue in Ridgewood, Queens, on Saturday, October 31. Nicky O and Jo Disco are on the bill and disco is the listed sound. Doors at 10 p.m. and it runs until 4 a.m., an hour longer than it looks because clocks fall back overnight. It is 21+.

Bloodlust is a Halloween dance party at Sleepwalk on Bushwick Avenue on Saturday, October 31, from 11 p.m. to 4 a.m. It was listed free on DICE when we checked, and entry runs through DICE rather than the door, so claim a spot early. It is 21+, a simple late finish if you spent the evening at the parade.

Horse Meat Disco brings its disco party to Knockdown Center in Maspeth, Queens, on Saturday, October 31, from 11 p.m. to 5 a.m. It is already sold out on DICE, so it is here for anyone holding a ticket or hoping some come back. Knockdown accepts a US state-issued photo ID or an original passport for its 21+ entry.

Teksupport's Circoloco Halloween Sunday runs from noon to midnight at Brooklyn Storehouse in the Brooklyn Navy Yard on Sunday, November 1. The lineup is long: Bedouin, Chloé Caillet, Dean Turnley, Dixon, Jimi Jules, Miguelle & Tons, Prospa and Rossi. The Friday edition is sold out; Sunday was still on sale when we checked. It is 21+.

sections.body: Thursday is the soft start, with only a handful of parties on the list. Friday is the second-busiest night, with electronic bookings at Brooklyn rooms like SILO and Signal and a string of rooftop and hotel parties in Manhattan. Saturday is Halloween itself: the most parties, the parade on Sixth Avenue, and the boat parties, which board in the evening. Sunday is for day-into-night sessions like Circoloco and a few dance parties that end before midnight, a good fit if you have to work on Monday.

Tickets: several Halloween nights, including Horse Meat Disco and Circoloco's Friday, are already sold out, and the parties we picked sell through DICE with no door sales listed, so buy before you travel. DICE refunds are usually limited to 24 hours after purchase. ID: every pick on this page is 21+, and venues such as SILO and Knockdown Center ask for a government-issued photo ID or passport. Subway: trains run all night, but Sixth Avenue cannot be crossed during the parade, so allow extra time if your route goes through the Village. Costumes: rules are set by each promoter, so check the party page; for the parade itself, only people in costume can march.

faq.a: Saturday, October 31, in the evening. It marches north on Sixth Avenue from Canal Street to 15th Street. Watching is free, and only people in costume can march, according to the parade organizers at halloween-nyc.com.
faq.q: When is the Village Halloween Parade in 2026?

faq.a: Yes. Daylight saving time ends at 2 a.m. on Sunday, November 1, and clocks go back to 1 a.m., per NIST. Saturday-night parties that run until 4 or 5 a.m. last an hour longer than the times suggest.
faq.q: Do the clocks change on Halloween weekend 2026?

faq.a: Yes. Late parties such as Bloodlust on Bushwick Avenue, Slash Her in Ridgewood and Horse Meat Disco in Maspeth open at 10 or 11 p.m., which leaves time to watch the parade first. Boat parties that board in the early evening overlap with it.
faq.q: Can I do the parade and a party on the same night?

faq.a: A few. Circoloco's Sunday edition at Brooklyn Storehouse runs from noon to midnight, SILO Brooklyn has a Sunday night bill, Somewhere Nowhere hosts a drum and bass night, 1 Hotel Brooklyn Bridge has a Day of the Dead party, and Bar 13 near Union Square throws a Sunday Funday dance party from late afternoon.
faq.q: Are there Halloween parties on Sunday, November 1?

faq.a: Do not count on it. The DICE listings for our picks show no door sales, and where a venue such as SILO does sell at the door, it is first come, first served. Buy ahead and keep the ticket in the app.
faq.q: Can I buy Halloween party tickets at the door?

intro:
Crown Heights spreads across central Brooklyn east of Prospect Heights, with Eastern Parkway cutting through its middle. The places we recommend for Crown Heights happy hour sit on the western side of the neighborhood, along Nostrand Avenue and Rogers Avenue. Nostrand Station Bar & Lounge is right by the Nostrand Avenue stop on the 3, at Eastern Parkway. Hello Bar Bk and The Green Room PLG are farther south near the Sterling Street station on the 2 and 5, where Crown Heights meets Prospect Lefferts Gardens, the PLG in The Green Room's name.

It is a short list, but each spot has its own angle. Nostrand Station builds its deal around margaritas, rum punch and themed food nights, The Green Room sells small plates at a set price, and Hello Bar keeps things simple with cocktails, wine and beer. Between them, every day of the week has at least one option. The Green Room is the one to pick for a Monday deal, while Hello Bar covers Friday through Sunday.

picks.why: Nostrand Station Bar & Lounge is a one-minute walk from the Nostrand Avenue stop on the 3. From late afternoon Tuesday through Friday it discounts beers, shots, sangria, rum punch and margaritas. The food specials change by day: Taco Tuesday pairs two tacos and street corn with a margarita, and Wing Wednesday brings wings and fries with a rum punch.

Hello Bar Bk on Nostrand Avenue runs its happy hour six days a week, Tuesday through Sunday, in the early evening, with cocktails, wine and beer each at a set price. The bar says its kitchen stays open late, so dinner can follow the deal. The Sterling Street stop on the 2 and 5 is three minutes away on foot.

The Green Room PLG on Rogers Avenue is the food-first option: its happy hour sets one price for small plates such as Korean chicken wings, chicken tacos, firecracker gyoza and a vegan lentil soup. It runs Sunday through Thursday in the early evening. Sterling Street on the 2 and 5 is three minutes away, and tables can be booked on Resy.

sections.body: Two subway routes cover our picks. The 3 stops at Nostrand Avenue on Eastern Parkway, a minute from Nostrand Station Bar & Lounge. The 2 and 5 stop at Sterling Street, about three minutes on foot from both Hello Bar Bk on Nostrand Avenue and The Green Room PLG on Rogers Avenue. Walking between the two stations takes a while, so pick one area per night.

Prices on the menu are before New York's 8.875 percent sales tax, and you should add an 18 to 20 percent tip. Happy hour terms can be limited to bar seating, so confirm when you order. We list the date each bar was last checked; look at it before you go, as deals here change.

faq.a: Hello Bar Bk runs happy hour Tuesday through Sunday, and The Green Room PLG runs Sunday through Thursday. Nostrand Station Bar & Lounge is Tuesday to Friday only.
faq.q: Which Crown Heights bars have happy hour on Sunday?

faq.a: The Green Room PLG sets one price for small plates like Korean chicken wings, chicken tacos and gyoza. Nostrand Station Bar & Lounge has day-specific combos, with tacos on Tuesday and wings on Wednesday.
faq.q: Where can I eat during happy hour in Crown Heights?

faq.a: Of our three picks, The Green Room PLG on Rogers Avenue is the one with a Monday deal, since it runs Sunday through Thursday.
faq.q: Is there a Monday happy hour in Crown Heights?

faq.a: Nostrand Avenue on the 3 for Nostrand Station Bar & Lounge, and Sterling Street on the 2 and 5 for Hello Bar Bk and The Green Room PLG.
faq.q: What subway stops are closest to Crown Heights happy hours?

intro:
Gowanus Gardens, a pub in Gowanus, is at 256 4th Ave, and Union Street on the R line is a 1-minute walk away. It is tagged for cocktails.

The Gowanus Gardens happy hour runs on weekdays from late afternoon into the early evening, with money off the house and non-alcoholic cocktail menu and off all taps, bottles and cans. It is a drinks deal; food is not part of it. Walk-ins appear to be the only option, since no booking link is published.

Harlem runs across upper Manhattan from the north end of Central Park into the 150s, and our list spreads across its full width. On the west side, the bars follow the 1 train along Broadway and Amsterdam Avenue: the Baylander a short walk from 125th Street, Lola La Marina on West 133rd Street, Cocteleria Perla Negra and Patrick's on the Hill near City College, and The Honey Well up near 145th Street. Central Harlem has Sylvia's on Malcolm X Boulevard, Ponty Bistro on Adam Clayton Powell Jr. Boulevard and BLVD Bistro on Frederick Douglass Boulevard.

Restaurants carry most of the deals, so food is a big part of a Harlem happy hour: Caribbean bites at Patrick's, tacos and a giant pretzel at the Baylander, deviled eggs and Cajun shrimp at The Honey Well, starters at BLVD Bistro. BLVD Bistro, Ponty Bistro and The Honey Well run their deals every day, and Lola La Marina pours two-for-one drinks on weekdays. Practical tip: the 2 and 3 at 125th Street and 135th Street are the quickest way to the central Harlem picks, while the 1 covers everything on the west side.

picks.why: Sylvia's is a Southern restaurant on Malcolm X Boulevard, two minutes from the 125th Street 2 and 3 station. Its weekday happy hour covers wines by the glass, prosecco and other bubbles, beer and cocktails like the Harlem Blues Margarita, and the menu lists zero-proof favorites too. It runs Monday through Friday from mid-afternoon, and reservations are available.

Ponty Bistro on Adam Clayton Powell Jr. Boulevard runs happy hour every day of the week, weekends included, with beers, wines, house cocktails and bar bites all on special. That daily schedule makes it one of the more flexible picks uptown. The 135th Street 2 and 3 station is a five-minute walk.

Patrick's on the Hill is a Caribbean bar and kitchen on Amsterdam Avenue, five minutes from the 137th Street-City College 1 stop. Its happy hour, Tuesday through Friday in the early evening, pairs cocktails with bites such as Jamaican beef cocktail patties, salmon cakes, its OMG Wings and french fries. Monday is not part of the deal.

Baylander Steel Beach is a restaurant whose happy hour runs Tuesday through Friday in the afternoon and leans on food: a giant pretzel with melted jalapeño cheese, fresh lime falafel tacos, grilled shrimp tacos and Mexican street corn ribs. It takes reservations, and the 125th Street 1 station is about six minutes away on foot.

The Honey Well is a restaurant at 3604 Broadway, three minutes from the 145th Street 1 stop, with happy hour every day in the late afternoon. Classic cocktails lead, with deviled eggs, cocktail meatballs and Cajun shrimp to eat. Its backyard has no heaters, so save it for a mild evening, and book on Resy if you need a table.

Cocteleria Perla Negra is a bar on Broadway near City College, four minutes from the 137th Street 1 station, with a happy hour that runs Tuesday through Sunday in the early evening, so both weekend days are covered. Chicken wings are on the menu, and the bar also lists an all-day Taco Tuesday and discounted wine bottles on Wednesdays.

BLVD Bistro is a restaurant on Frederick Douglass Boulevard, a minute from the 116th Street B and C stop, that lists its happy hour as all day, every day. Its happy hour page starts with food: lobster and crab cakes, BLVD wings and a watermelon and goat cheese salad. It takes reservations, useful if you are heading up on a weekend.

sections.body: The 1 is the spine of west Harlem on our list: 125th Street for the Baylander, 137th Street-City College for Patrick's on the Hill, Cocteleria Perla Negra and Lola La Marina, and 145th Street for The Honey Well. In central Harlem, the 2 and 3 stop at 125th Street near Sylvia's and at 135th Street near Ponty Bistro. BLVD Bistro is a minute from the B and C at 116th Street.

Harlem menus, like everywhere else in the city, show prices before the 8.875 percent sales tax and before the tip, and 18 to 20 percent is the norm. Patrick's and the Baylander skip Mondays, and The Honey Well's backyard is unheated. We note when each deal was last checked; if it has been a while, call ahead.

faq.a: Ponty Bistro, BLVD Bistro and The Honey Well run every day, and Cocteleria Perla Negra runs Tuesday through Sunday.
faq.q: Which Harlem bars have happy hour on weekends?

faq.a: Patrick's on the Hill has Caribbean bites like beef patties and salmon cakes, Baylander Steel Beach has tacos and a giant pretzel, The Honey Well serves deviled eggs, meatballs and Cajun shrimp, Ponty Bistro discounts bar bites, and BLVD Bistro lists starters such as lobster and crab cakes.
faq.q: Where can I get happy hour food in Harlem?

faq.a: Yes. Lola La Marina on West 133rd Street pours two-for-one drinks Monday through Friday from late afternoon into the early evening, five minutes from the 137th Street-City College 1 stop.
faq.q: Is there a two-for-one happy hour in Harlem?

faq.a: Yes. Sylvia's runs happy hour Monday through Friday from mid-afternoon, with wines by the glass, prosecco, beer and cocktails such as the Harlem Blues Margarita.
faq.q: Does Sylvia's have a happy hour?

intro:
Sadie's is the name of an American bar at 19 Fulton St in the Financial District, Manhattan, and tags point to cocktails and outdoor seating. The Sadie's happy hour runs on weekdays, though only the times are published and no deals are named.

Fulton Street station, with the 2, 3, 4, 5, A, C, J and Z trains, is a five-minute walk. Live hours are on this page.

Olea, at 171 Lafayette Ave in Fort Greene, is a bar whose listing describes tapas, Mediterranean food and brunch. Clinton-Washington Avenues on the G line is a 4-minute walk.

The Olea happy hour is open Monday through Thursday, ending in the early evening. The bar publishes the times but not the deal, so the drinks and plates covered are not named here. It is tagged for cocktails and wine. The price range is shown as two dollar signs.

Oysters are the one tag on Strange Delight, a restaurant in Fort Greene. The nearest subway is Fulton Street on the G line, a 1-minute walk; the address is 63 Lafayette Ave.

The Strange Delight happy hour covers Monday through Thursday, in the early evening. The restaurant publishes the times but not the deal, so the food and drinks included are not named. Reservations can be booked through a SevenRooms link, which makes planning a visit around that window straightforward.

American cooking is the focus at Walters, a restaurant at 166 Dekalb Ave in Fort Greene, tagged for wine and oysters. The nearest station is Fulton Street on the G line, 4 minutes on foot.

Oysters are the named item in the Walters happy hour, offered at a discount. The window runs Monday through Thursday in the late afternoon and early evening. The listing shows a price range of two dollar signs. Check the live listing on this page for current oyster pricing.

Winnie's sits on West 52nd Street in Times Square and counts as a cocktail bar. The closest subway stop is 50th Street (the 1 train), a two-minute walk away.

The Winnie's happy hour comes from Tuesday through Friday, ending in the evening. Deals named for it: wine, Aperol, well mixed drinks, espresso martinis and a light draft spritz.

Australian cooking is the focus at Dudleys, a restaurant at 85 Orchard Street on the Lower East Side. Its happy hour runs every day and ends in the afternoon, and the Dudleys happy hour has times but no published deal. The Delancey Street station, served by the F, J, M and Z trains, is two minutes away on foot. A weekend tag appears on the page.

Jackson Heights sits in northwest Queens, and the elevated 7 train over Roosevelt Avenue ties our list together. Most of the bars are closest to the 82nd Street and 90th Street-Elmhurst Avenue stations, either on Roosevelt itself or north of it on 37th Avenue and Northern Boulevard, where Barzola, Raices Colombianas, Uncle Peter's, Fabrika and Addictive Wine and Tapas line up. At the western end, Upstairs Cocktail Bar and Ovidio's are near the 69th Street stop, and Sabay Thai is two minutes from the big Roosevelt Avenue hub.

The drinks lean Latin: margaritas, mojitos, piña coladas, sangria and pisco cocktails, along with wine by the glass and plates like mussels. Long afternoon windows are common, with Barzola, Bistro Eloise and Raices Colombianas starting their Jackson Heights happy hour early in the day. Tip: the Northern Boulevard spots are a ten- to twelve-minute walk from the 7, so plan your route before hopping between them.

picks.why: Uncle Peter's is a restaurant on Northern Boulevard with a weekday happy hour of select wines by the glass, beers, sangrias, margaritas and mojitos, holidays excluded. It runs Monday to Friday in the late afternoon, and the regular cocktail list includes pisco drinks like the Fresa Fizz. Leave time for the walk: the 82nd Street-Jackson Heights 7 station is about eleven minutes away.

Addictive Wine and Tapas on Northern Boulevard runs its happy hour every day, weekends included, with sparkling, white, rosé and red wines by the glass. It takes reservations. Two practical notes: it is about twelve minutes on foot from the 90th Street-Elmhurst Avenue 7, and the restaurant adds a fee to card payments.

Barzola is a cocktail bar on 37th Avenue whose weekday happy hour starts in the early afternoon and runs into the evening, with half-price drinks across the list, including mojitos, margaritas, piña coladas and Moscow mules. It is one of the longer weekday windows on our list. The 90th Street-Elmhurst Avenue 7 station is four minutes away.

Bistro Eloise on 31st Avenue runs happy hour Tuesday through Friday from lunchtime into the evening. House wine, mimosas, mojitos and margaritas are on special, and there is a combo of mussels with a glass of house wine. It takes reservations. Transit is the catch: our data puts the nearest subway, 65th Street on the M and R, about sixteen minutes away on foot.

Upstairs Cocktail Bar is on the second floor of 71-22 Roosevelt Avenue, two minutes from the 69th Street 7 stop. Its happy hour runs Monday through Saturday in the early evening, one of the few Saturday options here, with a gimlet, a classic margarita, a martini and a Moscow or whiskey mule with ginger beer on the menu.

Raices Colombianas is a Colombian bar and restaurant on 37th Avenue, five minutes from the 90th Street-Elmhurst Avenue 7 station. Its happy hour runs Monday through Thursday from early afternoon into the evening, so it works for a late lunch that turns into drinks. Item details are missing from our data, so ask what the deal covers when you sit down.

sections.body: The 7 is the line to know. 82nd Street-Jackson Heights is the closest stop to Uncle Peter's and Fabrika on Northern Boulevard. 90th Street-Elmhurst Avenue serves Barzola, Raices Colombianas and Addictive Wine and Tapas, and 69th Street is closest to Upstairs and Ovidio's. Jackson Heights-Roosevelt Avenue adds the E, F, M and R, two minutes from Sabay Thai.

Expect the bill to come in above the menu: NYC adds 8.875 percent sales tax, and a tip of 18 to 20 percent is customary. Uncle Peter's and Fabrika exclude holidays. Check the last-checked date on each listing, especially for the Northern Boulevard spots that take a longer walk.

faq.a: Upstairs Cocktail Bar runs Monday through Saturday, and Addictive Wine and Tapas runs every day of the week.
faq.q: Which Jackson Heights bars have happy hour on Saturday?

faq.a: Bistro Eloise starts around lunchtime Tuesday through Friday, Barzola starts in the early afternoon on weekdays, and Raices Colombianas starts in the early afternoon Monday through Thursday.
faq.q: Which Jackson Heights happy hours start in the early afternoon?

faq.a: Yes. Addictive Wine and Tapas runs daily.
faq.q: Is there a Sunday happy hour in Jackson Heights?

faq.a: The 7 at 82nd Street and at 90th Street-Elmhurst Avenue cover most of the list, with 69th Street for the western end and Jackson Heights-Roosevelt Avenue for the E, F, M and R.
faq.q: Which subway stops are closest to Jackson Heights happy hours?

intro:
Fort Greene sits just east of Downtown Brooklyn and is home to Fort Greene Park, and our happy hour list follows its east-west streets. DeKalb Avenue carries most of it: Walters and Karasu share the address 166 DeKalb, with Colonia Verde and The Great Georgiana further east toward Clinton Hill. Olea is on Lafayette Avenue, Bar Francis is down on Fulton Street, and The Rockwell Place is on the Downtown Brooklyn side near Nevins Street.

The G is the neighborhood line, with the Fulton Street and Clinton-Washington Avenues stations within five minutes of most picks. Expect a Monday-to-Thursday rhythm: Walters, Karasu, Colonia Verde, Olea and Strange Delight all stop before Friday, and nothing on our list runs on the weekend, so a Fort Greene happy hour is a weeknight plan. The deals range from oysters and wine to sake, highballs and tapas. Tip: Karasu's menu is served at the bar only, so head straight for a stool.

picks.why: Walters is an American restaurant at 166 DeKalb Avenue whose happy hour, Monday through Thursday in the late afternoon, brings half-price oysters, wine, beer and frozen specials. It is four minutes from the Fulton Street G and takes reservations. The window closes on the early side, so this one rewards leaving work on time.

Karasu is a cocktail bar listed at the same 166 DeKalb Avenue address as Walters, with a bar-only happy hour Monday through Thursday. Select sake, a classic Toki highball, a Midori rum highball, a Kirin with a whisky shot, cold edamame, potato salad, the Karasu burger and furikake fries are on it. The Fulton Street G is four minutes away.

Bar Francis is a bar at 810 Fulton Street with a Wednesday-to-Friday happy hour in the late afternoon. Each month it features two house cocktails alongside a selection of wine and beer, plus oysters and bar snacks. It is three minutes from the C at Clinton-Washington Avenues, and reservations are available through Resy.

Olea is a Mediterranean tapas bar at 171 Lafayette Avenue with a Monday-to-Thursday happy hour, holidays excluded, covering beer, wine, sangria, cocktails and a selection of tapas. It sits four minutes from the Clinton-Washington Avenues G station and takes reservations, so a group can lock in a table for the short window.

The Great Georgiana is a bar at 248 DeKalb Avenue with a weekday happy hour, Friday included, through the late afternoon. Pacifico draft, house wines in red, white or rosé, well liquors and a Modelito with a shot are on the drinks side, with seasoned fries and chicken bites to eat. The Clinton-Washington Avenues G is three minutes away.

The Rockwell Place is a cocktail bar at 31 Rockwell Place, two minutes from Nevins Street on the 2, 3, 4 and 5, with happy hour Tuesday through Friday in the early evening. By its own description, the bar skips garnishes in favor of house-made aromatic tinctures. Specific drinks are not in our data, so treat it as a cocktail bar first and a deal second.

Colonia Verde is a restaurant at 219 DeKalb Avenue running happy hour Monday through Thursday in the early evening, with weekday lunch and weekend brunch on its schedule as well. What the deal covers is not in our data yet, so ask your server. It takes reservations, and the Clinton-Washington Avenues G is five minutes away.

sections.body: The G does most of the work. Fulton Street is four minutes from Walters and Karasu and a minute from Strange Delight, and Clinton-Washington Avenues serves Colonia Verde, Olea and The Great Georgiana. Bar Francis is three minutes from the C at Clinton-Washington Avenues on Fulton Street. From Manhattan, the 2, 3, 4 and 5 at Nevins Street put you two minutes from The Rockwell Place.

Prices on the menu leave out the 8.875 percent NYC sales tax and the tip, usually 18 to 20 percent. Karasu's deal is bar-only and Olea skips holidays. Most places here stop on Thursday, so check each bar's days, and its last-checked date, before planning a Friday.

faq.a: Walters on DeKalb Avenue serves half-price oysters Monday through Thursday, Bar Francis on Fulton Street includes oysters Wednesday through Friday, and Strange Delight, which runs a Monday-to-Thursday happy hour, is tagged for oysters on our site.
faq.q: Where can I get happy hour oysters in Fort Greene?

faq.a: The Great Georgiana, The Rockwell Place and Bar Francis all include Friday.
faq.q: Which Fort Greene bars have happy hour on Friday?

faq.a: Yes. Karasu on DeKalb Avenue serves select sake, highballs, Kirin and snacks like edamame and furikake fries at the bar, Monday through Thursday.
faq.q: Is there a sake happy hour in Fort Greene?

faq.a: Not on our current list. Every Fort Greene happy hour we track runs on weekdays only, most of them Monday through Thursday.
faq.q: Do any Fort Greene happy hours run on weekends?

intro:
Saturday is the thinnest day of the week for happy hour on our list, far below the Thursday count. Manhattan has most of them, led by Times Square, the Upper West Side, the Upper East Side, the East Village and Greenwich Village. Williamsburg leads Brooklyn and Bushwick follows, while Queens has a smaller group.

A Saturday happy hour in NYC often looks different from the weekday version. Many bars move it to the daytime, as a brunch-hour or early-afternoon window that ends before evening: Sir Henry's near Times Square, The Malt House in Greenwich Village and Third Avenue Ale House on the Upper East Side all wrap up by mid-afternoon. Others, like The Rosemont in Williamsburg and Tre on the Lower East Side, start in the afternoon and keep going into the evening. Tip: weekend windows are often shorter and earlier than weekday ones, so check the hours shown beside each listing before you leave home.

picks.why: The Rosemont is a cocktail and wine bar on Montrose Avenue in Williamsburg whose Saturday happy hour starts in the afternoon, earlier than on weekdays, and runs into the evening. Classic cocktails like the Old Fashioned, Manhattan, Negroni and Sazerac, plus well drinks, draft beers and wine, are on special. The Broadway G is three minutes away.

Bitter Monk is a cocktail bar on 34th Street in Sunset Park with happy hour Thursday through Sunday until mid-afternoon, so on Saturday it is a daytime stop. Cocktails include a Clover Club, a Vesper martini and a Gaia martini, built on Atheras Botanical spirits. The 36th Street D, N and R station is four minutes away.

Tre is a restaurant on Ludlow Street on the Lower East Side whose weekend happy hour starts in the early afternoon and runs to early evening, a longer window than its weekday version. House white, red and rosé wines, Champagne and Aperol are on the drinks list, with bites as well. The 2nd Avenue F is three minutes away.

Sir Henry's is a cocktail bar on Eighth Avenue near Times Square with a Saturday and Sunday happy hour that ends by mid-afternoon. It is built around shareables: a Greek yogurt parfait, avocado deviled eggs, smoked salmon dip with sourdough and sausage roll bites. The 50th Street C and E is two minutes away, and reservations are available.

Third Avenue Ale House is a pub on Third Avenue on the Upper East Side with a weekend happy hour from around lunchtime to mid-afternoon, plus a late-night happy hour on food and drinks every day, according to its own menu. That gives Saturday two windows. The 96th Street Q station is four minutes away.

Bob's Your Uncle, which calls itself a neighborhood bar, sits on Columbus Avenue on the Upper West Side and runs a weekend happy hour from mid-afternoon into the early evening. It takes money off well drinks and draft beer and adds select cocktails. The 103rd Street B and C is four minutes away, and weekday deals run Monday through Thursday.

The Malt House is a pub on Thompson Street in Greenwich Village whose happy hour runs only on Saturday and Sunday, until mid-afternoon. Jumbo wings and Parmesan herbed fries are on the food list. The West 4th Street-Washington Square station, served by the A, B, C, D, E, F and M, is five minutes away, and reservations are available.

sections.body: Saturday deals split into two camps. Daytime windows that end by mid-afternoon include Sir Henry's, The Malt House, Third Avenue Ale House and Bitter Monk. Evening windows include The Rosemont, Tre and Bob's Your Uncle, and for a late crowd, Bobo in Greenwich Village and Soho Diner run happy hours on Friday and Saturday nights.

Weekend tabs still carry the 8.875 percent NYC sales tax, and a tip of 18 to 20 percent is standard. Saturday windows are often short and early, and some bars set different weekend hours than weekday ones, so read the days carefully. The last-checked date on each listing tells you how fresh our information is.

faq.a: Some do. Our list has far fewer Saturday happy hours than Thursday ones, with the most in Times Square, the Upper West Side and the Upper East Side.
faq.q: Do NYC bars have happy hour on Saturday?

faq.a: Sir Henry's near Times Square, The Malt House in Greenwich Village, Third Avenue Ale House on the Upper East Side and Bitter Monk in Sunset Park all run Saturday deals that end by mid-afternoon.
faq.q: Where can I find a Saturday daytime happy hour?

faq.a: Yes. Bobo in Greenwich Village runs a late happy hour in its den, Soho Diner serves happy hour food late on Saturday night, and The Rosemont in Williamsburg runs into the evening.
faq.q: Is there a Saturday night happy hour in NYC?

faq.a: Times Square leads on our list, followed by Williamsburg, the Upper West Side and the Upper East Side.
faq.q: Which neighborhoods have the most Saturday happy hours?

intro:
Greenpoint is Brooklyn's northernmost neighborhood, bordered by the East River and Newtown Creek, and its happy hours cluster along two corridors. Manhattan Avenue, the main commercial street, holds Papacito's, Troost and Breeze, while Nassau Avenue near McCarren Park has Keg & Lantern, Raizes Churrascaria and Diamond Lil, with Ray's around the corner on Lorimer Street. Closer to the river, Panzón and Black Rabbit sit on Greenpoint Avenue and Nerina is on Commercial Street.

Only the G train serves the neighborhood, stopping at Nassau Avenue and Greenpoint Avenue, and nearly every bar on our list is within an eight-minute walk of one of them. The deals skew toward cheap beer, margaritas and bar food like tacos, nachos, wings and burgers, and most run Monday to Friday. For a Greenpoint happy hour on a weekend, Papacito's, Troost and Black Rabbit run every day, and Kinoko adds Saturday.

picks.why: Panzón is a Mexican bar and restaurant at 23 Greenpoint Avenue, toward the river, with a weekday happy hour that covers margaritas, micheladas, non-alcoholic cocktails, Modelo and Victoria, money off draft beer and wine, single tacos, adobo fries and guacamole with tostadas. The Greenpoint Avenue G is six minutes away, and Resy takes bookings.

Papacito's on Manhattan Avenue lists a daily afternoon happy hour with two-for-one frozen margaritas, Tecate and Modelo cans, a house margarita, pints of sangria, a tequila-and-Tecate pairing, nachos and tacos. It also advertises a third happy hour in the last hour of every night. The Greenpoint Avenue G station is three minutes away.

Troost is a cocktail and wine bar at 1011 Manhattan Avenue with a short daily happy hour, weekends included: money off beers, cocktails and house wine by the glass or quartino, plus a tap Negroni. It is three minutes from the Greenpoint Avenue G, so it works as a quick first stop on a Saturday or Sunday.

Keg & Lantern is a brewpub and sports bar at 97 Nassau Avenue, one minute from the Nassau Avenue G. The weekday happy hour is simple: any draft at one set price, Monday through Friday in the early evening. It also takes reservations, which is handy if you are bringing a group.

Ray's is a bar on Lorimer Street, two minutes from the Nassau Avenue G, with a weekday happy hour that runs until the early evening. The list mixes drinks and food: High Life, well shots, a beer and a shot, house cocktails, a burger with a Peroni, a martini with fries, hot wings and a High Life bucket. Resy handles reservations.

Breeze is a Sichuan and dim sum restaurant at 595 Manhattan Avenue, two minutes from the Nassau Avenue G. Its happy hour runs on weekdays from lunchtime into the evening, with any craft cocktail on the menu at one set price. Holidays are excluded, and reservations are available if you want a table for dumplings.

Raizes Churrascaria is a restaurant at 139 Nassau Avenue with a weekday happy hour from lunchtime into the evening. It covers money off all drafts, well drinks, house wine by the glass in red, white or rosé, and pitchers of sangria, plus a separate happy hour food menu. The Nassau Avenue G stop is three minutes away.

sections.body: The G is Greenpoint's only subway line. Nassau Avenue serves the southern half of our list, including Keg & Lantern, Ray's, Breeze, Raizes, Kinoko and Diamond Lil. Greenpoint Avenue serves the northern half: Papacito's, Troost, Black Rabbit, Panzón and Nerina, the last two about six to eight minutes toward the water. Coming from Manhattan, transfer to the G from the L at Metropolitan Avenue or from the 7 at Court Square.

Menu prices do not include NYC's 8.875 percent sales tax or the tip, which should run 18 to 20 percent. Most Greenpoint deals stop in the early evening on weekdays, so leave work on time if you can. Breeze excludes holidays, and every listing carries a last-checked date worth a glance.

faq.a: Troost, Papacito's and Black Rabbit run happy hour daily, and Kinoko runs Tuesday through Saturday.
faq.q: Which Greenpoint bars have happy hour every day?

faq.a: Papacito's on Manhattan Avenue lists two-for-one frozen margaritas at its daily happy hour.
faq.q: Where can I get two-for-one margaritas in Greenpoint?

faq.a: Yes. Keg & Lantern on Nassau Avenue has a weekday draft special.
faq.q: Is there a sports bar happy hour in Greenpoint?

faq.a: Panzón has tacos and adobo fries, Ray's has a burger and wings, Papacito's has nachos and tacos, and Raizes Churrascaria has its own happy hour food menu.
faq.q: Which Greenpoint happy hours include food?

intro:
Lydia's, a bar in the East Village, has 2nd Avenue station on the F as its closest subway, a 2-minute walk. The address is 16 1st Ave.

The Lydia's happy hour runs on weekdays and stays on the clock well into the evening. The drinks it covers are listed on this page, with live prices. If the specifics matter to you, check the bar's own website before heading over.

Friday has fewer happy hours than Thursday on our list, partly because a group of places run Monday to Thursday only. Manhattan still holds most of the Friday options. Williamsburg, the East Village and Times Square lead, followed by the Upper West Side and Greenwich Village, while Brooklyn has the most Friday listings outside Manhattan, then Queens, with only a handful in the Bronx.

A Friday happy hour in NYC splits into two shifts. The after-work window runs from late afternoon into the early evening at pubs like Jalopy Tavern in Carroll Gardens and Evalyn's Tap House in Gowanus. Then a smaller late-night shift picks up: Bobo in Greenwich Village pours happy hour martinis in its den on Friday and Saturday nights, and Soho Diner sends out wings and burgers in the small hours. Tip: a few spots, including Terravita in Washington Heights, start their Friday deal around lunchtime, useful if you get out of work early.

picks.why: Bobo is a French cocktail and wine bar on West 10th Street in Greenwich Village, a minute from Christopher Street on the 1. Its late happy hour runs only on Friday and Saturday nights in the den, with classic gin or vodka martinis, an espresso martini and wines. The den also hosts a daily early-evening apéro with oysters, per its menu.

Soho Diner on West Broadway is the Friday answer for very late: its happy hour starts when most others are long over and runs into the small hours on Friday and Saturday. Food is the draw, with Soho hot wings, crispy cheese curds, black-eyed pea hummus and a smash burger. The Canal Street A, C and E is one minute away.

Jalopy Tavern is a pub on Columbia Street in Carroll Gardens with money off all draft beer and well drinks in a late-afternoon window, and Friday is part of its schedule along with Wednesday and Thursday, per its listings. It is a ten-minute walk from the Carroll Street F and G, so it suits people already in the neighborhood.

Evalyn's Tap House is a pub on Butler Street in Gowanus where the Friday happy hour pairs Bavarian pretzels with craft draft beers in a late-afternoon window. The same deal runs on other weekdays too, according to its own page. The Union Street R station is six minutes on foot.

Terravita in Washington Heights starts its Friday happy hour around lunchtime, hours earlier than its Monday-to-Thursday version, and the deal covers all areas of the restaurant. Hibiscus, spicy chinola and classic margaritas, an old fashioned, sauvignon blanc, merlot, cava and Stella Artois are on the list. The 175th Street A is two minutes away.

Tin Marin Tapas Bar on Riverdale Avenue in the Bronx runs an earlier Friday happy hour, starting and ending ahead of its Monday-to-Thursday window. Sangria, margaritas, house wines and all beers are on special. The 238th Street 1 station is seven minutes away, and it is the northernmost pick on this page.

Greenwich Treehouse is a bar on Greenwich Avenue in the West Village, three minutes from the 14th Street station for the 1, 2, 3, F, L and M. Its Friday happy hour runs from early evening, with jell-o shots, a beer-and-shot pairing and money off all beer, wine and well drinks. By its own account it is dive-ish, with a jukebox and half a dance floor.

sections.body: Most Friday deals end in the early evening, so the after-work window is the main event. For later, the late-night options on our list include Bobo and Soho Diner, which run on Friday and Saturday only, and Tanner Smith's near Times Square, which runs nightly from late evening until close.

Friday tabs get a sales tax of 8.875 percent and a tip of 18 to 20 percent on top of what the menu shows. Bobo's late deal is served only in the den, and Terravita's early start applies only on Friday. Check the last-checked date on each listing before you commit to a plan.

faq.a: No. Our list has fewer Friday happy hours than Thursday ones. Walters, Karasu and Olea in Fort Greene, for example, run Monday through Thursday only.
faq.q: Do all NYC bars have happy hour on Friday?

faq.a: Bobo in Greenwich Village runs one in its den on Friday and Saturday nights, Soho Diner serves happy hour food in the small hours, and Tanner Smith's near Times Square runs nightly from late evening to close.
faq.q: Where can I find a late-night Friday happy hour in NYC?

faq.a: Terravita in Washington Heights starts around lunchtime on Friday, and Tin Marin Tapas Bar in the Bronx starts in the early afternoon.
faq.q: Which Friday happy hours start early?

faq.a: Williamsburg, the East Village and Times Square, followed by the Upper West Side and Greenwich Village.
faq.q: Which neighborhoods have the most Friday happy hours?

intro:
Orchard Street in the Lower East Side is where you will find this pub, which is listed as a sports bar. The closest subway is 2nd Avenue on the F, about a 3-minute walk.

The Hair Of The Dog happy hour runs on weekdays and covers all drinks plus a slider, so it pairs a drink deal with a small food deal.

Norfolk Street holds Nurse Bettie, a cocktail bar in the Lower East Side. Essex Street station is only a 1-minute walk, and the F, J, M and Z stop there.

The Nurse Bettie happy hour is on the schedule every day of the week and finishes in the early evening, starting from opening. The bar publishes the times but not the deal, so the specific drinks are not listed.

Sonnyboy, a restaurant on Rivington Street in the Lower East Side, is a 4-minute walk from Delancey Street station on the F, J, M and Z.

Its happy hour is spread over five days, Tuesday through Saturday, so it includes a weekend evening. The Sonnyboy happy hour lists bottle wine, the house craft cocktails, wines and beer.

Greek food is the draw at Souvlaki GR, a restaurant at 116 Stanton Street in the Lower East Side. Essex Street station, on the F, J, M and Z, is a 4-minute walk.

The Souvlaki GR happy hour is offered Tuesday through Friday, and the place publishes the times but not the deal, so no specific items or discounts are listed.

Mexican cuisine defines Bar Mexicana, a restaurant at 127A West 43rd Street in Midtown. Times Square station is just 1 minute away on foot, served by the 1, 2, 3, 7, A, C, E, N, Q, R, S and W.

The Bar Mexicana happy hour runs on weekdays in the late afternoon and early evening. The deal itself is not published, only the times.

Chelsea runs along Manhattan's West Side from 14th Street up to 34th Street, between Sixth Avenue and the Hudson River. Our list falls into three pockets. The south end sits on Seventh, Eighth and Ninth Avenues between 14th and 23rd Streets, near the 14th Street stations and the 23rd Street stops on the 1 and the C and E. A second cluster fills the side streets from West 24th to West 31st Street toward Sixth Avenue, where 28th Street on the 1 is the usual stop. The third is out west on Eleventh Avenue and West 26th Street, closest to the 7 at 34th Street-Hudson Yards.

Happy hour in Chelsea leans toward cocktails and restaurant bars rather than dive pours. Margaritas, highballs, house wine and draft beer show up again and again, and many places add food: tacos, olives, croquettes and Burmese disco fries. Most deals are weekday affairs, though Bar Avant Apres Bar, Porchlight, Rangoon and Friedman's on West 31st Street run theirs every day.

picks.why: El Coco is a Mexican taqueria and bar on Eighth Avenue, three minutes from the 23rd Street C and E stop. Its long window runs Sunday through Thursday from midday into the early evening, with classic, frozen, watermelon and Blue Hawaiian margaritas, a passionfruit martini, small bites and tacos. Friday and Saturday are full price, so plan around them.

La Devozione is an Italian restaurant on West 16th Street whose weekday happy hour leans on snacks: spaghetti aglio e olio pasta chips, marinated olives and fried mac and cheese lollipops. The deal is limited to the cocktail bar and the communal tables, so skip the dining room. The A, C, E and L at 14th Street are five minutes away.

Rangoon on Eighth Avenue has one of the longest windows on our Chelsea list, running from midday into the early evening every day of the week. The listed perk is an order of Burmese disco fries on the house, so ask staff how to claim it. It is three minutes from the 14th Street A, C, E and L station, and OpenTable takes bookings.

NºBetween is a cocktail bar on West 15th Street with a weekday happy hour built on shochu and Japanese whisky highballs, such as a lychee and Aperol mix and a lemon whisky highball, plus beer and a food item. The window opens in the late afternoon, early enough for a first round after work. The 8th Avenue station on the A, C, E and L is six minutes away.

OfCorsica, on Eleventh Avenue, runs its happy hour Tuesday through Saturday, so it covers a Saturday afternoon as well as the work week. Discounted drinks range from Vesper martinis to daiquiris, served next to a coastal Corsican menu. It is an eleven-minute walk from the 8th Avenue station on the A, C, E and L; book on Resy.

sections.body: Four stops do most of the work. The 14th Street and 8th Avenue complex on the A, C, E and L covers La Devozione, Rangoon, Salinas, NºBetween and OfCorsica, and District Local is two minutes from the 14th Street station on the 1, 2, 3, F, M and L. The 23rd Street stations on the 1, the C and E, and the F and M are a few minutes from El Coco, The Cooper Still and Jake's Saloon. 28th Street on the 1 serves El Lugar Cantina, Sid Gold's Request Room and Tara Mor. Porchlight and Bar Avant Apres Bar are nearest the 7 at 34th Street-Hudson Yards, The Fleur Room is closer to 28th Street on the R and W, and Friedman's to 34th Street-Herald Square.

Prices on the menu leave out New York's 8.875 percent sales tax, and servers expect 18 to 20 percent on top. In Chelsea the fine print matters: La Devozione keeps its deal to the cocktail bar and communal tables, and Salinas and El Lugar Cantina to the bar. Each bar page shows when we last checked it, so glance at that date before you go.

faq.a: Bar Avant Apres Bar, Porchlight, Rangoon and Friedman's on West 31st Street list happy hour every day. El Coco runs Sunday through Thursday, and OfCorsica covers Tuesday through Saturday. Most of the rest of our Chelsea list keeps the deal to weekdays.
faq.q: Which Chelsea bars have happy hour on weekends?

faq.a: El Coco discounts tacos and small bites, and La Devozione has pasta chips, olives and mac and cheese lollipops. Rangoon offers Burmese disco fries, and El Lugar Cantina has tacos.
faq.q: Where can I get food during happy hour in Chelsea?

faq.a: It depends on the block. Use 14th Street on the A, C, E and L for the bars near 14th to 16th Streets, the 23rd Street stations on the 1, the C and E, or the F and M for Seventh and Eighth Avenues, 28th Street on the 1 for the side streets in the upper 20s, and 34th Street-Hudson Yards on the 7 for Eleventh Avenue.
faq.q: Which subway stop is closest to Chelsea happy hours?

faq.a: Not quite, but close. Rangoon and El Coco both start their deals at midday, and The Cooper Still and District Local run from midday on weekdays. Friedman's on West 31st Street opens its window in the early afternoon every day.
faq.q: Is there an all-day happy hour in Chelsea?

intro:
Cobble Hill is the small neighborhood just south of Atlantic Avenue, with Court and Smith Streets as its commercial spines, and that is where its happy hours sit. Court Street has Congress, Smith Street has Bee's Knees Provisions, and Elsa is on Atlantic Avenue at the northern edge. Big Tiny, The Brazen Head and Xochitl Taqueria are a few minutes from the Bergen Street station, while Popina and Mazzat are about ten minutes on foot from the nearest F and G stop.
