The F and G trains cover almost everything, and the deals here are cocktail-forward with real food attached: oysters at Bee's Knees and Big Tiny, Roman pastas at Popina, pizza and tartines in Big Tiny's drink combos. Several places also stretch past weekday afternoons. For a Cobble Hill happy hour on a Sunday, try Big Tiny, Bee's Knees Provisions or Mazzat, or Elsa, which lists Sunday as all day. After dinner, Congress adds a late window on Thursday and The Brazen Head adds one Monday through Wednesday.

picks.why: Congress is a bar and restaurant at 208 Court Street with money off menu cocktails, draft beer and wine Monday through Thursday in the late afternoon. Its own page also lists a late-night window on Thursday and daytime happy hours on Friday and weekends. Bergen Street on the F and G is three minutes away, and reservations are available.

Bee's Knees Provisions is a cocktail bar at 215 Smith Street running happy hour daily, with an oyster special in the first part of the window. The list includes cocktails like a lavender gimlet and a ginger goldrush, a hazy IPA, a yuzu ginger cider and sparkling prosecco. The Bergen Street F and G is three minutes away, and you can book ahead.

The Brazen Head is a pub near the Bergen Street F and G with a weekday happy hour in the late afternoon and a second, late-evening one Monday through Wednesday. Well drinks, wine, a Misguided margarita and Aslin Old Town Lager are on the list, which makes it the go-to on this page for a cheap beer.

Big Tiny is a restaurant four minutes from the Bergen Street F and G with happy hour Sunday through Thursday in the early evening. Red, white, rosé, orange and sparkling wine, a house spritz and sangria are on special, and combos pair one drink with a classic pizza, six oysters or a tartine. Friday and Saturday are not included.

Popina is an Italian restaurant with Southern touches, per its own listing, whose happy hour runs Monday through Thursday in a short early-evening window. The menu features Roman pastas such as cacio e pepe, gricia, carbonara and amatriciana, plus a Negroni and a spritz. It is about eleven minutes on foot from the Bergen Street F and G, and reservations are available.

Elsa is a bar at 136 Atlantic Avenue, on the northern edge of Cobble Hill, with happy hour Tuesday through Friday in the early evening and, per the bar's own listing, all day on Sunday. We have its days, not its drink list. The Borough Hall station, served by the 2, 3, 4, 5 and R, is six minutes away.

sections.body: Bergen Street on the F and G is the anchor stop, three or four minutes from Congress, Bee's Knees Provisions, Big Tiny and The Brazen Head, a minute from Xochitl Taqueria, and a longer walk to Popina. Carroll Street, one stop south, is the nearer station for Mazzat. For Elsa on Atlantic Avenue, Borough Hall brings in the 2, 3, 4, 5 and R.

Add 8.875 percent sales tax and an 18 to 20 percent tip to whatever the menu says. Bee's Knees runs its oyster special for only part of its window, and Big Tiny skips Friday and Saturday, so plan around those. Every listing shows a last-checked date, and menus change, so look before you go.

faq.a: Bee's Knees Provisions on Smith Street runs an oyster special daily, and Big Tiny pairs six oysters with a drink Sunday through Thursday.
faq.q: Where can I get oysters at happy hour in Cobble Hill?

faq.a: Big Tiny, Bee's Knees Provisions and Mazzat all run on Sunday, Elsa lists Sunday as all day, and Congress lists weekend daytime hours.
faq.q: Which Cobble Hill bars have happy hour on Sunday?

faq.a: The Brazen Head runs a late-evening happy hour Monday through Wednesday, and Congress adds a late-night window on Thursday.
faq.q: Is there a late-night happy hour in Cobble Hill?

faq.a: Xochitl Taqueria discounts margaritas on weekdays, and The Brazen Head has a Misguided margarita on its list. For other cocktails, Popina has a Negroni and Bee's Knees Provisions has a lavender gimlet.
faq.q: Which Cobble Hill happy hours have margaritas?

intro:
Cuban, Chinese and Asian fusion are the cuisines listed for Calle Dao, a restaurant at 38 W 39th St in Midtown. Bryant Park's 42nd Street station is a 3-minute walk, with the 7, B, D, F and M.

There are two windows. The first covers weekdays and the second covers Saturday and Sunday, so weekends are included. The Calle Dao happy hour is published as times only, without a list of deals.

Little Beaver, a bar in Bushwick, Brooklyn, holds a weekday happy hour that begins in the afternoon and finishes in the early evening. The closest station is Jefferson Street on the L, two minutes away on foot.

The Little Beaver happy hour has no drinks or food listed, so the times are the only specifics. A website is listed.

An Aperol spritz, seasonal sangria, a housemade limoncello shot, a martini and marinated olives, each at a set price, are on the Santa Panza happy hour list. It is held Monday through Thursday in the early evening.

Santa Panza is an Italian restaurant at 1079 Broadway in Bushwick, Brooklyn, three minutes from Kosciuszko Street station on the J.

Table 87 Coal Oven Pizza operates at 473 3rd Avenue in Gowanus as a pizza restaurant. The 4th Avenue station, served by the F, G and R trains, is 2 minutes away.

Table 87 Coal Oven Pizza happy hour pricing covers house beer, cocktails and a Negroni. It runs on weekdays from late afternoon into the early evening. The price range shows as two dollar signs. The live listing on this page has current drink prices.

At 411 3rd Ave in Kips Bay, Bella Union is a restaurant with a bar side and a wine tag. The 28th Street stop on the 6 line is a 4-minute walk.

The Bella Union happy hour lists Down East cider, Wicked Hazy IPA, Fiddlehead IPA, Montauk Wave Chase IPA, Sloop Juice IPA and seltzers, plus a Friday beers item. It runs on weekdays, from late afternoon until the evening. The price range shows as two dollar signs.

A 2 for 1 happy hour in NYC means you pay for one drink and the bar pours a second of the same kind. It is the rarest format on our list: only a small group of bars flag it, against the many that simply set a lower price. Most of them are in Manhattan, from Kingston Hall in the East Village and Rockbar Nyc on Christopher Street to VERS in Hell's Kitchen and Sojourn Social on the Upper East Side. Brooklyn adds Papacito's in Greenpoint and Bati Ethiopian Kitchen on Fulton Street, and Queens has an entry in Long Island City.

What gets doubled varies a lot. Kingston Hall covers beer, prosecco and well drinks, Rockbar Nyc adds call liquor, Sojourn Social lets you mix and match signature cocktails, draft beer and wine, and VERS keeps it to well drinks. Weekday windows are the norm, but a few of these bars run the deal every day. Ask whether the free drink comes with the first one or on the next round, since bars handle it differently, and remember the deal ends with the window.

picks.why: Seven days a week, Kingston Hall pairs every beer, glass of prosecco or well drink with a second one at no charge, and its Sunday window opens earlier than the rest. The bar sits on 2nd Avenue in the East Village, four minutes on foot from Astor Place on the 6. Our listing shows no booking link, so just walk in.

Rockbar Nyc on Christopher Street in the West Village applies its 2-for-1 to beer, well liquor and call liquor, a step up from the usual well-only offer. The deal runs Monday through Friday in the early evening. Christopher Street–Stonewall on the 1 is about seven minutes away, and the bar's own listed hours run late on weekends.

Sojourn Social is a restaurant on 2nd Avenue on the Upper East Side, three minutes from the 86th Street Q station. Its weekday happy hour starts at lunchtime and lasts into the evening, with 2-for-1 drinks you can mix and match across signature cocktails, draft beer and wine by the glass, plus a short list of small plates. Book on OpenTable.

VERS, a bar on 9th Avenue in Hell's Kitchen, runs its deal every day until early evening. Well drinks are buy one, get one, appetizers are discounted, and house martinis and margaritas get a set happy hour price. The 50th Street station on the C and E is three minutes away, and Resy takes reservations if you are bringing friends.

Papacito's on Manhattan Avenue in Greenpoint runs a daily afternoon happy hour built around margaritas, frozen and on the rocks, plus pints, a tequila shot with a Tecate, nachos and tacos. Its own menu also lists a separate deal in the last hour before closing every night. Greenpoint Avenue on the G is three minutes away.

Bati Ethiopian Kitchen is a restaurant on Fulton Street in Clinton Hill, four minutes from Franklin Avenue on the C and the shuttle. Its 2-for-1 runs on Wednesday and Thursday until early evening, and the menu lists house cocktails made with berbere syrup and sorrel alongside wine and an IPA. Reserve through Resy.

sections.body: Most 2-for-1 offers on our list cover the cheaper end of the bar: beer, well drinks and sometimes prosecco. Rockbar Nyc stretches it to call liquor, and Sojourn Social to signature cocktails and wine by the glass. Weekday windows dominate; Kingston Hall, Papacito's and VERS are the ones that keep the deal going on Saturday and Sunday, so plan weekend rounds around them.

The menu price leaves out New York's 8.875 percent sales tax, and servers expect a tip of 18 to 20 percent; tipping on both drinks, not just the one you paid for, is good form. Some deals apply only at the bar. Each listing shows the date we last checked it, and offers like these change, so look at that date first.

faq.a: Kingston Hall in the East Village runs its buy one, get one every day, with a separate Sunday window. Papacito's in Greenpoint and VERS in Hell's Kitchen also run their happy hours daily.
faq.q: Which NYC bars have a 2-for-1 happy hour on weekends?

faq.a: Sojourn Social on the Upper East Side applies it to signature cocktails, draft beer and wine by the glass. Rockbar Nyc in the West Village includes call liquor along with beer and wells, and Kingston Hall adds prosecco.
faq.q: Which 2-for-1 deals include more than well drinks?

faq.a: Papacito's on Manhattan Avenue in Greenpoint has a daily happy hour with a 2-for-1, and Bati Ethiopian Kitchen on Fulton Street in Clinton Hill runs one on Wednesday and Thursday.
faq.q: Where can I find 2-for-1 drinks in Brooklyn?

faq.a: Usually not. Kingston Hall, Rockbar Nyc and Papacito's list no booking link, so walk in. Sojourn Social takes OpenTable bookings, and VERS and Bati Ethiopian Kitchen use Resy, which helps for a group.
faq.q: Do I need a reservation for a 2-for-1 happy hour?

intro:
Park Avenue South is the setting for Barbounia, a Mediterranean and Greek restaurant at 250 Park Avenue South in Gramercy. The 23rd Street-Baruch College stop on the 6 line is 3 minutes away on foot.

The Barbounia happy hour runs on weekdays, from the afternoon into the early evening. The restaurant publishes the times but not the deal, so no drinks or dishes are named here. The listing shows a price range of four dollar signs.

A cocktail happy hour in NYC can mean anything from a set price on house margaritas to a short menu of classics like the negroni, the old fashioned and the martini. It is the most common tag on our list, and most of these bars are in Manhattan. Times Square, the Upper West Side, the East Village, the Financial District and Murray Hill have the most. In Brooklyn, Williamsburg and Park Slope lead, while Astoria, Jackson Heights and Long Island City carry Queens.

Most cocktail deals cover a handful of named drinks, not the full menu. Spritzes, margaritas and espresso martinis turn up again and again, and some bars add a mocktail. Many windows end before dinner on weekdays, but a good share of these bars include Saturday or Sunday, and a few in Midtown run late at night instead. If one particular drink matters to you, read the offer list on the listing first, since the deal often names exact cocktails.

picks.why: Tanner Smith's on West 55th Street is a late-night pick: its happy hour starts in the late evening and runs until close every night of the week. Negronis, old fashioneds and Aperol spritzes share the list with pinot noir and two beers. It is a minute from 57th Street–7th Avenue on the N, Q, R and W, and it takes reservations.

La Perla Nascosta, a bar on West 79th Street on the Upper West Side, builds its happy hour around spritzes: Aperol, Campari and Hugo, plus a spritz margarita, a negroni, rosé and prosecco. The deal runs Sunday through Friday in the late afternoon. The 79th Street station on the 1 is a minute away, and booking is available.

Urban Cove Society & Kitchen is a New American restaurant on Peck Slip, near the South Street Seaport. Its happy hour runs every day of the week in the afternoon and covers featured cocktails, including a clear negroni and a Cynar negroni, along with beer and select wine. Fulton Street station is six minutes away, and tables can be reserved.

Santa Panza is an Italian restaurant on Broadway in Bushwick, three minutes from Kosciuszko Street on the J. From Monday to Thursday, its happy hour discounts an Aperol spritz, a martini, seasonal sangria and a housemade limoncello shot, with marinated olives on the side. Reserve through its booking link, or walk in after work.

Bitter Monk at 68 34th Street in Sunset Park runs its happy hour Thursday through Sunday, and it wraps up in the afternoon, so plan an early visit. The list includes a Vesper martini and a Gaia martini, and the bar's own menu describes gins and vodka from Atheras Monks. The 36th Street station on the D, N and R is four minutes away.

Upstairs Cocktail Bar is a second-floor bar on Roosevelt Avenue in Woodside, two minutes from 69th Street on the 7. Its happy hour runs Monday through Saturday in the early evening, with a gimlet, a classic margarita, a martini and a Moscow or whiskey mule. Our listing has no booking link, so just head up the stairs.

sections.body: Most cocktail deals finish by dinner, but a few Midtown bars flip the pattern. Tanner Smith's runs nightly from the late evening, Bartley Dunne's on West 54th Street does the same Sunday through Wednesday, and Central Park Tavern on West 57th Street runs Sunday through Thursday. For a Saturday or Sunday afternoon, The Grey Dog, Westville and Urban Cove Society & Kitchen run every day.

Cocktail prices on menus exclude the 8.875 percent New York sales tax, and a tip of 18 to 20 percent is expected on top. A happy hour price usually applies only to the drinks named on the deal list, and some bars serve it at the bar alone. Look at the last-checked date on each listing before you go.

faq.a: Tanner Smith's on West 55th Street runs nightly from the late evening, Bartley Dunne's on West 54th Street does so Sunday through Wednesday, and Central Park Tavern on West 57th Street covers Sunday through Thursday.
faq.q: Where can I get a late-night cocktail happy hour in NYC?

faq.a: Astoria has the most, including Spanglish NYC with frozen and hibiscus margaritas. Upstairs Cocktail Bar in Woodside runs Monday through Saturday, and Hellbender in Ridgewood discounts margaritas on weekdays.
faq.q: Which cocktail happy hours are in Queens?

faq.a: La Perla Nascosta on the Upper West Side lists Aperol, Campari and Hugo spritzes. The Grey Dog in Greenwich Village, Nolita and Union Square has a Venetian spritz, Tara Rose in Kips Bay has a Hugo spritz, and Santa Panza in Bushwick includes an Aperol spritz.
faq.q: Where can I find a spritz at happy hour?

faq.a: Urban Cove Society & Kitchen, La Perla Nascosta, The Ribbon on the Upper West Side, the three Grey Dog locations, Westville and Bitter Monk all include Sunday.
faq.q: Which cocktail happy hours run on Sunday?

intro:
Linen Hall works as an American restaurant at 101 3rd Avenue in Union Square. For the subway, take the L train to 3rd Avenue, then walk about one minute.

Linen Hall happy hour comes on weekdays, from late afternoon into the evening. The restaurant publishes the times but not the deal. The listing is for Union Square in Manhattan.

The Grey Dog, an American restaurant on University Place in Union Square, has its happy hour details below. Union Square is the nearest station, served by the 4, 5, 6, L, N, Q, R and W trains and a three-minute walk from the door.

The deal is posted as house wine, Tommy’s Margarita, Venetian spritz, bar bites and rose. The Grey Dog happy hour comes every day, from late afternoon into the early evening.

The Penny Farthing sits on 3rd Avenue in Union Square and counts as a pub and sports bar. The closest subway stop is 3rd Avenue (the L train), a one-minute walk away.

The Penny Farthing happy hour comes on weekdays, from late afternoon into the early evening. Deals named for it: draft, wines, burgers, espresso martinis, Aperol, green tea shots and well drinks.

At 1703 2nd Avenue on the Upper East Side, Cafe d'Alsace operates as a French restaurant. 86th Street is the nearest station, served by the Q train and a two-minute walk from the door.

Cafe d'Alsace happy hour comes every day, from late afternoon into the evening. Times are posted, but the restaurant does not publish the deal itself.

Dylan Murphy's works as a bar at 1453 3rd Avenue on the Upper East Side. The closest subway stop is 86th Street (the 4, 5 and 6 trains), a four-minute walk away.

Dylan Murphy's happy hour runs every day, from midday into the early evening. The bar publishes the times but not the deal. Check the page for live hours and prices before you go.

Sunday has more happy hours than Saturday on our list, partly because a common schedule runs Sunday through Thursday and skips Friday and Saturday. Manhattan has most of the Sunday options, led by Times Square, the Upper West Side, the East Village and the Upper East Side. Williamsburg leads Brooklyn, and Queens has a smaller group.

A Sunday happy hour in NYC comes in three forms on our list. Some places stretch the window on Sunday, like The Factory 380 in Kips Bay, which runs late into the night. Others open their Sunday-to-Thursday stretch with a regular early-evening window, as at Ella Social on the Upper West Side and The Green Room PLG on Rogers Avenue in Brooklyn. And a few late-night bars, such as Meller's Sports Hub on the Upper East Side, run from late evening into the small hours from Sunday through Thursday. Tip: El Coco in Chelsea starts its deal around lunchtime, which makes it a handy follow-up to brunch.

picks.why: The Factory 380 on Third Avenue in Kips Bay runs its longest happy hour on Sunday, from late afternoon until late at night, on top of a weekday window. Frozen and signature cocktails are on the list, along with a martini combo the restaurant calls the Happy Meal, with truffle parm fries on the side. It is four minutes from the 28th Street 6, and OpenTable takes reservations.

Kingston Hall on Second Avenue in the East Village runs a buy-one-get-one deal on beer, prosecco and well drinks, and its Sunday window opens an hour earlier than on other days and stretches into the evening. The food menu includes coconut shrimp and a warm spinach and artichoke dip. The Astor Place 6 station is four minutes away.

The Green Room PLG is a bar on Rogers Avenue with happy hour Sunday through Thursday in the early evening. It focuses on bites: Korean chicken wings with gochujang, chicken tacos, firecracker gyoza and a vegan lentil soup with crostini. The Sterling Street 2 and 5 station is three minutes away, and reservations are available.

El Coco is a Mexican taqueria on Eighth Avenue in Chelsea with happy hour Sunday through Thursday from lunchtime into the evening. The cocktail list runs from classic, frozen and watermelon margaritas to a blueberry coconut mojito and a passionfruit martini, with small bites and tacos too. The 23rd Street C and E is three minutes away.

Ella Social is a restaurant on Columbus Avenue on the Upper West Side with a Sunday-through-Thursday happy hour in the late afternoon. Wine, red sangria, draft beer, a house spritz, a Tommy margarita and beers are on the list, and walk-ins are welcome. The 72nd Street B and C is three minutes away.

The Beast Next Door Cafe & Bar on 27th Street in Long Island City runs happy hour Sunday through Friday in the late afternoon. Narragansett lager cans, a Narragansett with a well shot, house wine by the glass and money off house cocktails, wells and draft beer are on the list. Queensboro Plaza, on the 7, N and W, is two minutes away.

Meller's Sports Hub & Grill on Second Avenue on the Upper East Side runs a late-night happy hour Sunday through Thursday, from late evening into the small hours. Hard seltzers and ciders, Bud cans, wine, frozen drinks, mixed drinks, margaritas and Aperol are covered. The 86th Street Q station is two minutes away.

sections.body: Many bars on our list run Sunday through Thursday and skip Friday and Saturday. El Coco, Ella Social, The Green Room PLG, Coffee + Cocktails in the West Village and No No No in Midtown all follow it. That means a Sunday visit often gets the same deal you would find on a Tuesday, which is not true of Saturday.

On Sunday, as on any day, menu prices exclude NYC's 8.875 percent sales tax and a tip of 18 to 20 percent. Late-night deals like Meller's start well after dinner, and Kingston Hall's earlier start applies only on Sunday. Check the last-checked date on each listing before heading out.

faq.a: Yes. Our list has more Sunday happy hours than Saturday ones, with the most in Times Square, the Upper West Side and the East Village.
faq.q: Do NYC bars have happy hour on Sunday?

faq.a: Meller's Sports Hub & Grill on the Upper East Side, Central Park Tavern in Hell's Kitchen and Barfly in Gramercy all run late-night happy hours starting on Sunday.
faq.q: Where can I find a late-night Sunday happy hour?

faq.a: El Coco in Chelsea starts around lunchtime, and Kingston Hall in the East Village starts its Sunday deal in the mid-afternoon.
faq.q: Which Sunday happy hours work after brunch?

intro:
Every bar on this page has at least one happy hour drink priced at or under the cap in the page title, which makes it the list to open when the budget is tight. Cheap drinks in NYC are not spread evenly. Astoria and the Times Square area have the most entries, followed by Koreatown, Flatiron, the Financial District, Murray Hill and both the Upper East and Upper West Sides. In Brooklyn, Bushwick, Williamsburg, Park Slope and Greenpoint lead. Staten Island and the Bronx are represented too.

The low-priced pour is usually a draft beer, a well drink, a shot or a glass of house wine; cocktails rarely make the cut. Many bars list one cheap item next to pricier ones, so the number on each card is the floor, not the average. Most windows close in the early evening on weekdays. To stretch the budget, pick a bar where the cheap item is something you actually want, and check whether it is a specific brand, a can or a draft.

picks.why: 200 Fifth is a bar on 5th Avenue in Park Slope with one of the lowest-priced lineups on our list: bar drinks, house wine and champagne all sit near the bottom of the range. The deal runs Monday to Friday from late afternoon. Union Street on the R is three minutes away, and the bar takes reservations.

O'Flanagan's is a pub on 1st Avenue on the Upper East Side, and its deal is simple: well drinks at one of the lowest prices on this page, plus Bud Light, Yuengling and Coors Light on tap according to its own menu. Weekdays only, late afternoon to early evening. The 72nd Street Q stop is seven minutes on foot.

Gebhard's Beer Culture sits on West 72nd Street on the Upper West Side, a minute from the 1, 2 and 3 trains. Its happy hour drafts are the draw, priced well under most of the city, with a Guinness pint and house wine also on the list. It runs on weekdays and ends early, so come straight from work.

The Rabbit Hole, a bar on Broadway in Astoria, stacks its weekday happy hour with shots, house beers, house wines, mixers and mocktails, plus frozen drinks, discounted appetizers and a free hot dog. The window runs from after work into the evening. Steinway Street on the M and R is two minutes away, and tables can be booked.

Ben & Jack's Steakhouse on 5th Avenue near 28th Street lists one of the cheapest beers on our entire list during its weekday happy hour. House wine is also low, and prosecco, martinis, margaritas, sangria and Blue Point oysters round out the menu. The window lasts about two hours after work, and 28th Street on the 1 is two minutes away.

Tin Marin Tapas Bar is a restaurant on Riverdale Avenue in the Bronx, about seven minutes from 238th Street on the 1. Beer is the cheapest item, with sangria, margaritas and house wines on the same happy hour list. It runs Monday to Thursday from mid-afternoon, plus a shorter, earlier window on Friday that suits a long lunch.

Piccolino Restaurant is an Italian spot on Amboy Road in Staten Island, two minutes from Great Kills on the Staten Island Railway. Its Tuesday to Friday happy hour puts house wine at the low end, with mixed drinks, beer, a lychee martini and margaritas, plus wings, mozzarella sticks, penne vodka and fried zucchini. Reservations are accepted.

sections.h: What the cheap item usually is
sections.body: Draft beer and well drinks make up most of the low prices here, with house wine and shots close behind. Cocktails at this level are rare: Flying Cock in Kips Bay lists an espresso martini and La Caverna on the Lower East Side lists margaritas on Tuesday, both well under the cap. Several menus name a single beer or a can for the cheapest slot, so read the item name, not just the price.

The price on the board comes before tax and tip: New York adds 8.875 percent in sales tax, and 18 to 20 percent is the usual tip, which matters more when the drink itself is cheap. Bars often keep these prices to the bar area. Each listing carries the date we last checked it, and prices at this level move quickly, so look before you go.

faq.a: 200 Fifth in Park Slope, Post No Bills in Williamsburg and Papacito's in Greenpoint have some of the lowest prices in the borough. Bushwick has several more, including SURA and Mad Tropical, and Syndicated Bar Theater Kitchen in Williamsburg is another.
faq.q: Where can I get cheap happy hour drinks in Brooklyn?

faq.a: Flying Cock in Kips Bay, The Uptown Restaurant & Bar on the Upper East Side, Cafe Express Deli near Times Square, Post No Bills in Williamsburg and Boho Karaoke Orchard on the Lower East Side all list their deals every day of the week.
faq.q: Which cheap happy hours run on weekends?

faq.a: Yes. Astoria and the Times Square area have the most entries on this page, including The Rabbit Hole, Hutch Astoria, Burgerology Astoria, The Wolfhound and Sweet Spot Sporting Lounge & Bar.
faq.q: Are there cheap happy hour drinks in Queens?

faq.a: Piccolino Restaurant on Staten Island adds wings and penne vodka, Burgerology Astoria discounts sliders and a turkey burger, The Rabbit Hole hands out a free hot dog, and Papacito's in Greenpoint has tacos and nachos.
faq.q: Which cheap happy hours include food?

intro:
An oyster happy hour in NYC is a simple trade: shellfish at a discount, usually by the piece, next to a cheaper glass of wine or a beer. Dozens of places on our list discount oysters or include them in the deal, split between Manhattan and Brooklyn. In Manhattan they gather in Greenwich Village, Koreatown, Flatiron, Midtown and Tribeca. In Brooklyn, Williamsburg leads, followed by Prospect Heights, Fort Greene and Cobble Hill. Queens adds pán in Ridgewood.

The deals come in a few shapes. Some places price oysters singly, like Ten Bells and John Doe Craft Bar & Kitchen. Others sell a half dozen with a drink, as pán and Kissaki Sushi do, and Walters takes half off oysters, wine and beer together. Most run on weekdays in the late afternoon, and many restaurants honor them only at the bar. The variety is often the chef's or the shucker's choice, as Blue Fin notes, so ask what is on before ordering a round.

picks.why: Ten Bells at 247 Broome Street discounts oysters every day from opening until early evening, and pairs them with a carafe of wine. That makes it one of the few oyster deals here you can count on for a Saturday afternoon. Delancey Street on the F, J, M and Z is two minutes away, and its menu lists tapas such as papas bravas.

John Doe Craft Bar & Kitchen at 253 5th Avenue runs one of the longest oyster windows on our list, starting in the late morning and lasting into the evening every day. Oysters are the listed deal, and its site adds weekly specials such as a build-your-own burger night. The 28th Street R and W stop is two minutes away.

Filé Gumbo Bar at 275 Church Street in Tribeca char-grills the oysters on its deal, and the weekday list adds beef sliders, Cajun wings, house lager, house wines and specialty cocktails. It opens in the middle of the afternoon, so it suits an early finish from the office. Franklin Street on the 1 is a two-minute walk.

Walters is an American restaurant at 166 DeKalb Avenue in Fort Greene, four minutes from the Fulton Street G. From Monday to Thursday it takes half off oysters, wine, beer and frozen specials, a straightforward deal for an early evening. Karasu, a Japanese restaurant and cocktail bar at the same address, runs its own happy hour if you want a second stop.

The Ten Bells Brooklyn at 65 Irving Avenue brings the oyster deal to Bushwick every day until early evening, with wine specials and Spanish tapas alongside. Walk-ins are welcome by its own account, and group tables go through Resy. Jefferson Street on the L is three minutes away, which makes it easy to reach from Manhattan.

pán on Decatur Street is the Queens oyster stop, three minutes from Halsey Street on the L. Its daily deal pairs a half dozen or a dozen oysters with house red or white wine or a beer on tap, so it works on a weekend as well as after work. The menu lists both East Coast and West Coast varieties.

Blue Fin is a seafood restaurant at 1567 Broadway, two minutes from 49th Street on the N, R and W. The daily happy hour prices a chef-selected market oyster by the piece and adds mini lobster rolls and crispy cauliflower. Since it runs every day, it is an easy stop before a Saturday or Sunday matinee in the Theater District.

sections.body: Most oyster deals here are weekday affairs, and Walters, Strange Delight and Francie stop on Thursday. For Saturday or Sunday, look to the daily ones: Ten Bells, The Ten Bells Brooklyn, John Doe, Blue Fin, Jack & Charlie's No. 118, Docks Oyster Bar, Mayfield, Bayridge Sushi and pán. OTB in Williamsburg goes the other way and runs its oyster deal only on weekend afternoons.

Oysters are priced before the 8.875 percent New York sales tax, and a tip of 18 to 20 percent is customary on the full bill. Many seafood deals, including those at Legasea and Ben & Jack's Steakhouse, are bar-only, so take a stool. Check each listing's last-checked date before you plan a round.

faq.a: Williamsburg has Layla and OTB, Fort Greene has Walters and Bar Francis, Bushwick has The Ten Bells Brooklyn, and Crown Heights has Mayfield. Brooklyn Crab in Red Hook, Bayridge Sushi in Bay Ridge and Bee's Knees Provisions in Cobble Hill also include oysters.
faq.q: Where can I get an oyster happy hour in Brooklyn?

faq.a: Ten Bells, John Doe Craft Bar & Kitchen, Blue Fin, Jack & Charlie's No. 118 and Docks Oyster Bar in Manhattan run daily, as do The Ten Bells Brooklyn, Mayfield and Bayridge Sushi in Brooklyn and pán in Ridgewood, Queens.
faq.q: Which oyster happy hours run every day?

faq.a: Legasea Bar & Grill on 7th Avenue is two minutes from 34th Street-Penn Station, with oysters, fries, beer, wine and martinis at the bar on weekdays. Amelia's on Park Avenue South in Midtown also includes oysters.
faq.q: Is there an oyster happy hour near Penn Station?

faq.a: Often. pán and Kissaki Sushi sell oysters together with a glass of wine, beer or champagne, Lady Blue pairs a dozen oysters with a bottle of bubbly, Ten Bells adds a carafe of wine, and Walters discounts wine and beer alongside its oysters.
faq.q: Do oyster happy hours come with drinks?

intro:
Saturday and Sunday deals are more common than you might guess: plenty of bars on our list run a happy hour on at least one weekend day, and many of them run all seven days. The bars whose deal exists only for the weekend are rarer, and they tend to be afternoon affairs tied to brunch or a slow Sunday. Manhattan has most of the weekend list, led by Times Square, the Upper West Side, the East Village and the Upper East Side. Brooklyn comes next, with Williamsburg and Bushwick on top, followed by Queens.

A weekend happy hour in NYC tends to start earlier than the weekday version, sometimes in the late morning, and to wrap up by early evening. Plan around the afternoon rather than the night, and check which day applies, since a few bars cover only Saturday or only Sunday.

picks.why: Bob's Your Uncle is a Columbus Avenue bar on the Upper West Side with a separate weekend happy hour on Saturday and Sunday afternoons. Its own menu lists well drinks, draft beer and a few select cocktails at a discount. The B and C at 103rd Street are a four-minute walk.

169 Bar on East Broadway keeps its happy hour for Saturday and Sunday, running from early afternoon into the evening. The bar's own listing mentions a weekend DJ and a leopard-print pool table, and it is tagged for outdoor seating. The F at East Broadway is a minute away.

The Malt House is a pub on Thompson Street that saves its happy hour for Saturday and Sunday, from opening through mid-afternoon. It is a food deal: jumbo wings and parmesan herbed fries, a fair brunch alternative near Washington Square. The West 4th Street station, with seven lines, is five minutes away, and reservations are available.

Sir Henry's is a cocktail bar on Eighth Avenue near 50th Street whose happy hour runs only on Saturday and Sunday, until mid-afternoon. The menu leans on shareables, including sourdough sausage roll bites. It is two minutes from the C and E at 50th Street and takes reservations, handy before a weekend matinee in the Theater District.

Recette is a French restaurant on Havemeyer Street in Williamsburg with a Saturday and Sunday daytime deal that, per its own menu, takes money off wine by the bottle. It runs from morning into the afternoon, so it pairs with a late brunch rather than an after-work drink. The G and L at Metropolitan Avenue are five minutes away.

Via Trenta Osteria & Wine Bar is an Italian wine bar on 30th Avenue in Astoria with a happy hour Tuesday through Saturday, running from midday through the afternoon on Saturday. Saturday is the weekend day to go. The N and W at 30th Avenue are about six minutes away, and it takes reservations.

sections.body: Most bars on this page run the same deal all week, so the weekend is just another day for them. The weekend-only deals are different: they tend to start in the late morning or early afternoon and finish before dinner, and several belong to restaurants that serve brunch. If you want a Sunday evening drink, look at the daily deals instead, because most weekend-only windows have closed by then.

Restaurant deals are often limited to the bar, so ask before you sit down at a table. Every check in the city adds 8.875 percent sales tax, and servers expect a tip of 18 to 20 percent on top. Weekend hours shift more often than weekday ones, so check the last-checked date on each bar.

faq.a: 169 Bar on the Lower East Side, The Malt House in Greenwich Village, Sir Henry's near Times Square, Grand Street Social in SoHo and Recette in Williamsburg keep their deals for the weekend.
faq.q: Which NYC bars have happy hour only on weekends?

faq.a: Yes. Most of the daily deals on our list include Sunday, and weekend deals such as The Malt House, Sir Henry's and 169 Bar run on both Saturday and Sunday.
faq.q: Is there a Sunday happy hour in NYC?

faq.a: Often. Recette's deal begins in the morning, Sir Henry's and The Malt House run from opening into the afternoon, and Grand Street Social in SoHo covers Saturday and Sunday from morning through late afternoon.
faq.q: Do weekend happy hours start earlier?

faq.a: Yes. Via Trenta in Astoria runs a Saturday deal, and other Queens bars on our list include at least one weekend day.
faq.q: Are there weekend happy hours in Queens?

intro:
A Lavender Collins, prosecco and a negroni are named on the Friedman`s happy hour list, at set prices. The happy hour is held every day, weekends included, from the afternoon into the early evening.

Friedman`s is an American restaurant at 450 10th Avenue in Hell's Kitchen, four minutes on foot from 34th Street–Hudson Yards station on the 7.

Sunday through Thursday, from midday into the early evening, El Coco serves up its happy hour with a long list of set-price offers: Blue Hawaiian, frozen classic and watermelon margaritas, a passionfruit martini, a lemondrop cocktail, small bites and tacos.

The El Coco happy hour comes from a Mexican taqueria at 202 8th Avenue in Chelsea, three minutes from 23rd Street station on the C and E.

Wine, a spritz or a sour is the offer at the Big Tiny happy hour, held Sunday through Thursday in the early evening. Big Tiny is a restaurant in Carroll Gardens, Brooklyn, four minutes on foot from Bergen Street station on the F and G.

The address is 244 Smith St. Oysters and food deals appear among its tags, and a website is listed.

Carroll Gardens sits just south of Cobble Hill in brownstone Brooklyn, with the Gowanus Canal to the east and the Brooklyn-Queens Expressway separating the Columbia Street waterfront to the west. Court Street and Smith Street carry most of its restaurants and bars, and our list follows them: Cubana Cafe and Planted Cafe on Smith Street, Marco Polo Ristorante and Minibar on Court Street, and Jalopy Tavern out on Columbia Street. Every one of them names Carroll Street on the F and G as its nearest station.

Happy hour in Carroll Gardens is mostly a weeknight affair with a restaurant streak. Minibar covers bottled beer, well drinks, drafts, classic cocktails and house wine, Cubana Cafe adds small plates to its cocktails, and Planted Cafe keeps it to beer and wine. Marco Polo Ristorante is the one place on the list that keeps its deal going through Saturday and Sunday. Practical tip: Marco Polo is closed on Mondays, so start the week at Minibar or Cubana Cafe instead.

picks.why: Cubana Cafe is a restaurant at 272 Smith Street with a weekday window that opens in mid-afternoon and runs into the evening. Platitos include media noche, jicama salad, coconut shrimp, empanadas and croquetas, and the drinks run to rum punch, a spicy margarita, an espresso martini, a cosmopolitan and a mezcal paloma. Carroll Street on the F and G is four minutes away.

Minibar is a bar at 482 Court Street whose happy hour runs Monday through Friday into the evening. Bottled beer and well drinks sit at the low end, with drafts, classic cocktails and house wine above them, and a seasonal list of sparkling drinks alongside. It is five minutes from Carroll Street on the F and G.

Marco Polo Ristorante at 345 Court Street runs a set happy hour menu Tuesday through Sunday in the late afternoon, which makes it the weekend option on this page. Popular dishes on its own listing include oysters Rockefeller, grilled octopus and veal meatballs, so ask which ones the happy hour menu covers. It is closed Mondays and sits three minutes from Carroll Street on the F and G.

Planted Cafe at 333 Smith Street is a vegan, plant-based and gluten-free cafe that also discounts beer and wine at a weekday happy hour in the late afternoon. It is the closest stop on our list to the train, a minute from Carroll Street on the F and G, and it sells plants as well as drinks.

Jalopy Tavern is a pub at 317 Columbia Street, on the waterfront side of the neighborhood. Its posted happy hour takes a little off all draught beer and well drinks in the late afternoon, and its own listing shows the deal on Wednesday, Thursday and Friday. Carroll Street on the F and G is about a ten-minute walk.

sections.body: Carroll Street on the F and G serves the whole list. Planted Cafe is a minute from the station, Marco Polo Ristorante three minutes, Cubana Cafe four and Minibar five. Jalopy Tavern takes about ten minutes on foot, out toward Columbia Street. Bergen Street, one stop north on the same line, puts you among the Cobble Hill bars if you want to keep going.

Menu prices in New York leave out the 8.875 percent sales tax, and table or bar service usually gets an 18 to 20 percent tip. Marco Polo works from a separate happy hour menu, and Minibar's sparkling list is seasonal, so confirm what is on offer when you order. We show a last-checked date on every listing; give it a look before heading out.

faq.a: Yes, at Marco Polo Ristorante on Court Street, which runs its happy hour menu Tuesday through Sunday. Cubana Cafe, Minibar and Planted Cafe keep their deals to weekdays.
faq.q: Is there a weekend happy hour in Carroll Gardens?

faq.a: Cubana Cafe has platitos such as media noche, coconut shrimp, empanadas and croquetas on weekdays, and Marco Polo Ristorante has a happy hour menu Tuesday through Sunday.
faq.q: Where can I get food with happy hour in Carroll Gardens?

faq.a: Carroll Street on the F and G. Planted Cafe, Marco Polo Ristorante, Cubana Cafe and Minibar are one to five minutes away, and Jalopy Tavern on Columbia Street is about ten.
faq.q: Which subway stop is closest to Carroll Gardens happy hours?

faq.a: Minibar discounts bottled beer and drafts on weekdays, Jalopy Tavern takes a little off all draught beer, and Planted Cafe has a beer special on weekday afternoons.
faq.q: Where can I get a cheap beer in Carroll Gardens?

intro:
Gramercy sits east of Park Avenue South, centered on the private park that gives it its name, and our list here runs from 14th Street up to 23rd Street. The largest group is at the southern edge: Saperavi and The Belfry on East 14th Street, The Laurels on Second Avenue, and Little Rebel, all within a couple of minutes of the L at Third Avenue. Closer to the park, Barbounia and Oceans are on Park Avenue South, Carlotto is on East 19th Street and Pierre Loti on Irving Place, while Barfly and Seven Sins hold down Third Avenue in the low 20s.

The weekday deals lean on draft beer, house wine and cocktails, with oysters at The Laurels. Happy hour in Gramercy is a Sunday-to-Friday affair: no bar on our list here runs a Saturday deal, but Carlotto and Oceans include Sunday, and Barfly saves its happy hour for late nights from Sunday through Thursday. One tip: Barbounia serves its deal at the bar only, so skip the dining room.

picks.why: The Laurels is a restaurant on Second Avenue at the 14th Street end of the neighborhood, and its weekday happy hour is built around oysters, sold by the half dozen or the dozen. The deal runs Monday through Friday from mid-afternoon into the early evening. The 3rd Avenue L stop is a two-minute walk.

Barfly is a Third Avenue sports bar that saves its happy hour for late night, Sunday through Thursday, running from late evening until closing. Coors Light drafts and other domestic beers are on special, along with beer-and-shot pairings with Jameson or Screwball and a salted-rim spicy margarita. The 23rd Street 6 station is five minutes away.

Little Rebel is a cocktail and wine bar two minutes from the 3rd Avenue L with one of the longest weekday windows on this page: it starts the deal before lunch and holds it into the early evening, Monday to Friday. The happy hour cocktails include a tequila margarita made with Altos and a vanilla vodka drink. Book through Resy.

Seven Sins is an American restaurant and sports bar at 293 Third Avenue that serves as the game-watch venue of the New York Notre Dame Supporters' Club. Its posted happy hour runs Tuesday to Friday from late afternoon into early evening, with select drafts, house wine, mixed drinks and craft cocktails. The 23rd Street-Baruch College 6 stop is four minutes away, and you can book ahead.

Barbounia is a Mediterranean and Greek restaurant at 250 Park Avenue South with a weekday happy hour from mid-afternoon into the early evening. The deal is served only at the bar, so plan on a stool rather than a dining table. Reservations are available for dinner afterward, and the 23rd Street-Baruch College stop on the 6 is three minutes away.

Carlotto is a bar at 100 East 19th Street with a short early-evening happy hour that runs Sunday through Friday, so it is one of the few Gramercy deals that covers a weekend day. We have its days but not its drink list, so ask at the bar. The 14th Street-Union Square hub is four minutes away, and reservations are available.

Saperavi is a restaurant and wine bar at 245 East 14th Street with an early start: its happy hour opens in the early afternoon and runs into the early evening, Monday through Friday. We list its hours rather than its menu, so ask what is being poured. The 3rd Avenue L stop is two minutes away, and reservations are available.

sections.body: The L's 3rd Avenue stop is one or two minutes from The Belfry, Saperavi, The Laurels and Little Rebel. 14th Street-Union Square, which connects the 4, 5, 6, L, N, Q, R and W, is three or four minutes from Pierre Loti, Carlotto and Oceans. For Third Avenue and Park Avenue South in the low 20s, the 6 at 23rd Street-Baruch College is three to five minutes from Barbounia, Seven Sins and Barfly.

Menu prices here are pre-tax and pre-tip: add NYC sales tax of 8.875 percent and a tip of 18 to 20 percent. Several Gramercy deals, Barbounia's among them, apply only at the bar, so grab a stool rather than a table. Each listing shows when we last checked it, and an older date is a good reason to call first.

faq.a: Not on Saturday: none of the bars on our Gramercy list runs a Saturday deal. On Sunday, Carlotto and Oceans hold an early-evening window, and Barfly starts its late-night happy hour, which runs Sunday through Thursday.
faq.q: Is there a weekend happy hour in Gramercy?

faq.a: The Laurels on Second Avenue near 14th Street sells oysters by the half dozen or the dozen during its weekday happy hour.
faq.q: Where can I get oysters at happy hour in Gramercy?

faq.a: Yes. Barfly on Third Avenue runs its happy hour from late evening until closing, Sunday through Thursday, with cheap beer and beer-and-shot deals.
faq.q: Is there a late-night happy hour in Gramercy?

faq.a: The L at 3rd Avenue for the 14th Street end, 14th Street-Union Square for Irving Place, East 19th Street and the lower part of Park Avenue South, and the 6 at 23rd Street-Baruch College for Barbounia, Seven Sins and Barfly.
faq.q: Which subway is closest to Gramercy happy hours?

intro:
Every day, including Saturday and Sunday, Porchlight runs a happy hour from the afternoon into the early evening. The bar is at 271 11th Avenue in Chelsea, a six minute walk from 34th Street–Hudson Yards station on the 7.

The Porchlight happy hour has no drinks or food listed, so the bar publishes the times but not the deal.

Mazzat has a happy hour on all seven days, from late afternoon into the early evening. It is a restaurant in Cobble Hill, Brooklyn, about a ten minute walk from Carroll Street station on the F and G.

The Mazzat happy hour has no deals listed. A food-deal tag is attached, and a website is listed.

Hoptimist, an American bar, is at 422 Amsterdam Avenue on the Upper West Side, two minutes from the 79th Street station and the 1 train.

The Hoptimist happy hour is a food deal. Truffle fries and a baked pretzel are the items listed. It runs Monday through Saturday, from opening until the early evening, so Sunday is not covered. The price range is marked as moderate.

Mexican food is the focus at Playa Betty's, a restaurant at 320 Amsterdam Avenue on the Upper West Side. It is three minutes from the 72nd Street station and the 1, 2 and 3 trains, and it is in the lowest price tier.

The Playa Betty's happy hour runs every day, from the afternoon into the early evening. Offers include Pacifico pints, rose and Betty's Burger, so there is both a drink and a food item.

Sarabeth's serves breakfast, brunch and dinner, and its address is 423 Amsterdam Avenue on the Upper West Side. The 79th Street station and the 1 train are three minutes away. The price range is listed as moderate.

A happy hour is scheduled on weekdays, from late afternoon into the early evening. The Sarabeth's happy hour comes with times only, because the restaurant publishes the window but not the deal.

The Gin Mill, a sports bar and grill, is at 442 Amsterdam Avenue on the Upper West Side. The 79th Street station and the 1 train are three minutes away.

The Gin Mill happy hour covers weekdays, from opening through the afternoon. Listed offers include apps, beer, top shelf drinks and shots. The price range is moderate.

The Ribbon, a bar and fusion restaurant, sits at 20 West 72nd Street on the Upper West Side, a one-minute walk from the 72nd Street station and its B and C trains.

The Ribbon happy hour is available every day, from late afternoon into the early evening. Named items include a traditional margarita, draft beer, well drinks, the UWS Negroni, Bond Vesper gin and a food option.

Murray Hill sits on the East Side between Midtown and Kips Bay, roughly from 34th Street to 42nd Street, with Madison Avenue on one side and the East River on the other. Most of our list hugs the blocks just south of Grand Central: Albert's Bar on East 41st Street, The Shakespeare on East 39th, At The Office Bar on East 38th, Mulligan's Pub on Madison Avenue and Docks Oyster Bar on Third Avenue. Take Care on Lexington Avenue and Blue Haven are closer to the 33rd Street stop on the 6, and Hole In The Wall is out on East 35th Street near the river.

Murray Hill happy hour is built for people leaving the office: pubs and bar-restaurants near Grand Central run weekday deals on drafts, well drinks, wine and a house cocktail, often with something to eat. The Shakespeare opens its window in the late morning. For weekends, Docks Oyster Bar is the one place on our list that runs every day, and Blue Haven covers Sunday late at night. If you are catching a Metro-North train, the bars on East 38th to 41st Streets put you a few minutes from the terminal.

picks.why: The Shakespeare @ The William is a British bar on East 39th Street whose weekday happy hour opens in the late morning, one of the longest windows near Grand Central. Narragansett and Lagunitas Daytime IPA come off the regular price, house wines are offered by the glass and bottle, and the food list includes mini fish and chips and house-made ricotta.

Docks Oyster Bar on Third Avenue near 41st Street serves its happy hour at the bar every day, from mid-afternoon into the evening. The shareables list leans on seafood, with smoked oysters, grilled Spanish octopus and tuna carpaccio among the options. Grand Central is three minutes away, and reservations are available for the dining room.

Take Care, a restaurant at 303 Lexington Avenue in the Shelburne Sonesta hotel, keeps a clean weekday list: cocktails, martinis, select glasses of wine, select drafts and shareable appetizers, each at a set price, from mid-afternoon into the early evening. It is five minutes from 33rd Street on the 6, and you can book ahead.

Mulligan's Pub is an Irish pub at 267 Madison Avenue, three minutes from Grand Central, with a straightforward weekday deal: well drinks, green tea shots, select wines, bottles of Bud and Bud Light, Shock Top, Yuengling, Bud Light on draft and a house cocktail. It suits a quick round before a train, and the window runs into the early evening.

Hole In The Wall on East 35th Street pairs a weekday drinks list of espresso martinis, Aperol spritzes, wine and drafts with a full bites menu: wings, parmesan fries, sweet potato fries, regular fries and sliders. It sits near the river end of Murray Hill, about eleven minutes on foot from the 33rd Street 6 stop, so plan the walk.

Albert's Bar is an American cocktail bar at 140 East 41st Street, a minute from Grand Central, the shortest walk from the terminal on this page. Its happy hour runs Monday to Friday from mid-afternoon into the early evening. The bar turns 21 and over from late afternoon, so leave younger guests at home, and reservations are available.

Blue Haven is a pub four minutes from the 33rd Street stop on the 6 that saves its happy hour for late nights, Sunday through Wednesday, from late evening into the early morning. The menu covers liquor, beer, a margarita and an espresso martini. It skips holidays and major sporting events, so check before a big game night.

sections.body: Grand Central-42nd Street, with the 4, 5, 6, 7 and the shuttle, is one to four minutes from Albert's Bar, Mulligan's Pub, The Shakespeare, Docks Oyster Bar and At The Office Bar. The 6 at 33rd Street serves the southern end: Blue Haven is four minutes away and Take Care five. Hole In The Wall, near the river, is about eleven minutes from that stop, the longest walk on this page.

Menu prices skip the 8.875 percent sales tax, and the usual 18 to 20 percent tip comes on top. Docks Oyster Bar serves its deal at the bar, Albert's Bar is 21 and over from late afternoon, and Blue Haven drops its late happy hour on holidays and big game nights. Office-district happy hours change often, so read the last-checked date on each listing before you head over.

faq.a: Yes. Blue Haven, a pub near the 33rd Street 6 stop, runs a late-night happy hour Sunday through Wednesday that goes into the early morning, except on holidays and during major sporting events.
faq.q: Is there late-night happy hour in Murray Hill?

faq.a: Hole In The Wall has wings, fries and sliders, Take Care offers shareable appetizers, The Shakespeare serves mini fish and chips, house-made ricotta and a British grilled cheese, and Docks Oyster Bar lists smoked oysters and other seafood shareables.
faq.q: Which Murray Hill happy hours include food?

faq.a: Albert's Bar on East 41st Street is a minute away. Mulligan's Pub, The Shakespeare and Docks Oyster Bar are about three minutes away, and At The Office Bar on East 38th Street about four.
faq.q: Which Murray Hill bars are closest to Grand Central?

faq.a: Docks Oyster Bar runs its happy hour at the bar every day, Saturday and Sunday included, and Blue Haven's late-night window starts on Sunday. The rest of our Murray Hill list keeps its deals to weekdays.
faq.q: Which Murray Hill bars have happy hour on weekends?

intro:
Kips Bay covers Manhattan's East Side between roughly 23rd and 34th Streets, east of Lexington Avenue to the East River, with Gramercy to the south and Murray Hill to the north. Our list clusters on Third Avenue: The Gem Saloon, Sundays Well, The Factory 380, Tara Rose and Bella Union sit within a few blocks of each other in the high 20s, with Meze Mazi and Flying Cock farther up toward 33rd Street. Lexington Avenue adds The Broken Shaker, Pongal and Leonetta, and Second Avenue has Patrizia's and Sahara's Turkish Cuisine. The 6 train serves all of it from its 23rd, 28th and 33rd Street stops.

This is pub and restaurant-bar territory. A Kips Bay happy hour usually means draft beer, house wine and spritzes on weekdays, with food folded in at Sahara's, Leonetta and Tara Rose. Weekends are thinner: Flying Cock and The Broken Shaker run every day, and Sundays Well and The Factory 380 both have Sunday deals. One tip: Meze Mazi starts early in the afternoon but serves its deal at the bar only.

picks.why: Flying Cock is a pub at 497 Third Avenue with an American and seafood menu and a happy hour that runs every day from late afternoon into the evening. House margaritas, espresso martinis, green tea shots, Yuengling, Michelob Ultra and Miller Lite drafts, wine and food are all covered. The 33rd Street 6 stop is four minutes away, and reservations are available.

The Broken Shaker is a rooftop cocktail bar at 23 Lexington Avenue, on the southern edge of Kips Bay, with happy hour every day of the week in the late afternoon. The bar describes its menu as handcrafted cocktails and fresh bites. The 23rd Street-Baruch College 6 station is two minutes away, and reservations are available.

Tara Rose is a cafe and cocktail bar at 384 Third Avenue with a spritz-forward weekday deal: Aperol and Hugo spritzes, a non-alcoholic spritz, a paloma, the Kick Ass Mule, select draft beer and house wine, plus shareables. It runs Monday through Friday from mid-afternoon into the early evening. The 28th Street 6 stop is four minutes on foot, and you can book a table.

Sundays Well is a gastropub at 360 Third Avenue with a weekday happy hour that lasts until early evening, plus a Sunday window from mid-afternoon to close. Mondays bring select food and drink deals all day, so it covers both ends of the week. The 28th Street 6 stop is four minutes away, and reservations are available.

Sahara's Turkish Cuisine on Second Avenue builds its weekday happy hour around pairings, such as a cold appetizer with a glass of house wine or a bottle of beer. The deal runs Monday to Friday in the late afternoon, which makes it an easy early dinner. The 28th Street station on the 6 is about six minutes on foot.

Leonetta is a Mediterranean restaurant and bar at 181 Lexington Avenue whose weekday happy hour menu includes food, such as a Little Gem Caesar with parmesan-tahini dressing and Jack's Junior Burger. The window runs Monday to Friday in the late afternoon, ahead of the dinner rush. The 33rd Street 6 stop is three minutes away, and reservations are available.

Bella Union is a bar and restaurant at 411 Third Avenue where the weekday happy hour is mostly about beer: 20-ounce draft pours at the main bar, hazy and juicy IPAs from Wicked, Fiddlehead, Montauk and Sloop, Down East cider and seltzers. It runs Monday to Friday from late afternoon into the evening. Take the 6 to 28th Street, four minutes away.

sections.body: The 28th Street stop on the 6 does most of the work: it is two minutes from Pongal and about four from Bella Union, Sundays Well, Tara Rose, The Factory 380 and The Gem Saloon, with Sahara's Turkish Cuisine and Patrizia's on Second Avenue six or seven minutes away. 33rd Street on the 6 is closest to Leonetta, Flying Cock and Meze Mazi. The Broken Shaker is two minutes from 23rd Street-Baruch College.

Tax and tip are not on the menu: New York adds 8.875 percent sales tax, and an 18 to 20 percent tip is standard. Meze Mazi keeps its deal to the bar, and Bella Union lists its draft pours for the main bar. Bars update specials without notice, so check the last-checked date on each Kips Bay listing.

faq.a: Flying Cock and The Broken Shaker run happy hour every day. Sundays Well adds a Sunday window from mid-afternoon to close, and The Factory 380 runs its longest window on Sunday.
faq.q: Which Kips Bay bars have happy hour on weekends?

faq.a: Yes. The Broken Shaker at 23 Lexington Avenue is a rooftop cocktail bar with happy hour every day in the late afternoon, two minutes from 23rd Street-Baruch College on the 6.
faq.q: Is there a rooftop happy hour in Kips Bay?

faq.a: Sahara's Turkish Cuisine pairs cold appetizers with wine or beer, Leonetta has a Little Gem Caesar and a junior burger, Tara Rose lists shareables, Flying Cock includes food, and The Factory 380 serves truffle parm fries with its happy hour martinis.
faq.q: Where can I eat during happy hour in Kips Bay?

faq.a: Sundays Well runs select food and drink deals all day on Monday. Meze Mazi starts its weekday happy hour in the early afternoon and holds it into the early evening, at the bar only.
faq.q: Is there an all-day happy hour in Kips Bay?

intro:
Clinton Hill sits between Fort Greene and Bedford-Stuyvesant in Brooklyn, running from Flushing Avenue down to Atlantic Avenue, with Pratt Institute on its northern side. Our list here is mostly one street: Fulton Street, where Belli Osteria, Emily, Famous Last Words, Xochitl Taqueria and Bati Ethiopian Kitchen line up within a few blocks of the C train. Hartley's is a short walk off Fulton on Putnam Avenue, and The Emerson is the outlier up on Myrtle Avenue, closer to the G.

Happy hour in Clinton Hill is a neighborhood-restaurant affair more than a bar crawl. Expect discounted pints and house wine at Famous Last Words, margaritas at Xochitl Taqueria, wings and house cocktails at Emily, and two-for-one drinks at Bati on Wednesday and Thursday. Belli Osteria is the one spot that runs every day, weekends included. Practical tip: Clinton-Washington Avenues on the C is a one-minute walk from three of these places, so two stops in one evening is easy.

picks.why: Belli Osteria is a restaurant at 860 Fulton Street and the only Clinton Hill spot on our list with happy hour every day of the week, in a short early-evening window. Bar bites, cocktails, beer and wine all come at set happy hour prices. It is a minute from Clinton-Washington Avenues on the C, and Resy takes reservations.

Emily is a pizza restaurant at 919 Fulton Street whose happy hour runs Monday to Thursday in the early evening. House cocktails, beer and wine are discounted, and so are Hot Nguyen's Wings, a good start before a pie. The C at Clinton-Washington Avenues is a minute away, and you can reserve a table.

Famous Last Words is a bar at 925 Fulton Street with a weekday happy hour in the late afternoon covering pints, well drinks, house wine and a beer and shot. The draft list includes an Alewife pilsner, Flagship Blood Orange IPA, Sloop Juice Bomb, Franziskaner Hefeweizen and Left Hand Milk Stout. Clinton-Washington Avenues on the C is a minute away.

Bati Ethiopian Kitchen at 1057 Fulton Street runs a two-for-one happy hour on Wednesday and Thursday, starting in the early afternoon and lasting into the early evening. House cocktails such as the Viva le Bati, a Berberé highball and a Merkato rum punch sit alongside wine and Lagunitas IPA. Franklin Avenue on the C and the shuttle is four minutes away; book on Resy.

Xochitl Taqueria is a taqueria at 1015 Fulton Street with a simple weekday deal: discounted margaritas Monday through Friday from late afternoon into the early evening. Pair it with Bati Ethiopian Kitchen, a short walk further along Fulton, on a Wednesday or Thursday. The C at Clinton-Washington Avenues is five minutes away.

The Emerson is a sports bar at 561 Myrtle Avenue, on the northern edge of the neighborhood. Tuesday through Friday from late afternoon into the early evening it takes money off drafts and sets a happy hour price on well drinks, so it suits a cheap round before a game. The Classon Avenue G is about seven minutes on foot.

sections.body: Clinton-Washington Avenues on the C is the stop for the Fulton Street bars: Belli Osteria, Emily and Famous Last Words are a minute away, and Xochitl Taqueria and Hartley's about five. Bati Ethiopian Kitchen is closer to Franklin Avenue, where the C meets the Franklin Avenue shuttle. For The Emerson on Myrtle Avenue, take the G to Classon Avenue and walk about seven minutes.

Expect 8.875 percent sales tax on top of the prices you see, plus an 18 to 20 percent tip. Bati's two-for-one applies only on Wednesday and Thursday, and Emily stops before Friday, so match the bar to the day. Every Clinton Hill listing carries a last-checked date worth a glance before you set out.

faq.a: Belli Osteria on Fulton Street runs its happy hour every day, Saturday and Sunday included. Everything else on our Clinton Hill list keeps its deal to weekdays.
faq.q: Which Clinton Hill bars have happy hour on weekends?

faq.a: Yes. Bati Ethiopian Kitchen on Fulton Street runs two-for-one drinks on Wednesday and Thursday, from the early afternoon into the early evening.
faq.q: Is there a two-for-one happy hour in Clinton Hill?

faq.a: Famous Last Words discounts pints and a beer and shot on weekdays, The Emerson takes money off drafts Tuesday through Friday, and Belli Osteria and Emily both include beer in their deals.
faq.q: Where can I get a cheap beer in Clinton Hill?

faq.a: Clinton-Washington Avenues on the C for most of the Fulton Street bars, Franklin Avenue on the C and the shuttle for Bati Ethiopian Kitchen, and Classon Avenue on the G for The Emerson.
faq.q: Which subway stop is closest to Clinton Hill happy hours?

intro:
For a bar stop in Prospect Heights, 333 Lounge sits only a 1-minute walk from 7th Avenue, where the B and Q trains stop. The 333 Lounge happy hour is listed Tuesday through Friday, running from the late afternoon into the evening, with a shorter Saturday window in the late afternoon.

The bar publishes the times but not the deal, so the drinks and discounts are not named here. No booking link is on file, which leaves the live hours on this page as the main thing to check before going.

Mexican is the cuisine at LOLITA, a bar at 45 W 45th St in Midtown. From 47th-50th Streets-Rockefeller Center it is a 3-minute walk, served by the B, D, F and M.

The LOLITA happy hour covers cocktails such as the Lolita margarita, paloma and mezcal negroni, house wines, cervezas and bites. It is offered every day, from the afternoon until the early evening, with a second window late at night.

Late at night is when Blue Haven does its happy hour. This pub at 493 3rd Ave in Kips Bay has 33rd Street station on the 6 as its nearest subway, a 4-minute walk.

The Blue Haven happy hour runs Sunday through Wednesday and starts at night, continuing past midnight into the small hours. Listed deals are beer, a margarita and a Jeffersons espresso martini. No reservation link is listed.

Daytime is when the Cafe Luce happy hour runs, on weekdays from late morning through the afternoon. This restaurant is in Midtown, and Lexington Avenue-53rd Street station (6, E, F) is a 3-minute walk. The address is 235 E 53rd St.

The deal itself is not published, only the times, and no reservation link is listed. Check the live hours on this page before you go.

Pub and American food go together at The Wolfe, found at 425 Amsterdam Avenue on the Upper West Side. The 79th Street station and the 1 train are three minutes on foot, and the price range is moderate.

The Wolfe happy hour covers weekdays and starts at midday, running into the early evening. The listed offers are beer, draft, mixed drinks and classic Aperol drinks.

Grand Central (4, 5, 6, 7, S) is a 4-minute walk from 5 East 38th Street in Midtown, home of Mad Dog & Beans Mexican Cantina, a Mexican restaurant.

The Mad Dog & Beans Mexican Cantina happy hour runs Monday through Thursday, so Fridays are not covered. Listed deals are the signature margarita, frozen margarita, house wine and Mexican beer.

The Stag's Head sits at 252 E 51st St, near 2nd Avenue, in Midtown. It is a bar, and Lexington Avenue-53rd Street station is a 3-minute walk, with the 6, E and F.

The Stag's Head happy hour covers weekdays, starting in the morning and running into the evening. Listed deals include Snappy lager, Hudson North cider, well drinks, happy hour bites, can lager and Kittens New England IPA.

Grand Central-42nd Street (4, 5, 6, 7, S) is a 1-minute walk from 140 East 41st Street, the Murray Hill address of Albert’s Bar. It is listed as an American cocktail bar.

The Albert’s Bar happy hour runs on weekdays in the afternoon and early evening. The deal is not published, only the times.

Pizza is the cuisine at Emily, a restaurant on Fulton Street in Clinton Hill that sits 1 minute on foot from Clinton–Washington Avenues on the C train. The Emily happy hour runs Monday through Thursday in the late afternoon and early evening.

The offers are discounts on a house cocktail, beer and Hot Nguyen's Wings. Tags also mention wine.

Beer drinkers get the longest list at Famous Last Words, where the Famous Last Words happy hour names house wine, beer, IPA, hazy IPA, session IPA, pints and shot draft pints, all at set prices. It runs on weekdays from the afternoon into the early evening.

The bar is on Fulton Street in Clinton Hill, a 1-minute walk from the C train at Clinton–Washington Avenues.

An Irish pub on Putnam Avenue in Clinton Hill, Hartley's is a 5-minute walk from Clinton–Washington Avenues on the C train. The Hartley's happy hour is listed on weekdays, from the late afternoon into the early evening.

The pub publishes the times but not the deal, so there is no list of discounts here.

Brooklyn's places on our list are spread over more than a dozen neighborhoods. Williamsburg leads by a wide margin, followed by Park Slope, Bushwick, Prospect Heights and Greenpoint. Cobble Hill, Fort Greene and Bed-Stuy come next, and Crown Heights, Gowanus and Carroll Gardens have a handful apiece. The north Brooklyn trio of Williamsburg, Greenpoint and Bushwick accounts for a large share of the borough's list.

Brooklyn happy hour is mostly a weekday thing. Only a minority of the places on our list run anything on Saturday or Sunday, and in Park Slope almost none do. Williamsburg and Bushwick have the most weekend listings, so head north if your free time falls on a Saturday. The G train is worth knowing here, since it links Greenpoint, Williamsburg, Fort Greene and Carroll Gardens without a detour through Manhattan.

picks.why: La Loncheria on Wilson Avenue in Bushwick runs happy hour every day of the week from late afternoon. The list leans Mexican: guacamole, classic and spicy margaritas, mezcalitas, micheladas, red sangria, house wine and a tequila and beer combo, with tacos on the food side. Morgan Avenue on the L is about six minutes away on foot.

Papacito's on Manhattan Avenue in Greenpoint runs a daily happy hour with two-for-one frozen margaritas, cheap cans, house margaritas, pints of sangria and nachos. It also repeats the deal in the last hour of every night, the only late-night window among our Brooklyn picks. Greenpoint Avenue on the G is a three-minute walk.

Karasu is a Japanese restaurant and cocktail bar on DeKalb Avenue in Fort Greene, four minutes from Fulton Street on the G. The Monday to Thursday happy hour is bar only and covers select sake, highballs, Kirin with a whisky shot and wine, plus cold edamame, potato salad, furikake fries and the Karasu burger. Book on Resy.

Bee's Knees Provisions is a cocktail bar on Smith Street in Cobble Hill, three minutes from Bergen Street on the F and G. Happy hour runs daily, weekends included, with cocktails such as a lavender gimlet, craft IPAs, a yuzu ginger cider and prosecco, and a shorter oyster special inside the same window. Resy takes reservations.

Finn's Corner is a pub on Washington Avenue in Prospect Heights, about seven minutes from Clinton–Washington Avenues on the C. Its weekday happy hour has well drinks and house wine at a set price and money off all beer, hard seltzer and cider, with frozen piña coladas and margaritas on the menu too. Walk in, since there is no booking link.

Bitter Monk on 34th Street in Sunset Park is a weekend daytime pick: its happy hour runs Thursday through Sunday from opening until mid-afternoon. The list is all cocktails, including a Vesper martini, a Gaia martini and a Clover Club. The 36th Street station on the D, N and R is four minutes away.

Brooklyn Crab on Reed Street in Red Hook is the oyster stop among our Brooklyn picks. Its weekday afternoon happy hour covers oysters, peel and eat shrimp, beers and margaritas, with money off specialty cocktails. Our listing shows no nearby subway station, so plan the trip, and note that large groups get an automatic gratuity. Book on Resy.

sections.body: Three areas hold most of the list. North Brooklyn, meaning Williamsburg, Greenpoint and Bushwick, sits along the L and G. The brownstone belt of Park Slope, Prospect Heights, Cobble Hill and Carroll Gardens is served by the F, G, R, B, Q, 2, 3 and C, depending on the block. Fort Greene and Bed-Stuy fill in between. Red Hook, Sunset Park and Bay Ridge have only a few places each, so treat them as single-stop trips.

Expect 8.875 percent sales tax on top of any menu price, plus a tip of 18 to 20 percent. Karasu and several others keep their deals to the bar, so sit there if you can. Each listing shows the date we last checked it; happy hours change, so take a quick look before you go.

faq.a: Williamsburg, by a wide margin. Park Slope, Bushwick, Prospect Heights and Greenpoint follow.
faq.q: Which Brooklyn neighborhood has the most happy hours?

faq.a: La Loncheria, Papacito's and Bee's Knees Provisions run every day, and Bitter Monk runs Thursday through Sunday afternoons. Williamsburg and Bushwick have the most weekend listings on our Brooklyn list.
faq.q: Where can I find a weekend happy hour in Brooklyn?

faq.a: Papacito's in Greenpoint repeats its happy hour in the last hour of every night. Most other Brooklyn deals on our list end in the early evening.
faq.q: Is there late-night happy hour in Brooklyn?

faq.a: Brooklyn Crab in Red Hook includes oysters in its weekday deal, and Bee's Knees Provisions in Cobble Hill runs an oyster special during its daily happy hour.
faq.q: Where can I get oysters at happy hour in Brooklyn?

intro:
Battery Park City is the strip of Lower Manhattan along the Hudson River, west of West Street and the World Trade Center, running from Chambers Street down toward Battery Park. Our list sits in its northern half. Le District and Blue Ribbon Sushi Bar share the Brookfield Place address at 225 Liberty Street, El Vez is on Vesey Street, Friedman's is on Murray Street, and Mezze on the River is a little farther south on South End Avenue. Every listing names WTC Cortlandt on the 1 as its nearest station, four to six minutes away.

A Battery Park City happy hour is mostly a weekday ritual, and most deals here are served at the bar. Expect select beer, wine and cocktails at Le District, birria fries and quesadillas at El Vez, Greek dips with grilled pita at Mezze on the River, and hand rolls at Blue Ribbon Sushi Bar. Le District is the only place on the list that also runs on Saturday and Sunday. Tip: El Vez starts early on Fridays, so a long lunch can roll straight into happy hour.

picks.why: Le District is a French cafe and brasserie at 225 Liberty Street, inside Brookfield Place, and the only spot on our Battery Park City list with a daily happy hour. Select bottled beer, select glasses of wine and select cocktails are discounted at the bar in the late afternoon, weekends included. WTC Cortlandt on the 1 is four minutes away, and Resy takes bookings.

El Vez is a restaurant at 259 Vesey Street whose happy hour runs Monday to Thursday from late afternoon and opens earlier on Friday, in the early afternoon. Food includes birria fries and mushroom quesadillas, and the deal is served in the bar area only. WTC Cortlandt on the 1 is six minutes away, and Resy handles reservations.

Mezze on the River is a Mediterranean and Greek bar at 375 South End Avenue with a weekday happy hour in the early evening, indoors and at the bar. Hummus, baba ghanoush and spicy feta come with grilled pita, and the drinks run to a margarita, an old fashioned, a Moscow mule, a negroni, prosecco, pinot grigio, rosé and beer. WTC Cortlandt is six minutes away.

Friedman's is an American restaurant at 245 Murray Street with a weekday happy hour from mid-afternoon into the early evening, skipping public holidays. Our listing has its schedule but not its drink list, so ask your server what is included. It takes reservations through Resy, and WTC Cortlandt on the 1 is six minutes on foot.

Blue Ribbon Sushi Bar is a Japanese sushi bar at 225 Liberty Street with a weekday happy hour from late afternoon into the early evening. The posted deal covers hand rolls and two-for-one select sake and beer, but the menu text is shared with another Blue Ribbon location, so confirm the details at the bar. WTC Cortlandt on the 1 is four minutes away.

sections.body: WTC Cortlandt on the 1 is the listed station for every bar here: four minutes to Le District and Blue Ribbon Sushi Bar at 225 Liberty Street, and six to El Vez, Friedman's and Mezze on the River. All of them sit west of West Street, so the walk includes one wide crossing.

Posted prices do not include the 8.875 percent city and state sales tax, and an 18 to 20 percent tip is customary. Bar seating matters on this page: Le District serves its deal at the bar, El Vez in the bar area only, and Mezze on the River indoors and at the bar. Check the last-checked date on each listing before you walk over.

faq.a: Yes, at Le District at 225 Liberty Street, which runs its bar happy hour every day. The other bars on our Battery Park City list keep their deals to weekdays.
faq.q: Is there a weekend happy hour in Battery Park City?

faq.a: El Vez has birria fries and mushroom quesadillas, Mezze on the River serves hummus, baba ghanoush and spicy feta with grilled pita, and Blue Ribbon Sushi Bar lists hand rolls.
faq.q: Where can I get food at happy hour in Battery Park City?

faq.a: Mostly not. Le District serves its deal at the bar, El Vez in the bar area only, and Mezze on the River indoors and at the bar, so grab a seat at the bar to be safe.
faq.q: Do Battery Park City happy hours apply at tables?

faq.a: WTC Cortlandt on the 1. It is four minutes from Le District and Blue Ribbon Sushi Bar, and about six from El Vez, Friedman's and Mezze on the River.
faq.q: Which subway stop is closest to Battery Park City happy hours?

intro:
Ethyl's Alcohol & Food, a bar and restaurant on 2nd Avenue on the Upper East Side, has its happy hour details below. For the subway, take the Q train to 86th Street, then walk about one minute.

The deal is posted as house shots, beer, spiked seltzer, wine, well cocktails, Aperol, french fries and more. The Ethyl's Alcohol & Food happy hour runs from Tuesday through Sunday, from late afternoon into the early evening.

At 1454 2nd Avenue on the Upper East Side, Stumble Inn operates as a sports bar. The closest subway stop is 72nd Street (the Q train), a four-minute walk away.

Stumble Inn happy hour applies on weekdays, from opening into the early evening. The listing names the entire bar. Check the page for live hours and prices before you go.

At 118 Greenwich Avenue in the West Village, Jack & Charlie’s No. 118 is a New American bar with outdoor seating. The 8th Avenue station, with A, C, E and L trains, is two minutes away, and the price range is moderate.

The Jack & Charlie’s No. 118 happy hour is on every day of the week, from the late afternoon into the early evening. Oysters are the named deal.

Pizza is the cuisine at Emily, a restaurant at 35 Downing Street in Greenwich Village. Houston Street, on the 1 line, is a 2-minute walk.

Discounts apply to the house cocktail, beer and Hot Nguyen's wings during the Emily happy hour. It runs Monday through Thursday, in the late afternoon and early evening. The listing shows a price range of three dollar signs. It is also tagged for wine and a food deal, and the live page has current prices.

Judy Z's Sports Tavern & Kitchen sits at 1 7th Ave S in Greenwich Village, a bar whose listing mentions burgers, steak and wings, along with sports and cheap beer. Houston Street, on the 1 line, is a 2-minute walk.

Beers, mixed drinks and frozen drinks are covered by the Judy Z's Sports Tavern & Kitchen happy hour. It runs Wednesday through Friday, in the early evening. The price range shows as two dollar signs.

Manhattan holds the bulk of our list, with bars and restaurants across 25 neighborhoods. The largest groups are on the Upper West Side, in the East Village, around Times Square, in Greenwich Village, on the Upper East Side and in Hell's Kitchen.
