Murray Hill, Koreatown and the West Village come next, followed closely by the Financial District, Flatiron, the Lower East Side, Midtown and Nolita. Uptown the list thins out, with smaller groups in Harlem and East Harlem and only a few places in Washington Heights and Inwood.

Most Manhattan happy hour deals are weekday affairs, but plenty of places on our list run something on Saturday or Sunday, and Times Square, the Upper West Side and the East Village offer the most weekend choice. If you want food with your drinks, the West Village has more listings with a food deal than any other neighborhood. Each listing shows its nearest station and walking time, which makes it easy to string two neighborhoods together on one subway line.

picks.why: Filé Gumbo Bar on Church Street in Tribeca brings a long food list to happy hour: char-grilled oysters, grilled Cajun wings and beef sliders sit next to house lager, house wines and specialty cocktails. It runs weekdays from mid-afternoon into the early evening. Franklin Street on the 1 is two minutes away, and OpenTable takes reservations.

Toro Loco is on Stone Street in the Financial District, two minutes from Whitehall Street–South Ferry on the 1, R and W. The weekday happy hour starts in mid-afternoon and centers on the house lager, classic and frozen margaritas, red and white sangria, wine and rosé. It is a handy stop on the way to or from the Staten Island Ferry.

The Ribbon on West 72nd Street, a minute from the B and C at 72nd Street, runs happy hour every day except holidays. Margaritas, draft beer, well drinks and a house negroni share the list with food, including fresh fish tacos. With weekends covered and Resy bookings, it is an easy pick before or after a walk in Central Park.

Ethyl's Alcohol & Food sits on Second Avenue, a minute from the 86th Street Q station. Happy hour runs Tuesday through Sunday in the early evening, covering tap beer, house shots, a beer and shot special, wine, well cocktails, an Aperol spritz and cocktails on tap, with french fries and a house burger on the food side. Its listed weeknight hours run very late.

Ponty Bistro is a restaurant on Adam Clayton Powell Jr. Boulevard in Harlem, five minutes from the accessible 135th Street station on the 2 and 3. Its happy hour runs every day, weekends included, from late afternoon, with beers, wines, house cocktails and bar bites at set prices. The bistro also serves lunch, with burgers, sandwiches and pasta.

Republica on Dyckman Street is the northernmost pick on this page, three minutes from the Dyckman Street stop on the A in Inwood. Its weekday happy hour leans on food, with calamari, wings, chimi sliders, tacos and empanadas, and it runs from late afternoon into the evening. The kitchen lists Latin American, steak and seafood as its focus.

Vida Verde is a Mexican pub on West 55th Street, three minutes from 57th Street–7th Avenue on the N, Q, R and W. The weekday deal covers house margaritas on the rocks or frozen, an Aperol spritz, an espresso martini, a white wine spritz and the house light draft, with chorizo empanadas and french fries on the food side. Reserve on Resy.

sections.body: Weekday afternoons are the default in Manhattan, and downtown spots such as Toro Loco and Filé Gumbo Bar wrap up early in the evening. For Saturday and Sunday, look to the residential neighborhoods: The Ribbon, Ethyl's and Ponty Bistro all include the weekend, and Times Square, the Upper West Side and the East Village have the most weekend listings overall. Day patterns vary a lot from bar to bar, so check the days on each listing before you set out.

Manhattan menu prices exclude the 8.875 percent sales tax, and the standard tip is 18 to 20 percent on top. Plenty of deals apply only at the bar, so ask before you sit at a table. Happy hours change often, so check the date we last confirmed each bar on its page.

faq.a: On our list, the Upper West Side, the East Village and Times Square are close to tied at the top. Greenwich Village, the Upper East Side and Hell's Kitchen are not far behind.
faq.q: Which Manhattan neighborhood has the most happy hours?

faq.a: Plenty of Manhattan places on our list run a deal on Saturday or Sunday, most of them around Times Square, on the Upper West Side and in the East Village. The Ribbon and Ponty Bistro run every day, and Ethyl's runs Tuesday through Sunday.
faq.q: Where can I find a weekend happy hour in Manhattan?

faq.a: Filé Gumbo Bar has oysters, wings and sliders, Republica has tacos, empanadas and wings, Vida Verde has chorizo empanadas, and Ethyl's has a burger and fries. The West Village has the most listings with a food deal of any neighborhood.
faq.q: Which Manhattan happy hours include food?

faq.a: Yes. Harlem and East Harlem both have places on our list, Ponty Bistro in Harlem among them, and Republica in Inwood runs a food-heavy weekday deal by the Dyckman Street A stop.
faq.q: Is there happy hour uptown in Manhattan?

intro:
Astoria accounts for the biggest share of our Queens list by far. Jackson Heights follows, then Long Island City, Ridgewood and Forest Hills. Sunnyside and Flushing have a few between them, and a handful more sit farther out, on the Rockaway peninsula and in eastern Queens.

Most Queens happy hour deals run on weekdays, and only a minority of the list covers Saturday or Sunday. Astoria's bars cluster along 30th Avenue, Ditmars Boulevard, Broadway and Steinway Street, mostly reachable on the N and W, with the M and R serving the Steinway side. In Jackson Heights the 7 is the line to know. Food deals are less common in Queens than in Manhattan on our list, so the places that pair drinks with something to eat, such as The Rabbit Hole in Astoria and Cozy Corner in Ridgewood, are worth seeking out.

picks.why: The Rabbit Hole on Broadway in Astoria pairs drinks with food on weekdays: half-price appetizers, plus shots, house beers, house wines, mixed drinks or mocktails and frozen drinks at set prices. Order a beer or wine and a hot dog comes free. Steinway Street on the M and R is two minutes away, and reservations are available.

The Ditty on Ditmars Boulevard runs happy hour seven days a week from late afternoon. The list covers classic cocktails such as an old fashioned, paloma, daiquiri and negroni, any house spirit with a mixer, Narragansett and wine. It is four minutes from Astoria–Ditmars Boulevard, the last stop on the N and W, which makes it an easy weekend option.

Upstairs Cocktail Bar is on the second floor at 71-22 Roosevelt Avenue, two minutes from the 69th Street stop on the 7. Its happy hour runs Monday through Saturday in the early evening, a later start than most in Queens, with a gimlet, a classic margarita, a martini and a Moscow or whiskey mule on the list.

Blend on the Water sits on the Long Island City waterfront at Center Boulevard, about nine minutes from Vernon Boulevard–Jackson Avenue on the 7. Its weekday happy hour starts before lunch and runs into the early evening, with frozen drinks, pitchers of sangria and martinis. That long window suits a late lunch. Book through OpenTable.

Cozy Corner on 70th Avenue in Ridgewood has a daily happy hour with money off bottled and draft beer and Aperol or Campari spritzes, and a free slice of pizza with a qualifying drink. Saturday and Sunday are included, which only a minority of our Queens list can say. The Forest Avenue station on the M is about six minutes away.

Cobblestones Pub and Biergarten on Queens Boulevard sets one price for draught beers, glasses of wine and single mixed drinks on weekday afternoons, with half-price wings alongside a drink for dine-in guests. It is two minutes from the accessible Kew Gardens–Union Turnpike station on the E and F, at the eastern end of Forest Hills.

Sal y Lima on Rockaway Beach Boulevard is the beach pick, a minute from Beach 90th Street on the A and the Rockaway Park shuttle. Happy hour runs every day except Tuesday, which is taco night, in the afternoon, with margaritas and frozen drinks plus small chips and guacamole or nachos. It suits a post-beach stop on a summer weekend.

sections.body: Queens is big, so pick a line and stay on it. The N and W cover most of Astoria. The 7 runs through Long Island City, Sunnyside, Jackson Heights and on to Flushing. The E, F, M and R follow Queens Boulevard to Forest Hills, the M continues to Ridgewood, and the A and the Rockaway Park shuttle reach the beach. Our eastern Queens listings have no subway station nearby.

Add New York's 8.875 percent sales tax to menu prices, and tip 18 to 20 percent. Several Queens deals, Cobblestones' wings among them, are limited to dine-in or bar seating, so check the terms. Every listing shows when we last checked it, worth a glance since happy hours change.

faq.a: Astoria, by a wide margin, followed by Jackson Heights. Long Island City, Ridgewood and Forest Hills come next.
faq.q: Which Queens neighborhood has the most happy hours?

faq.a: The Ditty in Astoria and Cozy Corner in Ridgewood run every day, Sal y Lima in the Rockaways runs every day except Tuesday, and Upstairs Cocktail Bar in Woodside includes Saturday.
faq.q: Where can I find a weekend happy hour in Queens?

faq.a: The Rabbit Hole has half-price appetizers and a free hot dog with beer or wine, Cozy Corner gives a free slice with a qualifying drink, Sal y Lima has chips and guacamole or nachos, and Cobblestones has half-price wings with a drink.
faq.q: Which Queens happy hours include food?

faq.a: Yes. Sal y Lima is a minute from Beach 90th Street, and Rockaway Brewing Company near Beach 67th Street runs a weekday deal with money off select drafts and a beer and shot combo.
faq.q: Is there happy hour near the beach in the Rockaways?

intro:
An all day happy hour in NYC rarely means open to close. On our list it mostly means a deal that starts around lunchtime and runs into the early evening, long enough to cover a late lunch and the after-work hour in one go. Dozens of bars on our list have that kind of long window or an explicit all-day deal, and a small group, including Bar 314 in Morningside Heights, BLVD Bistro in Harlem and Tipsy NoMad, say their happy hour runs all day, every day.

Most long deals are weekday-only, which suits a late lunch or a midafternoon break. The biggest group sits on the East Side of Midtown, followed by Astoria, Koreatown, the Upper East Side and Hell's Kitchen. A handful extend through the weekend, among them Whiskey Trader near Times Square and Therapy Wine Bar in Bed-Stuy. Some bars pick a single day to run all day instead: Riviera Maya in Astoria on Tuesday, The Plaza At The Roxy in Tribeca on Monday.

picks.why: Whiskey Trader is a pub on West 55th Street with one of the longest windows on our list: from late morning to early evening, seven days a week. The deal covers wine by the glass, shots and cocktails. It is two minutes from the M at 57th Street and close to Fifth Avenue, so it fits between midday errands and an early dinner.

Therapy Wine Bar on Malcolm X Boulevard in Bed-Stuy runs its happy hour every day from midday into the early evening, weekends included. House cocktails and wine are on the list, along with happy hour bites such as lemon hummus, and the bar notes the deal is in-house only, not for takeout. The A and C at Utica Avenue serve it.

John Doe Craft Bar & Kitchen on Fifth Avenue in Midtown runs its deal daily from late morning into the evening, and oysters are the headline item on its own menu. It is tagged for outdoor seating, its menu also lists a build-your-own burger deal on Mondays, and the R and W at 28th Street are close by.

The Rock House Bar & Grill on Seguine Avenue is our all-day pick on Staten Island: the deal runs every day from midday to early evening. Its own listing mentions a lunch menu and a separate happy hour food menu. The closest rail stop is Prince's Bay on the Staten Island Railway.

Spanglish NYC is a Mexican restaurant and bar on Ditmars Boulevard with a weekday deal from lunchtime to early evening. Frozen and hibiscus margaritas, red and white sangria, wine and beer are all covered. It sits near the Astoria-Ditmars Boulevard terminal of the N and W, and it takes reservations.

Bar 314 is an Italian restaurant on Broadway near 125th Street that lists its happy hour as every day, all day. The deal applies to selected items marked on its lunch and brunch menu, so ask which plates qualify. The 1 train at 125th Street is the nearest stop, and reservations are available.

Hair Of The Dog is a pub and sports bar on Orchard Street with a weekday window from midday to early evening. Its listing says all drinks are discounted during that stretch, with some exclusions, and sliders cover the food side. On Monday evenings it adds a separate beer special. The F at Second Avenue is about three minutes away.

sections.body: Bars use the phrase loosely. Seven or eight hours is typical on this page, usually from late morning or lunch to early evening, and almost all of those windows close before dinner. Only a few, like Snafu on East 47th Street and Tipsy NoMad, say their deal lasts all day and all night, and Fogo de Chao near Times Square lists an all-day happy hour too.

Long deals often apply at the bar only, and some exclude holidays or big game nights. Every New York City check adds 8.875 percent sales tax, and a tip of 18 to 20 percent is expected on the pre-tax total. All-day offers get trimmed without much notice, so check the last-checked date first.

faq.a: Bar 314 in Morningside Heights, BLVD Bistro in Harlem, Tipsy NoMad, and Snafu on East 47th Street list their happy hour as running all day, every day. Fogo de Chao near Times Square also lists an all-day happy hour.
faq.q: Which NYC bars have happy hour all day?

faq.a: Yes. Whiskey Trader, Therapy Wine Bar, John Doe Craft Bar & Kitchen, Kurant, Dylan Murphy's on the Upper East Side and The Rock House Bar & Grill on Staten Island run long daily windows that include Saturday and Sunday.
faq.q: Is there an all day happy hour on weekends?

faq.a: Riviera Maya in Astoria does it on Tuesday, Limosneros in Williamsburg and White Oak Tavern near Washington Square on Thursday, and The Plaza At The Roxy in Tribeca on Monday.
faq.q: Which bars do an all day happy hour on one day only?

faq.a: Some do. Hair Of The Dog adds sliders, Therapy Wine Bar has happy hour bites, The Ragtrader Bo Peep in Koreatown lists fries and fried chicken sliders, and Half Moon in the Financial District includes a soft baked pretzel.
faq.q: Do all day happy hours include food?

intro:
The Brooklyn Crab happy hour at this Reed Street restaurant in Red Hook runs on weekdays from the afternoon into the early evening. Named offers include a discount on a specialty cocktail, plus oysters, beers and margaritas at set prices.

Tags also mention cheap beer and a food deal. The listing has no nearby subway station on file, so plan your route separately.

Any draft at a set price is the offer listed for the Keg & Lantern Brewery happy hour, which runs on weekdays in the late afternoon and early evening. The venue is described as a brewery, pub, gastropub and sports bar.

You will find it on Beard Street in Red Hook. No subway station is on file for the address.

Oysters are in the name and on the deal list at Docks Oyster Bar - Midtown East, NYC, a bar at 633 3rd Ave in Murray Hill. Its cuisines are listed as American, brunch and new American, and Grand Central-42nd Street (4, 5, 6, 7, S) is a 3-minute walk.

The Docks Oyster Bar - Midtown East, NYC happy hour runs every day and lists smoked oysters.

Happy hour food deals in NYC range from discounted oysters by the piece to sliders, wings and plates of tacos, and plenty of bars on our list include food in their happy hour. Manhattan has most of them, spread from the Financial District to Inwood, with Hell's Kitchen, Midtown, Murray Hill, the Upper West Side and Greenwich Village in front. Brooklyn has a good share, led by Williamsburg and Bushwick. Queens adds a smaller group, and the Bronx and Staten Island are represented too.

The food side of a happy hour is usually short: wings, fries, sliders, tacos, oysters or a few bar snacks, meant to go with a drink rather than replace dinner. Restaurants on the list sometimes discount a wider spread of small plates. Food deals are often served at the bar only, so sit there and order the food early.

picks.why: Filé Gumbo Bar on Church Street in Tribeca brings a Cajun angle to happy hour: kicked-up beef sliders, grilled Cajun wings and char-grilled oysters, plus a house lager, house wines and specialty cocktails. The deal runs on weekdays from midafternoon to early evening. The 1 train at Franklin Street is the nearest stop, and it takes reservations.

Republica is a Latin American restaurant and bar on Dyckman Street in Inwood with a food-heavy weekday happy hour: mini burgers, Republica wings, tacos and empanadas. It runs from late afternoon into the evening. The A train's Dyckman Street stop is the nearest station, far up in northern Manhattan.

Cha Cha Tang on Sixth Avenue near Houston Street keeps its happy hour short, a weekday window in the early evening, but it includes food: steamed crystal shrimp dumplings and other happy hour plates, alongside house cocktails and beer. The 1 train at Houston Street is the closest station, and reservations are available.

Karasu on DeKalb Avenue in Fort Greene runs a Monday to Thursday happy hour in the early evening with a proper food list: cold edamame, the Karasu burger and furikake fries, next to select sake, Toki and midori rum highballs and a whisky shot. Some items are bar only. The G at Fulton Street is nearest, and it takes reservations.

Burgerology on Ditmars Boulevard in Astoria makes sliders the center of its weekday happy hour: Burgerology sliders, short rib sliders and buffalo chicken sliders, plus a turkey burger, with draft beer and wine to match. It runs from late afternoon into the evening, and the Astoria-Ditmars Boulevard terminal of the N and W is nearby.

Kingsbridge Social Club on Kingsbridge Avenue is the Bronx entry on this page, with a weekday happy hour from midafternoon into the evening. Draft beer and Calabrian honey wings are the listed items. The 1 train at 238th Street is the nearest station in this corner of the northwest Bronx.

Piccolino is an Italian restaurant on Amboy Road in Great Kills, Staten Island, with one of the longest food lists on this page: chicken wings, mozzarella sticks with fries, fried zucchini and penne vodka, plus a lychee martini, margaritas, beer and wine. The deal runs Tuesday to Friday from midafternoon, and the Great Kills station on the Staten Island Railway is closest.

sections.body: Manhattan has the volume, with Hell's Kitchen, Midtown, Murray Hill, the Upper West Side and Greenwich Village leading the way. Brooklyn's are more concentrated: Williamsburg has the most, and Bushwick and Prospect Heights follow. In Queens, Astoria leads, and the outer edges of the city are covered by single spots like Kingsbridge Social Club and Piccolino.

Happy hour food is often limited to the bar or a lounge area, so read the fine print before you take a table. Sales tax of 8.875 percent applies to food and drinks alike, and an 18 to 20 percent tip is customary. Kitchens rotate their menus, so check the last-checked date on each bar.

faq.a: Wings show up on many food lists, including Filé Gumbo Bar in Tribeca, Republica in Inwood, Kingsbridge Social Club in the Bronx, Piccolino on Staten Island, Emmy Squared in the East Village and Park Slope, and Whiskey Tavern in the Financial District.
faq.q: Which NYC happy hours include wings?

faq.a: Yes, plenty. Karasu and Walters in Fort Greene, La Loncheria in Bushwick, Papacito's and Panzón in Greenpoint, and Hole In The Wall in Williamsburg all list food.
faq.q: Are there happy hour food deals in Brooklyn?

faq.a: Queens has a smaller group, including Burgerology and Oliver's in Astoria, Gilda's in East Elmhurst and Cozy Corner in Ridgewood. In the Bronx, Kingsbridge Social Club lists Calabrian honey wings.
faq.q: Are there happy hour food deals in Queens and the Bronx?

faq.a: Several do: La Loncheria in Bushwick, Panzón and Papacito's in Greenpoint, Republica in Inwood, El Coco in Chelsea and The Ribbon on the Upper West Side, which lists fresh fish tacos.
faq.q: Which NYC happy hours have tacos?

intro:
An outdoor happy hour in NYC usually means a sidewalk cafe, a patio or a garden, and several places on our list say plainly that the deal applies only at the bar or outside. Only a small group of spots carry the outdoor tag. Manhattan holds most of them, spread from the Upper West Side down through the West Village, SoHo, the Lower East Side and the Financial District. Brooklyn has entries in Williamsburg and Prospect Heights, and Queens is represented too.

Restaurants make up a large share, so these deals often lean on food as much as drinks: Mexican plates at Dos Caminos, Greek small plates at Meraki, truffle fries at Osteria Nonnino. Weekday windows dominate, while Osteria Nonnino, Jack & Charlie's No. 118 and John Doe Craft Bar & Kitchen also run on Saturday and Sunday. Outdoor seating depends on the season and the weather, so treat the patio as a bonus and confirm it is open before you make plans around it.

picks.why: Osteria Nonnino at 637 Hudson Street runs its happy hour every day, and its own menu says the deal is for the bar and outdoor area only. Red and white wine by the glass or carafe, beer, cocktails and truffle fries are on the list. The 8th Avenue station on the A, C, E and L is three minutes away.

The SoHo branch of Dos Caminos sits at 475 West Broadway, four minutes from Prince Street on the R and W. Its weekday happy hour is for the bar and patio only and pairs margaritas with Mexican snacks such as beef empanadas. The window opens in the middle of the afternoon, which suits a late lunch break more than an evening out.

Smoke Jazz & Supper Club at 2751 Broadway, three minutes from 103rd Street on the 1, is one of the few outdoor-tagged spots with a weekend deal, running Wednesday through Sunday. Carafes of wine are on the list, and its own menu adds spritzes, sparkling rose and sangria. It makes an easy late-afternoon stop before dinner on the Upper West Side.

Ainslie, a restaurant at 76 Ainslie Street in Williamsburg, is one minute from the Metropolitan Avenue G and L station, and its own site mentions a beer garden and a sidewalk cafe. The window on file runs Monday to Thursday, and its text adds an earlier Friday start and a Sunday evening slot. Book through SevenRooms for a group.

Meraki Greek Bistro Brooklyn at 252 Grand Street runs a weekday happy hour from mid-afternoon, with a set-price menu of Greek plates that its site says includes ceviche, horiatiki salad, halloumi, sliders, calamari and souvlaki. It is six minutes from Bedford Avenue on the L, and reservations go through SevenRooms, which helps with a bigger table.

sections.body: Several outdoor deals here come with a seating condition. Osteria Nonnino, Jack & Charlie's No. 118 and Dos Caminos serve happy hour only at the bar or outside, and Cotta Osteria says the same about its bar and outdoor seating. Wayward Fare in Brooklyn is the exception, honoring its deal in the dining area as well.

Menu prices leave out the 8.875 percent sales tax, and New Yorkers tip 18 to 20 percent on top. An outdoor-only deal may not be available when the patio is closed for the night, so ask before you order. Every bar page carries the date we last checked its happy hour; glance at it first.

faq.a: Osteria Nonnino, Jack & Charlie's No. 118 and John Doe Craft Bar & Kitchen run their deals every day. Smoke Jazz & Supper Club runs Wednesday through Sunday, 169 Bar on the Lower East Side keeps its happy hour to Saturday and Sunday, and e's Bar on the Upper West Side includes Sunday.
faq.q: Which outdoor happy hours in NYC run on weekends?

faq.a: Yes. Ainslie and Meraki Greek Bistro Brooklyn are both in Williamsburg, near the Metropolitan Avenue and Bedford Avenue stations, and Wayward Fare is listed in Prospect Heights near Clinton-Washington Avenues on the C. All three run their deals mainly on weekdays.
faq.q: Is there an outdoor happy hour in Brooklyn?

faq.a: Dos Caminos discounts Mexican snacks such as beef empanadas, Osteria Nonnino offers truffle fries, Meraki has a Greek small plates menu, and Jack & Charlie's No. 118 and John Doe Craft Bar & Kitchen both discount oysters.
faq.q: Which outdoor happy hours have food deals?

faq.a: Cotta Osteria on Columbus Avenue is near 86th Street on the B and C, e's Bar on Amsterdam Avenue is near 86th Street on the 1, and Smoke Jazz & Supper Club on Broadway is near 103rd Street on the 1.
faq.q: Where are outdoor happy hours on the Upper West Side?

intro:
French Roast can be found on Broadway on the Upper West Side. It is a French restaurant. For the subway, take the 1 train to 86th Street, then walk about one minute.

Times are posted, but the restaurant does not publish the deal itself. French Roast happy hour is the part to plan around, since it comes on weekdays, from early morning until late morning.

Dos Caminos, a Mexican restaurant on West Broadway in SoHo, offers beef empanadas and margaritas at set prices during its happy hour. The Dos Caminos happy hour is on weekdays in the afternoon.

Prince Street, served by the R and W trains, is a 4-minute walk. The restaurant is tagged for outdoor seating.

Deep dish and thin crust pizza are among the specialties listed for Emmett's, a SoHo restaurant on MacDougal Street. The Emmett's happy hour runs Tuesday through Friday, from late afternoon into the early evening, and names wines, beers and handcut fries at set prices.

Spring Street on the C and E trains is a 3-minute walk.

Seven minutes from the Bedford Avenue station and the L train, Kent Ale House is a pub at 51 Kent Avenue in Williamsburg.

On weekdays, from the late afternoon into the early evening, the Kent Ale House happy hour is on. The listed deal is a seltzer and a shot. The listing names that single offer and no other drinks or food.

In Williamsburg, six minutes from the Bedford Avenue station and the L train, Maracuya is a bar. The address is 279 Grand St.

The Maracuya happy hour runs every day in the early evening. Cocktails, draft and beer are on the list, and cheap beer and wine are in the tags. No booking link is attached, so ask the bar about seating.

A wine happy hour in NYC tends to cover house red and white by the glass, often with prosecco or rosé, and at a few places a carafe or bottle. Plenty of bars on our list carry the wine tag. Manhattan has most of them, led by the Upper West Side, the East Village, Hell's Kitchen and Murray Hill. Williamsburg and Park Slope top the Brooklyn count, Astoria leads in Queens, Staten Island and the Bronx have a few entries too.

Dedicated wine bars are a small share. Most entries are restaurants and cocktail bars that discount a house pour next to beer and well drinks, so the choice is often one red and one white. Weekday windows are the norm, though a fair share of the list includes Saturday or Sunday. If you want more than the house glass, look for places that name a grape, a carafe or a sparkling wine on the offer list, and ask which bottles count before you order.

picks.why: Therapy Wine Bar on Malcolm X Boulevard in Bed-Stuy runs its happy hour every day, starting early and going into the evening. House cocktails and a wine selection of the day are on the deal, with bites such as hummus and mozzarella sticks listed by the bar. It applies to dine-in orders only. Utica Avenue on the A and C is seven minutes away.

Ardesia Wine Bar sits on West 52nd Street in Hell's Kitchen, on the Hudson River side of the neighborhood. Its weekday happy hour covers wines, cocktails and beer in a short late-afternoon window, so leave work on time. The nearest subway is 50th Street on the C and E, about eight minutes on foot, and the bar takes reservations.

Tre, a restaurant on Ludlow Street on the Lower East Side, pours house white, red, champagne and Aperol at its happy hour. Weekdays get an after-work window, and Saturday and Sunday start earlier in the afternoon. On Thursday, by the restaurant's own note, the deal is served only at the bar. The 2nd Avenue F station is three minutes away.

Osteria Nonnino on Hudson Street in the West Village offers red and white wine by the glass or carafe at happy hour, with beer, cocktails and truffle fries. It runs every day, weekends included, in the late afternoon. The 8th Avenue station on the A, C, E and L is three minutes away, and you can book a table ahead.

Bobo is a French bar and restaurant on West 10th Street in Greenwich Village. Its happy hour is a late one on Friday and Saturday, served only in the den, with martinis and wines on the list, so it fits after dinner rather than before. Christopher Street–Stonewall on the 1 is a minute away, and reservations are taken.

Spanglish NYC is a Mexican restaurant and bar on Ditmars Boulevard in Astoria. Its weekday happy hour starts at lunchtime and runs into the evening, with red and white wine, red and white sangria, frozen and hibiscus margaritas and beer. Astoria–Ditmars Boulevard on the N and W is five minutes away, and bookings are taken.

Kyma Hudson Yards is a Greek and Mediterranean seafood restaurant on West 35th Street, four minutes from 34th Street–Hudson Yards on the 7. From Tuesday through Friday, its happy hour includes house wines, prosecco and beer, with a few bites. A second Kyma on West 18th Street near Union Square runs the same list.

sections.body: Most wine deals are by the glass. Osteria Nonnino adds carafes, and Sonnyboy on Rivington Street lists a bottle deal alongside its craft cocktails. For something sparkling, Tre includes champagne and both Kyma locations pour prosecco. Gebhard's Beer Culture on the Upper West Side names its white and rosé wines, which helps if you care about the grape.

Wine lists are priced before the 8.875 percent New York sales tax, and a tip of 18 to 20 percent goes on top. Happy hour pours are often limited to the house selection, and sometimes to the bar seats. Every listing shows the date we last checked it; give it a look before you head out.

faq.a: Yes. Therapy Wine Bar in Bed-Stuy runs one every day and Ardesia Wine Bar in Hell's Kitchen on weekdays. The Purple Tongue Wine Bar near Port Authority and 8th Street Winecellar in Greenwich Village also list happy hours.
faq.q: Are there wine bars with happy hour in NYC?

faq.a: Therapy Wine Bar, Osteria Nonnino, 8th Street Winecellar and Le District in Battery Park City run every day, Tre has a separate Saturday and Sunday window, and Bobo's late deal falls on Friday and Saturday.
faq.q: Which wine happy hours run on weekends?

faq.a: Astoria has the most, including Spanglish NYC. Addictive Wine and Tapas in East Elmhurst runs every day, and Long Island City, Forest Hills and Sunnyside have more options.
faq.q: Where can I find a wine happy hour in Queens?

faq.a: Osteria Nonnino adds truffle fries, Kyma includes bites, Therapy Wine Bar lists hummus and mozzarella sticks, and Filé Gumbo Bar in Tribeca pairs house red and white with beef sliders, Cajun wings and char-grilled oysters.
faq.q: Which wine happy hours include food?

intro:
Astoria fills the northwest corner of Queens along the East River, a short ride from Midtown on the elevated N and W trains above 31st Street. Our list splits into two main clusters of nearly equal size: Ditmars Boulevard and 23rd Avenue around the last stop, Astoria–Ditmars Boulevard, and the restaurant rows on 30th Avenue and 31st Avenue near the 30th Avenue station. A smaller group sits on Broadway close to Steinway Street, where the M and R stop, with a few more near the Broadway and 36th Avenue stations on the N and W.

Astoria happy hour runs mostly Monday to Friday, and the offers are broad rather than fussy: well drinks, house wine, drafts and frozen margaritas at a set price, often with bar food alongside. Mexican and Latin kitchens show up often, from Spanglish NYC and Hoja Santa to La Vecina, and sports bars and pubs fill in much of the rest. A few places start at midday, including Spanglish NYC and Daly's Pub. Many deals here are bar only, at Burgerology, AY GUEY and Lunera among others, so head straight for a stool.

picks.why: The Rabbit Hole is a bar at 38-04 Broadway with one of the widest weekday lists in the neighborhood: half off appetizers, set prices on shots, house beers, house wines, mixers, mocktails and frozen drinks, and a free hot dog offer. The window runs into the evening, Steinway Street on the M and R is two minutes away, and OpenTable takes bookings.

Burgerology on Ditmars Boulevard serves its happy hour at the bar only, Monday through Friday. Well cocktails, wine and select draft beers share the list with a lineup of sliders, including short rib and buffalo chicken, plus a turkey burger, and other cocktails and beers come off the regular price. The Astoria–Ditmars Boulevard station is three minutes away.

The Ditty is a bar at 35-03 Ditmars Boulevard and one of the few on our Astoria list with the same happy hour seven days a week. Classic cocktails such as a negroni or a paloma, spirits with any mixer, beer and wine are all included from late afternoon into the evening. Walk four minutes from the Ditmars Boulevard terminal; our listing shows no booking link.

Sweet Spot Sporting Lounge & Bar sits a minute from the Astoria–Ditmars Boulevard station at 22-72 31st Street. On weekdays it pairs happy hour beers and shots with a set-price food list that includes a grilled chicken quesadilla, a crispy chicken sandwich with fries and a classic burger. Its menu notes that items can change with availability.

The Wolfhound is a pub on 30th Avenue that keeps its weekday happy hour easy to remember: draught beer, mixed drinks and wine all at the same price until the early evening. It is a longer walk than most, about eight minutes from the 30th Avenue N and W stop, and our listing shows no booking link, so just turn up.

Spanglish NYC is a Mexican restaurant and bar at 36-03 Ditmars Boulevard whose weekday happy hour starts at midday, so it works for a long lunch as well as after work. Frozen and hibiscus margaritas, red and white sangria, house wines and beer are on it, and fruit flavors can be added to the margaritas. Book on Resy; Ditmars Boulevard station is five minutes away.

Oliver's Astoria, a bar at 37-19 Broadway near 38th Street, runs two windows: a weekday afternoon happy hour and a late one every night that lasts until close. Signature cocktails such as a smoked old fashioned and a spicy ginger margarita are on it, along with apps and jumbo chicken wings. Steinway Street on the M and R is three minutes away.

sections.body: The N and W run above 31st Street, stopping at 39th Avenue, 36th Avenue, Broadway, 30th Avenue, Astoria Boulevard and the end of the line at Astoria–Ditmars Boulevard. The 30th Avenue and Ditmars Boulevard stations are each the nearest stop for a large share of the bars on our list. The M and R stop at Steinway Street and Northern Boulevard, which suits the bars along Broadway east of the elevated tracks. A few spots on the far end of 30th Avenue are close to ten minutes on foot, so check the walking time on each listing.

As everywhere in the city, menu prices in Astoria exclude the 8.875 percent sales tax, and an 18 to 20 percent tip is customary on top. Bar-only rules are common here, so expect to sit at the bar for the deal at Burgerology, AY GUEY and Lunera. Small neighborhood spots change hours and menus often; the last-checked date on each bar's page tells you how fresh our details are.

faq.a: The Ditty, Hoja Santa, Daly's Pub and Rice K run happy hour every day. Via Trenta Osteria & Wine Bar has a Saturday window, and Mayahuel lists a Sunday evening window. Most other bars in Astoria keep their deals to weekdays.
faq.q: Which Astoria bars have happy hour on weekends?

faq.a: Oliver's Astoria runs a second happy hour every night that lasts until close, and The Bonnie on 23rd Avenue lists a late window seven days a week. Sala Astoria stretches its Monday happy hour into the late evening.
faq.q: Is there late-night happy hour in Astoria?

faq.a: Spanglish NYC on Ditmars Boulevard has frozen and hibiscus margaritas on weekdays, La Vecina on Steinway Street discounts margaritas, mojitos and slushies Monday to Friday, Hoja Santa on 30th Avenue includes margaritas daily, and Riviera Maya on Steinway Street runs frozen and classic margaritas all day on Tuesday.
faq.q: Where can I find margaritas at happy hour in Astoria?

faq.a: Burgerology serves sliders and a turkey burger, The Rabbit Hole takes half off appetizers, Sweet Spot Sporting Lounge & Bar has quesadillas, sandwiches and burgers, and Oliver's Astoria offers apps and jumbo chicken wings. Rice K lists appetizers in its daily deal.
faq.q: Which Astoria happy hours include food?

intro:
Midtown is the commercial core of Manhattan, taking in Times Square, Bryant Park, Grand Central and Rockefeller Center, and our list here runs from the upper 50s down past 34th Street into the NoMad blocks around East 28th Street. The biggest knot of bars sits just south of Bryant Park on West 37th to 40th Streets, and a second lines West 43rd to 45th Streets between Fifth and Sixth Avenues. The East Side adds a long row on Second and Third Avenues in the 40s and 50s, and Fifth Avenue, Madison and Park Avenue South in the high 20s form a fourth group.

Midtown happy hour is built around office schedules, and several places open the deal early: The Stag's Head, Cornerstone Tavern, Jane Doe and John Doe start in the late morning, and Calle Dao, Tavern29 and The Dawson 39 at midday. Expect margaritas, draft beer, house wine and well drinks, plus plenty of food, from sliders at Burgerology to oysters at Valerie and John Doe. A practical tip: Burgerology serves its deal only at the bar, so walk up rather than waiting for a table.

picks.why: Burgerology Midtown is a bar at 320 West 36th Street, two minutes from the 34th Street Penn Station stop on the A, C and E. Weekdays from late afternoon it pairs well cocktails, wine and select drafts with sliders in several styles, including short rib and buffalo chicken, plus a turkey burger. The deal is served only at the bar.

The Stag's Head is a bar on East 51st Street at Second Avenue with one of the longest weekday deals in Midtown, starting in the late morning and running into early evening Monday to Friday. Lagers, a New England IPA, Hudson North cider, well drinks, house wines and happy hour bites are all included. Lexington Avenue-53rd Street is three minutes away.

Valerie is a New American restaurant on West 45th Street whose weekday happy hour covers cocktails, house wines, draft beers, light bites and oysters, pitched by the restaurant itself as a post-work ritual. Groups need a reservation for happy hour, so book ahead if you are bringing the team. The Rockefeller Center station on the B, D, F and M is three minutes away.

LOLITA is a Mexican bar on West 45th Street with a happy hour every day from opening until early evening, and a late-night round of the same cocktails. The list runs to a Lolita margarita, paloma, daiquiri, mezcal negroni and Dark & Stormy, plus house wines and cervezas, and its Golden Hour from Friday to Sunday adds half-price guacamole and tacos.

Croton Reservoir Tavern is a pub on West 40th Street, a minute from the Bryant Park station on the 7, B, D, F and M. Its weekday happy hour runs into the evening, later than most nearby, with margaritas, classic cocktails, sangria, select wines, draft beer and well drinks, and it takes place in the downstairs speakeasy room. Reservations are available for after-work groups.

Jane Doe Bar & Restaurant on West 44th Street runs its happy hour daily from late morning into the evening, one of the few seven-day options on our Midtown list. The house Jane Doe Amber Ale shares the beer list with Bud Light, Budweiser, Michelob Ultra and Coors Light, with Malbec and other wines by the glass. The 5th Avenue station is two minutes away.

John Doe Craft Bar & Kitchen at 253 Fifth Avenue, in the NoMad blocks at the southern end of our Midtown list, runs its happy hour every day from late morning into the evening. Oysters are the headline, and its deal text adds Build-A-Burger Monday, Taco and Tequila Tuesday and half-price bottles of wine with a food order. The 28th Street R and W is two minutes away.

sections.body: Most major lines pass through Midtown, so the trick is choosing the right stop. The connected 42nd Street-Bryant Park and 5th Avenue stations, on the 7, B, D, F and M, cover the West 38th to 45th Street bars, including Croton Reservoir Tavern, The Dawson and Jane Doe. Rockefeller Center on the B, D, F and M is closest to LOLITA and Valerie, and Times Square-42nd Street puts you beside The Counter, Bar Mexicana and District Tap House. On the East Side, 51st Street and Lexington Avenue-53rd Street serve the Second Avenue row. In NoMad, 28th Street on the 6 is a minute or two from Tavern29, Wolfe Tone's, Desmond's Tavern and Midori Sushi.

Midtown menus list prices before tax and tip, so budget for the 8.875 percent sales tax plus 18 to 20 percent for the bartender or server. Bar-only deals are common here, Burgerology's among them, and Valerie asks groups to reserve ahead. Each listing shows when we last checked it, which is worth a look before you leave the office.

faq.a: LOLITA, Jane Doe Bar & Restaurant, John Doe Craft Bar & Kitchen, The Horny Ram, Chateau 49, Kurant, Copinette, Il Mulino and Wolfe Tone's are among the bars listing a deal every day. The Dawson runs Monday through Saturday, The Dawson 39 runs all day on Saturday and Sunday, and Margaux by La Sirène keeps its happy hour for Saturday and Sunday.
faq.q: Which Midtown bars have happy hour on weekends?

faq.a: Valerie on West 45th Street includes oysters in its weekday happy hour, and John Doe Craft Bar & Kitchen on Fifth Avenue discounts them every day. Amelia's on Park Avenue South and Ben & Jack's Steakhouse on Fifth Avenue also list oysters on weekdays.
faq.q: Where can I find oysters at happy hour in Midtown?

faq.a: The Stag's Head and Cornerstone Tavern start in the late morning on weekdays, Jane Doe and John Doe run from late morning into the evening every day, and Cafe China begins before lunch on weekdays. Snafu and Tipsy NoMad advertise happy hour all day and all night.
faq.q: Is there an early or all-day happy hour in Midtown?

faq.a: The Counter at 7 Times Square is a minute from the Times Square station and discounts bites and snacks on weekdays. Bar Mexicana on West 43rd Street and District Tap House on West 38th Street are also a few minutes away on foot.
faq.q: Which Midtown happy hour is closest to Times Square?

intro:
Sushi is in the name at Moody Tongue Sushi, a bar at 150 W 10th St in Greenwich Village, and the listing mentions a brewery and fine dining. Christopher Street-Stonewall Station, on the 1 line, is a 2-minute walk.

The Moody Tongue Sushi happy hour runs Tuesday through Friday and ends in the early evening, with no start time listed. The bar publishes the times but not the deal, so no beer or sushi is named here. The price range shows as two dollar signs.

Carmine Street in Greenwich Village has The Market Table, an American restaurant at number 54. The Houston Street stop on the 1 line is 2 minutes away on foot.

The Market Table happy hour runs Tuesday through Sunday, in the afternoon. The restaurant publishes the times but not the deal, so the drinks and dishes are not named. The price range shows as three dollar signs. The live page has the current hours.

American food is the label on The Grey Dog, a restaurant at 244 Mulberry Street in Nolita. Spring Street station on the 6 is a 2-minute walk.

The Grey Dog happy hour runs every day of the week in the late afternoon and early evening. Listed deals are house wine, Tommy's margarita, a Venetian spritz, bar bites and rose.

Pizza, burgers and salads are the listed cuisines at Emmy Squared Pizza, a restaurant at 315 5th Avenue in Park Slope. Union Street station on the R is a 6-minute walk.

The Emmy Squared Pizza happy hour runs on weekdays, from the afternoon into the early evening. Listed deals are house wine, well cocktails, beer and Sriracha glazed chicken wings.

Long Island City is the western edge of Queens, facing Midtown across the East River. Our list for happy hour in Long Island City splits between two parts of the neighborhood. Most spots sit in the waterfront section around Vernon Boulevard, Jackson Avenue and Center Boulevard, all walkable from the Vernon Boulevard–Jackson Avenue stop on the 7. The others are up by Queens Plaza and Queensboro Plaza, where The Beast Next Door and a ramen stall in the Mettra food hall are steps from the train.

Cocktails lead the way: frozen drinks and sangria pitchers at Blend on the Water, mezcal drinks and an espresso martini at R40, mules and margaritas at Jackson's. For a weekend, American Brass covers all seven days and runs later into the evening than anyone else on the list, and the Mettra food hall runs a daily window too. One planning note: R40 keeps its deal to the bar on Wednesday and Thursday only, so save that one for midweek.

picks.why: American Brass is a brasserie-style restaurant at 2-01 50th Avenue, five minutes from Vernon Boulevard–Jackson Avenue on the 7. It is one of the few places on our list here with happy hour all seven days, and the one that runs latest, with an even later finish on Friday and Saturday. The deal is served at the bar; tables book on Resy.

Blend on the Water sits on Center Boulevard by the river, about nine minutes from the Vernon Boulevard–Jackson Avenue station. Its weekday happy hour starts before lunch and lasts into the early evening, with frozen drinks, pitchers of sangria and martinis on the list. That long window makes it the pick for a late lunch with a drink. Book on OpenTable.

R40 on Vernon Boulevard has the narrowest window in the neighborhood: Wednesday and Thursday only, in the early evening, and only at the bar. The list is cocktail-forward, with the Bandolero (mezcal, tequila, ají amarillo and honey), red sangria, an espresso martini and wines. The 7 at Vernon Boulevard–Jackson Avenue is three minutes away.

Jackson's Eatery | Bar is a one-minute walk from the Vernon Boulevard–Jackson Avenue stop, the shortest walk from a train on our list here. Happy hour runs Tuesday through Friday from mid-afternoon, and the bar's own menu adds a Saturday window. Look for a house mule, a Georgia peach Collins, margaritas and red or white sangria.

The Beast Next Door Cafe & Bar is on 27th Street, two minutes from Queensboro Plaza on the 7, N and W. Happy hour runs Sunday through Friday, with cans of Narragansett, a well shot and beer combo, house wine by the glass, and money off house cocktails, well drinks and draft beer. Saturday is the one day without a deal.

Nagaiki Ramen is a stall inside the Mettra food hall on Jackson Avenue, two minutes from the accessible Queens Plaza station on the E, F and R. The food hall lists a daily happy hour from mid-afternoon into the early evening, so it works for a weekend bowl of ramen too. The hall notes that some vendors may close earlier.

sections.body: The 7 does most of the work. Its Vernon Boulevard–Jackson Avenue station, the first Queens stop on the line, serves Jackson's, R40, American Brass and, with a longer walk toward the river, Blend on the Water. Queensboro Plaza on the 7, N and W is two minutes from The Beast Next Door, and Queens Plaza on the E, F and R is the accessible choice for the Mettra food hall.

Menu prices do not include the 8.875 percent sales tax, and a tip of 18 to 20 percent is expected. R40 and American Brass both tie their deals to the bar, and others may do the same, so ask before you sit. Happy hours shift without much warning, so check the last-checked date on each listing first.

faq.a: American Brass runs happy hour every day, and the Mettra food hall, home to Nagaiki Ramen, lists a daily window too. The Beast Next Door includes Sunday, and Jackson's Eatery | Bar lists a Saturday window on its menu.
faq.q: Which Long Island City bars have happy hour on weekends?

faq.a: American Brass is the late option, with windows that run well into the evening every day and latest on Friday and Saturday. The other places on our list finish in the early evening.
faq.q: Is there a late happy hour in Long Island City?

faq.a: Blend on the Water has frozen drinks, pitchers of sangria and martinis on weekdays. R40 and Jackson's Eatery | Bar both pour sangria during their happy hours.
faq.q: Where can I get frozen drinks or sangria at happy hour in LIC?

faq.a: Vernon Boulevard–Jackson Avenue on the 7 serves Jackson's, R40, American Brass and Blend on the Water. Queensboro Plaza on the 7, N and W is closest to The Beast Next Door, and Queens Plaza on the E, F and R to the Mettra food hall.
faq.q: Which subway stops are closest to Long Island City happy hours?

intro:
Morningside Heights is the stretch of upper Manhattan between Morningside Park and Riverside Park, running from about 110th Street up to 125th Street, with Columbia University and the Cathedral of St. John the Divine at its center. Our list sits on its two main avenues. Broadway has The Heights Bar & Grill at the 110th Street end and Bar 314 and Toast near 125th Street, while Amsterdam Avenue has Massawa and Max Soha in the low 120s. The 1 train under Broadway covers almost all of it.

A Morningside Heights happy hour is mostly a restaurant affair: frozen margaritas at Toast and The Heights, pasta plates at Max Soha, Italian antipasti at Bar 314, and one set price on beer, wine and cocktails at Massawa. Weekends are well covered, since Toast, Bar 314 and The Heights Bar & Grill all run every day and Massawa adds weekend afternoons. Night owls have options too, with Toast and The Heights both adding late-night windows. Tip: Toast's specials are dine-in only, so skip it for takeout.

picks.why: Toast is a bar at 3157 Broadway, two minutes from the 125th Street 1 station, with a daily happy hour on drinks and bites in the late afternoon and a drinks-only late-night window on weeknights. Frozen margaritas are the signature, with peach, passionfruit, mango and strawberry among the flavor add-ons. The specials are dine-in only.

Bar 314 is an Italian restaurant at 3143 Broadway whose happy hour runs all day, every day, on items marked with a star on its menu. The menu opens with antipasti such as beef meatballs with whipped ricotta and fried Brussels sprouts with spicy honey, so ask which ones are starred. The 125th Street 1 stop is three minutes away, and Resy takes reservations.

The Heights Bar & Grill sits at 2867 Broadway, a minute from Cathedral Parkway-110th Street on the 1. Its own listing shows happy hour from midday on weekdays and from late afternoon on weekends, plus a late-night window every night, with frozen margaritas, well drinks, drafts and a pilsner and shot on the list.

Massawa is an Eritrean and Ethiopian restaurant at 1239 Amsterdam Avenue with a weekday happy hour from mid-afternoon into the early evening, when draft beer, wine and cocktails share one set price. Its own listing adds Saturday and Sunday afternoons. 116th Street-Columbia University on the 1 is about six minutes on foot.

Max Soha is a restaurant at 1274 Amsterdam Avenue whose Monday-to-Thursday happy hour in the late afternoon pairs pasta, such as fettuccine Alfredo, penne alla vodka and spaghetti primavera, with beer, prosecco, rosé, white wine and red or white sangria. Its nearest listed station is 125th Street on the A, B, C and D, about six minutes away.

sections.body: The 1 runs under Broadway with three useful stops: Cathedral Parkway-110th Street, a minute from The Heights Bar & Grill; 116th Street-Columbia University, about six minutes from Massawa; and 125th Street, two or three minutes from Toast and Bar 314. Max Soha on Amsterdam Avenue lists 125th Street on the A, B, C and D as its nearest station, about six minutes away.

Sales tax of 8.875 percent and an 18 to 20 percent tip are not in the posted prices. Bar 314 applies its all-day deal only to starred menu items, and Toast's happy hour is dine-in only. Check each listing's last-checked date before you head uptown.

faq.a: Yes. Toast on Broadway runs a drinks-only late-night happy hour on weeknights, and The Heights Bar & Grill lists a late-night window every night of the week.
faq.q: Is there a late-night happy hour in Morningside Heights?

faq.a: Toast, Bar 314 and The Heights Bar & Grill run every day, and Massawa's own listing adds Saturday and Sunday afternoons. Max Soha keeps its deal to Monday through Thursday.
faq.q: Which Morningside Heights bars have happy hour on weekends?

faq.a: Max Soha serves pasta plates Monday through Thursday, Bar 314 discounts starred items on its Italian menu every day, and Toast includes bites in its late-afternoon happy hour.
faq.q: Where can I get food with happy hour in Morningside Heights?

faq.a: Massawa on Amsterdam Avenue is about six minutes from 116th Street-Columbia University on the 1, and The Heights Bar & Grill is a minute from the 110th Street stop, one station south.
faq.q: Is there a happy hour near Columbia University?

intro:
Nolita, short for North of Little Italy, is a compact Manhattan grid bounded by East Houston Street, the Bowery and Lafayette Street, running south to around Broome Street. Our list here is small. The Grey Dog and Parm are a short walk apart near Mulberry and Spring Streets, Bondi Sushi is on Kenmare Street, and Botantica Bar sits on East Houston Street, with The GRID close to the Bleecker Street station on the northern edge. Spring Street on the 6 is the nearest station for the Mulberry and Kenmare spots, and the Bleecker Street complex adds the B, D, F and M.

Happy hour in Nolita leans on food and easy drinks. Parm puts Italian-American snacks like pizza knots and arancini on special, Bondi Sushi has crispy rice and hand rolls, and The GRID pairs cocktails with oysters and wings. The Grey Dog and Botantica Bar run every day, so they are the weekend options; the others keep to weekdays. Most windows close by early evening, so start early.

picks.why: The Grey Dog is an American restaurant at 244 Mulberry Street with a happy hour every day of the week, from late afternoon into early evening. House wine in red, white and rosé, a Tommy's Margarita, a Venetian Spritz, a mule and the house Michigan lager are on the list, with bar bites such as fried cheese. Spring Street on the 6 is two minutes away.

Parm, a restaurant two minutes from the Spring Street 6, pairs its weekday happy hour with Italian-American snacks: pizza knots, mozz sticks, buffalo cucumbers and pesto arancini are on special. Select specialty cocktails, wines and draft beers go for half off. The window opens mid-afternoon Monday through Friday and runs into early evening, which suits an early dinner.

Botantica Bar on East Houston Street runs its deal every day until early evening, weekends included. Draft beers get a discount, well drinks and house wines have a set price, and frozen drinks come down too. It is two minutes from the Bleecker Street station on the 6, B, D, F and M, an easy meeting point from almost any direction.

The GRID is a restaurant three minutes from the Bleecker Street station on the 6, B, D, F and M, with happy hour Tuesday through Friday from mid-afternoon into the early evening. Cocktails, oysters and wings are on special, and the menu highlights Great Jones whiskey distilled in the same building. Reservations are available.

Bondi Sushi is a sushi restaurant at 75 Kenmare Street, two minutes from Spring Street on the 6, with a weekday happy hour from mid-afternoon into the early evening. The posted menu leans on food, with crispy rice topped with salmon, yellowtail, spicy tuna or truffle avocado and hand rolls, plus cocktails. Ask what is on the list that day.

sections.body: The 6 at Spring Street is the closest stop for The Grey Dog, Parm and Bondi Sushi. The Bleecker Street station, served by the 6, B, D, F and M, sits on the northern edge two or three minutes from Botantica Bar and The GRID. Prince Street on the R and W works if you are coming from the SoHo side.

Plan for the extras: menu prices leave out the 8.875 percent New York sales tax, and a tip of 18 to 20 percent is expected on top. Parm's half-off deal covers select cocktails, wines and drafts rather than the whole list, so ask which ones qualify. Small neighborhood spots tweak their deals, so look at the date we last checked each listing before you set out.

faq.a: The Grey Dog on Mulberry Street and Botantica Bar on East Houston Street both run a daily happy hour. Parm and Bondi Sushi keep theirs to Monday through Friday, and The GRID runs Tuesday through Friday.
faq.q: Which Nolita bars have happy hour every day?

faq.a: Parm discounts pizza knots, mozz sticks and pesto arancini, The Grey Dog has bar bites such as fried cheese, Bondi Sushi lists crispy rice and hand rolls, and The GRID has oysters and wings.
faq.q: Where can I eat at happy hour in Nolita?

faq.a: Yes. The GRID puts oysters on special along with cocktails and wings, Tuesday through Friday from mid-afternoon into the early evening. It is three minutes from the Bleecker Street station.
faq.q: Is there an oyster happy hour in Nolita?

faq.a: Spring Street on the 6 is nearest to The Grey Dog, Parm and Bondi Sushi. Bleecker Street on the 6, B, D, F and M serves Botantica Bar and The GRID.
faq.q: What subway stops are near Nolita happy hours?

intro:
Along Wythe Avenue, Snowday In Brooklyn is an American bar at number 348 in Williamsburg, ten minutes from the Bedford Avenue station and the L train.

The Snowday In Brooklyn happy hour runs Wednesday through Friday, in the late afternoon and early evening. Wine and oysters are in its tags, but the deal is not itemized.

The Richardson, a bar at 451 Graham Avenue in Williamsburg, is six minutes from the Graham Avenue station on the L train. Cocktails are one of its tags.

The Richardson happy hour runs every day, from opening until the early evening. A bourbon whiskey drink is the only listed offer. The daily schedule includes Saturday and Sunday.

Ridgewood is the Queens neighborhood on the Brooklyn line, directly east of Bushwick, and the elevated M runs straight through it. Our list for Ridgewood happy hour stays close to that line. Bar Freda on Seneca Avenue and Ltauha on Myrtle Avenue sit near the Seneca Avenue stop, while Hellbender on Forest Avenue and Cozy Corner on 70th Avenue are nearer Forest Avenue. One more is on the L side: pán on Decatur Street, a short walk from Halsey Street.

Restaurants outnumber bars here, and the deals tend to pair a drink with something to eat: oysters at pán, a free slice at Cozy Corner, margaritas at Hellbender. Cozy Corner, pán and Ltauha run happy hour every day, so Saturday and Sunday are covered. Hellbender has the shortest window of the group and runs it on weekdays only, so arrive straight from work if that is your stop.

picks.why: Cozy Corner on 70th Avenue runs happy hour every day from late afternoon into the evening, with money off bottled and draft beers and Aperol or Campari spritzes. Buy a qualifying drink and a slice of pizza comes free, and the kitchen also turns out fries and mozzarella sticks. Forest Avenue on the M is about six minutes away.

For oysters, pán on Decatur Street pairs a half dozen or a dozen on the half shell with a glass of house red or white wine or a beer on tap. The deal runs daily, weekends included, from late afternoon. Halsey Street on the L is a three-minute walk, which makes it the easy pick if you are riding the L.

Hellbender is a restaurant at 68-22 Forest Avenue with a brief weekday happy hour built around margaritas: a classic, a pineapple version and a margarita with soda. The window is short and early, so come straight from work. It is three minutes from the Forest Avenue M stop, and tables can be booked on Resy.

Bar Freda sits on Seneca Avenue, three minutes from the Seneca Avenue M station. Happy hour runs Monday through Friday in the early evening, and the bar says it serves food into the small hours every night, so it works as a late stop too. Our listing does not break out the discounted drinks, so check the board when you arrive.

Ltauha Restaurant on Myrtle Avenue keeps its happy hour going every day of the week, from late afternoon into the early evening. Alongside a full bar it offers a range of non-alcoholic drinks, which helps when part of the group is not drinking. The Seneca Avenue stop on the M is about four minutes away on foot.

sections.body: Two lines serve the Ridgewood bars on our list. The M stops at Seneca Avenue, closest to Bar Freda and Ltauha, and at Forest Avenue, closest to Hellbender and Cozy Corner. The L stops at Halsey Street, three minutes from pán, so you can reach the list from either line without a long walk.

The 8.875 percent New York sales tax is not in the menu price, and a tip of 18 to 20 percent is expected on top. Some deals count only at the bar, so ask before you sit down. Each listing carries the date we last checked it, and happy hours shift, so glance at it before heading over.

faq.a: Cozy Corner, pán and Ltauha Restaurant list happy hour every day of the week. Bar Freda and Hellbender run theirs Monday to Friday only.
faq.q: Which Ridgewood bars have happy hour on weekends?

faq.a: pán on Decatur Street offers a half dozen or a dozen oysters with house wine or a tap beer every day of the week.
faq.q: Where can I get oysters at happy hour in Ridgewood?

faq.a: Cozy Corner gives a free slice of pizza with a qualifying drink, pán bundles oysters with a drink, and Bar Freda serves bar food late every night. Hellbender's listed deal is drinks only.
faq.q: Which Ridgewood happy hours include food?

faq.a: The M stops at Seneca Avenue and Forest Avenue, which cover most of the list. The L stops at Halsey Street for pán.
faq.q: What subway lines go to Ridgewood happy hours?

intro:
Thursday sits with Wednesday at the top of our list for happy hours: most bars across the five boroughs run a deal that day, well above the Friday total. Manhattan accounts for most of them, led by the East Village, Times Square, the Upper West Side and Greenwich Village. Williamsburg has the most of any single neighborhood, Park Slope follows it in Brooklyn, and Astoria leads Queens.

A Thursday happy hour in NYC is mostly the familiar after-work window, but some bars save something extra for the day. Limosneros in Williamsburg runs happy hour all day on Thursday, and a cluster of places, from Bar Baserri to R40, run short midweek schedules that end on Thursday. Expect drafts, wine and well drinks at most bars, with tapas and wings where food is involved. Tip: Thursday-only deals do not carry over to Friday, so if one of them is on your list, go on a Thursday.

picks.why: Limosneros is a restaurant on Union Avenue in Williamsburg, two minutes from the Metropolitan Avenue G and L, and Thursday is its big day: happy hour runs all day, with classic margaritas, sangria and wine on special, plus fried chicken wings in buffalo, BBQ or mango habanero. Its menu also lists a shorter Friday afternoon session.

At The Office Bar on East 38th Street in Murray Hill is four minutes from Grand Central on the 4, 5, 6, 7 and shuttle, which makes it an easy Thursday stop on the way home for Midtown commuters. Draft beer, select wines and well cocktails are on the happy hour, in a late-afternoon window, and the bar takes reservations.

R40 is a cocktail bar at 47-16 Vernon Boulevard in Long Island City, three minutes from the Vernon Boulevard-Jackson Avenue 7. Happy hour runs only on Wednesday and Thursday in the early evening, and only at the bar. Drinks include the Bandolero with mezcal, tequila and ají amarillo, a red sangria and an espresso martini.

Judy Z's Sports Tavern & Kitchen at 1 Seventh Avenue South in Greenwich Village runs happy hour Wednesday through Friday in the early evening, with beers, mixed drinks and frozen drinks on special. Its menu also lists beer buckets at six for the price of five. The Houston Street 1 is two minutes away, and reservations are available.

Bar Baserri is a Basque and Spanish bar at 225 Kent Avenue in Williamsburg with happy hour Tuesday through Thursday, so Thursday is the last chance each week. The menu covers pan con tomate, patatas bravas with miso mayo and chipotle, and marinated Spanish olives with bread. It is nine minutes from the Bedford Avenue L and takes reservations.

Whisk & Whiskey in Park Slope, two minutes from the Union Street R, runs happy hour Wednesday through Friday from mid-afternoon, plus all day Sunday per its menu. Draft beers, wines, well drinks, two house cocktails and a Narragansett with a well shot are on the list, which makes Thursday an easy pre-weekend stop.

sections.body: By count, Williamsburg leads for Thursday happy hours, followed by the East Village, Times Square and the Upper West Side, then Greenwich Village, Hell's Kitchen and Astoria. Outside Manhattan, Brooklyn has the most Thursday listings, with Queens next. If you want several options within walking distance of each other, Williamsburg and the East Village give you the most.

Thursday prices on this page are before tax and tip; add 8.875 percent sales tax and 18 to 20 percent for the bartender. R40 serves its deal only at the bar. Every listing shows when we last checked it, so look at that date before you make plans.

faq.a: Limosneros in Williamsburg runs its all-day happy hour on Thursday, and Mile 17 on the Upper East Side lists Thursday drink specials.
faq.q: Which NYC bars have happy hour only on Thursday?

faq.a: Yes. Limosneros in Williamsburg runs happy hour all day on Thursday, and White Oak Tavern near Union Square lists Thursday as all day too.
faq.q: Is there an all-day Thursday happy hour in NYC?

faq.a: Williamsburg, followed by the East Village, Times Square and the Upper West Side.
faq.q: Which neighborhood has the most Thursday happy hours?

faq.a: Bar Baserri in Williamsburg has pan con tomate and patatas bravas, and Limosneros has fried chicken wings as part of its all-day Thursday deal.
faq.q: Where can I get food at a Thursday happy hour?

intro:
Bedford-Stuyvesant covers a large swath of central Brooklyn, and our Bed-Stuy happy hour list spreads across it rather than bunching up on one strip. The central and eastern blocks have the biggest group: Bar LunAtico on Halsey Street, Therapy Wine Bar on Malcolm X Boulevard, Lucky's Cocktail Lounge on Marcus Garvey Boulevard, and BKB on Stuyvesant Avenue. Concrete sits on Broadway under the elevated J, M and Z, and The Holler is on the western edge near the Classon Avenue G.

Most of the places are bars rather than restaurants, and the deals are generous with time. Bar LunAtico, Lucky's, BKB and Therapy Wine Bar run every day, and Lucky's goes all day and into the night on Mondays. The A and C at Utica Avenue serve several of them, though each is a six- or seven-minute walk. Tip: Therapy Wine Bar's happy hour starts at lunchtime, every day, so it doubles as a weekend lunch plan.

picks.why: Therapy Wine Bar on Malcolm X Boulevard runs its happy hour every day, from lunchtime into the evening, in-house only. Happy hour bites include savory lemon hummus, buffalo chicken rolls and mozzarella sticks, alongside house cocktails made with sangria, vodka, whiskey, gin, rum or tequila, and wine. It takes reservations; the Utica Avenue A and C is seven minutes away.

Bar LunAtico on Halsey Street runs a daily happy hour that covers its dinner menu from early evening until late, longer than most on this page. The menu lists Spanish gordal olives, house focaccia with Marbella tapenade and gigante beans, with vegan and gluten-free options marked. The Utica Avenue A and C is seven minutes away.

Lucky's Cocktail Lounge on Marcus Garvey Boulevard runs happy hour every day of the week: a long Monday session from the afternoon deep into the night, and a late-afternoon window Tuesday through Sunday. We do not have its drink list yet, so ask at the bar what is included. It is about nine minutes on foot from the Kingston-Throop Avenues C station, so plan the walk.

The Holler is a cocktail bar four minutes from the Classon Avenue G whose weekday happy hour takes money off every alcoholic drink, Monday through Friday from late afternoon. The bar also advertises beer and shot specials. With one discount across the whole bar, it is the simplest deal on this page.

Concrete is a restaurant at 906 Broadway, two minutes from the Myrtle Avenue J, M and Z station, with happy hour Wednesday through Friday in the late afternoon. Its own page also lists long weekend hours with brunch. It takes reservations; we have the days but not the menu, so confirm what is discounted when you arrive.

sections.body: The A and C at Utica Avenue are the main stop for Therapy Wine Bar, Bar LunAtico and BKB, each six or seven minutes away. Lucky's is closest to Kingston-Throop Avenues on the C, while The Holler is four minutes from the Classon Avenue G. Concrete is two minutes from the Myrtle Avenue stop on the J, M and Z.

Bed-Stuy menu prices are pre-tax and pre-tip, so expect 8.875 percent sales tax and an 18 to 20 percent tip on top. Therapy Wine Bar's deal is in-house only, not for takeout. Check each listing's last-checked date, since hours can change between visits.

faq.a: Bar LunAtico, Lucky's Cocktail Lounge, Therapy Wine Bar and BKB | Brooklyn Brasserie all run a daily happy hour.
faq.q: Which Bed-Stuy bars have happy hour every day?

faq.a: Bar LunAtico runs into the late evening every day, BKB lists a second window late at night, and Lucky's Monday happy hour runs into the night.
faq.q: Is there a late happy hour in Bed-Stuy?

faq.a: Therapy Wine Bar has hummus, buffalo chicken rolls and mozzarella sticks, and Bar LunAtico's happy hour covers dishes like gordal olives, focaccia and gigante beans.
faq.q: Which Bed-Stuy happy hours include food?

faq.a: The A and C at Utica Avenue serve several bars on our list, with the C at Kingston-Throop Avenues, the G at Classon Avenue and the J, M and Z at Myrtle Avenue covering the rest.
faq.q: What subway is closest to Bed-Stuy happy hours?

intro:
Bushwick sits in north Brooklyn, east of Williamsburg and on the border with Ridgewood, Queens. The bars on our list follow the L. The biggest group is around the Jefferson Street stop, on Troutman Street, Wyckoff Avenue, Irving Avenue and Cypress Avenue, and a second sits near Morgan Avenue on Wilson Avenue. DeKalb Avenue on the L covers St. Nicholas Avenue and Suydam Street, Central Avenue on the M serves Hart Street and the far end of Troutman, and Kosciuszko Street on the J handles the Broadway end.

Bushwick happy hour is cheap-beer territory with a few kitchens that go further. Beer and shot combos, well drinks, Tecate, High Life and PBR tall boys show up on several menus, while SURA and La Loncheria build their deals around food. A good share of the list runs every day, including Hart Bar, Keybar and The Ten Bells Brooklyn, so Saturday works as well as Tuesday. One tip: on Mondays, Dive Bar BK and The Little Whiskey both stretch their deal across the whole day.

picks.why: The Ten Bells Brooklyn at 65 Irving Avenue runs its happy hour every day until early evening, built around oysters, wine specials and Spanish tapas. Walk-ins are welcome, and group reservations go through Resy. Jefferson Street on the L is three minutes away, close to the rest of the Troutman Street and Wyckoff Avenue bars.

Hart Bar at 538 Hart Street keeps the same deal every day of the week from late afternoon into the evening: Tecate or Miller High Life with a shot, wine, well drinks and signature cocktails. It is the simplest weekend option on the M side of the neighborhood, four minutes on foot from the Central Avenue station.

The Little Whiskey is a pub at 36 Wilson Avenue whose happy hour runs all day on Monday, then Tuesday to Friday until early evening. PBR tall boys, Miller High Life, wine and well drinks are on the list, and there is a whiskey and cocktail of the month. Morgan Avenue on the L is about six minutes on foot.

SURA is a bar at 31 Wyckoff Avenue that sells its weekday happy hour as combos: Korean crispy boneless chicken with disco potatoes and a Sura Spritz, vegetable kimbap with two shots of soju, or a crispy miso cod taco with a white peach highball. It sits a minute from Jefferson Street on the L, and Resy takes bookings.

La Loncheria on Wilson Avenue runs a daily happy hour from late afternoon into early evening, with classic and spicy margaritas, mezcalitas, micheladas, house wine, red sangria and tequila, plus guacamole and tacos. The Morgan Avenue L stop is about six minutes on foot, and The Little Whiskey is nearby on the same avenue for a second round.

Santa Panza is an Italian restaurant at 1079 Broadway with a Monday to Thursday happy hour that takes money off every pizza, wines by the glass and draft beers. An Aperol Spritz, seasonal sangria, a martini, a housemade limoncello shot and marinated olives are also on special. Kosciuszko Street on the J is three minutes away; book through Resy.

Vacations Bar & Rooftop at 48 Cypress Avenue is the rooftop on our Bushwick list. From Tuesday to Friday it knocks a little off everything during an early evening window, so it suits an after-work drink outdoors. Jefferson Street on the L is a four-minute walk, near the Troutman Street bars.

sections.body: The L does most of the work. Jefferson Street is the nearest stop for more bars on our list than any other, including Dive Bar BK, Juke Bar, Little Beaver, SURA and The Ten Bells Brooklyn, and Morgan Avenue is closest to La Loncheria and The Little Whiskey. DeKalb Avenue on the L serves Gordo's Cantina and Cherry On Top. Off the L, use Central Avenue on the M for Hart Bar and Keybar, and Kosciuszko Street on the J for Santa Panza. Talon Bar is near the Myrtle-Wyckoff Avenues hub on the L and M.

Bushwick deals are cheap, but the receipt still grows: 8.875 percent sales tax is added to menu prices, and bartenders expect an 18 to 20 percent tip. Talon Bar takes orders at the bar and says its prices are plus tax, and Santa Panza marks part of its list dine-in only. Specials here are posted by the bars themselves and can change, so check the last-checked date on each listing.

faq.a: Hart Bar, Keybar, La Loncheria, Mad Tropical and The Ten Bells Brooklyn all list a daily deal. Dive Bar BK runs Monday through Saturday, and Cherry On Top adds Saturday and Sunday afternoons in its deal text.
faq.q: Which Bushwick bars have happy hour every day?

faq.a: Gordo's Cantina starts at midday on weekdays with lime margaritas, micheladas and a beer and shot. Dive Bar BK and The Little Whiskey both run their deal all day on Monday, Keybar keeps it going all night on Tuesday, and Mad Tropical stretches it all night for Taco Tuesday.
faq.q: Is there an all-day happy hour in Bushwick?

faq.a: The Ten Bells Brooklyn discounts oysters, SURA pairs Korean fried chicken and kimbap with drinks, and La Loncheria has guacamole and tacos. Mad Tropical lists tacos, and Santa Panza takes money off its pizzas Monday to Thursday.
faq.q: Where can I get food with happy hour in Bushwick?

faq.a: Vacations Bar & Rooftop on Cypress Avenue is the rooftop on our list, with a discount on everything Tuesday through Friday in the early evening. It is a four-minute walk from Jefferson Street on the L.
faq.q: Is there a rooftop happy hour in Bushwick?

intro:
Flatiron takes its name from the wedge-shaped Flatiron Building, where Broadway crosses Fifth Avenue at 23rd Street, with Madison Square Park just to the east. Our list here is short and tightly grouped. Most of it sits just below the Flatiron Building on West 21st and West 22nd Streets between Fifth and Sixth Avenues, with Society Billiards + Bar across Fifth on East 21st. Hill Country Barbecue Market is the outlier, up on West 26th Street. The 23rd Street stations on the R and W and on the F and M are the ones to use, plus 28th Street on the R and W for Hill Country.

Flatiron happy hour is a weekday, after-work routine that mostly fits into a late-afternoon window. Beer, cocktails, wine and shots carry the deals, and Society Billiards + Bar adds bar food to the mix. Sagaponack runs its happy hour every day of the week. One tip: Hill Country serves its happy hour at the bar only, so head straight for a stool.

picks.why: Society Billiards + Bar on East 21st Street pairs pool with a weekday happy hour that runs from late afternoon into early evening, served inside or outside. The deal spans cocktails, shots, draught beer, wine and both lite and hearty bites, with a tequila and mezcal margarita among the drinks. The 23rd Street R and W stop is two minutes away.

Hill Country Barbecue Market is a barbecue restaurant at 30 West 26th Street with a short weekday happy hour on beers and specialty cocktails, served at the bar only. It suits an early drink before a barbecue dinner. The 28th Street station on the R and W is three minutes away, and Resy handles reservations for the dining room.

Sagaponack is a bar at 4 West 22nd Street, just off Fifth Avenue, and the weekend option on our Flatiron list, with happy hour every day of the week from late afternoon into early evening. We have its days but not its drink list, so ask at the bar. Reservations are available, and the 23rd Street R and W is two minutes away.

Le Bistroquet is a bar at 50 West 22nd Street, a minute from the 23rd Street F and M, the shortest walk from a train on this page. Its happy hour runs Monday through Friday in the late afternoon, and spirits lead its posted menu. Sagaponack is on the same block of 22nd Street if you want a second stop.

sections.body: Three stations cover the list. The 23rd Street stop on the R and W at Broadway is two minutes from Sagaponack and Society Billiards + Bar. The 23rd Street stop on the F and M at Sixth Avenue is a minute from Le Bistroquet and about four from Boqueria Spanish Tapas. Hill Country Barbecue Market is the one to reach from 28th Street on the R and W, three minutes away.

Nothing on a Flatiron happy hour menu includes tax or tip, so expect 8.875 percent sales tax and an 18 to 20 percent tip on top. Bar-only service is the rule at Hill Country, and several listings here give days without a full drink list, so ask what the deal covers when you order. Every listing notes when we last checked it; read that date before you go.

faq.a: Sagaponack on West 22nd Street lists happy hour every day of the week. Society Billiards + Bar, Hill Country Barbecue Market and Le Bistroquet run Monday to Friday.
faq.q: Which Flatiron bars have happy hour on weekends?

faq.a: Society Billiards + Bar lists lite and hearty bites alongside its drinks on weekdays. Hill Country Barbecue Market keeps its deal to beers and specialty cocktails.
faq.q: Which Flatiron happy hours include food?

faq.a: Society Billiards + Bar on East 21st Street runs its happy hour Monday through Friday, inside or outside, with cocktails, shots, draught beer, wine and bites. It is two minutes from 23rd Street on the R and W.
faq.q: Where can I play pool during happy hour in Flatiron?
