faq.a: 23rd Street on the R and W for Sagaponack and Society Billiards + Bar, 23rd Street on the F and M for Le Bistroquet, and 28th Street on the R and W for Hill Country Barbecue Market.
faq.q: Which subway stop is closest to Flatiron happy hours?

intro:
A rooftop happy hour in NYC trades a dim barroom for open sky, and the list is shorter than you might expect: only a small group of places on our list carry the rooftop tag. Most sit in Manhattan's middle band, from Times Square and Koreatown across to Murray Hill and Gramercy, plus entries in the Financial District and at the far west end of 14th Street. Outside Manhattan, Vacations Bar & Rooftop covers Bushwick and Leaf Bar & Lounge sits on a hotel roof in Flushing, Queens.

Expect a drinks-first deal. Cocktails, wine and beer at a set price are the norm, and a few add bar food, with wings, pizza and fries on Hide Rooftop's own menu and bar bites at Starchild. Nearly all of these run on weekdays and end early in the evening, so they suit an after-work round more than a weekend plan. The Broken Shaker and Leaf are the exceptions that run every day, and Glass Ceiling adds Saturday. Open-air seating depends on the weather, so check with the bar before heading up on a cold or wet evening.

picks.why: Glass Ceiling Rooftop sits at 1204 Broadway, one minute from the 28th Street R and W stop, and its happy hour runs Tuesday through Saturday. The list covers classic cocktails, martinis, flatbreads and a Caesar, so a Saturday works as well as a Tuesday. The first window is short and early, a second runs late at night, and bookings go through Tablz.

The Broken Shaker calls itself a rooftop cocktail bar, and it is at 23 Lexington Avenue, two minutes from the accessible 23rd Street-Baruch College stop on the 6. Happy hour runs daily in the late afternoon, weekends included. We have no itemized deal list on file, so ask the bartender which cocktails and bites are part of it.

Hide Rooftop at 24 John Street is the downtown option, one minute from the accessible Fulton Street station and its eight lines. The deal runs Monday through Friday and lasts longer early in the week than on Thursday and Friday. The bar's own menu lists margaritas, beers and bites such as boneless wings, margherita pizza and pomme frites.

Castell Rooftop Lounge is inside the AC Hotel Times Square at 260 West 40th Street, three minutes from the 42nd Street-Port Authority station. Its weekday happy hour covers cocktails, wines and beer, and the kitchen leans on Spanish tapas, small plates and flatbreads. It fits a drink before a Broadway show, though it wraps up early in the evening.

A to Z Rooftop on Fifth is at 16 East 39th Street, four minutes from Grand Central. The happy hour runs Monday to Friday in the late afternoon and covers cocktails, wine and beer, according to the bar's own listing, which also promises sunset views toward the Empire State Building. Go straight from work, since the window closes before most dinners start.

Leaf Bar & Lounge is the Queens rooftop pick, on the tenth floor of the Hyatt Place hotel on 39th Avenue in Flushing. Its happy hour specials run every day, so a Sunday after a meal in the neighborhood works too. Flushing-Main Street, the accessible last stop of the 7, is three minutes away on foot.

Vacations Bar & Rooftop at 48 Cypress Avenue is the Brooklyn pick, four minutes from the Jefferson Street L. From Tuesday to Friday it takes a flat amount off everything, food and drinks alike, which makes the deal easy to plan around. Its listed hours run deep into the night on weekends if you want to stay after the discount ends.

sections.body: Most rooftop deals on our list sit within a short walk of a big Midtown station: Grand Central for A to Z, 42nd Street-Port Authority for Castell, 28th Street for Glass Ceiling and 50th Street on the C and E for Starchild. Downtown, Hide Rooftop is next to Fulton Street. Brooklyn adds Vacations by the L, and Queens adds Leaf at the end of the 7.

Prices on a rooftop menu do not include New York's 8.875 percent sales tax, and an 18 to 20 percent tip is expected on top. Each bar page shows when we last checked the deal; look at it before you ride the elevator up.

faq.a: The Broken Shaker and Leaf Bar & Lounge run their happy hour every day of the week, weekends included, and Glass Ceiling Rooftop adds Saturday. The other rooftops on our list, including Castell, Hide, A to Z, Starchild and Vacations, keep the deal to weekdays.
faq.q: Which NYC rooftop bars have happy hour on weekends?

faq.a: Yes. Vacations Bar & Rooftop in Bushwick runs a Tuesday to Friday deal near the Jefferson Street L, and Leaf Bar & Lounge sits on a hotel roof in Flushing near the 7. Twist in Sunset Park also appears on our list, though its own site says its rooftop bar is still coming.
faq.q: Is there a rooftop happy hour in Brooklyn or Queens?

faq.a: Vacations takes money off everything, food included, and Rory's Rooftop discounts appetizers along with drinks. Hide Rooftop's menu lists wings, pizza and fries, and Starchild Rooftop pairs cocktails with bar bites from Tuesday to Thursday.
faq.q: Which rooftop happy hours include food?

faq.a: Glass Ceiling Rooftop is one minute from 28th Street on the R and W. Starchild is two minutes from 50th Street on the C and E, Castell is three minutes from 42nd Street-Port Authority, and A to Z is four minutes from Grand Central.
faq.q: Which Midtown rooftop happy hour is closest to the subway?

intro:
Staten Island's places on our list are spread out rather than clustered. Chili's and Dave & Buster's sit on Richmond Avenue, the big commercial road through the middle of the island, and Cantina Valencia is on Richmond Road near the Jefferson Avenue station. The rest are on the South Shore: Joyce's Tavern by the Eltingville station, Piccolino Restaurant and Marina Cafe near Great Kills, and The Rock House Bar & Grill on Seguine Avenue toward Prince's Bay.

Staten Island happy hour on our list is mostly a weekday, after-work affair at pubs, Tex-Mex spots and Italian and American restaurants. The Rock House stands out with a deal every day, and it starts at midday. The Staten Island Railway, not the subway, is the train to know: it runs from St. George down to the South Shore. The Richmond Avenue restaurants are far from any station, so plan on a bus or a car for those.

picks.why: Piccolino Restaurant is an Italian restaurant on Amboy Road, two minutes from the accessible Great Kills station on the Staten Island Railway. From Tuesday to Friday in the afternoon, the bar serves a happy hour list with chicken wings, mozzarella sticks, fried zucchini and penne vodka, plus wine, beer, margaritas and a lychee martini. The deal is bar only; tables book on Resy.

The Rock House Bar & Grill on Seguine Avenue has the longest window on our Staten Island list: every day, from midday into the early evening. The bar mentions a happy hour food menu and a lunch menu, plus outdoor seating with a menu for dogs when the weather allows. Prince's Bay station is about seventeen minutes on foot, so a car or bus is easier.

Joyce's Tavern is a pub on Richmond Avenue, a one-minute walk from the Eltingville station on the Staten Island Railway. Happy hour here is a Friday-only affair, from mid-afternoon into the early evening, with drink and food specials served in the bar area only. The tavern also hosts a country music night on Thursdays.

Cantina Valencia Tex-Mex & Tequila Bar is on Richmond Road, about eight minutes on foot from the Jefferson Avenue railway station. Its weekday happy hour starts in mid-afternoon with drink and bite specials, available at the bar only. The restaurant also runs a boozy brunch, and Resy handles reservations for both.

Dave & Buster's on Richmond Avenue is the late option on the island: on top of a weekday afternoon happy hour, it runs a second window late in the evening from Sunday through Thursday. The deal covers cocktails, large domestic drafts and house wine. Our data shows no railway station within walking distance, so plan on a car or bus.

Chili's at 1497 Richmond Avenue keeps a weekday afternoon happy hour with a margarita of the month, a classic tequila margarita, house red and white wine, and domestic beers in two sizes. It is a straightforward chain option if you are already on the Richmond Avenue corridor. Like Dave & Buster's, it has no nearby station in our listing.

sections.body: The Staten Island Railway runs from St. George, at the ferry terminal, to the South Shore, and three of our picks are within a short walk of a station: Cantina Valencia near Jefferson Avenue, Piccolino by Great Kills and Joyce's at Eltingville. The Rock House is a long walk from Prince's Bay, and the two Richmond Avenue chains are best reached by bus or car.

Staten Island prices are subject to the same 8.875 percent New York sales tax, and an 18 to 20 percent tip is still the norm. Piccolino, Cantina Valencia and Joyce's all keep their deals to the bar area. Because happy hours here change, check the last-checked date on each listing before making the trip.

faq.a: The Rock House Bar & Grill runs happy hour every day from midday, and Dave & Buster's late-evening window includes Sunday. The rest of our Staten Island list runs on weekdays, with Joyce's Tavern on Fridays only.
faq.q: Which Staten Island bars have happy hour on weekends?

faq.a: Dave & Buster's on Richmond Avenue runs a second happy hour late in the evening from Sunday through Thursday, in addition to its weekday afternoon window.
faq.q: Is there a late-night happy hour on Staten Island?

faq.a: Piccolino Restaurant discounts wings, mozzarella sticks, fried zucchini and penne vodka at the bar. The Rock House has a happy hour food menu, and Cantina Valencia and Joyce's Tavern offer bite specials.
faq.q: Which Staten Island happy hours include food?

intro:
Monday happy hour in NYC is easier to find than the day's reputation suggests. Most bars on our list run a deal on Mondays, a little fewer than midweek, because a share of restaurants either close on Mondays or begin their week of discounts on Tuesday. Manhattan holds most of them, led by the East Village, Times Square and the Upper West Side, while Williamsburg and Astoria are the busiest pockets in Brooklyn and Queens.

Expect the classic after-work format: a window that opens in the afternoon and closes in the early evening, with draft beer, house wine and well drinks at a set price. A few places treat Monday as a day of its own, like The Hunterian on the Upper East Side, and a small group of late-night deals in Gramercy, Murray Hill and around Times Square restart on Sunday and run through the early part of the week. Tip: most Monday windows close in the early evening, so leave work on time or plan around one of the late-night spots.

picks.why: The Hunterian is a wine-leaning bar on East 70th Street, and its own deal text calls Monday an all-day happy hour, with other days running from opening into the early evening. Draft beer, wine by the glass and well shots are on the list. The Q at 72nd Street is about five minutes away, and there is no booking link, so just walk in.

Walters, an American restaurant on DeKalb Avenue in Fort Greene, runs its deal Monday through Thursday, so Monday opens a four-day stretch. The headline is half-price oysters, and the deal text adds wine, beer and frozen specials. It is four minutes from Fulton Street on the G, and tables can be reserved online.

Kingsbridge Social Club sits a one-minute walk from the 238th Street stop on the 1 in the northwest Bronx. Its happy hour runs Monday through Friday from mid-afternoon, with a discount on draft beer and calabrian honey wings at a set price; the deal text also lists meatballs and a fried eggplant roll-up.

Hutch Astoria on 31st Avenue opens its weekday happy hour in the early afternoon, earlier than most Monday deals on our list, and keeps it going into the evening. The offer is simple: well mixed drinks at a set price. Its listed hours run late every night, and the 30th Avenue stop on the N and W is about six minutes away.

For a Monday that starts late, Barfly on 3rd Avenue in Gramercy runs a late-night happy hour Sunday through Thursday that lasts into the small hours. It is a sports bar, and the list covers Coors Light draft, beer and shot combos with Jameson or Screwball, Altos tequila and a spicy margarita. The 6 at 23rd Street is five minutes away.

Edward's, an American restaurant at 136 West Broadway in Tribeca, lists a Monday afternoon happy hour with one catch from its own deal text: it skips the last Monday of each month. Our listing has no itemized offers, so ask at the bar what is included. Chambers Street on the 1, 2 and 3 is two minutes away, and reservations are available.

sections.h: Monday vs. the rest of the week
sections.body: Our Monday count trails Tuesday through Thursday by dozens of bars. Most of the gap comes from places whose deals run Tuesday to Friday or Tuesday to Sunday, such as Monarch in Williamsburg and Hello Bar Bk in Crown Heights. On the other side, Walters and Karasu in Fort Greene and Sweet Afton in Astoria keep a Monday-to-Thursday schedule, so Monday is one of four chances to catch them. Late-night deals that restart on Sunday, including Barfly and Meller's Sports Hub & Grill, count Monday in as well.

Prices on our pages are before the 8.875 percent sales tax, and a tip of 18 to 20 percent is expected on top. Several Monday deals, Karasu's sake among them, apply only at the bar, so grab a stool. Each listing shows when we last checked it; take a look before you head out.

faq.a: The Hunterian on East 70th Street calls Monday an all-day happy hour in its deal text. Elsewhere, John Doe Craft Bar & Kitchen in Midtown runs its oyster deal from late morning into the evening every day, and Hutch Astoria starts its well-drink deal in the early afternoon.
faq.q: Is there an all-day Monday happy hour in NYC?

faq.a: Barfly in Gramercy, Blue Haven in Murray Hill and Meller's Sports Hub & Grill on the Upper East Side all run late windows from Sunday through at least Wednesday. Central Park Tavern in Hell's Kitchen runs a late deal Sunday through Thursday, and Tanner Smith's near Times Square has one every night.
faq.q: Where can I get a late-night happy hour on a Monday?

faq.a: Walters in Fort Greene discounts oysters Monday through Thursday, and Kingsbridge Social Club in the Bronx has calabrian honey wings. Karasu, at the same DeKalb Avenue address as Walters, adds cold edamame, a burger and furikake fries, and Santa Panza in Bushwick lists marinated olives.
faq.q: Which Monday happy hours include oysters or food?

faq.a: Yes, a handful. On Staten Island, Cantina Valencia Tex-Mex & Tequila Bar, The Rock House Bar & Grill, Chili's and Dave & Buster's include Monday. In the Bronx, Kingsbridge Social Club, Tin Marin Tapas Bar and New Green Dragon do too.
faq.q: Do Staten Island and the Bronx have Monday happy hours?

intro: Steaks and burgers sit alongside a cocktail bar at Kings of Kobe, an American restaurant at 650 West 42nd Street in Hell's Kitchen. The Kings of Kobe happy hour runs every day, though only the times are published and not the deal. The 34th Street-Hudson Yards station, on the 7 line, is eight minutes away on foot. An all-day tag appears on the page.

Small plates with an amount off, cocktails, draft beer, wines and classic cocktails all feature in the Lady Blue happy hour, which runs on weekdays. The cocktail bar is at 363 W 46th St in Hell's Kitchen, five minutes on foot from the 50th Street station, where the C and E trains stop. Oysters appear among the listing tags.

Margaritas, an Aperol drink, an espresso martini and a white wine spritz share the menu with chorizo empanadas, French fries and a light draft at the Vida Verde happy hour. It runs on weekdays at this Mexican pub, 248 West 55th Street in Hell's Kitchen, three minutes on foot from the 57th Street-7th Avenue station (N, Q, R and W trains).

Nine minutes on foot from 1st Avenue station on the L train, The Summit is a bar in Manhattan's East Village, at 133 Avenue C. The Summit happy hour runs on weekdays.

No deals are published, only the days and hours, so the bar lists the times but not the deal. No reservation link is listed. See this page for live hours before you set out.

Monday through Thursday, Mad Dog and Beans lists a happy hour at its Mexican restaurant at 83 Pearl Street in the Financial District, Manhattan. The Mad Dog and Beans happy hour covers a signature margarita, a frozen margarita, house wine and Mexican beer.

The 1, R and W trains stop at Whitehall Street-South Ferry, a three-minute walk. Live prices and hours are on this page.

The Industry Kitchen happy hour runs on weekdays and lists draft beer, wines, margaritas and an Aperol spritz. The American restaurant is at 70 South Street in the Financial District, Manhattan.

Wall Street station, served by the 2 and 3 trains, is a five-minute walk. Tags point to a food deal as well. Live prices and hours are on this page.

Specialty cocktails get a set-price deal during the Rivercrest happy hour, which runs on weekdays and ends in the early evening. Rivercrest is a bar listed with American traditional cuisine at 33-15 Ditmars Boulevard in Astoria.

Astoria–Ditmars Boulevard station, served by the N and W, is a three minute walk away. Cocktails and wine are among its tags.
